title: Our guide to every Week 10 game: Matchup previews, predictions, picks and nuggets
summary: There are 13 more games in Week 10, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is here. The trade deadline came and went, with some surprising moves. QB Kirk Cousins is expected to be the Vikings' starting quarterback once again, the Chiefs added WR Josh Downs and ... RB Jonathan Taylor is still in Indianapolis. A few teams added and others subtracted from their rosters. So, now it's time to dive back into the games.
We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Aaron Schatz makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Schatz all give us final score picks for every game.
Let's get into the full Week 10 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Chargers and Ravens on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)
Jump to a matchup: NE-DET | BUF-NYJ | CAR-NO JAX-TEN | KC-ATL | MIA-IND MIN-GB | HOU-CLE | SEA-LV LAR-ARI | SF-DAL | PIT-CIN LAC-BAL
Thursday: WSH-NYG Bye: CHI , DEN , PHI , TB
9:30 a.m. ET | Fox | DET -2.5 (51.5 O/U)
What we're hearing on the Patriots: New England is hoping to rebound from a poor defensive effort last week. Coordinator Zak Kuhr said CB Christian Gonzalez had some plays he would want back, but also said there were other plays where he could have been the closest defender because of breakdowns elsewhere. Kuhr acknowledged that very little went right for the defense but thought the unit took steps Wednesday in a spirited practice that featured better communication and connectivity. Kuhr added that the team's belief in Gonzalez hasn't wavered. -- Mike Reiss
What we're hearing on the Lions: It's not every day that the Lions are selected to play in an international game. In fact, it hasn't happened since 2015, so this is a huge deal for the franchise. WR Amon-Ra St. Brown 's mother, Miriam, hails from Germany, and he frequently visited the country as a child. This will be a new experience for coach Dan Campbell. "As far as I've been across the pond is London, and that was for [a game]," Campbell said. "And I already mentioned, I had an extra pair of underwear and socks and that was it, all right. And a toothbrush, but that's as far as I've been over there." -- Eric Woodyard
Stat to know: Lions QB Jared Goff has had consecutive games with fewer than 200 passing yards for just the second time over the past five seasons. -- ESPN Research
Bold prediction: Patriots QB Drake Maye will not throw an interception against the Lions. His 11 interceptions this season are the second most in the league. In general, about 20% of passes defensed turn into interceptions. It's been a little lower leaguewide this season (16%). For Maye, it has been 34%. So he has been unlucky and shouldn't be as interception prone going forward. -- Schatz
Injuries: Patriots | Lions
Fantasy nugget: Corey Kiner could be the Patriots' lead RB against the Lions. Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to miss the game with a knee injury , and TreVeyon Henderson has been ruled out . Kiner has topped 50 rushing yards in three of his past five games despite playing a reserve role. Detroit is a difficult matchup, allowing the second-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs. However, Kiner could see enough volume to be a viable flex option. See Week 10 rankings . -- Moody
Betting insight: The Patriots have failed to cover four straight games, tied for the NFL's longest active streak and their longest since a five-game stretch in 2024. Detroit can keep that going. New England allows 10.6 yards per pass attempt against play-action, which Goff uses constantly. St. Brown can attack the slot, while New England's battered offensive line leaves Maye dodging pressure. Read more . -- Maldonado
Maldonado's pick: Lions 28, Patriots 23 Moody's pick: Lions 31, Patriots 24 Schatz's pick: Patriots 27, Lions 24 FPI prediction: DET, 52.6% (by an average of 0.7 points)
Matchup must-reads: Pats' Stevenson expected to miss time with knee tendon issue
1 p.m. ET | CBS | BUF -8.5 (50.5 O/U)
What we're hearing on the Bills: Coming off a short week following "Monday Night Football," the Bills are still easing LT Dion Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson back into the lineup. But the Bills are plenty aware of Jets coach Aaron Glenn's aggressive tendencies and standout rookie edge rusher David Bailey 's recent hot streak. Coach Joe Brady and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael said they'll have to be aware of where Bailey lines up every play, and the task of keeping him out of the backfield is urgent: "He's already a star right now," Brady says, "but he's going to be a problem for a lot of years." -- Nick Suss
What we're hearing on the Jets: The spiraling defense has allowed 32 points per game over the team's current four-game losing streak. Glenn said he's "looking at everything" in an attempt to halt the slide. He doesn't have many personnel options, though it appears that disgruntled edge rusher Will McDonald IV will get more playing time than usual. The Jets have another long interception drought brewing -- five straight games without a pick, 15 shy of the league record (set by them just prior to the current five-game slump). -- Rich Cimini
Stat to know: Bills RB James Cook III has had 75-plus rushing yards in seven straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest by a Bills player since Travis Henry in 2003 (eight). -- ESPN Research
Bold prediction: Jets WR Garrett Wilson ( concussion ) will return and set a season high with at least 110 receiving yards. Buffalo currently ranks 27th in DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) against WR1s, and Wilson is the Jets' clear top option. -- Schatz
Fantasy nugget: Jets RB Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence last week and led the Jets' backfield with 18 touches and 11.7 fantasy points. Before a quad injury, Hall had been the clear lead back on early downs, but he split that work much more evenly with Braelon Allen in Week 9. Allen also played more snaps and ran twice as many routes. Hall could see his snap share increase this week and has a favorable matchup against a Bills defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to RBs. See Week 10 rankings . -- Moody
Betting insight: The Jets are 1-7 ATS (against the spread) in division games since the start of last season, worst in the NFL. Their defense has been getting picked apart lately, and now QB Josh Allen gets his turn. Buffalo scores on more than half its possessions. The Jets struggle to finish drives with touchdowns, and trading field goals for touchdowns makes keeping up much harder. Read more . -- Maldonado
Maldonado's pick: Bills 30, Jets 20 Moody's pick: Bills 34, Jets 20 Schatz's pick: Bills 24, Jets 16 FPI prediction: BUF, 82.8% (by an average of 9.4 points)
Matchup must-reads: New Bills safety Hooker will be 'ready to go' ... Why 2-7 Jets preferred to keep roster intact at trade deadline ... Jets' McDonald has 'earned' bigger role, coach says
1 p.m. ET | Fox | NO -2.5 (48.5 O/U)
What we're hearing on the Panthers: Interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash won't mince words when he talks about his philosophy: "We're going to load the box. We're going to stop the run and make you throw to beat us." Rookie defensive tackle Lee Hunter , a second-round pick, should be a big part of that plan against the Saints. Hunter played only 13 snaps against Denver, but Wash says the lineman's playing time will be a "major, major point of emphasis" moving forward. -- Mike Kaye
What we're hearing on the Saints: The run game could look different for the second straight week. One week after claiming Audric Estime , the Saints could get Travis Etienne Jr . back from a…
author: NFL Nation, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody and Aaron Schatz

title: 15 predictions for NFL Week 10
summary: Touchdown for Chuba Hubbard? Fantasy upside for Aaron Rodgers. Let's predict 15 things for Week 10.
full_text:
Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Commanders beat the Giants on Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.
First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.
Will the Steelers upset the Bengals? How many yards will Trey McBride have against the Rams? Could Jadarian Price score his first NFL touchdown? And will Raiders coach Klint Kubiak dial up a trick play in Fernando Mendoza 's first start?
Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.
Jump to: Upset picks | Projected stat lines Fantasy sleepers, surprises TD scorers | Other predictions
Carolina Panthers +2.5 (+110 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints
Quarterback Bryce Young is getting the ball out more quickly recently without sacrificing chances downfield, which could be helpful against New Orleans' pass rush. The Saints are allowing 7.8 yards per pass attempt, giving Tetairoa McMillan opportunities to make big plays.
New Orleans hasn't gotten much from its running game, and it will be without starting center Erik McCoy ( biceps injury ) on Sunday . That puts more stress on quarterback Tyler Shough , enabling Carolina to keep this close and potentially win outright.
Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Cincinnati Bengals
Running back Jaylen Warren gives Pittsburgh a way to control this game. He already piled up 176 total yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati , and the Bengals keep giving up long runs this season.
Cincinnati also struggles to defend the middle of the field, where Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has strong options in WR Germie Bernard and TE Darnell Washington . Bengals QB Joe Burrow will get his points, but Pittsburgh can answer without asking Rodgers to force deep throws.
Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins : 11 targets, 7 receptions, 78 receiving yards, 1 touchdown
Every year I look for the players who are excelling in ESPN's open score -- which measures a receiver's ability to get open on all routes , regardless of target -- but struggling in catch score. That's because open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates better with future production.
Washington fits this profile exactly with an 82 open score (tied with Garrett Wilson for second best) but just a 38 catch score (below average). So there is a decent chance Washington's production will increase, and it could happen as early as this Sunday -- even with backup quarterback Kyle McCord throwing him the ball. Washington should line up against Colts nickel cornerback Justin Walley , who missed the past two games with a knee injury and is allowing 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's well above the 1.1 average.
Trey McBride , TE, Arizona Cardinals : 13 targets, 9 receptions, 99 receiving yards
If I were quarterback Carson Beck , I would make a point of throwing to McBride when in doubt during my NFL debut . But that would be especially true now that Michael Wilson is out for the season with a neck injury . And even further because 23% of targets against the Rams' defense have been to tight ends, the sixth-highest rate in the league.
As long as cornerback Trent McDuffie isn't on McBride, he ought to be the priority target on most plays. If the Cardinals fall behind, McBride should be in line for quite a bit of garbage-time production to come close to the 100-yard mark.
Justin Eboigbe , DT, Los Angeles Chargers : 1.0 sacks, 4 pressures, 19% pass rush win rate
Eboigbe recorded 6.0 sacks a year ago but has just 0.5 this season. Plus, he has a well-below-average pass rush win rate. So why am I forecasting a big game for Eboigbe on Monday ? Because of who he'll line up against. Ravens right guard John Simpson has a sixth-percentile pass block win rate at the position, while center Cam Jurgens is literally last in pass block win rate at his position since he started playing for the Ravens in Week 7.
Aaron Rodgers , QB, Pittsburgh Steelers (35.4% rostered in ESPN leagues)
Rodgers has averaged just 8.9 fantasy points over his past two games, with Pittsburgh leaning heavily on its running game. That could change Sunday night against a Bengals offense that ranks second in points per game, which could force the Steelers to throw more to keep pace.
Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdown passes against Cincinnati in Week 3 , finishing with 22.6 fantasy points. The Bengals have also allowed 17.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.
Corey Kiner , RB, New England Patriots (31.9%)
Kiner could lead the Patriots' backfield against the Lions this week , with Rhamondre Stevenson listed as questionable ( knee tendon issue ) and TreVeyon Henderson is out . Kiner rushed for 55 yards and a touchdown on eight carries against the Packers last week ; he leads New England with 4.9 yards per carry this season.
Detroit has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, so it's a tough matchup. But Kiner could see 14-plus rushing attempts, while Lan Larison handles more of the work on passing downs.
Tutu Atwell , WR, Los Angeles Rams (8.1%)
With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both sidelined, Atwell could see a lot more targets against the Cardinals . He has drawn nine targets over his past two games and played more snaps than any other healthy Rams receiver against the Commanders.
Arizona has allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers and the second-most passing touchdowns in the league. Atwell's production has been inconsistent, but his ability to make plays downfield and the opportunity for more targets make him worth considering in deeper leagues.
Jadarian Price , RB, Seattle Seahawks
Price had 78 total yards in the Week 9 win over the Cardinals , and he looked explosive in the pass game with four receptions for 54 yards. He will continue to split touches with Zach Charbonnet on Sunday versus the Raiders , but I see him scoring his first pro touchdown here -- off a screen pass.
George Kittle , TE, San Francisco 49ers
Take the target volume with Kittle, plus the prime matchup versus the Dallas defense . Kittle has seen at least seven targets in three straight games, and coach Kyle Shanahan can scheme up his tight end to press the seams against the Cowboys' split-safety coverages.
I'd expect multiple red zone targets for Kittle on Sunday. And the 49ers are the best in the league at turning those targets into touchdowns (84.6% red zone touchdown percentage this season).
Chuba Hubbard , RB, Carolina Panthers
Hubbard has at least one rushing score in three of his past five games, and he is seeing consistent volume with 20 or more touches in four contests. Meanwhile, the Saints are giving up 133.9 rushing yards per game (fourth most) and have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns this season (tied for second most). With steady volume and red zone touches, Hubbard could easily find the end zone Sunday.
Rams WR CJ Daniels will score a touchdown
The Rams' undrafted free agent receiver is in line for his first NFL action now that Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on IR. Daniels critically has something that projected starting receivers Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell lack: size. At 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, don't be surprised if Daniels sees third-down and red zone usage against the Cardinals.
There will be four combined missed field goals in Chiefs-Falcons
The Chiefs are rolling with Harrison Butker for another week despite his 12-for-19 start on field goal attempts -- he's 6-for-13 on anything 40-plus yards. Meanwhile, the Falcons signed Jake Moody off the Ravens' practice squad following the release of Nick Folk (13-for-18). I'm…
author: Matt Bowen, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody, Ben Solak and Seth Walder

title: Sources: Vikings made initial Cousins trade call before MNF meltdown
summary: The Vikings initially reached out to the Raiders about a Kirk Cousins trade before their MNF game against the Bills, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
full_text:
The first time the Vikings reached out to the Raiders about a potential trade for Kirk Cousins was midday Monday, hours before Minnesota played the Bills on "Monday Night Football," league sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
During that call, the Vikings made it clear to the Raiders that they wanted to see how Monday night went first before having any further conversations about Cousins, but they would be in touch if needed.
Bright and early the next morning, hours after Minnesota's offensive meltdown, the Vikings called the Raiders before 6 a.m. PT and set the wheels in motion for a potential Cousins trade.
It was not a deal the Raiders wanted or were looking to make, especially when Minnesota's initial offer was a fifth-round draft pick, according to sources.
But once the Vikings upped their offer to a third-round pick, the Raiders had discussions about whether the trade made sense, and here's where they landed:
Not only would they be receiving a third-round pick, but they also would free up $10 million in cash for the 2027 season, as the bonus guarantee owed to Cousins would shift to Minnesota's responsibility. It was not a trade that the Raiders enjoyed making, but one they believed would be in the best interests of the organization.
The Raiders also believed 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza has looked, in the word of one source, "phenomenal" in practice. There never was going to be a right time to insert Mendoza into the starting lineup, but Minnesota made this as good a time as any.
Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, and Mendoza will make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .
Competition committee to discuss trade snafus
The NFL's competition committee is expected to discuss a potential solution after multiple trades this week were voided or altered, according to sources.
In the last week alone, the Bengals declined to make a trade for linebacker Arnold Ebiketie after agreeing to terms with the Eagles ; the Lions and Jets altered the compensation they initially agreed to in a trade for safety Andre Cisco ; and the Broncos voided a trade with the Chargers for Daiyan Henley after concerns about the linebacker's knee and the sides were unable to agree to revised compensation.
Last offseason, the Raiders and Ravens agreed to a Maxx Crosby trade before the star pass rusher failed his physical and the deal was voided.
Now front office executives are complaining, and the competition committee is expected to address the issue during the offseason.
Various front office executives last week pointed out that trade terms should not be negotiable once they are agreed to, as the Lions attempted to do in a deal for Cisco and the Broncos attempted to do with Henley.
Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said as much to reporters Thursday, asserting that the loophole in the NFL's trade system needs to be closed so that teams cannot back out of deals.
The Eagles were not pleased that the Bengals reneged on their deal for Ebiketie after learning they would lose a third-round compensatory pick, and the Chargers were unhappy that the Broncos tried to change the terms on their deal for Henley after he took a physical that led to questions about his knee.
It is an issue that bears watching this offseason, and some around the league believe rule modifications are in order.
A possible solution would be preventing the teams from altering draft picks after a trade is agreed upon, only giving teams the option to accept or not.
The Jaguars and Bills will be in competition to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl, but both were in competition for some of the same players ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles.
The two teams most aggressive for former Falcons safety Jessie Bates also were the Bills and Jaguars, who traded second- and fifth-round picks to Atlanta.
After the Jaguars traded for Davis and Bates, the Bills pivoted to two safeties: Arizona 's Budda Baker and Tennessee 's Amani Hooker . The Cardinals declined to trade their respected veteran safety, but the Titans listened and agreed to trade Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Bills for a second-round pick.
In the end, two of the AFC's best each got better. They competed for some of the same players and now are expected to be competing for the AFC championship.
Keeping up with the Joneses
The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones .
When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done.
Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers.
This was not the first time the teams had spoken about Jones in a possible trade and not the first time San Francisco had set a price that high. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback and would trade him only for a deal they had no choice but to accept.
To add to that value, Jones won four of his first five starts in place of the injured Brock Purdy last year despite battling injuries of his own and ended up with a 5-3 record and a QB rating of 97.4 for the season.
In the final year of his two-year, $8.41 million contract, Jones is a free agent after the season.
The Packers and Broncos checked in on Titans running back Tony Pollard , whom Tennessee would not have traded for anything less than a third-round pick.
While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted -- Dallas Goedert .
Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027.
author: Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport

title: NFL reassigns backup referees to work games within driving distance
summary: The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues from Friday's FAA ground stop, has reassigned officials to Week 10 games within driving distance of their homes.
full_text:
The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues stemming from the FAA ground stop Friday, has adjusted its officiating assignments for domestic games in Week 10, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns.
Airlines across the U.S. worked Saturday to recover from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years that canceled more than 2,000 flights, spread ripple effects around the world, stranded passengers and forced professional and college sports teams to scramble for alternate transportation.
The NFL's changes mean three backup referees -- umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard -- will work as referees on Sunday.
Heydt will be at the Carolina - New Orleans game, while Anderson will serve as referee for Jacksonville at Tennessee .
Willard will serve double duty Sunday. He will work the Miami - Indianapolis game at 1 p.m. ET and then travel approximately 110 miles for the Pittsburgh - Cincinnati game, which kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET.
The NFL said each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified who trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise.
The nationwide stop, attributed to new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system that caused "intermittent" communications and radar gaps, was the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys
summary: The 49ers are listing left tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, while receiver Mike Evans has been ruled out.
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers had two important additions to their injury report this week with left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) now listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys .
According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Williams and Greenlaw suffered their injuries in Thursday's practice, with both players listed as limited for that day because of it. Greenlaw was again limited Friday, while Williams did not practice.
"Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said of Williams. "Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that's enough time for him to be all right."
If Williams is unable to play, the Niners will turn to swing tackle Vederian Lowe to step into the lineup. And if Greenlaw can't play, rookie Jaden Dugger will move into the weakside linebacker spot, according to Shanahan.
"Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday, but if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far," Shanahan said.
Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) will miss his third straight game. He's the only Niner officially ruled out against the Cowboys as he continues to work his way through the tendinitis that flared up in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders .
Shanahan offered a bit more clarity Friday afternoon on when Evans could return, saying there's "a chance" for next week against the Minnesota Vikings but adding that he's "not sure yet."
"It's been going well," Shanahan said. "I'm sure if this was the last game or something, he'd be able to go out there. But we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again, but it's going in the right direction."
In addition to Williams and Greenlaw, all three of San Francisco's top cornerbacks -- Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) -- are questionable against the Cowboys.
So, too, are defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) and defensive back Nate Hobbs (adductor), both of whom are working their way back from injured reserve and could be activated Saturday.
Meanwhile, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 5, practiced all week and is cleared to return against the Cowboys.
"He had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it, but [he] took care of himself real well while he was injured and had a good week."
author: Nick Wagoner

title: Ravens eye 6-10 weeks for Jackson return; sources say QB had surgery last week
summary: Ravens coach Jesse Minter's update on Lamar Jackson's recovery process calls such timelines "challenging to predict."
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens say Lamar Jackson 's dislocated and broken right thumb has a typical recovery timeline of six to 10 weeks, with a source telling ESPN the quarterback has undergone surgery for the injury.
Ravens coach Jesse Minter addressed Jackson's status in a statement released by the team Friday in which he said recovery timelines are "challenging to predict."
"He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."
Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Jackson underwent surgery on the thumb last week.
With nine weeks remaining in the regular season, Jackson could come back as early as Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns . If Jackson needs 10 weeks to recover, a return would come in the postseason.
The Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight games but are one game out of the final playoff spot in the AFC. Baltimore's playoff chances are projected at 3.7%, according to ESPN Analytics.
To help keep the team's postseason hopes alive, the Ravens traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett , who is set to start Monday night in Baltimore against the winless Los Angeles Chargers .
Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first play of a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. His right hand hit the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau while trying to throw a pass.
This is the second significant injury this season for Jackson, who missed three games with a high ankle sprain. He has played only 14 full quarters.
The Ravens have usually struggled without Jackson. With Jackson as its starting quarterback, Baltimore is 82-38 (.683), including playoffs, and averages 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as their starter since 2019, the Ravens are 7-15 (.318), including the postseason, and average 17.3 points per game.
author: Jamison Hensley

title: Chiefs RB Walker (groin) misses practice, status uncertain vs. Falcons
summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III missed practice Friday with a sore groin, leaving his status for Sunday's matchup against the Falcons in question.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Chiefs listed running back Kenneth Walker III as questionable for Sunday's road game against the Atlanta Falcons after he missed Friday's practice with a groin injury.
Coach Andy Reid said Walker reported tightness in his groin to the team in the morning before the Chiefs' final on-field practice of the week, resulting in the running back being held out of the session as a precautionary measure.
"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."
Walker, who joined the Chiefs in March after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract, has been one of the NFL's best offseason acquisitions. He enters Week 10 with 872 rushing yards, second in the league behind Atlanta's Bijan Robinson (880).
If Walker is unable to play, the Chiefs are expected to rely heavily on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , the fifth-round pick who has played most often on third downs. In eight games, Johnson has been effective as a runner (111 rushing yards and one touchdown on 26 attempts) and a receiver (237 yards and one touchdown on 14 receptions).
"He'll be ready to go," right guard Trey Smith said Friday regarding Johnson, who could make his first career start. "I like Emmett, man, his juice, his energy. He oozes enthusiasm, emotion and positive energy. You can tell the guy wants to be great, and you can tell he works at it. He really cares, man. I'm really excited for him. It's not hard to root for guys like that."
Meanwhile, the Chiefs expect to have wide receiver Xavier Worthy available after he left in the second half of last week's win over the Jets with a hamstring injury. That should take a little pressure off Josh Downs , who intends to play after being acquired from the Colts just before the NFL trade deadline Tuesday in an attempt to build out Kansas City's depth at the position.
"I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days," Reid said of Downs. "He's a smart kid and knows how to play. He's been playing, which is great, and playing at a high level. He worked into the things we asked him to do and did well. I think he's ready to play in a game for us."
Downs had 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown in nine games with Indianapolis.
The Chiefs expect to have first-round pick Mansoor Delane back after the cornerback missed a couple of games with a shoulder injury. However, they likely will be without right tackle Jaylon Moore because of an ankle injury and Peter Woods due to a neck injury.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.
author: Nate Taylor

title: Veteran receiver Brown gets his wish, released by Eagles
summary: Receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Eagles upon his request.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Wide receiver Hollywood Brown , who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday upon his request.
The two sides came to terms on a noninjury settlement that will offer financial relief to Philadelphia as part of the agreement, a source told ESPN. The Eagles are comfortable moving on from Brown with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due to soon return from injuries, and with Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon emerging as solid options.
Brown, 29, signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. He was brought in along with Wicks, Elijah Moore and Lemon to help complement Smith following the trade of A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots .
A significant role for Brown never materialized, however, even with injuries to Smith and Wicks. He appeared in four games (one start) and had five catches for 63 yards on eight targets. All five of his catches resulted in first downs.
Brown acknowledged he anticipated playing more when he joined the team but said he wasn't taking anything personally.
"I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said in October as questions swirled about whether he'd be traded before the Nov. 10 deadline.
"It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for.
"Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play," he added, "but at the end of the day, it's not my plan."
Brown has played for the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs , Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens over his eight-year career. He had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Chiefs in 2025.
author: Tim McManus

title: Independent experts to play role in Hurts review, NFL says
summary: The NFL provided some additional details about the investigation into how Jalen Hurts' blood clots were handled in response to an inquiry from a U.S. senator.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts ' blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive.
The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.
"As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester's office Friday.
"The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely. For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA. Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance."
The joint review into Hurts' situation has not officially begun as the NFL and NFLPA work to hammer out its parameters.
Hurts, 28, is expected to sit out the rest of the 2026 season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs in October.
He was originally diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London before the Philadelphia Eagles ' Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars . He played in the game, flew home with the team and practiced in full the following Wednesday before a follow-up ultrasound that evening showed the blood clot had moved.
Hurts was placed on injured reserve Oct. 17. Two days later, his agent, Nicole Lynn, and the team released a joint statement about Hurts, saying, "After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations."
His treatment involves anticoagulation or "blood thinners," which prevents him from participating in any contact activities, including football.
The NFLPA has not invoked Article 39 of the CBA, which allows the union to launch a formal investigation into the health, safety or medical care provided by club-affiliated personnel, but as the statement shows, some of its guidelines will be used during this process.
Under the CBA, the neutral physicians must issue a written report within 60 days of their selection, and their recommendations to address and correct any issues need to be acted upon by both parties.
Blunt Rochester penned a letter to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in October seeking answers on the circumstances surrounding Hurts and clarity on the league's blood clot protocols.
In a statement Friday, Blunt Rochester expressed gratitude to the NFL for providing an update while encouraging the league to use its platform to further education around blood clots.
"We welcome the opportunity to provide additional information, and find ways to support your efforts around raising awareness and improving outcomes related to blood clot disorders," Miller wrote.
author: Tim McManus

title: Jaguars holding out new players Davis, Bates to give them bye
summary: The Jaguars are holding out newly acquired Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates to give them a bye week.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jaguars are holding newly acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III out of Sunday's game at Tennessee because the duo has not yet had a bye week.
Defensive tackle Davon Godchaux , who also was acquired via trade on Monday along with Davis and Bates, will play because he has had a bye week.
"Want to be able to make sure that we're in a player safety [mode], putting them in a position to succeed, also learn the system and just give those guys a week to be able to do that," head coach Liam Coen said Friday morning. "We've been talking about it, working through it as the week goes and made the decision to ultimately do it today."
Coen also said Friday that running back Bhayshul Tuten , who didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, will practice today and will play against the Titans.
The Jaguars traded for Davis, Bates and Godchaux on Monday. They sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia for Davis, a 2027-second round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta for Bates, and a conditional 2027 sixth-round pick to New Orleans for Godchaux.
Philadelphia has its bye this week and Atlanta has a bye in Week 11. New Orleans had its bye in Week 8.
author: Michael Dirocco

title: 🌹 Commanders QB Sam Hartman to star as 'The Bachelor' in show's 30th season
summary: The 30th season of ABC's "The Bachelor" that will premiere in March 2027 will star the former Notre Dame standout.
full_text:
After a two-year hiatus, "The Bachelor" has found the apple of its eye for its upcoming season: Sam Hartman .
On Friday, the hit reality dating show announced that the Washington Commanders backup quarterback will be the lead of its milestone 30th season. The premise of the show is Hartman finding love, with the goal of a marriage proposal by the finale.
But if the contestants want Hartman's heart, they might have to know ball a bit.
Meet Sam Hartman, your new Bachelor. 🌹

Don't miss the season premiere of #TheBachelor March 21 on ABC. Stream on Hulu. https://t.co/MbUwN7jqiE
Hartman, 27, went undrafted in the 2024 NFL draft before the Commanders signed the former Notre Dame and Wake Forest standout to their practice squad after selecting Jayden Daniels with the No. 2 pick in that draft.
The Charlotte, North Carolina, native spent five seasons at Wake Forest (2018-22) and transferred to Notre Dame ahead of the 2023 season.
He averaged 8.2 yards per pass attempt, threw for 15,656 passing yards and 134 touchdowns, and completed 59.8% of his passes during his collegiate career.
Athletes being featured in "The Bachelor" franchise is nothing new, though. On the 29th season of the dating show, Grant Ellis -- who played college basketball at Iona and Southern -- held the titular role. The show also counts a list of former NFL players as alumni, including Mel Owens, Jesse Palmer, Colton Underwood and Clay Harbor.
Jordan Rodgers, Josh Murray, Dale Moss and Matt James, who played for Wake Forest like Hartman, are other former college football players who have been featured in the franchise.
The season is slated to premiere in March on ABC -- though the filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate Hartman's day job.
I asked one of Hartman's NFL agents Brian McLaughlin, who said: "[Filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate the [Commanders] schedule. He did run it by the team and they understood."

title: Love throws for 5K yards? Mendoza shines in Vegas? Don't be surprised!
summary: Elite WRs compensate for the lack of a running game in Green Bay, while there's unwarranted caution for Vegas' QB.
full_text:
Each week in the NFL is its own story -- full of surprises, both positive and negative -- and fantasy football managers must decide what to believe and what not to believe moving forward. Perhaps we can help. If any of these thoughts come true ... don't be surprised!
NOTE: All mention of fantasy points is for PPR formats, unless otherwise mentioned.
MVP candidate Love continues to shine, throwing for 372 yards in Sunday's high-scoring road victory over the New England Patriots . With eight games left in the regular season, Love boasts a league-leading 2,618 passing yards, pacing toward 4,945 yards. Nine quarterbacks in NFL history have thrown for 5,000 yards, doing so 15 times. Matthew Stafford , Justin Herbert , Patrick Mahomes (twice) and -- of course -- Jameis Winston are the only active QBs to have done so.
The Packers cannot run the football effectively, forcing Love to throw more than the team's original plan. Love threw for 4,159 yards in his first season as starter back in 2023 but had 11 interceptions, and the team went 9-8. They wanted Love to take fewer chances, release the ball quicker and play more efficiently. Last season, the Packers went 9-5-1 in Love's 15 starts, as he threw for only 3,381 yards with a mere six interceptions. The Packers were fifth in the league in rushing in 2024 and 15th in 2025. That plan worked, and it figured to be the plan again.
Let's just say things haven't worked out in the running game -- thanks to offensive line and running back issues -- and there is little indication that will change in the coming weeks and months. The Packers are last in the NFL with 68.2 rushing yards per game. (For perspective, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers average 163.9.) The Packers average a brutal 3.0 yards per carry because healthy, proven options are limited. Love must throw often for the team to succeed and he has a pair of top-10 WRs in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . The Packers are 6-3, in last place in a tough division, but their path to January is Love piling on numbers.
Sticking with the powerful NFC North, it sure would be anything but bold to predict Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson will return to WR1 status now that the franchise reunited with a competent QB in Kirk Cousins . Watching Carson Wentz against the Buffalo Bills on Monday was painful, regardless of rooting interest and Jefferson looked miserable. Now he won't be! What if this division now boasts more than half of the top 10 WRs in fantasy this season? Assume the two Packers, plus Jefferson, Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown and ... has anyone noticed Chicago Bears WR Luther Burden III is currently No. 10? Inconsistent but tantalizing Lion Jameson Williams is 19th in WR scoring, but capable of delivering 20-point outings at any time. How about six of the top 10 WRs in one division? Perhaps!

I suppose one could reasonably debate whether the Raiders did the right thing in moving Cousins to the Vikings because it means the team must turn to Mendoza, the top pick in the NFL draft, potentially before he is ready. Then again, how do you find out if a QB is ready? Watch Mendoza step right in and perform much the way Cousins was doing, rocking the play-action pass and leaning heavily on TE Brock Bowers and RB Ashton Jeanty (as a receiver). Perhaps the Raiders will barely adjust a gameplan that is working. The Raiders are eighth in points this season. They don't think Mendoza will fail. Why should we?
Fantasy managers should be aggressive in adding Mendoza, though not necessarily activating him this week against a Seattle Seahawks defense that stymied Kansas City Chiefs QB Mahomes in Week 7. Then again, the Seahawks permitted 30 points in three games this season, to QBs Caleb Williams , Brock Purdy and ... Marcus Mariota ! The Seahawks haven't seen Mendoza before. Again, I am not saying he scores 20 fantasy points or the Raiders score 20 points, but let's not be so dismissive. Perhaps the Raiders will even win the game at home.
After Seattle, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos , who rank 19th in permitting QB fantasy points this season. They're not No. 2, like the Seahawks. The Broncos get thrown on and they are permitting 355 yards per game, fourth in the NFL. It's a common mistake in evaluating fantasy options for managers to simply assume because everyone told them the Broncos were formidable. The Raiders also face the Los Angeles Chargers , Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans before the end of the season.
Only the Packers rank worse in rushing yards per game. The Raiders must throw the football, and Mendoza is certainly capable of making the same throws that Cousins was thriving at. Also, who are the QBs outside the top 10 in season scoring that may be starters for deep-league fantasy managers? Bryce Young , Tyler Shough , Stafford, Bo Nix ? Why can't Mendoza be comparable for fantasy scoring? OK, don't expect Cousins-type numbers for the rookie, but I don't think we will be ranking Mendoza so cautiously after this week.
Another Raiders thought: Jeanty might not be the RB1 option so many fantasy managers expected, but he isn't a fantasy bust. He is 14th in running back scoring because he leads the position in receptions and he boasts more receiving yards than rushing ones. That is not entirely his fault, as the Raiders struggle to run block. Jeanty is an electric option as a receiver, averaging 8.8 yards per catch, which is excellent for a running back. No top 30 RB had more receiving yards than they did rushing yards last season, though Kenny Gainwell came relatively close as a Pittsburgh Steeler. Jeanty may do so.

This isn't the first time we have discussed McCaffrey and his lack of volume this year, but really, this is all working out quite well for fantasy managers. Only three running backs boast more fantasy points than McCaffrey, even though he's tied for 22nd in rushing attempts (with Rhamondre Stevenson and Omarion Hampton ). Oh, so you think McCaffrey must have a million receptions, right? Nope, his 36 catches are tied with Kyren Williams for third among RBs, but this is hardly a pace for 102 receptions, like last season. It is a pace for 76 catches.
Credit the 49ers for keeping the mercurial McCaffrey productive and healthy. Many were skeptical. He totaled a ridiculous 413 touches last season. Everyone expected some regression, but now he is pacing toward a manageable 292 touches. That is a huge drop-off and, while acknowledging McCaffrey has gone from averaging 24.5 fantasy points per game to 20.8 points is a big deal, we certainly cannot complain! McCaffrey has 10 touchdowns. He hasn't missed a game. He remains a fantasy star despite pacing for just 971 rushing yards.
Still, backup 49er Kaelon Black remains available in 65% of ESPN standard leagues. I think he should be more popular for the final months, not only if one rosters McCaffrey, but just in general. If McCaffrey were to get hurt (and nobody is rooting for this), this would be a potential RB1 option. Of course, we may say this about myriad RBs available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues, right? Or would we?
Kansas City Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson looks like a future star and the Chiefs are trying harder to get the football to this fellow in open space, where he is dynamic. Nobody wants Kenneth Walker III to get injured either, but Johnson could be a legit RB1 if he gets a chance. The Chiefs and 49ers are built and managed well. Their backup RBs could be special. Would Seth McGowan rock if the Indianapolis Colts had traded the great Jonathan Taylor ? Perhaps, but it is not the same…
author: Eric Karabell

title: 'I thought he was speaking gibberish': Untold stories of Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing
summary: For Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sunday's NFL game in Munich will mark the ultimate convergence of his dual heritage. Here are stories that shed more light.
full_text:
DETROIT -- When the Detroit Lions take the field to face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown will feel right at home.
For St. Brown, Germany is as much his home as the United States. It's where he and his family frequently took trips to visit his maternal grandparents. It's where St. Brown went to preschool (Die Rheinpiraten Kindergarten, to be exact), and where he and his older brothers, Equanimeous and Osiris, spent countless hours on bike tours and fishing trips with their grandfather, Helmut Steyer, who enjoyed entertaining his American-born grandsons.
• AFC North showdown: Steelers-Bengals! • The X factor to spark Panthers' turnaround? • Your Week 10 guide to every NFL game • NFCN: Bears win it? Cousins in command?
It's where Amon-Ra (and Osiris) was a standout for the country's under-19 national football team. It's where he has hosted football camps since becoming a pro in 2021. And it's where the Lions star was once asked by an uncle to stay in order to become a star in the other type of football.
"It's not strange to him. It's all familiar ... everything," St. Brown's mother, Miriam Brown, said. "Going to restaurants, everything is different but for him it's familiar."
The deep connection and familiarity St. Brown has with the country is because of Miriam. Born and raised in Leverkusen, in western Germany, she instilled her German values into Amon-Ra and his brothers, who are all fluent in German.
Those values, and experiences, are a part of St. Brown's identity and have always been at the forefront of who he is. As a result, when the Lions face the Patriots in one of the country's most famous arenas (9:30 a.m. ET on Fox), St. Brown will be the headline act.
More than 80 NFL players who were born in Germany (West Germany and East Germany included) have appeared in a game, per ESPN Research, including 10 who have debuted since 2018. Although he was born in Anaheim Hills, California, few have experienced as much popularity in Germany as St. Brown, who, according to NFL Germany general manager Alexander Steinforth, is the subject of multiple documentaries currently being produced there.
"He's probably the poster boy for the NFL in the German-speaking world these days," Steinforth told ESPN. "He works a lot and has worked a lot with our local broadcast partners, so it's amazing to see when he's kind of talking to his German fans. He's a really big and important name for us here in Germany."
St. Brown wears decals of both the German and American flags on his helmet. He says he's fortunate and proud to be so immersed in both cultures, each of which he has drawn from throughout his life.
"Being half German, half American you kind of get to experience both cultures, and you admire different things in both cultures," St. Brown said. "You feel as if, you know, some things you wish the Americans would do more, some things you wish the Germans would do more.
"But I'm both, so I can pick and choose what I like from each culture. And I think both cultures have amazing, amazing qualities. But I'm just glad that I was able to dip my feet into both cultures and be around both of them."
What does Germany really mean to St. Brown? These are stories that shed more light.
Very early in St. Brown's eighth grade basketball season, coach Brian Liles began getting annoyed.
Liles, who was coaching in the National Junior Basketball youth league in Irvine, California, had taught the boys a pass-first style of hoops that he expected his Titans team to follow. But throughout the first four or five games, John Brown -- the father of a teenage Amon-Ra St. Brown -- was in the stands instructing his youngest son to do the complete opposite.
"Every time Amon-Ra got the ball, he would go, 'Shoot the ball! Shoot the ball!' After a while, I just walked over and I go, 'John, I'm trying to get him to pass the ball because the minute he gets the ball everybody swarms to him,'" Liles recalled. "Guys are open underneath the basket and if he makes the pass, we will be able to get an easy layup."
• Kiper's draft grades | Draft superlatives • Ranking best 100 picks | Yates' favorites • See every pick | Judging overreactions • Kiper's winners: Day 1 | Day 2 • Pick analysis | Round 1 spin | More
During the chat, Liles said Brown was kind and immediately receptive.
He said, "Oh yeah, sorry, Coach. I won't say anything else."
Liles said Brown held his tongue for the next few possessions. Then, suddenly, he heard him calling to his son again ... but in an unfamiliar language.
"I'm like, 'Is that German? I think he's talking in German.' And all of a sudden Amon-Ra starts shooting the basketball again," Liles said. "And I go, 'That son of a gun is telling him to shoot the ball in German!'
"So, he tried to outsmart me, but I picked it up."
Those interactions weren't uncommon for Amon-Ra and his brothers during their youth sports careers. Whether it was basketball, football or soccer, Brown was frequently on the sidelines delivering instructions in German.
They weren't always well received by his sons.
"This was in football specifically and my brother was in Pop Warner, and I think he was telling him to do some type of move," Osiris said. "He's like, 'Spin, spin.' And my brother, and even me, we all got annoyed that he kept yelling at us to do something.
"So, my brother got so frustrated that he would just do the move like when he didn't need to do it, just to do it. He's like, 'You want me to spin? Forget it, I'll spin' even when he wasn't near someone."
Brown said he learned enough German to deliver commands. He figured Liles, or anyone else, would never know what he was saying.
"I used that to my advantage, yeah," he said, laughing.
As teenagers, word was starting to spread throughout Germany about the three brothers who lived in California and also held German citizenship.
The St. Brown brothers spent nearly every summer with Miriam Brown's family in Leverkusen. In 2015, Amon-Ra played for the German U-19 national American football team alongside Osiris.
Equanimeous, who was a freshman wide receiver at the University of Notre Dame at the time, didn't play, but the younger boys were happy to have each other for the trip.
"So, we go to the first game and it wasn't that many people in the stands," John Brown said. "I can't recall which country we played, but when we played France, Osiris got kicked out of the game because he got into a fight with a French guy because he did something to him and he said, 'I'm not going to let some French guy talk s--- to me.'"
Jürgen Siebmanns, team manager of the German junior national team, was responsible for recruiting and selecting both brothers and has continued to follow their pro and college careers.
"Their talent, athleticism and attitude were not only an enrichment in the game, but also a role model for all players," Siebmanns told American-Football.com in 2020. "It was clear to everyone that both would make their way -- and of course we are all the more pleased when it even leads to such highlights and records."
At the European Championship in Dresden, Germany, Amon-Ra, just 15 years old and undersized compared with the competition, won MVP honors -- a feat that wasn't surprising to his brothers.
Representing Germany was meaningful to the boys and the family. And even after all these years, they still keep in contact with former teammates from that trip.
"We were younger than these guys and a lot of these guys look like grown-ass men," Osiris said. "So, I'm like, 'F---.' But I don't even know if we ever talked about it, but then as soon as we get out there you can immediately see that these guys were at least like a good 10-15 years behind in skillwise when it came to football and we immediately started tearing it up in practice and then games."
The experience playing sports on an international level was eye-opening for the family but not entirely shocking. When he was 5 years old, Amon-Ra's…
author: Eric Woodyard

title: Can the Patriots rebound again vs. the Lions?
summary: New England plays in Munich, Germany, this week. Catch up on what's happening abroad in this week's Patriots notebook.
full_text:
MUNICH -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:
1. Patriots resolve: The Patriots are 6-0 under coach Mike Vrabel in regular-season games after a loss, and they look to keep that streak alive Sunday as underdogs against the Detroit Lions at FC Bayern Munich Arena (Fox, 9:30 a.m. ET).
Quarterback Drake Maye summed up Vrabel's knack for bringing out the best in his team in those situations, saying, "Coach Vrabes always says, 'Try not to ride the roller coaster. Try to ride the merry-go-round.' Keep going around and trying to keep the same mindset."
A seven-hour international trip to Munich after the sting of last week's 45-27 home loss to the Packers has created a unique challenge. Not to mention the 6-2 Lions are among the league's upper-echelon teams, playing in arguably the league's best division, the NFC North.
The 5-4 Patriots have their bye after the game, but the urgency around the team has been evident as it tries to stay afloat in the AFC playoff chase . If the playoffs started today, the Patriots would be the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC.
Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson , who has a knee tendon issue that is threatening his availability for the game, has been pushing to play. Likewise with receiver A.J. Brown , who missed the past two games because of a knee flare-up but returned to practice this week and had Vrabel feeling "pretty good" about his status early Friday.
As for the defense, which was carved up by the Packers in an uncharacteristic string of fundamental and communication breakdowns, the unit struck Vrabel's merry-go-round theme with its approach this week.
"We've been there before. You get another opportunity and what you do with that is up to us," said cornerback Marcus Jones , one of the team's six captains. "We went back into the film room, accepted the situation of what we put out there on film, and our job is to not put that back out again. We have the guys that can do it."
Cornerback Christian Gonzalez , the 2024 second-team All-Pro, is under the brightest spotlight. He was targeted relentlessly last week, allowing a career-high 10 catches for a career-high 187 yards, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Gonzalez will need to rebound against top Lions receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown (ranks ninth in receiving yards per game at 82.1) and Jameson Williams (leads NFL receivers in air yards per target at 15.43).
Asked about the Patriots' resolve after losses under Vrabel, Gonzalez said it comes back to the team identity Vrabel preaches.
"Leaning on the guys; after a loss, you stick together," he said. "You have a bad taste, so you want to go out there and play better."
Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was pleased with how defenders responded in their biggest practice of the week on Wednesday. That was held in Foxborough before players traveled to Munich later that night, and Kuhr cited energy, execution, and improved communication and connection among defensive backs as areas that created a "let's get this thing right" vibe.
The Patriots had a similar situation after their 35-6 loss to the Jaguars in Week 3 and rebounded with a 29-26 upset road win over the Bills. Can they do it against the Lions in Munich?
"It's always a good reminder after a loss. It kind of wakes you up a little bit," tight end Hunter Henry said. "And obviously, the way we lost the other day will definitely wake you up."
2. Travel strategy : Will it make a difference that the Patriots arrived in Munich on Thursday morning and the Lions arrived on Friday morning? The Patriots went the earlier route so they could have a walkthrough Thursday and then more of a higher-tempo practice Friday.
"Just having done this a few times, maybe how you feel coming over here Friday and what you're able to get done, I felt like we maybe wanted to do a little more than what had been done in the past on Friday," Vrabel said.
As for the Lions, coach Dan Campbell said he was "very confident" in the approach to arrive Friday. He acknowledged Friday is the "hardest day," as he saw "a little bit of the head bob" from players in meetings, but promised things would evolve.
"I know every eight hours here, we're going to begin to acclimate," Campbell said. "I know by the time we hit Sunday morning into that Sunday afternoon game, we're going to be ready to go."
3. Milton's fine system: The Patriots have had seven offside or encroachment penalties over the past two games, and defensive tackle Milton Williams has had enough. He shared Friday that he has instituted a fine of $1,000 for any front-seven defender who commits those infractions this week, with the proceeds going to Patriots support staff.
• AFC North showdown: Steelers-Bengals! • The X factor to spark Panthers' turnaround? • Your Week 10 guide to every NFL game • NFCN: Bears win it? Cousins in command?
"I had a couple earlier in the season. I feel like we talked about it, but it's not enough consequences that come with it, other than hurting the team," he said. "So hurt your pockets -- make you think about it a little bit more."
4. Turnover tale: The Patriots have failed to record a positive turnover differential in all nine games this season, which is their longest drought since 2005, according to ESPN Research. It has been one of the top storylines of their season, along with injuries, and the theme resonated in Munich leading up to kickoff.
Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels pointed to timing as a key factor in Maye's three interceptions last week against the Packers, saying, "If we see things a hair earlier, it might be a big play."
Playing a turnover-free game was a noted goal among players this week.
"It starts with the ball for us. Obviously, we haven't treated it well and have turned it over a lot," tight end Hunter Henry said in reference to the 19 giveaways that are tied for most in the NFL. "We've got to make a change in some aspect and put our foot down."
5. German flavor: Among the lighthearted Patriots tales from Munich:
Vrabel introduced trivia in Friday's team meeting by asking players if they knew the nine countries bordering Germany. No surprise that German-born practice squad offensive lineman Lorenz Metz had some of the answers.
Metz hosted the weekly offensive line dinner and introduced his teammates, who included tight ends and quarterbacks, to traditional German fare. "That was a lot of pork," center Jared Wilson said.
Some players visited McDonald's and relayed a surprise that chicken wings were on the menu. "The McDonald's here is top tier," Wilson cracked.
Milton Williams and special teamer Brenden Schooler said they were wide awake at 2 a.m. Friday, trying to adjust, with Schooler hitting the weight room in the hotel at 4 a.m. to get himself moving.
6. A.J.'s faith : DeMario 'Pop' Douglas said having Brown return to practice this past week gave the team a boost because he's the leader among receivers, and that has also shown up behind the scenes in a different way.
"He started a bible study with some of the guys. I'm loving his growth in faith, and I feel like that's been getting us closer," Douglas said.
7. They said it : "We're just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out. At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there's pretty much nobody out there that's 100%. We have to recognize that, but we also have to find ways to do our job. And Rhamondre's one of those players looking for a way in." -- Vrabel, on Rhamondre Stevenson pushing to play through a knee tendon issue
8. Maye and FIFA: The Patriots spent three days at FC Bayern Munich's training facility leading up to Sunday's game, and that had Maye reflecting on the days he played the FIFA video game with his brothers, one of whom often beat him with Bayern.
"First thing that comes to mind is Harry Kane. Big fan of him," Maye said, before rattling off some players on the roster in a moment the German media seemed to appreciate.

title: 'He's got a lot of talent': Why do Raiders believe No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza is ready to be a starting QB?
summary: The Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter shortly after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- There isn't a particular moment that convinced the Las Vegas Raiders players and coaches that No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was ready to be the team's starting quarterback. It's a collection of things the rookie has done since he arrived at the facility in April.
For coach Klint Kubiak, it's Mendoza's improvement in his accuracy and knowledge of the offense each week. A month ago, backup quarterback Aidan O'Connell recalled watching Mendoza make a few throws in practice, causing him to turn to quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan and assistant head coach Mike McCoy and say, "Those were incredible."
Wide receiver Tre Tucker , on the other hand, knew Mendoza was capable of being QB1 when he watched the College Football Playoff National Championship game this past January and saw him lower his shoulder to knock off a Miami defender before diving into the end zone for a touchdown that helped Indiana secure its first-ever title.
"That shows you the kind of guy we are getting," Tucker said.
On Tuesday, Mendoza was named the starting quarterback after the Raiders traded veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings . The Raiders' decision to move on from Cousins sent shock waves through the locker room. But with Mendoza, the first quarterback taken by the Raiders in the first round since 2007, waiting in the wings, the team knew this moment would come at some point.
As abrupt as the change of power might have felt, the Raiders believe Mendoza is ready for his starting debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks , the reigning Super Bowl champs and one of the league's most menacing defenses.
"Obviously there's a learning curve there, but Fernando is someone who just works extremely hard," starting center Tyler Linderbaum said. "... Anytime you get that with someone who wants to be great, and then on top of that has great mentors with them, I think it's very important. He's ready. We're ready."
The Raiders might have been more hesitant to move on from Cousins, who is second in the league in touchdown passes this season, if they felt Mendoza couldn't handle the role. To that point, Kubiak doesn't plan to make things easy for Mendoza in his debut.
Kubiak won't hold anything back from Mendoza and believes the 23-year-old signal-caller can operate the entire playbook. That confidence comes from Mendoza preparing as if he was the starter since Week 1.
"One of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared," Mendoza said. "All three of us prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we'd like to make."
Mendoza went above and beyond to make sure he was ready in case his number was called. During games, Mendoza stood hip-to-hip with Sullivan. He wore his helmet while relaying the calls to Sullivan as delivered through the helmet communication device.
Sullivan said Mendoza became more comfortable rattling off plays and helped make in-game adjustments on the sideline with Cousins and O'Connell. At practice, when the first-team offense was getting reps, Mendoza was off to the side with Sullivan working on his footwork, pocket management and timing.
Playing with the scout team in practice, Mendoza impressed the coaching staff with the tight-window throws he made against the starting defense.
Sullivan said Mendoza also did a lot of extra work on his own. At night, Sullivan said Mendoza would be on the indoor practice field at the team's training facility with the game script on his phone. Mendoza would visualize the play and call it as he would in the huddle.
"He literally walks through the play and goes through what his reads [are], his pre-snap communication [and] footwork," Sullivan said. "His command of the offense, his ability to articulate the huddle calls [and] communicate at the line of scrimmage, has improved consistently. It's certainly credit to him."
Sullivan saw Mendoza's training come together in his NFL debut in Week 5's loss to the New England Patriots . The game was out of reach, but New England didn't take it easy on Mendoza.
The Patriots pressured Mendoza on 55.6% of his dropbacks, and he didn't flinch. He looked calmer and felt more in control of the offense compared with the preseason. Mendoza completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards during the Raiders' final possession.
"It's kind of hard to come off the bench at the end to get a feel for the game, and how they're rushing and how your offense is blocking, and he handled it like a champ," tight end Ian Thomas told ESPN. "I don't think anything different this upcoming week. He'll do the same thing."
Mendoza is not walking into a perfect situation. Sure, Brock Bowers has been one of the league's best tight ends. But the Raiders have lacked consistent production from their wide receivers outside of Tucker. The speedy wideout has 33 catches for 529 yards, while the rest of the receivers have 33 combined catches for 347 yards. Las Vegas has struggled to run the ball. On top of that, the defense has allowed opponents to score with ease over the past six weeks.
Mendoza, on the other hand, has been comfortable playing in difficult situations, dating back to his time at Christopher Columbus High School in Miami. During his senior season in 2021, Mendoza had to lead a young team that featured four new starters on the offensive line.
His former coach Dave Dunn said that was Mendoza's best season from a leadership standpoint because the team struggled in pass protection and didn't have the offensive weapons that it did in previous years. Dunn said Mendoza never complained and rallied the team to make a trip to the state semifinals.
• AFC North showdown: Steelers-Bengals! • The X factor to spark Panthers' turnaround? • Your Week 10 guide to every NFL game • NFCN: Bears win it? Cousins in command?
"He was taking the brunt of the pass rush, and there were times when we couldn't throw it as we did in the past, but you could never tell in his demeanor that he was upset," Dunn told ESPN. "All he did was lead the team."
As a rookie, Mendoza doesn't have the knowledge that Cousins possesses from 15 years in the NFL. Tucker told ESPN that Mendoza, however, "has a different element to his game" that can help the Raiders. That element is Mendoza's mobility.
Mendoza's speed is not his strong suit by any means. Nonetheless, he can use his legs when necessary to escape pressure and extend plays.
"He's young. He will probably get out and scramble or whatever it is," Tucker said. "We always say, any guy that hasn't had a bunch of snaps, they got some fresh legs, so they're going to be out there running fast."
Mendoza will also allow Kubiak to incorporate more designed rollouts into the game plan. When Kubiak was the offensive coordinator for the Seahawks last season, starting quarterback Sam Darnold had a designed rollout rate of 11%. On designed rollouts, Darnold completed 42 of 56 passes (75%) for 656 yards, eight touchdowns and an interception.
In Las Vegas, Kubiak used designed rollouts on only 0.05% of Cousins' dropbacks. The expectation is for that number to increase with Mendoza under center.
"[Mendoza] brings his own unique things, and yes, he's a young man with some juice in his legs, and he's got a lot of talent," Kubiak said. "But in this game on Sunday, it's going to be about way more than his physical talent. It's going to be about his leadership, his knowledge of the offense [and] his ability to read defense."
The Raiders believe in Mendoza. At the same time, the rest of the team will have to do its part to ensure Mendoza's transition into the starting role is smooth. The Raiders can do that by fixing the run game, which has seemed like a tall task all season. But if they can establish a consistent rushing attack in the final eight games, that should take some pressure off Mendoza.
