title: Lions elevate LB Owen Pappoe from practice squad
summary: The Lions elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe from the practice squad to the game-day roster, the team announced Saturday.
full_text: ' The Lions elevated linebacker Owen Pappoe from the practice squad to the game-day roster, the team announced Saturday. The Lions play the Patriots in Germany on Sunday. Pappoe, 26, signed with the Lions' practice squad on Nov. 3 after injuries to Jimmy Rolder and Jack Campbell. A third-round pick of the Cardinals in 2023, Pappoe played for the Titans against the Eagles on Sept. 20. He played 19 special teams snaps in his only action of this season. He likely will play a special teams role for the Lions on Sunday. In his career, Pappoe has played 49 games with two starts. He has seen action on 341 defensive snaps and 964 special teams snaps.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Vikings first reached out to Raiders about Kirk Cousins on "midday Monday"
summary: As it turns out, the Vikings contacted the Raiders about a possible trade for quarterback Kirk Cousins before Monday night's meltdown from quarterback Carson Wentz.
full_text: As it turns out, the Vikings contacted the Raiders about a possible trade for quarterback Kirk Cousins before Monday night's meltdown from quarterback Carson Wentz. But not long before. Via ESPNFL, the Vikings initially contacted the Raiders during "midday Monday," prior to Minnesota's Week 9 game against the Bills. The Vikings told the Raiders they wanted to see how things went during the Monday night game before having any further conversations. Then came Wentz's 8.9-passer rating performance in a 23-6 loss, and Minnesota mobilized. The Vikings, per the report, contacted the Raiders before 6:00 a.m. PT on Tuesday and commenced the talks that culminated in a deal being done. Said Raiders G.M. John Spytek during a Tuesday press conference: “I never made one call on Kirk Cousins. And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning .” The Vikings initially offered a fifth-round pick for Cousins, per the report. The report doesn't specify the Raiders' opening position. Once the Vikings moved to a third-round pick, the Raiders pounced. Beyond avoiding the $10 million guaranteed bonus and clearing the path for rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza (which are mentioned in the article), the Raiders ultimately bought a third-round pick for $650,000 (which is not). That's the most attractive aspect of the entire transaction, in our view. Nearly 10 years ago, the Browns bought a second-round pick from the Texans by assuming quarterback Brock Osweiler's $16 million full guarantee for the 2017 season. Any team would sprint for the chance to purchase a third-round pick in the 2027 draft for only $650,000. In this case, that bargain came with nine starts from Cousins, four wins, and months of excellent mentorship for Mendoza. As to the lingering sense in some circles that the Raiders could have gotten even more for Cousins, they risked driving a bargain so hard that the Vikings would have walked away and made a trade with another team. So it was a win for the Vikings, who got their first choice . It was a win for the Raiders. And it definitely was a win for Cousins, who went from waiting to be benched for Mendoza to having nine games as the starter for a contender — plus the strong possibility that the Vikings will make the playoffs.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ground stop results in side judge Don Willard serving as referee for two games on Sunday
summary: Flight disruptions result in multiple changes to Week 10 officiating assignments.
full_text: '' Friday's nationwide ground stop won't keep NFL teams from getting to their road games on Sunday. It will, however, impact the ability of officials to get to where they need to be. The NFL has announced that officiating assignments have changed for Week 10. And the situation will result in a backup referee serving as the referee in two games on the same day. "Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns," the NFL said in a statement. "The changes will necessitate that three backup referees — umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard [pictured] — will work as referees in the following games: Carolina-New Orleans – Duane Heydt; Jacksonville-Tennessee – Barry Anderson; Miami-Indianapolis and Pittsburgh-Cincinnati – Don Willard. "Each of the league’s 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise." The situation creates the likely unprecedented situation of a referee working two games in one day. Willard will handle Dolphins-Colts at 1:00 p.m. ET, and then he'll make the 109-mile trip from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Sunday night game. Making the unprecedented even more unusual is the fact that Willard's usual crew (led by referee Scott Novak) wasn't scheduled to work at all this weekend. The announcement doesn't address where the referees for those three games will be working, or what their roles will be. Shawn Smith was scheduled to be the referee for Panthers-Saints, Alex Moore was set to be the referee for Jaguars-Titans, Carl Cheffers was due to be the referee for Dolphins-Colts, and Clete Blakeman was slated to be the referee for Steelers-Bengals. The league's statement also doesn't specify other shifts that were required as to the established crews that work together throughout the regular season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones: "I don't think we're far away" from 18 regular-season games
summary: As to the timeline, Jones says, "Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe."
full_text: As the NFL embarks on the second half of its current 18-week regular-season schedule, it's just a matter of time before the current structure changes. It's no secret that the NFL wants to expand the regular season from 17 to 18 games. The league is sufficiently confident about it happening that folks like Cowboys owner Jerry Jones speak of it as a given. " I don’t think we’re far away from it ," Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, regarding the addition of an extra game. "I don't know how — what is far away. Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players. "But it's in everybody's best interests. You'd cut back on the preseason games. You'd have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason. But it's in everybody's interest, and it certainly is in the players' best interest in my mind, for sure. And having said that, I would anticipate that coming." His comments presume the NFL Players Association will happily agree to 18 regular-season games. They likely won't. At a minimum, they'll seek major concessions in exchange for the willingness to add yet another game that counts. The unspoken goal had been 2027. The NFL delayed picking a date for Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta in order to accommodate the possibility that the game will slide a week or two deeper into February. That would make 2028 the earliest year for expansion, as a practical matter. (Adding a game for 2027 would be possible only if the dead week between the conference championships is wiped out or if the season starts a week earlier. If an 18th game will result in a second bye, both would be required.) Expansion by 2027 would require expedited negotiations. Expansion by 2028 would hinge on the NFL and NFLPA striking a deal within the next year or so. The union has shown no inclination, however, to engage in talks aimed at extending the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which runs through the 2030 season. Still, if push comes to shove, there will be 18 games. The blueprint was created in 2011. The NFL will lock the players out until the players agree to the things the owners want. Most notably, 18 regular-season games and 16 annual international games. Beyond that, Jones's comment about the early games of the season is odd. " You'd have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason. " He says that as if it's a good thing. It definitely is not. Already, teams struggle in September to get up to speed, given that most teams (with the exception of those assigned to the Hall of Fame Game) play only three preseason games. When the preseason reduces to two games, that's even fewer chances to prepare. It's also fewer chances for the non-starters to get the attention of coaches and General Managers in games that don't count in the standings. It will become harder for undrafted free agents to make the 53-man rosters. Regardless, the motivation isn't football. It's money. More inventory equals more weekends equals more broadcast windows equals more revenue. And that likely will continue until the preseason shrinks to zero games — and the regular season expands to 20 games.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
summary: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
full_text: ' For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter. That's a 59.7-percent win rate. Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That's a 25-percent win rate. In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions. Sunday's game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff's time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel's tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths. Goff's first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3. In 2020, the Patriots beat Goff and the Rams, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0. Sunday's game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans is getting better, we're trying to make sure he fully heals
summary: The 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Sunday's game in Dallas, but head coach Kyle Shanahan says Evans is getting healthy enough to play.
full_text: ' The 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Sunday's game in Dallas, but head coach Kyle Shanahan says Evans is getting healthy enough to play. Evans is dealing with Achilles tendinitis and Shanahan said that while Evans' recovery is progressing and he could probably play if he had to, the 49ers want to prioritize his long-term health and not the short-term benefit of having him on the field on Sunday. "It's been going well. I'm sure if this was the last game or something he'd be able to go out there, but we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again. But it's going in the right direction," Shanahan said. Although Evans won't play this week, Shanahan said Evans could be good to go for next week's game, Sunday night against the Vikings in Mexico City. "There's a chance for next week, but not sure yet," Shanahan said. The 33-year-old Evans was off to an outstanding start this season, and he's the 49ers' team leader with an average of 70 receiving yards per game. The 49ers want to get that production back, but the top priority is having Evans produce in the playoffs.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ground stop nudges Ole Miss-Oklahoma game to Sunday (and OU doesn't like that)
summary: Friday's nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday.
full_text: Friday's nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday. One of them was moved to Sunday — and the home team isn't happy. The Ole Miss visit to Oklahoma shifted from 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday to Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET. "The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage," the SEC said in a statement. "After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team's departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon." Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny strenuously objected to the decision to move the game to Sunday. "After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection," Denny said. "He further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit. I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation." Oklahoma nevertheless will comply with the decision. Even if the Sooners don't like the decision to play the game later. "Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans," Denny said. "Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight. . . . We are obligated to play the game when directed. But we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening." On one hand, there's no point huffing and puffing if Oklahoma ultimately wasn't going to blow the house down. On the other hand, the school may have felt compelled to do something to deflect the frustrations of those who weren't happy with having the game moved to the next day. The bottom line is that the ground stop created travel disruptions and inconveniences for millions of people. And few are thrilled about that. Oklahoma chose to complain. If it makes them feel better, fine. In the end, it doesn't change the fact that the game will be added to the cluster of NFL games that begin at the same time on Sunday afternoon.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deion Sanders, Colorado score huge upset over No. 14 Houston
summary: After the loss that dropped the Colorado Buffaloes to 3-6, coach Deion Sanders said, among other things, "The fans deserve better."
full_text: After the loss that dropped the Colorado Buffaloes to 3-6, coach Deion Sanders said, among other things, "The fans deserve better." On Friday night, they got it. Colorado upset No. 14 Houston on Friday night in Boulder. The 42-32 victory moved the Buffaloes to 4-6. Houston led 20-7 in the first half. Colorado had taken the lead by halftime, 21-20. Eventually, Colorado scored 28 straight points, taking a 35-20 lead. For Houston, the loss killed any realistic hope of qualifying for the final 12-team College Football Playoff. For Colorado, the win keeps them alive for bowl eligibility — and possibly saves Sanders from having his fourth year in Colorado be his last. Especially since he has a $25.5 million buyout .
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints sent Jordyn Tyson to renowned hamstring specialist at University of Wisconsin
summary: In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr.
full_text: In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr. Bryan Heiderscheit and his team at the University of Wisconsin to research new ways to prevent and treat hamstring injuries. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson may benefit from that research. Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team. Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn't run at either Arizona State's Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring. But there's hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson's hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following. Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he's leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch. That's the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit's treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Joe Burrow can join Peyton Manning as only QBs with 4 total TDs in 5 straight games
summary: A big game from Burrow on Sunday night would put him in some very exclusive company in NFL history.
full_text: '' Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been racking up touchdowns recently, and if he continues to do it on Sunday night against the Steelers, he'll join some very exclusive company in NFL history. Burrow has had at least four touchdowns, combined rushing and passing, in each of the last four games. If Burrow has another four-touchdown game on Sunday night, he will join Peyton Manning as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games. Burrow's last four games: Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons. Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans. Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens. Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins. Manning became the first quarterback to have five straight games with four touchdowns in Weeks 8-12 of 2004 with the Colts, when he had a six-touchdown game, two five-touchdown games and two four-touchdown games. (All of Manning's touchdowns were passing, not rushing.) Manning was named NFL MVP that season. And Burrow is an MVP candidate with the way he's playing now. A win over the Steelers on Sunday night would put the Bengals in first place in the AFC North, and a big game with those big stakes would give a big boost to Burrow's MVP chances.
author: Michael David Smith

title: At least 50 different quarterbacks will have started games through Week 10
summary: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday.
full_text: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday. Two others will make their debuts, too: Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck and Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord. Via NBC Sports research, they'll become the 48th, 49th, and 50th different quarterbacks to start games during the 2026 season. It will be only the second time in the last 15 years (excluding the 1987 strike season) during which 50 different quarterbacks have started games in the first 10 weeks of a season. If, for some reason, another quarterback makes his first start of the season on Sunday (that's unlikely with Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock not having an injury designation for Sunday), it will be the second-most starters through 10 weeks since 1950. In 1999, 55 different quarterbacks started games through the first 10 weeks of the season. Most of the changes have arisen from injury. For the Raiders, the transition to Mendoza happened after Kirk Cousins was traded to the Vikings.
author: Mike Florio

title: FAA lifts ground stop, clearing the way for NFL teams to travel on Saturday
summary: Eleven teams will be flying for Sunday games.
full_text: The ground stop has stopped. Friday's sudden, and objectively concerning, decision by the FAA to issue only the second nationwide order to keep all planes from flying since 9/11 has ended. The situation should result in no impact on NFL teams traveling to their road games for Sunday. It also should allow college teams to get to wherever they need to go for Saturday. If it had happened one day later, the end result could have created chaos for NFL teams, significantly delaying their travel and turning their schedules for the night before the game upside down. The situation came as a surprise to some NFL teams. For example, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan learned about it during his Friday press conference. Asked about the ground stop impacting the team's plans for travel to Dallas on Saturday based on the ground stop, Shanahan said, "When did they do that?" He also asked, "Why'd they do that?" Eventually, Shanahan said, "I didn't know. I just first heard." The 49ers plan to leave San Francisco at 1:00 p.m. PT on Saturday. Ten other teams will be traveling on Saturday, too.

title: Victims claim Rex Ryan "almost killed" them with truck in Nasvhille
summary: The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward.
full_text: The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward. And they are making specific and clear accusations about Ryan's driving. Via the California Post , attorney Michael Holland said that Ryan " almost killed " Holland and his wife with Ryan's pickup truck, as they crossed the street. “If we had been six inches further out,” Holland said, “I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife.” Added Holland regarding Ryan: “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.” Holland contends that Ryan didn't stop, and that Holland caught up with the truck and pounded on the window. “He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off," Holland said. Holland gave the Post a photo of his wife's injuries. “I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” Holland said. “His tire literally was like so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that. . . . My wife has already lost one of her toenails; I’m probably going to lose a couple of mine. Her leg is kind of scraped up . . . it hurt.” Holland took a photo of Ryan's red Ford Truck, with a Jets license plate holder and a vanity tag that says "HIT QBS." It's entirely on brand for Ryan. Really, everything about the situation is. Ryan faces six misdemeanors and is due in court next month. It remains to be seen whether he appears on ESPN's Sunday morning pregame show. Then again, with the Patriots playing the Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, it's not as if anyone will be watching.

title: John Harbaugh: Cam Skattebo was not supposed to push on Jameis Winston sneak
summary: Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders.
full_text: Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders. Harbaugh said the call was a quarterback sneak but not a tush push, and Skattebo wasn't supposed to be pushing Winston. "We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing . We didn't call the same [QB sneak] that we've been calling," Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . "What else am I supposed to say? He wasn't supposed to be up there pushing." Why the Giants wouldn't want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn't hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

title: Nationwide ground stop potentially complicates NFL, college games
summary: Some teams could get to game locations by ground. Many would have a hard time.
full_text: The sudden nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA will potentially impact this weekend's football games. It's only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. It's apparently due to a widespread outage impacting air-traffic control functions. Visiting NFL teams typically travel to the sites of their games on Saturday; if the situation lingers, some teams may not be able to get to where they need to be. More immediately, college teams that travel on Friday have a mess. As noted by Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, the 49ers usually travel on Friday for games that are at least two time zones away. For Sunday's game against the Cowboys, they plan to travel on Saturday . Some teams can get to the locations of their games by car or train. The distance from Minneapolis to Green Bay is 279 miles. For Buffalo to New Jersey (for Bills-Jets), it's also less than 300 miles. It's roughly 290 miles fom Pittsburgh to Cincinnati, and 373 miles from L.A. to Phoenix. For the other games (particularly Chargers-Ravens on Monday night), it's a long way to go via ground transportation.

title: Eagles will release WR Hollywood Brown, at his request
summary: Say goodbye to Philadelphia.
full_text: Say goodbye to Philadelphia. Receiver Hollywood Brown, who was available in trade but had no takers, will now be released at his request , via Tim McManus of ESPN. Thanks to a "noninjury settlement" (which presumably includes Brown waiving his right to termination pay), Brown will be released. Because the trade deadline has passed, Brown's contract will be subject to waivers. Brown signed a one-year deal with a $3.7 million signing bonus and a $1.3 million base salary. In addition to waiving his right to termination pay, Brown possibly agreed to return a portion of the bonus money. A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2019, Brown appeared in only four games for the Eagles, with one start. He caught five passes for 63 yards. Brown spent three years with the Ravens. In 2022, he was traded to the Cardinals. After two seasons in Arizona, he spent 2024 and 2025 with the Chiefs. The minimum base salary could prompt another team to make a waivers claim — especially if that team would be willing to pay more than the prorated minimum to add him to the roster for the rest of the season. Brown's best year came in 2021, with 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns.

Walker leads the league averaging 109.0 rushing yards per game. He’s tallied a total of 872 yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four TDs. If Walker is not able to play, rookie Emmett Johnson would be in line to start and carry the load. “Yeah, if Emmett has to do it, then we all have [confidence],” Reid said. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not there, he’s gonna play. title: Robert Saleh says he and Liam Coen are good after "misunderstanding" last year
summary: When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't appreciate.
full_text: When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't appreciate. Last year, Saleh said that Coen's team was good at stealing signals, intending it as a compliment for how good they are at recognizing what the opposing defense was doing. Coen interpreted it as an accusation of cheating and confronted Saleh on the field after the game. Today Saleh was asked about that, and he said he and Coen have spoken and there are no hard feelings. “Liam’s great, man," Saleh said. "We’ve had plenty of interactions. The whole thing is what it was, a little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they’re doing a great job. I love what they're doing offensively. They've definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Overall as an organization, they've done a really nice job." Coen's confrontational approach toward Saleh after the game last year seemed like an overreaction, but no one can dispute that Coen has done a great job building the Jaguars. Saleh knows he's going up against a good coach on Sunday, and he won't provide any bulletin-board material.

title: Vikings officially announce Kirk Cousins will start vs. Packers following trade deadline
summary: Minnesota traded for their old friend on Tuesday at the NFL trade deadline, and he will start for the Vikings right away on Sunday
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings (6-2) aren't providing their old friend Kirk Cousins any ramp up before throwing him back in the fire. After trading for the 38-year-old quarterback at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday in a deal with the Las Vegas Raiders , Cousins will start against the Green Bay Packers (6-3) on Sunday at Lambeau Field.
That means he will join Cam Newton with the Carolina Panthers and Boomer Esiason with the Cincinnati Bengals as the only quarterbacks since 1950 to start for a team in a second stint after they previously won 50-plus games with said team in their first tour of duty.
Head Coach Kevin O'Connell has announced that QB Kirk Cousins will start Sunday at Green Bay. pic.twitter.com/zSMqWo0pHQ
"Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's gone about the week, both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said during Friday's media availability . "It's been really impressive what he's been able to do and just the command and just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by."
Minnesota is desperate for the jolt the four-time Pro Bowl quarterback can provide for their sagging offense. Cousins has 22 total touchdowns in 2026, and the Vikings have scored just 11 offensive touchdowns, tied for the fewest in the NFL with the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers . His 20 passing touchdowns rank as the second-most in the league this season, just three behind Joe Burrow's league-leading 23 and one ahead of Jordan Love's 19.
This news certainly makes four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Justin Jefferson's Friday a happy one. Jefferson won NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors in 2022, his last season with a fully healthy Cousins, after leading the league in targets (184), catches (128), receiving yards (1,809), and receiving first downs (83).  The 98.9 passing yards per game that Cousins averages to Jefferson is the most by a quarterback-receiver duo in NFL history (min. 50 games together).
Coach Kevin O'Connell also hopes Cousins' presence can halt the quarterback carousel Minnesota has gone through since Cousins tore his Achilles in his last Vikings start at Lambeau Field against the Packers in Week 8 of the 2023 season. They have made an NFL-high 17 starting quarterback changes since then.
Should the Vikings hang on and make the playoffs in the 2026 season, Cousins could become the first quarterback in NFL history to start a playoff game in the same season he started a game for multiple teams.

title: Week 10 underrated games: 3 games you should watch this week, from divisional matchups to first QB starts
summary: A look at three games that should be on your radar this week
full_text:
It's Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season, and the trade deadline is officially behind us. We saw the Jaguars go all in, the Vikings add a familiar face in QB Kirk Cousins and the Bears land Jeffery Simmons . Some players will make their debuts on their new teams in an exciting week for the league.
As we go down the stretch of the regular season, these games each mean more and more, and we have some big ones coming up. While some are obvious matchups to circle on the schedule, there are a few that are flying under the radar but could turn out to be a great watch.
Here is a look at three games you should keep an eye on this weekend:
Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX (Stream on fubo, try for free )
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is set to return after missing last week due to a concussion, and the return holds more significance than normal. Watson is facing his former team, the Houston Texans, who drafted him at No. 12 overall in 2017 and where he stayed until 2021.
The Cleveland Browns (5-4) are the first team outside the playoff bubble, sitting at No. 9, and the Houston Texans (3-5) are No. 11 in the AFC. According to CBS Sports projections, if the Browns lose, their playoff chances drop to 19.0%, and a win puts their playoff chances up to 52.6%. If the Texans lose, their postseason odds drop to 16.75%, while a win would put them at 50.1%.
The AFC North is in a tight race, and this game could be big for the Browns' standings.
This matchup intrigues me because these two teams have potential, aren't quite out of the race but are long shots, and are finding their identities. The offense vs. defense matchups also make this game a fun one to watch.
The Texans are third in passing yards per game at 296.4 and face a Browns defense that has allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards per game at 201.0. The Browns offense is among the bottom in rushing yards, and the Texans defense is in the top half in terms of rushing yards allowed, so the run game could be a major factor in who wins here. Another mismatch is the Browns' struggling offensive line and the Texans' ability to generate sacks. Houston had eight sacks last week, tying a franchise record.
Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a huge win, tying a career-high with five touchdowns, while the Browns are looking to snap a two-game losing streak.
Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
In the last few hours of the trade deadline, the Raiders traded Cousins to the Vikings after nine starts and a 4-5 record. He finished his time with Vegas this season with 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. With Cousins in Minnesota, first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza will get his first NFL start.
This game marks the beginning of what should be a lengthy Mendoza Era in Las Vegas, and it will be interesting to see how Mendoza comes out. The Seahawks defense won't make it easy, though; they are at the top of the league, allowing the fewest passing yards (155.1) and the fewest total yards allowed (244.2).
The Raiders offense has been moving the ball, at least in the air, landing fifth in passing yards per game (259.7). Their run game is what they need to improve on, as it's second worst in the league in yards per game (71.3).
The run game will be crucial this week, especially with what they're dealing with at QB. Sam Darnold is sidelined, leaving Drew Lock to run things for a second straight week, but he is dealing with an oblique/elbow injury himself. His injury could mean Seattle leans more toward the run, something that hasn't been their strongest offensive element. They have a defensive mismatch on their side, since the Raiders' defense has allowed the most rushing yards per game (151.2).
Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC (Stream on fubo, try for free )
This game is big in terms of divisional standings and the playoff picture, but these are two teams who haven't received as much attention as some of the other AFC heavy hitters.
The Steelers and Bengals are both 6-2, but Pittsburgh has the edge in the division and the top spot thanks to a 2-1 record among AFC North teams, compared to Cincinnati's 1-1 record.
This is their second meeting of the year, and with such a close race, their head-to-head record could be the difference maker when it comes to crowning a divisional champ. The Steelers won their last meeting, a close one, 30-27. I expect this game to be an exciting, close matchup as well.
Both are playoff teams right now, with the Steelers currently occupying the No. 4 seed and the Bengals at No. 6, and both teams are currently in four-game win streaks. One of those streaks will have to come to an end this week, though.
These teams are coming off very different weeks. The Steelers return from a bye, while the Bengals are coming off an international game in Madrid.
This game will be one that's looked back on as crucial for both teams this season, and with so much on the line, this game should be one you watch this week.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Jerry Jones reveals when he thinks NFL expands to 18-game season, but process to get there is complicated
summary: Jones sees the NFL 'maybe' expanding to an 18-game regular season sooner than one might think
full_text:
The National Football League regular season could be expanding once again.
From 1978 to 2020, the NFL played a 16-game regular season, but that changed in 2021 as the league expanded to a 17-game regular season. However, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, one of the league's most influential voices, feels an expansion to an 18th regular-season game is just around the corner.
"I don't think we're far away from it," Jones said Friday, via 105.3 The Fan in Dallas . "What is far away? Next month? No. Next year? Next year, maybe. Next year, maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players, but it's in everybody's best interest."
Why would a greater physical toll in the regular season benefit the league's players playing one of the most violent sports? Jones claims the compromise would be to trim the NFL preseason once again. Teams typically play three exhibition games as a warm-up and to evaluate the back-end depth on their respective rosters. Two teams end up playing four preseason games if they participate in the "Hall of Fame Game" centered around the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinements in August.
Jones feels simply erasing more preseason games and having the early regular season games, which already have a preseason feeling to them, is in everyone's best interest, players included. The NFL would certainly be in a position to ask for more money on its next media rights deals with its broadcast partners in that scenario. The league signed its current 11-year, $110 billion media rights deal with CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN/ABC and Amazon Prime Video   in 2023.
"You would cut back on the preseason games," Jones said. "You would have teams develop more in the first few games as the type of thing you're trying to get done in the preseason, but it's in everybody's interest. It certainly is in the player's best interest, in my mind, for sure. Having said that, I would anticipate that coming."
The league's current CBA with the players' union is locked in through the 2030 season, so any tweaks to the regular season would necessitate additional negotiation between the league and the union. Commissioner Roger Goodell didn't see an 18-game regular season on the horizon like Jones does now when he addressed the topic at Super Bowl LX in February.
"We have not had any formal discussions about it and frankly very little of any informal conversations," Goodell told reporters back in February . "It is not a given that we will do that. It's not something we assume will happen. It's something we want to talk about with the union leadership."
One league source voiced concern to CBS Sports about increased injuries in an 18-game regular season in April. That is believed to be the biggest holdup to adding an additional regular-season game.
"The bigger concern is now we're going to add another game, even if you multiply everything out with sensible assumptions, there are going to be more injuries," a league source told CBS Sports in April . "And it won't just be hamstrings. There are going to be season-enders and next-season-enders in Week 18 and 19. That's the biggest sticking point on the field."
One player, who requested anonymity, also told CBS Sports in April that some of the NFL's top stars could sit out games at the end of an extended 18-game season to charge up for the playoffs or to reduce the risk of injury.
"The NFL's issue will be more related to getting top players to play in games beyond playoff contention, which I believe get exacerbated the more regular season games they play," the player told CBS Sports in April . "Top players will check themselves out more because games that don't matter late in the season will happen more often."
While Jones has been able to bring many major changes to his Cowboys and the league at large over the years, an expansion to an 18-game regular season may be a little more complicated than he thinks.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Did the Titans take the right receiver at No. 4 overall?
summary: Carnell Tate has given quarterback Cam Ward a reliable target against zone coverage, but ball security issues and questions about his ultimate ceiling complicate the pick
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans had been associated with linebackers, pass rushers and even Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft . With a defensive-minded incoming head coach, the reasoning for interest in Ohio State's Arvell Reese or Sonny Styles seemed well-founded.
There had been some speculation that Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate would be taken earlier than anticipated but there had only been loose speculation with Tennessee. A month earlier, the team had signed free agent wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson and returned veteran Calvin Ridley .
When commissioner Roger Goodell took to the stage in Pittsburgh, he announced the name of Tate, who alongside phenom Jeremiah Smith, recorded 51 receptions for 875 yards and 9 touchdowns in his final season with the Buckeyes.
The Titans would trade back up into the first round for Auburn edge rusher Keldric Faulk . Faulk had been a popular inclusion in top-10 overall preseason prospect rankings, but never realized his full potential. By the time the Auburn product heard his name called, there were four other pass rushers off the board. Shortly after Faulk was picked, so too were Clemson's T.J. Parker at 35th, Oklahoma's R Mason Thomas at 40th, and Texas A&M's Cashius Howell at 41st overall.
Ownership had previously been adamant about a plan to support former quarterback Will Levis to evaluate whether he was the future of the franchise at quarterback. It is reasonable to suspect a similar edict may have been given to new leadership regarding Cam Ward . Hence, the Tate selection.
If the plan was always to support Ward, then was Tate the best option? Tate has been a good player, but four drops and three fumbles are frustrating. He has a great feel for spacing and is most effective against zone coverage. Tate has the ability to snap off a defender in the short-to-intermediate portions of the field, but he has not yet shown an ability to stretch the field or consistently win against man coverage. Tate has just one reception for 33 yards on eight targets 20-plus air yards downfield, according to Next Gen Stats. He also ranks 42nd in EPA per target against man coverage among 53 receivers with at least 10 targets vs. man, per NGS
With Robinson in the fold, the team was likely seeking size at the position; a player who could align as the X or Z (off the ball) in the formation. Jordyn Tyson wasn't available until Week 9 this season. There is a conversation about Denzel Boston perhaps being a better player, but the production has been inconsistent, with growing pains there as well.
There had always been questions about Tate's ceiling, but the same was also true of Jaxon Smith-Njigba . As a rookie, Smith-Njigba had 63 receptions for 628 yards and 4 touchdowns. Tate is on pace for 77 receptions for 944 yards. Can Tate follow a similar path, going from a high-end No. 2 wide receiver to one of the best in the league?
The Titans are coming off a bye week, so it will be interesting to see whether there have been any changes in his usage.
A quick look at NFL Draft history shows that the first wide receiver drafted often does not always become the most productive one. Last year was a bit unorthodox with Travis Hunter Jr. playing both ways, but Tetairoa McMillan has been a better receiver. In 2024, Malik Nabers outperformed Marvin Harrison Jr . Justin Jefferson was famously the fifth wide receiver drafted in his class behind the likes of Henry Ruggs and Jalen Reagor . Hollywood Brown and N'Keal Harry were the only first-round selections in a 2019 class featuring A.J. Brown , D.K. Metcalf, Terry McLaurin and Deebo Samuel .
Tennessee traded up from its position at No. 35 overall to select Faulk at defensive end. Saleh likely wanted to add talent on defense after using the No. 4 overall selection on offense.
Faulk was a young prospect with great size and length, but had never realized his full potential at the college level. By landing him late in the first round, the hope is that they can foster his development and acquire the equivalent of a talent who should have been taken much earlier.
To this point in the season, Faulk has struggled to get off blocks. He could do a better job developing his counter moves and setting up those moves. Too often, he attempts to play through the body, which requires superhuman strength to win consistently against NFL linemen. His 2.8% pressure rate ranks No. 26 among 27 rookies with 50+ pass rush snaps, according to TruMedia. Comparatively, the aforementioned three rushers taken after Faulk rank No. 5 (Thomas), 7 (Howell), and 12 (Parker) in the metric, respectively.
Those struggles persist into the run game. Just like he does in the pass rush, Faulk gets too far into the body of run blockers and struggles to disengage. He has 4 run tackles and 3 run stops through 89 running downs this season. That 4.5% run tackle rate and 3.4% run stop rate are 54th and 46th, respectively, among 56 rookies with at least 50 run downs, according to Next Gen Stats.
Tate's baseline looks like a high-end No. 2 wide receiver with the potential to be a top-20 receiver in the NFL. He has struggled with fumbles and drops early in his professional career, but history suggests that is an aberration. While at Ohio State, he had 0 fumbles and 5 drops over 39 games played.
Because Faulk just turned 22 years old, the Titans will be patient with him, but slow starters rarely become elite performers. There is usually a quality with which a young player can win while other aspects of his game develop.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Eagles release wide receiver Hollywood Brown upon his request, according to report
summary: Brown wasn't used much in the Eagles offense this year
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly releasing wide receiver Hollywood Brown at his request, according to a report from ESPN's Tim McManus. The team and Brown agreed to terms on a non-injury settlement that offers financial relief to the Eagles, the report states.
Brown has not been utilized much on Philly's offense. Playing in just four games with one start, Brown saw just eight targets for five receptions -- all first downs -- for 63 yards and no touchdowns. He also had two additional rushing attempts for 12 yards.
The Eagles offense has had its fair share of struggles across the board, and injuries have been a major storyline for the team. They are set to get wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back soon after being sidelined with injuries, so the need for Brown has diminished even further.
The wide receiver room also includes Makai Lemon , who has led the team the last three weeks in receiving yards and leads the team in total receiving yards (312), and Darius Cooper .
Brown was initially brought to Philadelphia to help relieve pressure on the pass game after A.J. Brown was traded to the New England Patriots during the offseason. The 8-year veteran signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia, his fifth team since entering the league in 2019. The move clearly didn't work the way either side wanted, and despite injuries, the Eagles offense didn't ever feel a need to lean on Brown.
Back in October, the 29-year-old discussed not being on the field as much as he expected.
"I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said during the late-October media availability . "... It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for. ... Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play, but at the end of the day, it's not my plan."
In his career with the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs , Arizona Cardinals, and Baltimore Ravens , he has played in 94 games, with 73 starts, and has 376 receptions for 4,385 yards and 33 touchdowns. Last season, he had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns in 16 games for the Chiefs.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Cardinals reportedly extend No. 2 TE Elijah Higgins, going all-in on tight ends amid WR injuries
summary: Coupled with the McBride extension in 2025, the Cardinals have now signed over $100 million in contracts for their top two tight ends
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are locking in one of their tight ends with a long-term contract extension. No, not Trey McBride . He already signed a four-year, $76 million deal back in 2025. This time, it's No. 2 tight end Elijah Higgins , who will sign a three-year, $26.8 million extension to remain with the Cardinals through the 2029 season, according to ESPN and NFL Media . The contract makes him the 20th-highest paid tight end in the league by average annual value.
Higgins has primarily been the No. 2 blocking tight end playing alongside the more receiving-oriented McBride through the first four seasons of his career. He's played between 26% and 42% of the team's offensive snaps in his four years, according to Pro-Football-Reference, and is at 41% so far this year. He has 82 catches for 798 yards and four touchdowns in his career to date, with 18 catches for 162 yards and one score so far in 2026. The deal would make Arizona the only team in the league with over $100 million in total contract value committed to their top two tight ends since 2025.
Higgins might be about to become more important to the offense, though, because the Cardinals' receiving corps has been decimated by injuries this season. Arizona traded away No. 2 wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . earlier this year, and has seen each of No. 1 Michael Wilson , No. 3 Kendrick Bourne and No. 4 Jalen Brooks go down with season-ending injuries in recent weeks.
The Cardinals are now left with the likes of Simi Fehoko , Reggie Virgil , Devin Duvernay and Harrison Wallace III at wide receiver for the rest of the season, unless they call someone up from the practice squad and/or make an addition in free agency. They are therefore likely to lean into even more multi-tight end sets, which means Higgins will play a larger role through the rest of the season.
Even before they lost the team's top four receiving options, the Cardinals were already extrenely reliant on their tight ends. Arizona has run the third-highest rate of 13 personnel this season at 26.5% of all offensive plays, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. They currently have the second-most targets to tight ends in the league (119) behind only Las Vegas and the fourth-highest success rate on passes to tight ends (61.3%) behind the Bills , Patriots , and Vikings , per Next Gen Stats.
Arizona has turned to rookie Carson Beck as its starting quarterback for the remainder of the year, with Jacoby Brissett having been benched and then traded, and Gardner Minshew having suffered his own season-ending injury last week. Higgins could emerge as one of Beck's more important targets alongside McBride while he plays out the stretch run of the season.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Cowboys' Joey Porter Jr. breaks silence on chatter that absence is contract related
summary: Porter Jr. missed Week 5 with a stomach bug and Week 9 at the Indianapolis Colts because of a foot injury
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Every game Dallas Cowboys Joey Porter Jr. misses in 2026 will come with scrutiny.
Dallas acquired him via trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers after the pending free agent felt "disrespected" in contract extension talks. Porter Jr. led the NFL in passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage in 2025, among 128 players with at least 60 pass attempts thrown their way per TruMedia, with a 49.1 passer rating allowed. Since becoming a Cowboy, Porter Jr. has played in four of a possible six games. He missed what would have been his AT&T Stadium debut in Week 5 on "Thursday Night Football" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a stomach bug . Porter Jr. (ankle) also didn't suit up in Week 9 at the Indianapolis Colts.
Porter Jr. made it clear that his current issue is health-related, not contract-related. There's nothing extra to it.
"That has no, I don't even know where that narrative comes from. I get it, it's the internet. I don't really pay attention to that. I don't really care for that," Porter Jr. said after practice on Thursday. "My goal is to win games and play football. That's what I want to do. If there's any chance I can get on the field, I'm going to get on the field and do what I do best."
So what is going on with his injury? The Cowboys' official injury report lists Porter Jr. as dealing with an ankle injury, but he claims his heel and entire foot are currently "jacked up." He said he tweaked it in his Dallas debut at the Houston Texans in Week 4, and his desire to keep playing on it for his new team made it worse. He feels his 70% still "looks good." That's why he kept playing on it, but trying to power through the injury only made it worse.
"It's all of the above. The whole foot is jacked up. I was playing on it for a while, and it kept getting worse to where I had to shut it down," Porter Jr. said. "I feel like all the guys are wanting me to get back. They know what I can do when I'm out there on the field. I bring a presence out there, a game-changing type of presence. I'm just trying to get back out there as fast as possible. ... I know exactly what is wrong with my foot, and we're doing everything we can to get back to normal."
So what does he need to do to get back out there?
"Just need to be able to run, to cut. I play a position where I have to guard the most athletic people on the field. So if I can't run, skip or jump, then I'm no use out there."
Porter Jr. didn't participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday, instead just working off to the side with Cowboys director of rehab Britt Brown. Friday will be the big test of whether Porter Jr. will return in Week 10 against the San Francisco 49ers (7-1), the NFC's top seed. It's eating at him that he can't be out there for his teammates. When Dallas pulled him out of the game in the second half of Week 8 against the Arizona Cardinals, he slammed his helmet in frustration.
"It really just depends on tomorrow and how I feel moving around. If they see and trust how I'm moving around is good enough to play on Sunday. We're going to go from there with that. I did some running today, that was pretty good. I feel confident with that. First time in a little while," Porter Jr. said. ... "It got to the point to where it felt like I was a liability out there. I never want to be that for my team, especially if I feel like I can't go, and I can't keep up with guys that I should be keeping up with, then what am I doing out there on the field? I'm just hurting the team. It was definitely a hard conversation to have with them because I'm a competitive person. I always want to be out there and do good, so when I can't be out there, it's frustrating."
CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) stood off to the side during the position drills portion of #DallasCowboys practice on Thursday. pic.twitter.com/Q8vh6EaHb6
Some may maintain their doubts that Porter Jr. will delay in order to maintain his reputation ahead of free agency. Among 289 players with at least 10 passes thrown their way, Porter Jr. leads the league in completion percentage allowed (25%) and pass yards per attempt allowed (1.6) while ranking 12th in passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage.
"I just always have the most confidence in myself to feel like I can do what I can do against anybody, 70% or not," Porter Jr. said. "That's why I was out there with the 70% [health]. It was just getting worse. I really don't care too much about the stats. I feel like my tape is going to speak for itself. It is what it is with that ... Still trying to keep the main thing the main thing and get back out there as fast as possible."
author: Garrett Podell

title: Star on the rise: Cowboys' Dak Prescott feels Jason Witten could 'absolutely' be an NFL head coach
summary: Dallas' future Hall of Fame tight end has risen quickly from being a Texas high school head coach to being the interim offensive coordinator at the University of Oklahoma
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- How does Dallas Cowboys head coach Jason Witten sound?
That's certainly a number of years away, but the Cowboys' future Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end's ascent up football's coaching ladder has been quick. After his NFL retirement following the 2020 season, Witten took the head coaching job at Liberty Christian School in Argyle, Texas. Just a few years later, he led the Texas private school to back-to-back Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools (TAPPS) state championships in 2023 and 2024. Those were the school's first consecutive football state titles.
In January of 2026, Witten ascended to the college ranks as the Sooners' tight ends coach. Oklahoma promoted him to the role of interim offensive coordinator after firing Ben Arbuckle on Nov. 2. In his debut as Oklahoma's play caller, the Sooners upset the 24th-ranked Florida Gators in a 23-7 road win.
So could he be an NFL head coach one day? Cowboys four-time Pro Bowl quarterback Dak Prescott "absolutely" thinks that could be in Witten's future.
"Absolutely, if that's what he wants to do," Prescott said after practice on Thursday. "I think there's a big difference between high school, college and NFL and what coaches are asked to do and what coaches are trying to accomplish. But if that's what he wants, then absolutely."
Eleven seasons into his NFL career, Prescott is now the undisputed locker room leader in Dallas. However, when the now-33-year-old kicked off his career as a fourth-round rookie filling in for Tony Romo , Witten was one of the Cowboys' locker room leaders who empowered him. That's why he isn't surprised by Witten's ascent.
"Not surprised by anything he's done, just knowing that football runs in Witt's veins, and that he'd be a coach and good at it," Prescott said. "Seeing his climb happen so fast in a sense from a high school coach to being the tight ends coach to being a coordinator by the end of the year. Understanding that might get him a coordinator job next year either at Oklahoma or a head coaching job somewhere else. He's a guy that I followed and understood what he was trying to get done, whether it be the offense or the whole team, and a guy that was doing it the right way. I know that from the time I spent with him and the man that he is."
Keep stacking 📈 pic.twitter.com/xjwFLAcJ7m
Witten went viral for chewing out one of his Oklahoma wide receivers for running the wrong route on Saturday night in The Swamp. Did he ever chew Prescott out as a rookie?
"No, I don't think I got any of the chew-outs. I got maybe some silent treatments here or there between plays or something if I didn't throw it his way. I know he thought he was open. He didn't chew me out. He understands that I'm just as pissed at myself."
Jason Witten gave a coaching clinic tonight. Masterful in his 1st game as a college play caller. And if you run the wrong route, you WILL hear about it!!! pic.twitter.com/rUBVrZIzDM
If Witten's Sooners can consistently replicate their initial success under Witten for the foreseeable future, it wouldn't be shocking to see Jerry and/or Stephen Jones give him a call.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 10 picks: Our experts face off on Vikings at Packers, Steelers at Bengals and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run?
This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Credit to CBS Sports Research
Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back.
When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20
Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late.  … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21
Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21
Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16
Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17
Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game.  … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14
Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26
Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense.  … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23
Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24
Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches.  … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20
Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17
Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Prisco's Week 10 NFL picks: Lions top Patriots in Munich, Cowboys upset 49ers
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 10 picks, including the Packers to spoil Kirk Cousins' return with the Vikings
full_text:
A perfect week. Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said.
