title: Bengals facing massive NFL scheduling disadvantage vs. Steelers in Week 10: No team has ever overcome this
summary: The NFL didn't really think through this part of the schedule
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals enter Week 10 as one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Not only are they on a four-game winning streak, but the Bengals have scored at least 30 points in all four of those wins, marking the first time since 1997 that they've hit the 30-point mark in four straight games.
If the Bengals want to keep their hot streak going, it won't be easy. They'll be facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome: they're coming off an international game while their opponent, the Pittsburgh Steelers Steelers, are coming off a bye.
So, how bad of a disadvantage is this? It's only happened five times — so it's a small sample size — but the team coming off the international game is 0-5 against the team coming off a bye and 0-4-1 against the spread, which suggests this scheduling quirk may actually put teams at a competitive disadvantage.
Over the past decade, the NFL has generally tried to avoid situations like this, but the league essentially gave up on that this year, with five teams — the Eagles, Bengals, Lions, Vikings, and 49ers — stuck in this exact situation. Of those five teams, only the Eagles have played their game, and they lost.
Here's a brief look at the five games in which a team coming off an international game faced a team off a bye, including Philadelphia's loss earlier this season.
Here's where things get even uglier: The team coming off the international trip has averaged just 15 points per game, and they've been outscored 83-37 over the first three quarters in those five games.  Again, it's a small sample size, but those numbers are eye-opening.
One reason the sample size is so small is that this scenario wasn't even possible for most of NFL history. The first London game was played in 2007, and for the first nine years of the international series, every team that played in Europe was given a bye after its game. However, in 2016, the Colts decided they didn't WANT a bye after their London game because they didn't want their off week so early in the season. Since that point, the NFL has allowed teams to request a bye after playing abroad, but even if a team requests one, there's no guarantee they'll get it.
After the NFL schedule came out in May, NFL  vice president of broadcast planning Mike North explained why teams are no longer guaranteed a bye after an international game .
"I know it's not quite routine, but it's getting to the point where it's pretty routine," North said of international travel. "You play an afternoon (game) over there, it's morning over here, you're back in the facility by what? Midnight Sunday night? That's better than if it's played out in Seattle or Los Angeles … That's the new normal for us."
What North didn't mention is the impact of asking a team coming off an international trip to face a team coming off a bye in their next game. Yes, you might get back to your facility late Sunday night, but if your body is still on European time, there must be an adjustment period. That could impact practice for your next game. According to research, it takes about one day to readjust for each time zone you travel. Madrid is six hours ahead of Cincinnati, so most players likely wouldn't feel 100% recovered from the trip until this weekend.
If the Bengals lose on Sunday, that will drop NFL teams to 0-6 all-time in this specific situation, and if that happens, the NFL is going to have to give some serious thought about whether it's fair to schedule a team coming off an international game to face a team coming off a bye.
If the Bengals lose, all eyes will be on Detroit, because the Lions will be in this exact same situation in Week 11. After facing the Patriots on Sunday in Germany, they'll be facing a Buccaneers team in Week 11 that will be coming off a bye.
It also doesn't help that NFL teams have been almost unbeatable this year after a bye. Heading into Week 10, NFL teams are a combined 13-1 coming out of their bye. The Steelers have already beaten the Bengals once this year and they'll have two trends working in their favor for the game on Sunday, which kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET in Cincinnati.
author: John Breech

title: Fernando Mendoza, Carson Beck, Kyle McCord set to make NFL history with first starts, debuts
summary: A look at the three QBs set to make their first starts this week and what they had to say
full_text:
This season feels like a unique one for quarterbacks, especially rookie quarterbacks. Undrafted Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels took over when Baker Mayfield was hurt, undrafted QB Joe Fagnano started for the Baltimore Ravens when Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down, and No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza came in for the Las Vegas Raiders during garbage time. Washington Commanders seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis also made an appearance this season.
This week, we have more to look forward to: Three QBs each get their first starts and make history while doing so. Mendoza is set to make his first start for the Raiders, facing the Seattle Seahawks, and rookie third-rounder Carson Beck will make his NFL debut with the Arizona Cardinals . Another quarterback joining the group of first-timers is 2025 sixth-rounder Kyle McCord , who is making his NFL debut this week as the Miami Dolphins starter.
If the three of them do start, 50 quarterbacks will have made at least one start through Week 10 this season, tied for second-most in the past 20 seasons. Only 2019 saw more quarterbacks, when 51 quarterbacks had at least one start through Week 10.
This will be the second time multiple quarterbacks made their NFL debuts as a starter (Beck, McCord) in the same week (excluding Week 1 and the 1987 players' strike). The last time it happened was in 2019, when Drew Lock made his NFL debut with the Denver Broncos and Detroit Lions' David Blough also made his debut as a starter.
Mendzoa, Beck and McCord would also be the third trio in the past 30 seasons to make their first career starts in the same week (excluding Week 1 and season finales).
Since 2000, we've seen 158 QBs start at least one game as rookies and just 22 of those made their first start between Week 10 and Week 13. Only five of the 22 won their debuts.
Let's take a look at these three quarterbacks, how they ended up getting the starting job and where their teams stand:
Mendoza was drafted No. 1 overall in April after winning the Heisman and College Football National Championship. He went 16-0 in his final collegiate year with Indiana, finishing the year with career highs in completion percentage (72.0), passing yards (3,535) and touchdowns (41), with just six interceptions.
Kirk Cousins got the starting job in Sin City, but his recent trade to the Minnesota Vikings set Mendoza up to take over. This won't be Mendoza's debut, as he played at the end of the Raiders' 45-17 loss against the New England Patriots in Week 5. He started 5-for-5 on his first drive and ended the game going 6-of-8 for 48 yards.
Any team that drafts a QB first overall is planning on him being the long-term guy, but that doesn't always happen right away. As Mendoza prepped for the day we all knew would eventually come, he had a veteran QB to learn under. Mendoza praised Cousins for mentoring him and helping him to prepare for the eventual moment when he would begin his time as a starter.
"It would have been really easy for Kirk... being a veteran quarterback and kind of having already proved everything to be a little bit more dismissive, but he's had me with open arms and has taught me so many things," Mendoza said .
The first-year QB continued: "Whether it was film study, how to operate as a starting quarterback, all the different multifaceted approaches that have made him so successful throughout his career, he's shared with no restrictions and with no constraints. So I really appreciate him... he was a great mentor."
Next game vs. Seahawks on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:05 p.m. on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
Beck started the season as the emergency third quarterback and has found himself starting just 10 weeks later. The Cardinals season started with Jacoby Brissett as QB1, but he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew , and Beck was made the backup. Brissett was eventually traded to the Ravens, leaving Minshew and Beck on the depth chart. Minshew was only able to get in one start before he was sidelined with what is feared to be a torn UCL in his throwing arm .
Beck summed up his depth chart climb by saying, "It's been a crazy season," adding that he was "super excited" about the opportunity to play. As with Mendoza and Cousins, Beck has gained value by watching his predecessors, Brissett and Minshew.
"I think the biggest thing is just watching those two and how they carry themselves and how they handle themselves not only in the meeting room around the coaches, but during the walkthrough, during practice, and during the game," Beck said. "I think that's the biggest thing that you can learn from those guys, of everybody's looking at you as a quarterback, and your attitude has to be right each and every day. The moxie [of] going out there, having confidence, and making everyone around you better."
The 24-year-old was the No. 65 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, coming off a long collegiate career that included two College Football Playoff titles (albeit none as a starter). Last season with Miami (FL), he had conference highs in completions (338) and completion percentage (72.4), along with 3,813 yards, 30 touchdowns and 12 interceptions
Next game vs. Rams (5-4) on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
McCord was named the Dolphins starter after the team placed Malik Willis on injured reserve Tuesday. The 24-year-old has been active for every Dolphins game this season, but he has yet to take any snaps. Now, he will make his debut as the starter for a struggling 1-7 Miami team.
McCord was drafted in the sixth round of the 2025 draft by the Philadelphia Eagles, went to the Packers in Jan. 2026 and headed south ahead of Week 1 this season, thanks to a trade. During the preseason, he went 46-of-70 with 446 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions with the Packers.
He spent his college career with Ohio State before transferring to Syracuse in his last season. He led the NCAA in completions (391), attempts (592) and yards (4,779) in orange in 2024. He also had 34 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in the 10-3 season, starting all 13 games.
"Being at a school like Ohio State and playing some big games at Syracuse, too, I think it should give you confidence that you've played on a big stage before you've played against some of the top guys in the league right now," McCord said ahead of his first start . "So, yeah, I mean, I think that the confidence level coming from those games is definitely there. It's not my first time playing in a big game. So yeah, I feel like that's where I'm drawing a lot of confidence from."
Next game vs. Colts (2-7) on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. on CBS, streaming on Paramount+

title: Giants players blast controversial DPI penalty in loss to Commanders: 'This league is funny, bro'
summary: The late-game penalty led to a game-winning Commanders touchdown
full_text:
The Giants and their fans are criticizing a late-game, controversial pass interference call in a drive that ended in a Washington Commanders game-winning touchdown.
With less than two minutes remaining in the game, the referees called a defensive pass interference penalty on Giants cornerback Deonte Banks for his coverage on Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks , but not everyone agrees with the call.
Many argue that Burks initiated contact by pulling Banks to draw the penalty. Some argue it was an uncatchable ball and others are saying that it should've been offensive pass interference. Banks not turning towards the ball didn't help his case, however.
Here is a look at the play:
Big pass interference call... pic.twitter.com/rLieCQZ0W7
The penalty pushed Jayden Daniels offense up 33 yards and just four plays later, Washington capped off a 71-yard drive with a touchdown. The trip to the end zone put them up 24-21, and it would stay that way. The Commanders got their third victory of the year to improve to 3-5-1, while the Giants fell to 5-3-1.
After the game, Banks left the locker room without speaking to reporters , but some of his teammates did the talking and weren't happy.
"This league is funny, bro," safety Tyler Nubin said . "This league is funny. There's really nothing you can do about it, man. When you're in trail position, nine times out of 10, they're going to call that PI. That's just how the league is. Just got to weather it."
When asked what he meant by "funny," Nubin continued, with some commentary on the league as a whole.
"What do I mean by funny? S---, it's an offense-driven league. They want to see points. You can't control what the refs do. But you've got to know [that] in those situations, it's probably going to be called," Nubin said.
Safety Jason Pinnock also had some comments, being careful what he said, while also making it clear how he felt about his penalty and other ways he feels offensive players are capitalizing on plays like the one on Thursday night.
"I'm going to be honest, and I ain't going to say nothing that gets me fined," Pinnock. "But it's getting to a point now where [offensive coordinators] are taking advantage of it. They're not calling real plays. They're going four wide, and they're throwing that junk outside. And it looks like these receivers literally have techniques to get PIs. They're grabbing the back of DBs' necks. It's almost like it's becoming a technique."
Pinnock said these "techniques" he feels like offenses are using are impacting the value of the game, calling it "boring" and "frustrating." Defensive players have been openly critical of the difficulty of playing on that side of the ball, and Pinnock added some more insight into how players are feeling.
"When they need a big play, and they can't get nothing going, they're throwing balls on the outside — and these receivers are grabbing the back of DBs' necks," Pinnock continued. "It's getting boring. It's getting frustrating. You can't play defense in this league."
It was a game-defining penalty and as they say, one play doesn't completely define a game, as the Giants should've set themselves up to where the penalty wouldn't matter, but a late-game controversial call can certainly feel like the one thing that led to the loss.
The Giants still stand atop the NFC East, with all four teams in the division struggling. The Dallas Cowboys are right behind the Giants at 4-5.

title: Jaguars' trade deadline acquisitions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis won't play in Week 10 vs. Titans
summary: Bates and Davis have yet to take their bye weeks, while the Jaguars have already had theirs
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars made three significant acquisitions at the trade deadline, but two won't be on the field for their Week 10 game against division rival Tennessee .
Head coach Liam Coen told the media on Friday that safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis will not play in Jacksonville's road game in Tennessee. Coen cited that neither player has had a bye week yet, while the Jaguars have already taken theirs, as the primary reason for sitting them out in their first game with their new team. The second-year head coach added that they wanted to emphasize player safety and give the two an extra week to learn the Jaguars' playbook.
Defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, whom Jacksonville also acquired at the deadline in a trade with the New Orleans Saints , will play Sunday.
Jacksonville traded a 2027 second-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for Bates, who is in the final year of his contract. He has recorded one interception, three forced fumbles, and 60 total tackles in nine games so far this season. Bates is expected to be a significant upgrade to the Jaguars' safety room, where they have given snaps to Antonio Johnson , Eric Murray , Rayuan Lane III and Kaevon Merriweather at different times this season.
The Jaguars traded a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for Davis, who is in the first year of a three-year, $78 million contract extension he signed with Philly this past offseason. Davis has recorded 31 tackles, two tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hits while playing 52% of the Eagles' snaps so far this year. Davis will slot into a defensive line that features Josh Hines-Allen , Travon Walker , Arik Armstead , the also-recently-acquired Davon Godchaux and Ruke Orhorhoro , among others, but that lost DaVon Hamilton to a significant injury.
The Jaguars paid a premium to acquire them, but Bates and Davis should prove important down the stretch and into the playoffs. We'll just have to wait at least a week to see them in uniform for the first time.

title: Top Week 10 battle to watch: Packers' surging offensive trio vs. No. 1 Vikings defense
summary: A closer look at the key factors in the Week 10 battle between the NFL's most exciting passing offense and the league's No. 1 defense
full_text:
Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season provides the tantalizing matchup of the NFL's best defense against the NFL's most exciting passing offense when the Minnesota Vikings (6-2) take on the Green Bay Packers (6-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday afternoon.
Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores' YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics entering Week 10:
On the other side, Packers quarterback Jordan Love leads the NFL in passing yards (2,618) and completions of 20-plus yards (40) with the league's fastest average time to throw (2.67 seconds). Oh, he is also third in the league in passing touchdowns (19). Love is also up to three games with five-plus completions of 30-plus yards this season, which already ranks as the most in any season in the last 35 years.
Green Bay wide receiver Christian Watson ranks first in the league in yards per reception (17.9) and third in receiving yards (873), while fellow wideout Matthew Golden is fourth in the NFL in receiving yards (783). Per NFL Research, Watson and Golden could become just the third teammate duo in the 21st century to each finish a season in the top four in receiving yards. The only two teammate duos to pull that off since 2000 are the St. Louis Rams duo of Torry Holt and Isaac Bruce in 2000 and the Indianapolis Colts duo of Marvin Harrison and Reggie Wayne in 2006.
So why is this the top battle to watch this week? Let's take a look.
One of the most remarkable elements of the Packers' aerial assault is that opponents know the downfield heaves from Love to Watson and Golden are coming, but they still can't stop it. Green Bay is dead last in the NFL in rushing offense, averaging 68.2 rushing yards per game. That is the fewest rushing yards per game for a team with a winning record through the first nine games of a season in NFL history, and bell cow running back Josh Jacobs is now sidelined after undergoing finger surgery.
The Packers have also dropped the most passes, 23, seven more than the next closest team. Green Bay's 39 accepted offensive penalties are the third most in the entire league, and the Packers' offensive line is allowing an average time to pressure of 2.48 seconds, the second-fastest in the league, better than only the Carolina Panthers (2.46 seconds). That's because the Packers' best offensive lineman, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele , went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2, and Green Bay is currently starting their third-string center. Love has also been hit 57 times this season, the fifth most in the league.
Yet, none of it has slowed the Packers down. Will Minnesota be able to stop them at Lambeau with Love, Watson and Golden having caught fire the last six weeks, a stretch that involves five Green Bay wins? Or will Love keep raining downfield haymakers? Let's take a look at what happened all the way back in Week 1, a 39-22 Vikings win in Minnesota, and what that tells us about what could happen on Sunday.
One thing that will already be much different the second time around is the Packers' offensive line. With left guard Aaron Banks (knee) sidelined in Week 1, Green Bay started Donovan Jennings (no starts) at left guard and Jacob Monk (one start) at right guard. That didn't go well. They ended their Week 9 game, a 45-27 road win at the New England Patriots , with two in-season, free-agent pickups at both guard spots when they pulled the offensive starters with eight minutes to play: 12-year veteran Pro Bowler Laken Tomlinson at left guard and 15-year veteran Pro Bowler Kevin Zeitler at right guard.
With Jennings and Monk at Green Bay's guard spots in Week 1, Love was blitzed on 76% of his dropbacks, the highest rate of his career and over 13 percentage points higher than his next closest game (63.6% at the Vikings in Week 17 of the 2023 season). Love was under pressure on 54.3% of his dropbacks, the second-highest rate in a game during his four-year career as the Packers' starting quarterback. He still produced 387 yards, two touchdowns and an interception on 21-of-42 passing with a couple of fumbles (one lost). Yet, no quarterback has thrown for more passing yards (387), yards per pass attempt (9.2), passing touchdowns (2) or a better passer rating (88.1) than Love has against Minnesota's blitzkrieg unit this season.
When Love was blitzed, he was actually somewhat efficient, completing 17 of his 31 throws for 285 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. The key for Love against the blitz that day was whether it actually got home with a quick pressure (pressure within the first 2.5 seconds after the snap). When the Vikings blitzed him without producing a quick pressure, he completed 11 of 18 throws for 181 yards and two touchdowns with two sacks. When they blitzed and did get quick pressure, Love completed six of his 13 throws for 104 yards and an interception.
For the season, Love is averaging 8.1 yards per pass attempt against the blitz, the sixth-best in the NFL, and a 109.3 passer rating when blitzed, the seventh-best in the NFL. Going up against Flores and Co. again with a much more experienced interior offensive line could make a big difference on Sunday.
* The NFL's Next Gen Stats defines quick pressure as getting pressure on the quarterback within the first 2.5 seconds after the snap
Love and Watson have connected for 341 yards passing on throws downfield (10-plus air yards per the NFL's Next Gen Stats) against the blitz in 2026, which is more than double the next closest quarterback-wide receiver duo — Joe Burrow's and Tee Higgins ' 161. In Week 1, Love hit on eight downfield throws against the blitz, the most ever against a Brian Flores defense, according to Next Gen Stats.
Watson, who leads the NFL with a 17.9 yards-per-reception average in 2026, cooked the Vikings in Week 1 with 147 yards receiving and two touchdowns while catching six of his eight targets. One of those catches was an 81-yard catch-and-run touchdown on a pass Watson caught over the middle before exploding down the left sideline.
The key to slowing Watson and Golden down in Week 1 was Minnesota cornerback Isaiah Rodgers . He has allowed just 2.9 yards per target entering Week 10, the fewest among outside cornerbacks (min. 20 targets), and a 36% completion percentage, the second-lowest among outside cornerbacks. He lined up across from Golden and Watson 13 times each, per Next Gen Stats, and he limited Golden to one catch on three targets for eight yards. Rodgers had similar success against Watson, surrendering just one catch on two targets for six yards.
Christian Watson goes 81 YARDS for the TD! pic.twitter.com/79tTcsjlzT
The problem for the Vikings is they only have one Isaiah Rodgers, so Love will most certainly look at whoever isn't lined up across from him.
Another way Green Bay can slow down the blitz is by finding even a sliver of success in the run game, despite their historically rough ground game. Packers fans have given coach Matt LaFleur a lot of grief for running inside zone runs on early downs, particularly out of the shotgun, but that's where Green Bay could find success. They have used inside-zone concepts on just over a quarter of their run plays (25.7%, the seventh-highest rate in the league), and LaFleur should hammer it against the Vikings on Sunday. Minnesota has allowed the third-most yards per carry (5.2) and the highest explosive run rate (20%) to inside zone runs, according to Next Gen Stats.
So who will prevail on Sunday? The Packers have a great chance if Love can avoid quick pressure and continue to find Watson and Golden with regularity. Plus, establishing their run game with inside zone concepts is important. The Vikings similarly have a strong chance if their exotic and unique pressure packages can get home early. Get your popcorn ready for the best chess match of Week 10 from Lambeau Field on Sunday afternoon.

title: NFL Week 10 bold predictions: Joe Burrow lights up first-place Steelers, Tony Pollard bulldozes new-look Jags
summary: Plus, the Packers ruin Kirk Cousins' Vikings return
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 10 of the 2026 season certainly confirmed that hypothesis.
In the Washington Commanders ' (3-5-1) 24-21 upset win on the road over the NFC East-leading New York Giants (5-3-1), there were two passing touchdowns and three interceptions in the game's final 8:25. That made the Week 10 opener the first game in 25 years — the first since Week 16 of the 2001 season between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals — with multiple passing touchdowns and at least three interceptions in the final 10 minutes of a game.
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the go-ahead touchdown from 32 yards out to wide receiver Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left before Washington cornerback Rasul Dougal hauled in the game-winning interception with 25 seconds left. Daniels became the first player with multiple interceptions in the fourth quarter and a game-winning touchdown in the same game since Carson Wentz in 2022, who also did so for Washington.
What other stunning turn of events could go down across the rest of the NFL's Week 10 lineup of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
First place in the AFC North is on the line in the Week 10 Sunday Night Football matchup of the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) at the Cincinnati Bengals (6-2). Cincinnati is powered by quarterback Joe Burrow and the NFL's second-highest-scoring offense (30 points per game), while Pittsburgh is driven by edge rusher T.J. Watt and a defense tied for the fourth-fewest points allowed per game (18.0).
The Steelers have been so stingy that they have allowed just 12 total touchdowns in eight games. That mark is tied for the second-fewest touchdowns allowed in the league this season and is just one behind the Minnesota Vikings (11 allowed) for the top spot in that statistic.
However, Burrow will join Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning (2004) as the second quarterback in NFL history with four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games by racking up at least four on the Steelers Sunday night. He is in the midst of a never-before-seen heater as the first player in NFL history with four straight games with a completion percentage of 70% or better and four-plus total touchdowns.
When these two teams faced off in Week 3 in Pittsburgh, the Steelers prevailed 30-27 after Burrow fumbled the football away with 53 seconds left. He still performed admirably that day, completing 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and 3 passing touchdowns, a quarter of the touchdowns the Steelers have allowed in 2026. Watt, whose 7.5 sacks are tied for the fourth most in the NFL this season, may affect Burrow, but Burrow will stay in the zone and still produce four touchdowns against a Steelers defense that has allowed just 12 all year.
The AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) had the NFL's No. 2 scoring defense (15.1 points per game allowed) before the 2026 NFL trade deadline eve on Monday. That's when the Jaguars unloaded a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl champion defensive tackle Jordan Davis , Atlanta Falcons Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux .
In their first game playing all together, they will be no match for contract-year Tony Pollard when they head to Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans (1-7). Pollard just became the fourth player in Titans history with 100-plus rushing yards and multiple rushing touchdowns in consecutive games in Week 7 vs. the Cleveland Browns (129 yards rushing and 3 rushing touchdowns on 25 carries) and in Week 8 at the Cincinnati Bengals (117 yards rushing and 2 rushing touchdowns on 21 carries). The other three players in franchise history to pull off this feat are Derrick Henry , Chris Johnson and Pro Football Hall of Famer Earl Campbell.
Pollard will keep the good times rolling, somehow, in pursuit of one last payday in the 2027 offseason at age 30 by steamrolling the new-look Jacksonville defense.
The Minnesota Vikings' 2026 season is back on track now after trading a third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders to reunite with Kirk Cousins . Despite having the league's best defense, their offense, quarterbacked by the tandem of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, mustered just 12 offensive touchdowns, tied for the fewest by a team during a 6-2 or better start since 1950. Their 12 touchdowns are the second fewest in the NFL, just one more than the league-low 11 by the winless Los Angeles Chargers .
Cousins should provide a big lift to the Vikings' offense as he returns to Minnesota with 20 passing touchdowns, the second most in the NFL. However, that lift won't begin on Sunday at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers (6-3), when Cousins throws multiple interceptions. Yes, Cousins' connection with Justin Jefferson averages 98.9 passing yards per game, the best by any quarterback-wide receiver duo with at least 50 games played together. The problem is the Packers have the second-most takeaways (19) and interceptions (13) in the NFL. Green Bay All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney co-leads the league with five interceptions, while fellow Packers safety Evan Williams ' three are tied for the seventh-most in the NFL.
McKinney and Williams will provide Cousins with a rude return to life in the NFC North, as he throws multiple interceptions Green Bay's way en route to another miserable outing at Lambeau Field.
Atlanta Falcons All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson has been worth every penny of his three-year, $66.75 million contract extension. He entered Week 10 leading the league in rushing yards with 880, and his 6,778 career scrimmage yards are the fifth-most in NFL history before age 25.
However, he is set to run into a big, red wall on Sunday in the Kansas City Chiefs defense. They're the NFL's No. 3 scoring defense (17.9 points per game allowed) and have allowed just 12 touchdowns all season, tied for the second fewest in the league with the Steelers. Kansas City is also allowing just 97.5 rushing yards per game this season, the 10th fewest in the NFL.
Despite facing one of the NFL's best defenses, Robinson is going to run for 120-plus yards against the Chiefs on Sunday. With Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . struggling (one touchdown pass to five interceptions over the last two weeks), Atlanta will hand Robinson the ball over 20 times — a mark he's only hit three times this season — and he'll wear down the Chiefs en route to a huge game on the ground.
No player has been sacked more than Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson : he's been sacked an NFL-high 33 times. Now, he'll face a Houston Texans defense led by All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , whose 9.5 sacks stand as the most in the league through nine weeks. That's a problem for Watson, whose average time to throw of 3.08 seconds ranks ninth-longest in the NFL among the league's 31 qualified quarterbacks.
However, Watson will get the ball out faster on Sunday to his rookie wide receiver duo of KC Concepcion and Benzel Boston because he knows his life depends on it against Anderson Jr. That's why the Texans will sack him no more than twice on Sunday, even though it would appear that Watson is in for a long afternoon.

title: Ravens announce Lamar Jackson had surgery on broken and dislocated thumb, will be out 6-10 weeks
summary: The Ravens will turn to Jacoby Brissett under center in Jackson's absence
full_text:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced on Friday morning that quarterback Lamar Jackson will be out 6-10 weeks after undergoing surgery on a broken and dislocated thumb.
"Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," Minter said in a statement released on social media. "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."
Jackson injured his thumb on the first snap of the Ravens' Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills , which was billed as a showdown between two of the most recent NFL MVPs (Jackson and Josh Allen ). He missed the previous 3.5 games with a high ankle sprain suffered at the end of the first half of the Ravens' Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans before returning against Buffalo, only to see his return cut short.
With Jackson out, Tyler Huntley filled in early in the season, going 1-2 in his three starts. Huntley also got injured in the same game against the Bills, though, leaving undrafted rookie free agent Joe Fagnano as the only healthy quarterback on the roster. (Huntley is out for the season.) Fagnano also suffered an ankle injury during that game, but played through it last Thursday night against the Jaguars and struggled badly.
Prior to his injuries, Jackson went 68-of-97 for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while rushing 19 times for 144 yards and an additional score. The Ravens' offense looked efficient and explosive, with Jackson targeting Zay Flowers all over the field and Derrick Henry running between the tackles, but we only saw that version of the offense for about two full games. (Flowers was injured in Week 1, missed Week 2 and played only a third of the snaps in Week 3, while Jackson missed the second half in Week 4.)
In the wake of the various quarterback injuries, the Ravens traded for former Cardinals starter Jacoby Brissett , who is expected to take over under center for the remainder of the season. Now they will have to hope Brissett can guide them to enough wins to make it worth Jackson's potential late-season return to the lineup for a potential playoff push in the AFC.
Jackson currently sits at a pivotal point in his current contract with the Ravens. While Baltimore still has one year of control on the two-time MVP's five-year contract, the 2027 contract year is currently structured as an $84.3 million cap hit with zero guaranteed money attached. This number, which would take up more than a quarter of Baltimore's 2027 cap space at present per Over the Cap, all but forces a contract renegotiation next year. Jackson does not have an agent and represents himself in contract and business dealings.

title: Former Notre Dame, current Commanders QB Sam Hartman to star in new season of 'The Bachelor'
summary: Hartman is currently on Washington's practice squad
full_text:
Sam Hartman is swapping his helmet for a suit, and instead of footballs, the Commanders quarterback will soon be passing out roses.
The 27-year-old has been named as the next star of "The Bachelor," as the ABC series kicks off its 30th season in March 2027. Following Washington's Week 10 victory over the New York Giants on Thursday night, Hartman was on "Good Morning America" on Friday morning for the official announcement.
"I'm excited but also very nervous," Hartman said, via ABC News .
He added: "I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl — 30 is going to be pretty tough."
Our own Sam Hartman is the next Bachelor! 🌹 #GoIrish ☘️ pic.twitter.com/sjpBv0fwtq
As noted by NFL Network , the show is slated to shoot early in 2027 over the course of the offseason, so Hartman's day job doesn't appear to be impacted by him starring in the show.
Hartman, who is currently on the Commanders practice squad, has been with Washington ever since he signed with the franchise as an undrafted free agent out of Notre Dame in 2024. Over the course of his tenure with the organization, he's volleyed between the active roster and the practice squad. Hartman has yet to make an appearance in an NFL regular season game.
At the collegiate level, Hartman started his career at Wake Forest before transferring to Notre Dame for his final season in 2023 before opting for the pros. At Wake Forest, he was All-ACC second team in 2021 and All-ACC third team in 2022. During the 2022 season, Hartman was awarded the Brian Piccolo Award for the "most courageous" player in the ACC following a diagnosis of Paget-Schroetter syndrome, a condition that causes blood clots in a vein near the collarbone. That required Hartman to undergo surgery, but the quarterback missed only one game.
Hartman played 48 games at Wake Forest and is the program's all-time leading passer with 12,967 yards. Over his lone season at Notre Dame in 2023, he led the Fighting Irish to a 9-3 record while completing 63.5% of his throws for 2,689 yards, 24 touchdowns, and just eight interceptions.

The Seahawks should be able to take care of a reeling Raiders team that has lost five of six after a 3-0 start and just traded away Kirk Cousins . Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first start on short notice (Cousins wasn't traded until Tuesday) against one of the league's best defenses. This seems like a straightforward parlay for me.

author: Carter Bahns

title: One fatal flaw of every Super Bowl contender from 49ers depth to Packers run game
summary: What could stop your favorite team from winning it all?
full_text:
Normally, when I write, I deal in optimism. Giving fans a reason for hope, something to look forward to when their favorite team takes the field.
Today is not one of those days.
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and while most teams have improved their chances at winning a Super Bowl , I'm here to pour a little bit of cold water on the excitement. No team is perfect, especially this year, when it feels like there's much more parity across the board. While there are obvious Super Bowl contenders , even those teams have flaws that could stop them from hoisting the Lombardi Trophy come February. Let's break down the fatal flaw of every contender at midseason, and if it comes true, then you can blame me.
*Contenders chosen using DraftKings Sportsbook midseason Super Bowl odds
I'm convinced the 49ers are living their own separate version of the movie "Groundhog Day." Every year they come in as legitimate contenders, then it all unravels because of injury. Well, this year is no different, with their depth already being tested.
On the defensive side of the ball, standout rookie DT Gracen Halton is going to miss the rest of the season with a broken ankle, and CBs Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green are both nursing foot injuries (but those are more day-to-day, according to Kyle Shanahan). Offensively, WR Mike Evans hasn't played since week 6, and WR Deebo Samuel hasn't played since week 5. They've gotten by with playing WRs Jordan Watkins , Brandin Cooks and Demarcus Robinson , but that's not a Super Bowl-winning trio. However, they did recently trade for Keenan Allen .
The spin zone here is that the cavalry is coming for reinforcements. Adding DT DeForest Buckner before the trade deadline was a huge move for the defensive line, helping them get more pressure without blitzing (the 49ers are 30th in the NFL in blitz rate and 20th in sack rate without blitzing). I've been a fan of what DC Raheem Morris has been able to get out of this defense, playing to the speed at the second and third level, and adding Buckner to that group should let the secondary play even faster (losing Halton sucks, though).
The more worrisome part is Evans, who is still more than likely not going to play against Dallas next week. Achilles tendinitis is scary, especially at Evans' age. He was such a critical part of why the Niners offense was back to the face-melting unit they've been in previous years, and if he can't go for the long haul, I worry about how this team can win the Super Bowl.
Despite adding safety Amani Hooker at the trade deadline, I still think the Bills ' pass defense overall is the weakest part of the unit. As long as they don't get to play Carson Wentz every week, the Bills' pass defense is going to be what holds them back.
The Bills' defensive line has been a revelation this season; with the growth of EDGE Greg Rousseau and DT Deone Walker , the Bills are eighth in the NFL in pressure rate. However, their splits when they're under pressure versus when they're not are staggering. According to TruMedia, when they get pressure, they have a 69.5% defensive success rate and 0.15 defensive EPA/dropback. Combine all plays where they force a PBU, INT, TFL and sack together when they get pressure, and you get a 21.9% havoc rate when recording a pressure. When they don't get pressure, their defensive success rate drops to 45.5% (only above the Raiders ), -0.31 defensive EPA per dropback, and that havoc rate? Yeah, it drops to 11.4%. Not a great look for their coverage unit.
The biggest problem is that they give up explosive plays, and while some of that should be ironed out by adding Hooker, I worry that DC Jim Leonhard just doesn't have the guys to prevent explosive plays in the middle of the field. If you just whittle it down to passing attempts between the hashmarks in the middle of the field, they've given up the second most completions of 20 or more yards in that area in the NFL. If they can't limit big plays, I worry about how much will be on the offense to keep cleaning up the defense's mistakes.
The Jacksonville Jaguars have arrived. After starting the season 6-2, the Jaguars made a massive splash at the trade deadline, acquiring S Jessie Bates and DT Jordan Davis to shore up two of their bigger issues on the defensive line. However, if this team falls before winning a Super Bowl, it'll be because of their pass protection.
On the surface, the Jaguars' offensive line looks good. They're tied for the fifth-lowest sacks allowed this season and eighth-lowest pressure rate allowed. On top of that, the Jaguars' ability to grind games down by running the football has been evident this season. However, digging into those numbers and watching the Jaguars play tells a different story.
In the passing game, Trevor Lawrence has been incredible this season at mitigating pressure and getting the ball out (a major part of his MVP case). Then, in the run game, the Jaguars are only above the Raiders in average yards before contact per carry, at 0.68 (their yards after contact per carry are 3.40, 6th in the NFL). The offensive line has been overwhelmed by interior pressure, with rookie LG Emmanuel Pregnon and RG Ezra Cleveland up and down in pass protection. Starting LT Anton Harrison has been lost for the season, and while Walker Little has performed admirably in his absence, it'll always be a worry for the Jaguars.
Lawrence has, like I said, been amazing at mitigating pressure and making plays around it. But in order to get out of the AFC, they'll have to face guys like Zach Allen , Dexter Lawrence , Cameron Heyward and more. If this team doesn't get to the Super Bowl, it'll be because the offensive line fell apart.
The Bears and the Jaguars back-to-back in Super Bowl contender stories — what a beautiful world we live in. The Bears look like one of the most complete teams in the NFL, with an offense that can score at will or grind teams into dust. To complement that offense, the Bears added a nitro boost to the defense by trading for DT Jeffrey Simmons, and that trade already looks like it paid off. However, if this team doesn't win the whole thing this year, it'll be because of a secondary that has been…volatile to say the least.
This isn't to say the Bears' secondary isn't talented. Kyler Gordon is an awesome nickel, and I've been impressed with the play of rookie Malik Muhammad on the outside. However, Muhammad has missed the last two games with a toe injury, leaving the Bears thin in the secondary. The mainstay of the group, CB Jaylon Johnson , has been inconsistent this season as well. I was of the belief that the Bears should've added another corner at the deadline to just give them some more insurance, but by not adding anyone, it shows a lot of belief in that group. I wouldn't believe in that group as much, and if they don't win it all, it'll be because the secondary fell apart.
I never thought I'd say this about a Patrick Mahomes-led unit, but the Chiefs ' passing game isn't very explosive. Kansas City is only 21st in the NFL in completions of 20 or more yards this season, despite having a high rate of explosive passes. That is probably because only 14.4% of Patrick Mahomes ' passing attempts this season are between 11 and 20 air yards, and only 8.4% are over 20 air yards, both near the bottom of the NFL.
Without WR Tyquan Thornton on the field, there's nobody who can win on passes downfield. Among all the Chiefs receivers this season, Thornton still leads the team in receptions of at least 16 or more air yards, despite going down in Week 4. Xavier Worthy leads the team in targets in that metric, but he only has two catches at that range. Not being able to hit any explosives makes the offense so much more congested, leaving the run game too little space to breathe and allowing opposing defenses to squat on all the crossing routes Kansas City likes to run.
The Chiefs did add a receiver at the deadline, trading for Indy's Josh Downs . Where Downs will help is in…
author: JP Acosta

title: NFL Week 10 picks, odds, best bets: Lions cover in Munich, Bills crush Jets
summary: After an unusual Week 9 in which 11 favorites covered the spread, here are Jordan Dajani's top five picks
full_text:
Week 9 in the NFL was a weird one, as 11 favorites covered the spread. That's usually a lucrative week for bettors, but we went 2-3 against the spread.
We knew the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks would cover the spread in their games, but the New Orleans Saints and Chicago Bears unfortunately could not cover despite both winning. Then, there was the Minnesota Vikings . Carson Wentz brought potential to open up Kevin O'Connell's passing attack against the Buffalo Bills . Instead, he registered one of the worst quarterback performances in Vikings history. Good thing they brought Kirk Cousins back!
Here's a look at what's next. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Top five picks ATS record: 21-23-1 Overall ATS record: 68-66-2 Straight-up record: 85-50-1
Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
Check out the " pretenders and contenders " column this week. Spoiler: The Detroit Lions are a very intriguing team, while it's not time to buy stock in the New England Patriots .
It's an underrated storyline: The new Detroit defense. Kelvin Sheppard looked like he was on the hot seat at the beginning of the season, but during this four-game win streak, the Lions actually rank second in points per game allowed (15.5) and yards per game allowed (286.3). As for the Patriots, it was pretty shocking to see them give up 45 points to the Green Bay Packers . Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and now he could be down his top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That means it could be Corey Kiner and Lan Larison running the ball for Mike Vrabel. I'll take the Lions with the number under a field goal.
The pick: Lions -2.5 Projected score: Lions 28-20
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
The Bills lead the NFL with 32 points per game, while the New York Jets allowed 31.8 points per game over their last four. Aaron Glenn's has lost four straight games after starting 2-3, and the team is 0-8 SU and 1-7 ATS in divisional games under this head coach.
The Bills also lead the league in total offense with 386.4 yards per game, but I'm interested in this defense. It's true that their past two opponents, the Baltimore Ravens and Vikings, weren't exactly offensive juggernauts, but Buffalo allowed just 8.0 points per game in those matchups, and an NFL-low 161.0 total yards per game over the last two weeks. It's not far-fetched to say this unit is finding their groove, and Jim Leonhard just added safety Amani Hooker at the trade deadline -- who is tied for the league lead in interceptions with five. It's crazy that he picked off Joe Burrow three times in one game a couple of weeks ago.
The Bills have won their last two games by at least 16 points. Take them to cover the big number against a struggling team here.
The pick: Bills -8.5 Projected score: Bills 30-17
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
The last time the Atlanta Falcons played at home, they handed the San Francisco 49ers their lone loss of the season. However, it feels like a lot has happened since then. The Falcons scored zero points in a rain-soaked Raymond James Stadium while allowing 324 rushing yards to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 16-point loss. Then, the Falcons went to Madrid and got dominated by the Cincinnati Bengals , 34-17. Ja'Marr Chase exploded for 155 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions, while Tee Higgins caught two touchdowns. Now, the Falcons return to the U.S. with no break to host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs . Plus, Atlanta just traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars three days ago.
The Chiefs also made an addition at the trade deadline in wide receiver Josh Downs . I would have preferred a perimeter, deep-threat weapon. I mean, Sunday will mark 42 days since Mahomes' last completion on a pass traveling 20+ air yards. But Downs has been one of the most productive slot weapons in the NFL, and I think he could jump-start this passing attack. With the number at a field goal, take the Chiefs.
The pick: Chiefs -3 Projected score: Chiefs 26-21
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
The 1-7 Miami Dolphins travel to Indy to take on the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts . The big story from this matchup is that former sixth-round pick Kyle McCord will be making his NFL debut under center after Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve. That's a scary spot to be in if you're one of the worst teams in the NFL. Maybe McCord is Tom Brady , but I'm not betting on it.
As for the Colts, they traded away two receivers this week in Josh Downs and Keenan Allen , but at least star running back Jonathan Taylor knows he's staying put. The Colts kept up with the Dallas Cowboys last Sunday before ultimately losing, 27-23, and take them to cover the spread against Miami. Indy is actually 5-4 ATS and 11-2 ATS in its last 13 games against teams entering with one win or fewer.
The pick: Colts -3.5 Projected score: Colts 23-14
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Bengals are rolling, having won four straight games. They've scored 34 points in three straight games, and 30 points in four straight. Joe Burrow could join Peyton Manning in 2004 as the only quarterback in NFL history to score four total touchdowns over five straight games, and he just became the first player in NFL history to complete 70% of his passes with four total touchdowns over four straight games.
Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are basically unguardable, having combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. I understand this is a divisional matchup where games are typically close, and that the Steelers dropped 30 points on the Bengals in Week 3 and defeated Burrow in Pittsburgh. But I'll take the Bengals to even the series in prime time. That primetime factor is important, as Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games.
The pick: Bengals -3.5 Projected score: Bengals 30-24

author: Jordan Dajani

title: Grading every NFL team at the midway point: Chargers get an 'F,' three teams get solid 'A' grade
summary: Buffalo is among the highest-rated teams, while the Eagles sit at the opposite end as a big disappointment
full_text:
We're just past the midway point of the NFL season, which means it's time to start thinking seriously about who has and has not met the expectations we set for them at the start of the year. Everyone came into the season with a different set of hopes, and everyone has had plenty of time to meet, exceed or fall short of them now that we have played nine weeks of football.
For some teams, whether they have done what was expected of them is fairly obvious: The Chargers have not, for example. For other teams, it's not so obvious: The entire NFC South would fit that description. But what about the rest of the teams in the league? How have they performed, and how would we grade them relative to what was expected of them entering the season?
That's why we're here. We're assigning letter grades to each team's performance through the midway point of the season. We broke down where each team stands, and why, below.
Dallas came into this season with high hopes but has instead disappointed. The Cowboys ' defense remains a disaster, and the offense hasn't lived up to expectations. They've also blown a couple of games with poor situational football awareness. The only thing saving them from a worse grade is that the rest of the NFC East is bad enough that they're in second place and potentially in position to make a run at the playoffs.
Notwithstanding their Thursday night loss to Washington, the Giants could hardly have hoped for the start of the John Harbaugh era to go any better results-wise. They're in first place in the division despite having lost their starting quarterback in the second game of the season. Rookie Arvell Reese looks like a total monster. They have mostly won close games, so they might not be as good as their record indicates, but that doesn't matter when it comes to how they've performed relative to expectations.
The Eagles would have an F if not for Howie Roseman's smart pivot to selling off pieces at and around the trade deadline, which restocked the cupboard full of draft picks for the future. Philly is always smart about knowing when to pull the plug on a lost season, which is exactly what this year has been.
The Commanders weren't necessarily expected to be all that competitive in the NFC East this year, but the degree to which they've fallen behind the Giants and Cowboys is disappointing. The game management issues under Dan Quinn have also persisted, which contributes to this grade.
The Bears , like the rest of the NFC North, have to be happy with how their season has gone to date. The offense looks explosive, and the defense looks better after the addition of Jeffery Simmons . The only thing holding them back from getting a straight 'A' here is the surprising lack of run game efficiency, though Kyle Monangai's absence has contributed to that.
The Lions have one of the most explosive offenses in the league, with Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta combining with Jared Goff to light up scoreboards. The defense has even been playing better lately, albeit in light matchups. There have been some issues here and there (like the loss to the Panthers ), but overall, things have gone quite well relative to expectations.
The Packers have to be thrilled with how their season has gone. Despite the absence of Micah Parsons , the defense has been excellent. Jordan Love is playing near an MVP level. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden look like superstars. The one thing holding them back from an 'A' is how they started the season, with a bad loss to Minnesota and the blowout against Atlanta. Otherwise, things have gone about as well as could be expected.
The Vikings ' defense gets an A+++++, but the offense has been bad enough to knock the team down nearly a full letter grade despite Minnesota's 6-2 record. Here's hoping that Kirk Cousins can at least prop things up a bit for the rest of the season.
I can't justify giving any NFC South team anything other than a 'C' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.
Same as above: I can't justify giving any NFC South team anything other than a 'C' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.
I'll say it one more time: I can't justify giving any NFC South team anything other than a 'C' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.
Sorry, this is the last time: I can't justify giving any NFC South team anything other than a 'C' based on what they have done to date. They're all living down to relatively low expectations.
The Cardinals have actually been better than anybody expected. They have three wins, and they've played a couple of other close games mixed in there. They do have five double-digit losses, though, so it's hard to give them a grade in the 'B' range. Things will also likely get worse the rest of the way, given their injury issues. That said, getting a second-round pick back for Marvin Harrison Jr . looks like a good deal.
The Super Team expectations were probably always a bit too high, but the Rams haven't come close for a variety of reasons. Whether it's injuries, Matthew Stafford's regression or even more injuries, you have to dock the Rams for not even being a surefire playoff team at the midpoint of the season. Being over .500 despite the injuries is mildly impressive, but not enough to give them a grade in the 'B' range.
The 49ers are a team that has overcome nearly as many injuries as the Rams have faced. It seems like as long as they have Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle , they are just going to keep humming. And Raheem Morris has the defense playing well despite its own injury issues. They've been great on both sides of the ball.
We initially had the Seahawks at a 'B-' grade, but then we remembered the odd loss to the Commanders in Week 3 and had to knock them down. Seattle has navigated some offseason losses (Klint Kubiak, Kenneth Walker III and more) and injury issues (the entire backfield), and three of its four losses came in one-score games, but we expected the Seahawks to be closer to the top of the division than they are right now.
The Bills have overcome a questionable defense to emerge midway through the season with a 7-1 record. Josh Allen is firmly in the MVP mix once again. James Cook is averaging even more rushing yards per game than he did a year ago. The offense has kept humming despite DJ Moore missing time. The Joe Brady era is off to a very good start.
The Dolphins have played right around expectations so far this year. They have smartly played at a snail's pace on offense to try and shorten games and stay competitive, which has resulted in them losing by less than expected in some contests, and they even beat the Jets . Still, it's hard to justify better than a 'C' grade when you're 1-7 at the halfway point.
The Patriots ' start to the season was terrible. They then got on a little bit of a run to bounce back, and it looked like they might recapture some of what they had last year. But they've lost two games against good teams over the last three weeks, and they got smacked by the Packers in the most recent one. The injury issues on offense matter, but sitting at 5-4 before their trip to Munich is a slight disappointment.
The Jets look like they have a nice corps of young players on both offense and defense, but they're also 2-7. It's hard to find the appropriate grade for that type of team, especially when it's coming off its worst loss of the season, where it was totally non-competitive. It feels like a 'C+' is just right, relative to what we expected from them coming into this year.
Considering they haven't had Lamar Jackson for much of the season (he basically played 3.5 games), it's at least somewhat impressive that the Ravens are still in the mix in the AFC at 4-5. But they've lost four games in a row and have looked inept offensively of late…
author: Jared Dubin

title: 5 bold NFL predictions for second half of season: Packers take NFC North; Seahawks, Rams miss playoffs
summary: Plus, we may have our first coach firing of the season soon
full_text:
The second half of the NFL season kicked off on Thursday night, and now that we've hit the back half of the schedule, we're officially on the path to Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles.
There were quite a few surprises during the first half of the season, including the Browns making it to November with a winning record and the Vikings finishing as the NFL's final undefeated team. As we get ready to head down the stretch, there will probably be a few more surprises, and I'm here to tell you what those surprises are going to be. I'll be making five bold predictions for the second half of the season.
So what's in store for the next nine weeks? Let's get to the predictions.
If someone had made this prediction back in August, they probably would have been laughed off the Internet, but now, it seems like a very real possibility. The Seahawks are the defending champs and the Rams were the preseason Super Bowl favorites, and neither team has quite lived up to the hype.
The surging Rams (5-4) have won three games in a row, but they just lost Puka Nacua to injury, and if you throw in the fact that Davante Adams is also hurt, it's getting to the point where Matthew Stafford might have to throw passes to himself. The Rams have the fourth-most difficult remaining strength of schedule in the NFL, with games still to come against the 49ers , Packers and Chiefs .
As for the Seahawks, quarterback play has hampered their season, and it doesn't look like things are going to get much better on that front. Sam Darnold has struggled all year, and to make matters worse, he's been banged up. Drew Lock has been serviceable during his time on the field, but he doesn't exactly make you feel good about this offense. It's hard to see the QB spot improving, and if it doesn't, the Seahawks could end up missing the playoffs.
Oh, and there's one more thing: These two teams still have to play each other twice, with both games coming over the final three weeks of the season. If one team sweeps that series, that will pretty much eliminate the other team. If they split the series, both teams would have to go at least 5-2 in their seven other games just to get to 10-7. In the NFC this year, there's no guarantee that 10-7 is going to get in the playoffs.
If you look at the NFC North odds right now, the Packers are currently viewed as the long shot to win the division (odds via DraftKings ):
The oddsmakers have given up on the Packers, but I have not. Despite having almost no rushing attack, Jordan Love and the Packers have gotten hot over the past few weeks by winning five of their past six games. Their only loss in that span came against the Lions in a 20-17 game where Trey Smack became the first kicker in eight years to miss two field goals from inside 35 yards in a single game. They were a bad kicking performance away from pulling out the win.
On Love's end, he's playing some of the best football of his career. As a matter of fact, he's been so good that CBS Sports NFL Writer Garrett Podell argued this week that Love is the NFL's midseason MVP . On top of that, the Packers defense has been playing at an incredibly high level, and that unit is only going to get better with the expected return of Micah Parsons , which will likely come in Week 12.
Based on how the division has played out this year, the Packers (6-3) will likely have to go 7-1 down the stretch, and this team is talented enough to pull that off.
As things currently stand, the 7-1 Bills have control over the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but I think the Broncos eventually catch them. Not only that, but I think the top seed ends up being decided on Christmas Day in Denver when the Broncos host the Bills. The winner of that game will pick up the all-important head-to-head tiebreaker, and if it's the Broncos, they already have a win over the Jaguars , giving them a head-to-head win over two of the AFC's top teams.
Not to mention, the Broncos have already beaten the Chiefs once, and they could add a head-to-head win over the Steelers when they play Pittsburgh on Black Friday.
The biggest advantage for the Broncos (7-2) is that they have the second-easiest remaining strength of schedule at .426. Of their eight remaining games, they still get to play the Chargers , Dolphins , Jets and Raiders (twice). If they win those five games, that gets them to 12 wins, and at that point, a 14-3 season becomes very possible. I think that would be enough to get them the No. 1 seed for the second straight year. If that happens, it would mark just the second time in franchise history that the Broncos have been the top seed in back-to-back seasons.
If you're wondering what it might take for the NFL to change its playoff format, this might do it.
Heading into Week 10, all four teams in the NFC South have exactly three wins. The Saints and Panthers are technically tied for first place at 3-5 with the Falcons and Buccaneers right behind them at 3-6. There's a very real chance that the winner of this division ends up with a 6-11 record. For that NOT to happen, the Panthers or Saints would have to go at least 4-5 down the stretch, and I'm not sure either team is capable of doing that. The Bucs or Falcons could also get to seven wins, but they have an even smaller margin of error: If they want to get to 7-10, they'll have to go 4-4 down the stretch.
The Panthers and Saints actually play each other in Week 10, so one of those teams will be getting to four wins on Sunday. Even taking that into account, I'm not fully convinced we're going to see either one of them win seven games.
If we don't count the NFL's strike years (1982, 1987), there have been just three teams in NFL history that won their division with seven wins, but NO TEAM has ever won a division with six wins.
If that happens in the NFC South and we also see the NFC East produce a division winner with a bad record, that will pave the way for an 11-6 to possibly get left out of the playoffs. There's a very real chance that every team in the NFC North is going to hit 11 wins, and it won't be surprising if the Seahawks or Rams also hit 11 wins. If you take out the NFC North winner, that leaves four or five 11-win teams battling for three playoff spots.
Since the NFL expanded to a 16-game schedule in 1978, there have only been two instances when an 11-win team missed the playoffs: the 1985 Broncos and the 2008 Patriots . In both instances, there was a division winner that made the playoffs without finishing above .500 (8-8 Browns in 1985, 8-8 Chargers in 2008), and that's what we're likely going to see here.
If a six-win NFC South team ends up winning the division and hosting a playoff game, the NFL might have to go back to the drawing board with its playoff format. In early 2025, the Lions offered a proposal to change the seeding in the playoffs, basing the seeding on each team's final record.
All four division winners would still have gotten in under this proposal, but they wouldn't have been guaranteed a home game. If this prediction pans out, the league might have to revisit the proposal during the upcoming offseason.
The most surprising part of the NFL season so far might be the fact that we still haven't seen a head coach get fired. The last time we made it this deep into the season without a coaching change came all the way back in 2017, when we didn't get our first one until December.
This year, it feels like there are several head coaches on the hot seat heading into the second half of the season, including Steichen, Dan Quinn, Aaron Glenn, Nick Sirianni and you could probably even throw in Jim Harbaugh and Brian Schottenheimer.
When you look at that list, it feels like Steichen has the best chance of being fired first. For one, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has already proven that she's willing to fire someone after dumping GM Chris Ballard in October .
At 2-7, it's been an ugly year for the Colts, and they have an upcoming schedule that's built for a firing:
Week 10: Dolphins Week 11: at Texans…

title: NFL predictions: Can the Falcons slow down Kenneth Walker?
summary: The Falcons had a rough outing in Week 9, falling by two scores to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Atlanta was able to compete for the first part of the game, but quickly fell behind and ultimately looked outclassed by one of the NFL’s premier offenses. That result, and the way it unfolded, seemed to […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 22: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons is tackled by Nick Bolton #32 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons had a rough outing in Week 9, falling by two scores to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Atlanta was able to compete for the first part of the game, but quickly fell behind and ultimately looked outclassed by one of the NFL’s premier offenses. That result, and the way it unfolded, seemed to prompt some soul-searching from the Falcons coaching staff and front office. In the ensuing days, Atlanta traded away star safety Jessie Bates III and starting center Ryan Neuzil. That seems to signal a change in philosophy for the Falcons to more prominently focusing on the future. Atlanta isn’t going to tank or anything close to it—the NFC South is led by a 3-win team at the moment, so nobody is even close to being “out of it”. But this is at least a tacit acknowledgement that the current construction of the team isn’t close enough to turn down future assets. It’s the right move, and an important realization for the new staff. That said, there’s still a big game coming up this weekend against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 10. The Falcons are currently 3.5-point home underdogs, per FanDuel, and there are some significant injury question marks to consider heading into this one. Falcons vs Chiefs Week 10 predictions The biggest matchup to watch here will be the beleaguered Falcons run defense against the electric Chiefs rushing attack headed by former Seahawks star Kenneth Walker. Walker has been a godsend for Kansas City, finding a new level of success beyond even his final Super Bowl-winning season in Seattle. With the Chiefs passing game still a bit lackluster, Walker’s dominance on the ground has been a key cog in their offensive machine. Even though Atlanta started out the season with fantastic run defense, teams have largely figured out how to beat the Falcons attacking-style front with inside runs and a lot of man/gap concepts. The Falcons haven’t yet developed a counterpunch, and until they do…it’s going to be a long day for the defense against any team with even a semi-competent rushing attack. Slowing down Kenneth Walker—or having him not play, as he’s currently questionable for the game—is a pivotal matchup to watch. On the other side of the ball, the Falcons will have to build some offensive consistency. Michael Penix Jr. is in the midst of a two-game slump and was unable to find much success against a fairly beatable Bengals defense. The bigger issue might be the ground game, which should be the backbone of the offense but hasn’t had any consistent success in over a month. With Ryan Neuzil heading out and Corey Levin taking over at center, I’m not expecting significant strides there. But perhaps Levin is a better fit for what Bill Callahan wants to do, given their experience together. This is a tough matchup for Atlanta against a Super Bowl-contending Chiefs team. I’m not expecting much from the offense or defense, to be completely honest. With a bye coming up in Week 11, I worry we might see a “let’s just get to the bye” performance. Hopefully I’m wrong, and the Falcons can at least give us an entertaining game on Sunday. An upset victory would keep Atlanta right in the thick of things in the NFC South, and the latter part of the schedule is considerably easier than the last month and a half. title: Falcons ink CB C.J. Henderson to new two-year deal
summary: Ian Cunningham is not sitting around and waiting to lock up players the Atlanta Falcons feel good about. In fact, he just got his second new contract of the day done with a Falcons defender. After the team reportedly locked up Cameron Thomas, they’ve signed veteran cornerback C.J. Henderson to a two-year deal. It’s well-deserved […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: C.J. Henderson #26 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian Cunningham is not sitting around and waiting to lock up players the Atlanta Falcons feel good about. In fact, he just got his second new contract of the day done with a Falcons defender. After the team reportedly locked up Cameron Thomas , they’ve signed veteran cornerback C.J. Henderson to a two-year deal. It’s well-deserved for a player who has gone from a first round bust in Jacksonville to a valuable starter in Atlanta, and it means Henderson will likely be in the starting mix at corner for 2027 and beyond. He’s earned it by battling his way up the depth chart here and beginning to really deliver on the promise that once made him a top pick. We've agreed to terms with C.J. Henderson on a two-year extension! https://t.co/eqXtHKagqn pic.twitter.com/yhz785gxMZ — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) November 13, 2026 Henderson was originally drafted ninth overall in 2020, ahead of fellow Falcons starter A.J. Terrell, and had an up-and-down tenure in Jacksonville that ended when the team shipped him off to Carolina alongside a fifth round pick for a third rounder and a backup tight end. Henderson was a part-time starter with more ups and downs from 2021 to 2023 with Carolina, and spent time with the Texans and Steelers before winding up on Atlanta’s practice squad. He did fine work in limited spot duty in 2025, but was pressed into more significant action with injuries piling up in 2026 and has been solid-to-stellar in every game except the rough matchup against the Bengals last week. For the year, Henderson has allowed just 54.5% of the passes thrown his way to be completed for 252 yards, 10.5 yards per reception, three touchdowns, and five pass breakups. That completion percentage is the lowest number allowed by any Falcons defensive back this year, and he’s kept his missed tackle rate low while only being penalized once. It’s a renaissance year for Henderson, who has the coaching staff’s trust and is at worst a very high-end backup for Atlanta that they can count on to start for extended stretches when called upon; I would not be surprised if he keeps his starting job all year. We don’t have the terms of the deal yet, but keeping Henderson around gives the Falcons a quality, deep cornerback corps well into 2028 with A.J. Terrell, Avieon Terrell, Billy Bowman Jr., Sydney Brown, and maybe Mike Hughes all here too. Congratulations to Henderson, and let’s hope he can keep this good thing going.

title: Falcons lock up EDGE Cameron Thomas with 3-year deal
summary: Cameron Thomas has been one of the most pleasant surprises of the 2026 season for the Atlanta Falcons. The 26-year-old edge rusher has played more snaps than any other player at his position—by a very wide margin at this point—and has provided 26 pressures, two sacks, consistently solid run defense, and a forced fumble. That […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Cameron Thomas of Atlanta Falcons warms up before the 2026 NFL Madrid Game match between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cameron Thomas has been one of the most pleasant surprises of the 2026 season for the Atlanta Falcons. The 26-year-old edge rusher has played more snaps than any other player at his position—by a very wide margin at this point—and has provided 26 pressures, two sacks, consistently solid run defense, and a forced fumble. That pressure number is tied with Brandon Dorlus for the team lead and tied for 28th overall in the NFL through nine games, and both players are on pace to beat James Pearce Jr.’s team-high 45 pressures in 2025. Because of injuries and Pearce’s suspension making for a thin outside linebacker group, the Falcons have needed to lean heavily on Thomas, and he’s delivered consistent, well-rounded play for them. Given his relative youth, the caliber of season he’s having, and the ability to take on a heavy workload, Thomas has seemed like a logical candidate to return to the Falcons in 2027. Atlanta’s reportedly gotten ahead of free agency on that one, giving Thomas a three year, $33 million deal. The Falcons and EDGE Cameron Thomas reached agreement on a three-year extension worth up to $33 million, tying him to Atlanta through the 2029 season, per @rapsheet and me. @EquitySports CEO Chris Cabott and Falcons GM Ian Cunningham and SVP Bryce Johnston wrapped up the… pic.twitter.com/k09xDv0RgX — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 13, 2026 This front office is not content to wait around when they want to keep players in the fold, which is very evident by now. With Pearce under contract, Jalon Walker hoping to return at full health for 2027, and Thomas sticking around, the Falcons already have a solid young core in their EDGE group that they can build around, and the first-year hit on that extension is likely to be fairly modest to ensure the Falcons still have plenty to spend. The annual average puts Thomas around 40th in the league, so it’s not as though Atlanta broke the bank to keep a player they clearly think is going to be a good starter going forward; the “up to $33 million” here also means there’s likely plenty of incentives in the deal. I have zero complaints. Congratulations to Thomas, and let’s hope he keeps the good times rolling with a sack or two against Patrick Mahomes this weekend. Doesn’t hurt to be greedy, right?
