title: Ravens update QB Lamar Jackson’s status after successful thumb surgery
summary: The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on Lamar Jackson’s return from a thumb injury suffered 0n November 1. Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8. Recovery timelines are […]
full_text: Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens released a statement from head coach Jesse Minter on Friday morning that delivered the team’s first rough timeline on Lamar Jackson’s return from a thumb injury suffered 0n November 1. Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8. Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season. The statement is the most concrete update on Jackson’s status since he went down two weeks ago in Buffalo. However, it lacks the following information: Has Jackson undergone surgery on his thumb? If so, when? If not, when will he get surgery on his thumb? Is the given timeline based on when he suffered the injury, when the statement was released, or when he undergoes surgery? The first three questions were subsequently answered by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley and The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec, who both reported that Jackson has undergone surgery and is currently in the rehab process. It is somewhat baffling why the Ravens would not include that information in their statement. Presumably, the beat reporters who confirmed the surgery received their information from a team source. Why, then, couldn’t the team just say that Jackson had undergone successful surgery? Giving a precise date is not even necessary – the type of thing fans and media would love to know, but do not really need to.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Report: Buffalo Bills were aggressively in pursuit of more than Amani Hooker before NFL trade deadline

In Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport’s trade deadline notebook, they wrote on Buffalo’s interest in Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, both of whom were dealt to […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills traded for safety Amani Hooker earlier this week and were apparently in on two other big names who were eventually moved before the NFL trade deadline. In Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport’s trade deadline notebook, they wrote on Buffalo’s interest in Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates, both of whom were dealt to the Jaguars: “The Jaguars and Bills will be in competition to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl, but both were in competition for some of the same players ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles. The two teams most aggressive for former Falcons safety Jessie Bates also were the Bills and Jaguars, who traded second- and fifth-round picks to Atlanta.” They later went on to write that after the Jaguars trades, the Bills pivoted to Cardinals safety Budda Baker and Hooker. Time will tell if Jacksonville or Buffalo made the right decisions at this year’s deadline. How do you feel about this report from the league’s two biggest insiders? Do you wish the Bills swung a deal for Davis and/or Bates or are you glad Brandon Beane and Co. landed on Hooker?

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch at the New York Jets
summary: The Buffalo Bills are Jersey bound, heading to East Rutherford to take on the New York Jets this week. It’s just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are Jersey bound, heading to East Rutherford to take on the New York Jets this week. It’s just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds of AFC East games with Sunday’s matchup. While New York may be just 2-7 this season, they’ve played a lot of tight games, including two against the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. The Patriots defeated the Jets 26-19, while the Dolphins squeaked out a 28-25 victory. Really, the only game the Jets were entirely demolished in came last week, when they lost 35-12 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Can the Jets play the Bills tight this week? Will Buffalo overlook their division rivals and lose the game outright? There’s no question that Buffalo is the better football team, but there’s a reason why they play the games rather than just talking about them. The Bills will need to come out ready to roll in order to maintain their hold on the No. 1 seed in the AFC. Here are five Bills to watch on Sunday as they try to do just that. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Josh Allen Last week, after a slow start, Allen caught fire in the second half against an outstanding Minnesota Vikings defense. Allen started his night just 7-of-14 for 51 yards and an interception, but from the Bills’ two-minute drive at the end of the first half until the end of the game, he was electric. Allen completed 14 of his next 21 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown, and while those numbers might sound pedestrian, Allen finished his day as just the second quarterback to eclipse 200 yards passing against the Vikings this season. It was the first time anyone had done it since Jordan Love did it for the Green Bay Packers in Week One. Allen isn’t immune from the occasional stinker, and sometimes, those stinkers come against subpar opponents in the immediate aftermath of a big win. OF Buffalo’s three AFC East foes, Allen also has fewer touchdown passes against the Jets (16) than he does against either the Patriots (25) or Dolphins (42) in his career, and he’s thrown 11 interceptions in 15 games against them. I want to see Allen work just as patiently as he did on Monday night, taking what the Jets’ defense gives him while trusting his teammates to do their part. He doesn’t have to play hero ball this week. He just has to be Josh Allen. RB James Cook III Part of me is watching Cook because I expect him to have a big game, as he averaged 4.53 yards per rush in seven career games against the Jets. However, part of me is also watching how head coach and offensive play-caller Joe Brady manages his workload. Cook carried 31 times on Monday, and coming into a short week, I wouldn’t be surprised to see more of Ray Davis in the backfield this week. Cook still needs his touches, but I wouldn’t be mad if his snap share were dialed back a bit in the interest of saving him for later in the season. Davis and Ty Johnson, who is a former Jet, should see some more work this week. If Cook can slip some big runs early, it could help Buffalo to build the kind of lead where he’s hopefully wearing a baseball cap in the fourth quarter. WR DJ Moore Yeah, we’re going heavy-hitters this week. Moore has looked good since returning from a shoulder injury, but I’m waiting for him to take over a game like he did when he had five catches for 100 yards and a score on opening day. That’s also, perhaps not coincidentally, the only game he’s played this season where he wasn’t banged up in some way. Moore is doing his job, as he has 19 catches fo 285 yards and 2 touchdowns on 32 targets; however, he hasn’t looked like a bona fide No. 1 wideout. Against a struggling Jets squad that has allowed 16 passing touchdowns against just one interception this season, I’d like to see Moore have a bigger day. The Jets rank well in passing yards allowed—they’re No. 4 in passing yards against—but that’s misleading since they’re often trailing and they’re ranked just 26th against the run. A scoring pass from Allen to Moore on the first drive of the game for the Bills would be a nice way to kick off a Sunday. OLB Michael Hoecht Maybe it’s unfair to single him out, as Hoecht hasn’t played more than 41% of the defensive snaps in a game this season, and he’s coming off of Achilles surgery last year. However, he’s been mostly pedestrian when he’s been out there, and he just hasn’t had the burst that he showed in limited action last year. Yes, that’s a byproduct of the injury, as he is just past one calendar year since he tore his Achilles in a win over the Chiefs. But, Hoecht has just 15 tackles to show for his work this season, and half a combined sack of Jared Goff in Week Two is his whole pass-rush output so far. He nearly made a cool play last week when he dove and nearly intercepted a spike. Making a play on Geno Smith and bringing the veteran quarterback to the turf would be nice. If Hoecht can find a groove, given how well Greg Rousseau is playing and the strides that T.J. Parker and Bradley Chubb have made as a duo, it would add another layer to Buffalo’s pass rush as they enter a difficult stretch of schedule. S Amani Hooker It has to be the new guy, right? Hooker was exactly the kind of addition the Bills needed. He’s a rangy safety who isn’t afraid to hit, and it sure doesn’t hurt that he’s the NFL’s current leader in interceptions, either. Hooker has allowed just a 60.2 quarterback rating when he’s the closest player in coverage. That’s significantly better than Buffalo’s two starting safeties last week, Cole Bishop (90.3 passer rating allowed) and Damar Hamlin (106 passer rating allowed). Even if the Bills ease him into the festivities, it’s going to be nice to have a high-end safety in the back of the defense. Sunday is a good time to try him out, as the Jets rank just 22nd in passing yards on the year. I’m excited to see what No. 22 brings to Buffalo’s ever-improving defense.

title: Buffalo safety Amani Hooker will make his Bills debut Week 10 vs. Jets
summary: It took all of three practices for Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady to decide that Amani Hooker, the team’s new addition at safety, will play in Week 10 against the New York Jets. In meeting with members of the media, Brady revealed that Hooker “definitely is gonna play, and excited to see whatever that […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Amani Hooker #37 of the Tennessee Titans reacts after making an interception during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took all of three practices for Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady to decide that Amani Hooker, the team’s new addition at safety, will play in Week 10 against the New York Jets. In meeting with members of the media, Brady revealed that Hooker “definitely is gonna play, and excited to see whatever that role kind of looks like.” The Bills and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane knew the time was right to take advantage of the looming trade deadline. In doing so, Buffalo has brought in someone they immediately identified as a starter for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s system. Brady, ever the master press chess player, was careful not to reveal too much about their plans for Hooker. He did say that play time is yet to be determined, noting that “from a comfort level, we don’t want to put him out there and do anything that is not fair to him and the team.” Brady and the team’s defensive coaches have been impressed with Hooker’s ability to quickly assimilate within the team’s defense, including the ability to “communicate in our language.” Hooker’s arrival means that once again veteran safety Damar Hamlin is likely to take a step back into a reserve role. Despite that, Hamlin has embraced his new teammate, helping him get comfortable with his new role in Buffalo. Brady was asked about Hamlin and he emphatically stated that “Damar Hamlin has an incredibly important role on this football team, and he’s gonna play a big part on this football team in a lot of different areas.”He did acknowledge that Hooker’s arrival might prove frustrating for Hamlin, who seemed to play well the last two games, and spoke about the situation at length, saying: “Look, regardless of (if) someone says it or not, anytime you have an opportunity to be a starter and then you trade for somebody else, it can be a natural tendency to kind of maybe get frustrated. Right? But I believe Damar, and the safeties, and the team — we have a lot of guys on this team that can put pride aside and say ‘hey whatever we gotta do to win a football game’… …that’s what Damar Hamlin’s all about and that’s what he’s always been about. He just wants opportunities to compete, and he’s out there competing. And if it helps the Buffalo Bills, that’s what he’s about. So, that’s why we love him and that’s why — the trade was not an indication of Damar Hamlin, and more so just an opportunity for us to improve our football team.” Though Hooker will, in fact, make his Bills debut in Week 10, it’s possible we still see Hamlin in action on defense depending on the situation. He may also reclaim a significant role on special teams, where the last two games Hamlin played zero snaps with the special teams units.

title: Bills at Jets Week 10 final injury report and game day designations
summary: We have officially entered the Week 10 weekend, and with that come game day designations. For the Buffalo Bills that meant one doubtful and two questionable. Yes, I know there are four players listed, but let’s be realistic – two are not on the 53-man roster and barring someone tripping and ending up with turf […]
full_text: Buffalo Bills Jacob Bayer, Sedrick Van-Pran-Granger, Tylan Grable, Alec Anderson, Dion Dawkins and Connor McGovern line up and stretch during their voluntary workout at their practice facility on May 27, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We have officially entered the Week 10 weekend, and with that come game day designations. For the Buffalo Bills that meant one doubtful and two questionable. Yes, I know there are four players listed, but let’s be realistic – two are not on the 53-man roster and barring someone tripping and ending up with turf toe while walking through the airport tomorrow, there is no reason to assume that will change before Sunday morning. Friday injury report pic.twitter.com/vXSsIJIsrJ — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 13, 2026 The good news is that the Bills will have four-fifths of their starting offensive line wearing a jersey on Sunday. Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson both missed last week’s game in Minnesota. Today, they had a full practice and are listed as ready-to-go for game day. The same can be said of Connor McGovern who has been dealing with a neck injury this week. Spencer Brown, however, is doubtful. Brown already missed Week 8 with a back injury after an early exit from Week 6’s game in Las Vegas. Now the Bills starting right tackle is dealing with an ankle injury sustained Monday night against the Vikings. I would expect that doubtful to be an out by game time. The other active-roster question mark is next to Sam Franklin’s name. Franklin popped up with a shoulder injury on Thursday. It could have been a game thing. It could have been a practice thing. Either way, he’s been limited for two days. With Amani Hooker playing – and Joe Brady said he would be – it’s likely that we will see Damar Hamlin playing special teams again. Which means Franklin could take the day off. _____________________________________________________________________________ The New York Jets have ruled out Trevin Wallace and then listed half the rest of their roster as questionable. Okay, that may be an exaggeration, but they do have eight players listed as questionable. Essentially, they don’t want to make a decision on any of their injury list just yet. Friday's injury report for #BUFvsNYJ pic.twitter.com/DiZEdOXzHc — New York Jets (@nyjets) November 13, 2026 The big one to watch here is Garrett Wilson. It looks like he has made it almost through the league’s concussion protocol. If he wakes up tomorrow with no concussion symptoms, he should be good to go. Keep your eyes on former Buffalo Bill Harrison Phillips as well. Phillips had an identical practice schedule this week as he did last. Two days of DNP, a full practice, a questionable designation. He played last week. He will probably play this week as well. Remember, game day rosters are due an hour and a half before kickoff, so we won’t really know more until 11:30 EST on Sunday morning. But I would bet on Phillips and Wilson in for the Jets with Brown and Franklin out for the Bills.

title: 5 New York Jets to watch vs. the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets face off this weekend, and their seasons couldn’t be going in more opposite directions. Buffalo has won four straight games, and they are 7-1 overall for the season. The Jets, meanwhile, have lost four straight games, and they sit at just 2-7 overall. Where both teams are equal, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and New York Jets face off this weekend, and their seasons couldn’t be going in more opposite directions. Buffalo has won four straight games, and they are 7-1 overall for the season. The Jets, meanwhile, have lost four straight games, and they sit at just 2-7 overall. Where both teams are equal, though, is in the win column vs. other AFC East foes. The Jets have dropped games to both the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins this season, while the Bills had their only loss come at the hands of those Patriots. Neither Buffalo nor New York has a division win this season, something that both teams want to change on Sunday. How can the Bills overcome the Jets? Well, they’ll have to start by taking care of their own business, but they’ll also need to keep tabs on the Jets’ top players. Here are five Jets to watch this week against Buffalo. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Geno Smith The veteran has been solid in his second go-round with the Jets, as he’s thrown 12 touchdown passes against just three interceptions so far this season. Smith’s 100.5 quarterback rating is outstanding, as is his 67.5% completion rate on the year. However, he’s also taken a whopping 28 sacks for a league-leading 236 yards lost. If the Bills can win their matchups up front, Smith will hold the ball, and at 36 years old, he doesn’t have the mobility he once had. Smith was never a great runner, but he’s not someone I’d call elusive in the pocket. Buffalo should look to heat him up early in the game before giving him more simulated pressure looks as the game progresses. Speed up his clock to force him to make mistakes. He’ll hold the ball and take a sack over throwing an interception more often than not, so Buffalo’s defensive front needs to be ready to feast. RB Breece Hall The explosive runner has ten career 100-yard games on the ground, and two of those 100-yard games are against the Bills. Hall missed time this year with a quad injury, and he returned last week for the Jets’ 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. He carried 15 times for 61 yards in the game, which was his second-best output of the season. Given the difference in styles between Hall and teammate Braelon Allen, the Bills need to be ready for Hall’s speed and elusiveness this week. Allen is the thunder while Hall is the lightning, and the best way for the Jets to score an upset win would be to notch some explosive plays on offense. Buffalo needs to stay sound in its tackling lanes and keep Hall from notching big runs. If the Bills can stop him on early downs, it will only help the pass rush to sack Smith, which could lead to a negative game script where Hall becomes less of a factor by default. WR Garrett Wilson After sitting last week due to a concussion, Wilson is working his way back and should be able to suit up this week. I assume that Christian Benford will continue his tour of duty against opposing No. 1 wideouts by shadowing Wilson for most of the game; however, Benford missed much of the second half last week with an injury to his wrist. If that limits him in any way, Smith has the arm to make Buffalo pay by finding Wilson, who has had some big catches against the Bills in his career. Buffalo has to make somebody else beat them, and while a healthy Benford would go a long way towards helping to achieve that goal, the Bills can roll coverage Wilson’s way even if they think Benford is going to be limited in some capacity. Shutting Wilson down makes the game easier for Buffalo to win. DE David Bailey Bailey is a legitimate Defensive Rookie of the Year threat, as he already has 7.5 sacks and a league-leading five forced fumbles on the year. Dion Dawkins sat last week due to a rib injury, and Spencer Brown played through a back issue last week only for his ankle to be rolled up on late in the game. Yes, he finished the game, but if either of Buffalo’s starting tackles is compromised, it makes it that much easier for the rookie to keep up his excellent first professional season. Buffalo might want to treat Bailey as if he were someone like Dallas Turner or Andrew Van Ginkel—that is, they should consider using some of the same counters to pressure that they did last week, like motioning tight ends into the backfield and putting Allen on the move on bootlegs and in spread formations. Bailey is a stud. The Bills need to account for him on every play. CB Jarvis Brownlee The Jets’ primary nickle corner is someone who the Bills can beat. Brownlee has allowed 18-of-29 passes to be completed when he’s the closest man in coverage. He’s allowed three touchdowns without so much as breaking up a single pass this season. His quarterback rating allowed so far is 112.3 on the year. Given that the Bills have so many options out of the slot—Khalil Shakir, Dalton Kincaid, Keon Coleman, and DJ Moore, to name a few—this is a matchup that Buffalo should watch and look to exploit this week.
author: Sean Murphy

title: Buffalo Bills Week 10 rooting interests and AFC playoff picture
summary: That was some kind of ugly beautiful.  I’m not sure what we watched for the first hour of Monday Night Football, but I’m glad we got back to our regularly scheduled programming before halftime.  That’s when the NFL’s No. 1 offense shifted gears and dared the NFL’s No. 1 defense to keep up. They couldn’t. […]
full_text: That was some kind of ugly beautiful. I’m not sure what we watched for the first hour of Monday Night Football , but I’m glad we got back to our regularly scheduled programming before halftime. That’s when the NFL’s No. 1 offense shifted gears and dared the NFL’s No. 1 defense to keep up. They couldn’t. Not because the Buffalo Bills were playing with the gas pedal down, but because Josh Allen and Co. were flipping the script. Let the pass rush in, and James Cook gets out. Then Josh Allen gets out. And just when it looked like the Minnesota Vikings might have things figured out, the Bills changed it up again. Was it glorious? Nope. But it was brilliant, and somehow, by the fourth quarter, the stress level of Bills Mafia was actually down. And when does that ever happen? Anyway, when Kyle Allen (yep, Josh got to sit out the entire victory formation so he didn’t accidentally drop back below that 5,000-yard rushing mark) took the final knee, the Bills were on top. Of the Vikings. Of the AFC East. Of the AFC. Heck, of the whole league. Yes, you read that right. Buffalo is currently the NFL’s top team. But all that really matters to us right now is the AFC playoff picture and what needs to happen for the Bills to keep their grip on the conference’s No. 1 seed and force everyone else to make a trip to the icy tundra of Western New York in January. So, let’s take a look at who Bills fans should be rooting for this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ Buffalo Bills (7-1) Denver Broncos (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) New England Patriots (5-4) Cleveland Browns (5-4) Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) Baltimore Ravens (4-5) Houston Texans (3-5) New York Jets (2-7) Indianapolis Colts (2-7) Miami Dolphins (1-7) Tennessee Titans (1-7) Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East Buffalo Bills at New York Jets Root for: Bills You don’t need me to tell you why, but here it is anyway. The Bills control their own destiny from here until they lose. And the longer they put that next loss off (I mean, none of us here are going to complain if it doesn’t happen until next August, right?), the less effect it will have on the standings. As long as they keep winning, it doesn’t matter what anyone else does. Go Bills! New England Patriots at Detroit Lions Root for: Lions The Patriots are still Buffalo’s closest competition in the AFC East, and they’re heading to Munich with a 5-4 record and one of those wins came at Buffalo’s expense. A loss to Detroit would give the Bills a little more breathing room in the East, and we certainly aren’t going to complain about that. Miami Dolphins at Indianapolis Colts Root for: Colts Miami isn’t exactly threatening Buffalo’s division lead at 1-7, but there’s no reason to give the Dolphins anything to celebrate. Indianapolis is sitting at 2-7, so neither team is making much noise in the AFC playoff race. We’ll take a Colts win and another Miami loss, thank you very much. _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns Root for: Texans A Houston win would give Buffalo a little help in the strength-of-victory department while moving the Texans a little farther away from the top of next year’s draft. Neither is a bad thing for the Bills. But if Cleveland wins, we won’t complain too much. A Browns win, paired with a Patriots loss, could knock New England out of the playoff picture, at least for now. So, either way, there’s a little something in it for Buffalo. Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals Root for: Steelers Both teams are sitting at 6-2, so somebody has to get that third loss. And looking at the remaining schedules, we’d rather it be Cincinnati. The Bengals have Kansas City and then a bunch of teams sitting below .500 on their schedule, while Pittsburgh still has to face Denver, Jacksonville, and Baltimore twice (and the Ravens are always a threat for a late-season rebound). There are plenty of opportunities for the Steelers to pick up a few losses down the stretch. Let’s give Cincinnati its third one now and worry about Pittsburgh later. Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons Root for: Falcons Kansas City is sitting at 6-2, just behind Denver in the AFC West and still very much in the hunt for the conference’s No. 1 seed. A loss to Atlanta would give Buffalo a little more breathing room and maybe take some of the stress out of that Thanksgiving night showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Besides, do we really need an excuse to root against Kansas City? Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee Titans Root for: Titans Jacksonville is sitting at 6-2 and currently holds the AFC South lead. That’s a little too close to Buffalo for comfort. Tennessee, meanwhile, has managed just one win all season, and now that Buffalo owns the Titans’ fifth-round pick in the 2027 draft, we don’t need them getting too win-happy. But knocking Jacksonville down a notch in the AFC standings is worth more than a few spots in the fifth round. Titan Up! Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Root for: Seahawks The Raiders are sitting at 4-5, outside the playoff picture but not completely out of the race. Seattle is an NFC team, so a Seahawks win keeps Las Vegas from gaining any ground in the AFC without helping another conference contender. A Raider win would help the Bills’ strength of victory, but right now we aren’t playing for ties. Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens Root for: Chargers The Chargers haven’t won a game all season, and we’d certainly appreciate it if they decided to start now. Baltimore is sitting at 4-5, and while the Ravens are floundering around right now, Lamar Jackson is promising to return to the field soon. We’d prefer he didn’t have much of a playoff race left to return to. Another Baltimore loss would make that climb even harder. Plus, a winless team knocking off the Ravens on Monday night? We’d happily watch that. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Rooting Interests Minnesota Vikings over Green Bay Packers – Strength of Victory Los Angeles Rams over Arizona Cardinals – Strength of Victory Games that don’t move the needle for Buffalo: San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys Washington Commanders at New York Giants _____________________________________________________________________________ Teams on Bye Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers _____________________________________________________________________________ If the football gods are feeling generous this weekend, the Bills could wake up Monday morning with a little more room to breathe at the top of the AFC. Denver and Pittsburgh would still be close enough to make things interesting, but Kansas City and Jacksonville would need binoculars to see Buffalo two full games ahead of them. And the Patriots? Three and a half games back sounds like a lovely place for them to be. Of course, none of those favors mean a thing if the Bills don’t handle business against the Jets. So, let’s beat New York, enjoy a little scoreboard watching, and see just how much separation we can put between the Bills and everyone chasing them. Go Bills!
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Exploring New York Jets tendencies ahead of Week 10’s game against Buffalo Bills
summary: The Jets are 2-7 entering Week 10’s game in MetLife Stadium against the Buffalo Bills after Aaron Glenn’s club lost 35-12 against the Chiefs a week ago. But Gang Green is slightly better than their record indicates. Let’s dive into New York’s tendencies before this AFC East clash on Sunday. Jets offense Geno Smith, pocket […]
full_text: The Jets are 2-7 entering Week 10’s game in MetLife Stadium against the Buffalo Bills after Aaron Glenn’s club lost 35-12 against the Chiefs a week ago. But Gang Green is slightly better than their record indicates. Let’s dive into New York’s tendencies before this AFC East clash on Sunday. Jets offense Geno Smith, pocket passer On Sunday, the Bills will face their fourth pure pocket passer of the 2026 campaign in Smith. The others being Jared Goff, Matthew Stafford, and Kirk Cousins. How often a QB scrambles (run, pass, sacks included) and their EPA on those plays pic.twitter.com/k6VArSkELa — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 11, 2026 Smith resides that lower-left quadrant, escaping the pocket on on a little over 10% of his dropbacks. First-round talents The Jets offense features five former first-round picks at marquee positions. Both of their tackles (Olu Fashanu and Armand Membo) were first-round picks. Two of their receivers (Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr.) — former selections in the first-round. And the wild-card of them all, tight end Kenyon Sadiq — first-rounder in 2026. While some of this talent hasn’t fully acclimated to the NFL just yet, there’s plenty of inherent talent within the Jets offensive unit. As for Wilson, who missed last week’s contest against the Chiefs, he has the seventh-best Average Separation Score, per Fantasy Points Data, among receivers who’ve run at least 99 routes entering Week 10. And it’s Cooper Jr., not Wilson, who finds himself inside the Top 10 among all qualifying receivers in yards per route run currently at a hefty 2.73. Minimal motion + play-action The Jets don’t use a lot of window dressing in their offense. They’re currently owners of the sixth-lowest motion rate at 56.0%. And Smith has used play-action on 25.1% of his dropbacks, the 20th-highest among qualifying quarterbacks. More than most teams, what you see is what you get with the Jets offensively. Jets defense Blitzing + base defense + man coverage The Bills will get a reprieve from the blitzing extravaganza they experienced in Week 9’s game against the Vikings, but they better stay prepare to deal with extra rushers. Entering this game, the Jets are fourth in the NFL in blitz rate at 41.2%, per Fantasy Points Data. In most years, that’s probably Top 2 or even the highest in the league. The blitz-happy way is foundational to Glenn’s defenses. Two other core elements of who the Jets are defensively — they don’t move out of base often (so more linebackers, fewer defensive backs on the field), and they want to man-up in coverage. New York has the 10th-highest base defense rate 33.3% — two spots lower than the Bills — and play man at the league’s fourth-highest rate (31.7%). David Bailey The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has gotten out to an rather productive start to his NFL career. My No. 1 overall player in the class, whom I gave a “Jared Verse Lite” comparison to, Bailey has 31 pressures through nine games, the 13th-most among all edge rushers in the NFL. He hasn’t regularly destroyed all left and right tackles in his path as much as the pressure total would indicate, but in Week 9 against the Chiefs, Bailey was genuinely tremendous. He displayed his whole pass-rush arsenal, highlighted by his patented outside speed rush and a speed-to-power based bull. He’s a big-time talent starting to come into his own getting after the quarterback — 20 of his 31 pressures have occurred in the past four games. Pass defense vs. run defense The Jets don’t have the horses up front along the defensive line of a few years ago. But they’re still a stingy run defense thanks to the likes of explosive linebacker Jamien Sherwood and thumping safety Dane Belton. Discounting garbage time, New York’s defense is currently ninth in the NFL in EPA per rush allowed. The Jets also no longer boast Sauce Gardner out wide, D.J. Reed in the slot, and Jordan Whitehead at safety. And those truths have taken a toll on their pass defense. The Jets are 30th in EPA per dropback surrendered and have allowed the fifth-highest passer rating at 103.5. This matchup calls for the Bills to take to the air.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Buffalo Bills records to watch in Week 10 vs. Jets
summary: The Buffalo Bills gave us plenty of reasons to break out the permanent markers Monday night. Josh Allen and James Cook both joined the 5,000-yard rushing club, and Cook finally caught his quarterback on Buffalo’s all-time rushing list. In fact, he didn’t just catch him. He ran right past him, leaving Allen in fifth place […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills gave us plenty of reasons to break out the permanent markers Monday night. Josh Allen and James Cook both joined the 5,000-yard rushing club , and Cook finally caught his quarterback on Buffalo’s all-time rushing list . In fact, he didn’t just catch him. He ran right past him, leaving Allen in fifth place while claiming fourth for himself. That’s three records we can officially cross off our watch list, which means the pencils and erasers can take a little break. But don’t put them completely away just yet. We’ve still got a few names moving up the franchise and NFL leaderboards, and Greg Rousseau is making a pretty good case for getting another permanent marker entry before the season is over. This week, the Bills head to New Jersey to face the New York Jets, and we’ve got another Hall of Famer in Josh Allen’s sights, a couple of familiar former Bills receivers who could be moving down the rankings, and a few records that might require something a little extraordinary. So, sharpen those pencils, keep the erasers close, and make sure the permanent markers haven’t dried out. It’s time to open the Buffalo Bills Record Book. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1 — Sure Things Nothing to see here this week, folks! After all the permanent ink we used Monday night, we’re giving this chapter a little time to dry. Don’t worry, though. There are still plenty of records waiting in the chapters ahead. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2 — A Good Bet Josh Allen passes Peyton Manning Apparently, Josh Allen isn’t quite finished rearranging the NFL record books. After tying Peyton Manning’s mark of 322 combined passing and rushing touchdowns through a player’s first 10 seasons, Allen needs just one more to claim the record for himself. And, of course, he’s doing it in only his ninth season. Considering Allen has accounted for at least one touchdown in every game this season, this one feels like a pretty safe bet. We might want to have that permanent marker ready at kickoff. Greg Rousseau sets a new personal best Greg Rousseau has been making regular appearances in our Record Book lately, and he’s back again this week with another milestone within reach – this one of the personal variety. Rousseau’s sack against Minnesota brought his season total to eight, matching the career highs he set in 2022 and matched in 2024. Just one more sack against the Jets would give him nine on the season, setting a new personal best with plenty of football still left to play. With eight games still remaining in the regular season, the question might not be whether Rousseau breaks his personal record, but just how high he can push that number before January. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3 — Not Impossible Dawson Knox moves up the Bills’ all-time receiving touchdowns list Dawson Knox is hanging out with a couple of familiar faces on Buffalo’s all-time receiving touchdowns list. With 28 career touchdown catches, he’s currently tied with Stevie Johnson and Gabe Davis. That’s not bad company to keep, but we’re guessing Knox would say he’s not planning to stay long. One more touchdown catch would move Knox ahead of both former Bills receivers and into a tie with Jerry Butler, who finished his Buffalo career with 29. And if Allen happens to find his tight end in the end zone twice on Sunday? Knox would hit 30 career receiving touchdowns and move ahead of Butler, too. Knox might not be the first name that comes to mind when we’re predicting who will score on Sunday, but he’s been one of Allen’s trusted targets for years. Don’t bet against him is all we can say. Josh Allen joins the 90 rushing touchdowns club Josh Allen has already checked off one major rushing milestone this week, but there’s another one waiting just around the corner. With 88 career rushing touchdowns, Allen is just two away from joining Hall of Fame running backs Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin at 90. Two rushing touchdowns against the Jets would put Allen in a tie with both legendary backs, while three would move him past them. That’s a pretty remarkable neighborhood for a quarterback to be hanging out in, especially one who still has plenty of football ahead of him. Of course, two rushing touchdowns in a single game isn’t exactly an everyday occurrence, even for Allen. But we’ve seen him take over games with his legs often enough that we’re certainly not ruling it out. And if Buffalo finds itself near the goal line a few times Sunday, those pencils might get a workout. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4 — Superhuman Greg Rousseau makes a run at Mario We’ve already got Greg Rousseau penciled in for a new personal best this week, but what if he decides one sack just isn’t enough? Rousseau enters Sunday’s game with 40 career sacks, putting him just three behind former Bills defensive end Mario Williams, who recorded 43 during his four seasons in Buffalo. Now, a three- or four-sack afternoon is asking quite a bit, even from a player who’s been making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks. But that’s why we have a Superhuman chapter, isn’t it? _____________________________________________________________________________ Of course, the Jets probably aren’t particularly interested in helping Buffalo rewrite any records on Sunday. But if the Bills take care of business in New Jersey, we might just have a few more entries to cross off our list when we meet back here next week.

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 10
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries For once, the Panthers got some good news on the injury front heading into their Week 10 showdown against the New Orleans Saints. Offensive lineman Brady Christensen nearly returned […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 22: Carolina Panthers guard Brady Christensen (70) and Carolina Panthers guard Damien Lewis (68) during an NFL football game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Carolina Panthers on December 22, 2024 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte N.C.(Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries For once, the Panthers got some good news on the injury front heading into their Week 10 showdown against the New Orleans Saints. Offensive lineman Brady Christensen nearly returned from injury last week, but was held out to ensure he was fully ready to go. Hopefully this is the week the versatile player can help plug one of the many, many holes on the Panthers offensive line. He’s currently listed as questionable for Sunday. Speaking of the Panthers offensive line, guard Damien Lewis was a full participant in practice on both Wednesday and Friday, though he was limited on Thursday. The incumbent starter has missed the Panthers last two games. He looks good to go Sunday. The Panthers have three additional questionable players this week in outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, and wide receiver Xavier Legette. Carolina could definitely use all three of them, at least situationally. Both cornerback Mike Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks are doubtful, while linebacker Bobby Okereke is out. Transactions Signed LB Claudin Cherelus to the practice squad The Panthers have brought back linebacker Claudin Cherelus to the practice squad after waiving him back in September with an injury designation. This is Cherelus’s fourth season in Carolina after beginning his NFL career with the Panthers as an undrafted free agent back in 2023. He has appeared in 35 games for the Panthers with six starts, registering 61 tackles. Released WR David Moore then signed to the practice squad Since joining the Carolina Panthers in 2024, wide receiver David Moore has been a fixture on the roster more for his veteran stability than his actual on-field productivity. This past week the Panthers waived him then re-signed him to the practice squad, just in case the wide receiver room suffers any more injuries. This year Moore has appeared in six games with one reception 27 yards. He has also returned four punts and eight kickoffs this year. Signed DT Cam Horsley to the practice squad Cam Horsley joined the Tennessee Titans last year as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Boston College. To his credit, he made the 53-man roster and appeared in one game, playing 14 defensive snaps without recording any stats. Horsley is a diamond in the rough the Panthers will look to polish to provide some additional depth along the defensive interior. Placed WR Ihmir Smith-Marsette on practice squad-injured Ihmir Smith-Marsette is a bit of a blast from the past for Panthers fans. He joined the Panthers in 2023, which was his third NFL season at the time. He saw the field, too, appearing in all 17 games that year as Carolina’s primary punt returner who also had 11 kick returns. Back in 2023 he also contributed eight receptions for 51 yards and eight carries for 74 more yards. He left Carolina for the New York Jets in 2024, then didn’t appear in any games in 2025. The Panthers added him to the practice squad back in September 2026, and now he has an injury designation.

title: Brian Answers: Injuries, blame for losses, early look at free agency, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I think all the fans are looking for answers following a 3 game skid, I’m here to try and give you those. Let’s dive in! TXPanther: Which of these guys would be priority for designated to return from IR? […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Head Coach Dave Canales of the Carolina Panthers congratulates Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos after their 26-21 win at Bank of America Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I think all the fans are looking for answers following a 3 game skid, I’m here to try and give you those. Let’s dive in! TXPanther: Which of these guys would be priority for designated to return from IR ? Would you save any spots? They have used 2 designations so far which leaves 6 to be used. Well, the Panthers answered that question this week by activating RB Jonathon Brooks, CB Mike Jackson, WR Xavier Legette, and OL Brady Christensen (last week on that one). Those would have been my choices, and I expect one of the remaining spots is earmarked for Jaycee Horn unless they feel he cannot return. I have a feeling they’ll have used up all of their IR to return designations before the seasons end, sadly. Only one I’m not entirely sure about is Xavier Legette, but hopefully he comes out and shows us some of the promise that made him a first round pick. @WTMealey: rank these in order of who you feel is too blame for losses or put another way what change would give the most results Injuries Evero Lack of talent on the roster-feel free to point fingers Canales Bryce Morgan Tepper I don’t really feel I can put it in a particular order, but I blame Ejiro Evero and Dave Canales mostly for the unpreparedness of the players and the lack of discipline on bone headed penalty plays. Obviously, injuries certainly play a role since the Panthers have been very snake bitten by them. I know Bryce Young hasn’t played in the out of his mind way he did to start the year every game, but I’m still not going to blame him for the majority of the Panthers losses. storybook: Would you rather win the division at 8-9 again or have a better draft pick? I’m still of the mindset that you should try to make the playoffs. This fan base really enjoyed the playoff game last season and that’s really the point of all of this right? Get into the dance, see what happens. I also trust this front office to make good decisions no matter where they are picking in the first round, so having a better draft pick doesn’t give me as much anxiety as it did in the past. GooseCreek: The Panthers will have 25 free agents (13 offense/11 defense/1 special teams) at season’s end (3 ERFA* & 22 UFA** players). ERFA players (B. Tremayne, C. Bullock, & TeRah Edwards) are routinely tendered leaving 22 players (11 offensive/10 defensive/1 spec. teams) for resolution. I suspect the team allows J.J. Jansen (special teams) to decide his own fate (return?/retire?). My question to you, Brian: Who makes your priority list in each of the following categories? Three (3) Offensive players to retain? Three (3) Offensive players to let walk? Three (3) Defensive players to retain? Three (3) Defensive players to let walk? Any practice squad players you would seek to retain under a Futures contract? *ERFA: Exclusive Rights Free Agents **UFA: Unrestricted Free Agents I think at this point you look to retain OT Ikem Ekwonu. Rasheed Walker isn’t the answer and you probably need to have Monroe Freeling playing one of the tackle spots since I suspect Taylor Moton won’t be around next season. I also think you retain TE Tommy Tremble if his contract demands are relatively reasonable, which they should be. Finally, I think you hold onto WR Brycen Tremayne, who has been very good for the Panthers when called upon and is excellent on special teams. You can probably let C Luke Fortner walk since he hasn’t been good and should be looking for a replacement. The rest of their free agents on offense are fairly retainable but not priorities in my opinion, Brady Christensen may change this answer depending on how he looks in action. I think you have to retain CB Mike Jackson, even despite his injury. The Panthers still need 3 starter level corners and they won’t have a need (when healthy) if they bring him back to pair with Horn and Will Lee III. I think you also have to retain LB Bobby Okereke after his performance as a guy they signed off roster cuts. And of course, you gotta retain the Ace That Runs The Place 2.0, Nick Scott. The rest of their list doesn’t feel like people I’d worry too much about if they walk. I’d say WR Ja’Seem Reed, CB Corey Thornton, and CB Marco Wilson. Beyond that I really have no idea on some of these guys. SmoothC: What head coaching jobs will be available by season’s end? My guess would be the Eagles, Ravens, Chargers, Buccaneers, and maybe the Cowboys. I hope not for Carolina, but time will tell. Senanima: How long does Waller sip the youth giving Kool Aid? Probably at least two more seasons. He’s a pretty specialized player and doesn’t have as much mileage for an NFL player at his age as you’d expect. Might make sense to bring him back again in 2027. Highmiles: We all know injuries have killed us this year. The question is why are we more injury prone than most teams? Bad trainers and conditioning coaches? Poor draft selections? By this I mean trying to draft better players that drop in the draft due to injury history. Turf field? I’ve never been a fan of the turf field regardless of what the NFL points to as “statistics” correlating to the injuries on turf vs grass. I’ve played on both and can tell you turf definitely seemed to feel like it did more damage. I don’t blame the coaches or staff for it, the Panthers just seem to have bad luck especially this season. And as far as draft selections go, you can really only point to Jonathon Brooks, and I still feel like his issues were mostly just bad luck. I think you can make an argument his first injury after entering the league MIGHT have been a coaching/staff oversight by playing him too fast, but they’ve given him more than enough rehab time since then. Sometimes injuries just happen and there are many players’ careers that fizzled out more due to bad luck than anything. I’m hoping he gets a chance to show off on his return stint this year. positivebob: Was Morgan right to stand pat at the trade deadline or should he have moved a high value player, Derrick Brown? for draft capital? Or was he handcuffed by having less than 1 mil in cap space, until todays restructure of Moton’s contract? That still only freed up less than 4 mil. I think this is a great question. The Panthers have been in a weird spot where they looked like they could (and still can) compete for a playoff spot, but their roster isn’t one where you can trade for a guy or two and make a run like other teams. The Panthers are also not actively rebuilding and have been in the “talent collection” stage if that makes sense. Letting Derrick Brown go is a move that basically signals the season is over, and wholesale changes are coming in the off-season. I think Dan Morgan was right to just stand pat, this team doesn’t need to be blown up again right now. Slick22: How many activations from IR do we have left? They appear to have 2 left following this week. 2 more if they somehow make the playoffs. That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Join us next week for another edition of the weekly mailbag!
author: Brian Beversluis

title: Panthers vs Saints: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers are 3-5 after three straight losses, but they play in the NFC South, so naturally that’s still good enough to lead the division going into Week 10. They currently sit in a tie with the New Orleans Saints, and both teams are a half game up on both the Falcons and Buccaneers. […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 09: Devaughn Vele #14 of the New Orleans Saints catches a pass against Mike Jackson #2 of the Carolina Panthers during the first half in the game at Bank of America Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are 3-5 after three straight losses, but they play in the NFC South, so naturally that’s still good enough to lead the division going into Week 10. They currently sit in a tie with the New Orleans Saints, and both teams are a half game up on both the Falcons and Buccaneers. This Sunday will have a big impact on the race for the NFC South crown, particularly if the Panthers are able to win on the road in New Orleans. The Saints are having a weird season, so it’s a game that’s ripe for the Panthers’ taking. They just need to control a few matchups to give themselves their best chance to win. Let’s look at what those are. Mike Jackson vs Chris Olave Mike Jackson seems like he’ll be back in the lineup since he’s practiced in full so far this week. He walks right back into the fire against one of the better wide receivers in the NFL. Chris Olave got forgotten about a little bit after an injury plagued 2024 season and an up and down start to the 2025 season, but he’s thrived with Tyler Shough under center. He’s currently sixth in the NFL in receiving yards and has given the Panthers problems in the past. He went for 189 yards in two touchdowns in the two meetings between these teams last season. Mike Jackson and whoever else is tasked with limiting Olave are going to have their hands full. He’s the big play threat, and keeping him under wraps will go a long way to keeping the Saints offense under wraps. Panthers offensive tackles vs Saints edge rushers On paper, the Saints’ edge rushers are one the strengths of their defense. Cameron Jordan is still there, though he’s more of a prop than a standout player at this point of his career. Chase Young is actually good in New Orleans after busting in Washington, and Carl Granderson is pretty good in the rotation as well. The Panthers have had a lot of struggles on their offensive line, but the tackles have been a pretty consistent problem. The Saints pass defense as a whole is not that great, but that won’t matter if the edges are bearing down on Bryce Young all game. He needs Monroe Freeling and Rasheed Walker to hold up so he can take advantage of the Saints’ struggling secondary. Lee Hunter and the interior line vs Cesar Ruiz and Jeremiah Wright The Saints lost their starting center Erik McCoy for the next few weeks. To fill the void at center, they’re kicking over starting guard Cesar Ruiz and starting rookie Jeremiah Wright at right guard. Ruiz has a little bit of experience at center, but he’s a guard by trade, so you wouldn’t expect him to be at his best at a new position. Wright is a fourth round rookie with just one start under his belt, so I’d like to he think he could be had as well. Lee Hunter was incredibly disruptive in limited snaps last week. Hopefully Dave Canales and Todd Wash figured out how to get him more snaps. He and the rest of the interior line have a chance to make some noise. The Saints vs their own stadium The Dome used to be one of the most intimidating places to play in back in the days of Drew Brees and Sean Payton. That’s gone by the wayside in recent years, and it seems to have reached a low point in terms of intimidation factor. The Saints had two big home events this year—the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming and some sort of Drew Brees honor night. They were beat down in both of those games. They’re 1-4 at home this seaosn with the only win coming in overtime against the Shedeur Sanders-led Browns last week. The Saints vs the first quarter The Saints have scored 10 points in the first quarter all season long. They are last in first quarter scoring and 30th in first half scoring. The Panthers need to jump on the Saints early, which will also help amplify the struggles the Saints are having at home.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: 5 biggest needs for Bears in 2027 offseason
summary: Heading into their Week 10 bye week, the Bears find themselves with a favorable 7-2 record and a first-place standing in the loaded NFC North. Even with the slight derailment of Caleb Williams missing three games due to injury, they are firmly positioned as one of the top teams in the NFL entering the second […]
full_text: Heading into their Week 10 bye week, the Bears find themselves with a favorable 7-2 record and a first-place standing in the loaded NFC North. Even with the slight derailment of Caleb Williams missing three games due to injury, they are firmly positioned as one of the top teams in the NFL entering the second half of the season. Since the Bears don’t play a game this weekend, now is as good of a time as any to look towards the future. I’m not in full mock offseason mode yet, especially since a few potential cut candidate veterans still have a lot to prove before I feel comfortable projecting who stays and who goes. But for the most part, we know what their biggest strengths and weaknesses will be heading into the 2027 offseason. I’ll be ranking the Bears’ five biggest needs this offseason are, and I’ll include a few prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft that could be of interest in the second round. Since Chicago traded its first-round pick this year for Jeffery Simmons, highlighting potential Day 2 prospects will make up a lot of our draft coverage in the weeks and months ahead. I’ll include players ranked around the Round 2 range using the PFN Consensus Big Board , and I’ll include my own rankings for each player accordingly. 5. Offensive guard Guard is much more of a long-term need than a short-term one, as Joe Thuney is the reigning Protector of the Year, and Jonah Jackson is playing at an All-Pro level in 2026. However, Thuney is experiencing slight regression; his 75.8 PFN OL Impact grade is a considerable dip from his 91.1 grade last year. He’ll be turning 34 years old in a few days, and if the Bears do well enough in the playoffs, it’s possible he could look to call it a career. Obviously, the ideal scenario sees Thuney stick around in Chicago for at least another season. But the team could eventually use a long-term successor to him along its interior offensive line. I wouldn’t expect the Bears to draft a guard early this year, and they have solid depth with the likes of Luke Newman and Jordan McFadden. That said, it’s a position they could address earlier than people expect if the value is right, or if Thuney chooses to retire this offseason. 2027 draft prospects in Round 2: Austin Siereveld, Ohio State (Consensus: 45; Infante: 59) Cayden Green, Missouri (Consensus: 56; Infante: 58) Carter Smith, Indiana (Consensus: 61; Infante: 34) Evan Tengesdahl, Cincinnati (Consensus: 85; Infante: 139) 4. Linebacker Should the Bears let go of T.J. Edwards this offseason, it would free them $8.5 million in cap space in 2027. Among 78 qualified linebackers, his 66.2 PFN LB Impact grade ranks just No. 72 at the position. They could just slide D’Marco Jackson in his place in the starting lineup next year, but there’s also a chance they could draft a linebacker early. I’d keep an eye on speedier players at the position, as defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has emphasized the importance of speed and mobility on his defense. The 2027 draft lacks the blue-chip talent at linebacker that 2026 had in Sonny Styles and Arvell Reese, but there are a handful of solid Day 2 prospects who could be right up Chicago’s alley. 2027 draft prospects in Round 2: Sammy Brown, Clemson (Consensus: 53; Infante: 40) Tony Rojas, Penn State (Consensus: 78; Infante: 67) Sammy Omosigho, UCLA (Consensus: 124; Infante: 81) Rasheem Biles, Texas (Consensus: 183; Infante: 82) 3. Defensive end All things considered, the Bears’ group of defensive ends has been better than I expected it would be going into 2026. Austin Booker has performed at a high level, Dayo Odeyingbo showed improvement before his injury, and Montez Sweat’s play has gotten better since Chicago traded for Jeffery Simmons. There’s still plenty of long-term uncertainty at the position, however. The Bears will need cap space to work with in the 2027 offseason, and it’s likely that a big move will be made at defensive end to free some up. Sweat’s release would create $21 million in cap space, while Odeyingbo’s release would free up $15 million. It’s unlikely they choose to cut both, but one of them could end up as a cap casualty. At that point, Chicago would need a new edge rusher to pair with the likes of Booker, Shemar Turner, and whichever veteran they choose to keep around. Luckily for them, the 2027 draft is deep with high-floor, powerful edge rushers who fit the physical mold that Allen historically prefers in his hand-in-the-dirt defensive ends. 2027 draft prospects in Round 2: Will Heldt, Clemson (Consensus: 54; Infante: 53) Clev Lubin, Louisville (Consensus: 55; Infante: 66) Kenyatta Jackson Jr., Ohio State (Consensus: 72; Infante: 78) Matayo Uiagalelei, Oregon (Consensus: 75; Infante: 64) Jordan Ross, LSU (Consensus: 80; Infante: 73) 2. Defensive tackle The addition of Jeffery Simmons has had a massive impact on the Bears’ defense, and part of why the team was willing to give up two first-round picks for him was the fact that he recently signed an extension with the Titans. As a result, Chicago can hold onto him through 2030. His presence definitely helps the interior defensive line, but that group is otherwise pretty thin. Grady Jarrett projects as a cap casualty with the $13.5 million the Bears would free up by releasing him. Elsewhere, they don’t have a proven long-term option at the position outside of Simmons. The likes of Neville Gallimore, Jordan van den Berg, and Jayden Loving could end up as decent depth pieces, but none of them have proven to be starting-caliber players in the NFL (at least not yet, in the case of the latter two). Adding another interior defensive force should be a priority for the Bears, and there happen to be several defensive tackle prospects I like in the Day 2 range of this 2027 draft class, even though they’ll be missing out on some of the first-round talent. 2027 draft prospects in Round 2: Tavion Gadson, Kentucky (Consensus: 46; Infante: 68) Ahmad Moten, Miami (FL) (Consensus: 47; Infante: 18) Justin Scott, Miami (FL) (Consensus: 49; Infante: 44) Bear Alexander, Oregon (Consensus: 57; Infante: 109) A.J. Holmes Jr., Texas Tech (Consensus: 74; Infante: 32) 1. Cornerback This season has been very exciting for the Bears so far, but the biggest disappointment with this team in 2026 has to be the cornerback room. Malik Muhammad has surpassed expectations as a fourth-round rookie, and Kyler Gordon’s return in the slot has been valuable, but Chicago has otherwise faced rocky play at the position along the perimeter. Jaylon Johnson had a pick-six and shut down the Buccaneers’ offense last Sunday night, but he’s played poorly for most of the season. It’s possible the Simmons addition can help turn his season around, but with the $16 million the Bears would free up by releasing him, Johnson remains on the bubble. Tyrique Stevenson is also an impending free agent, and much like Chicago’s many secondary free agents from the 2026 offseason, it feels unlikely that the team extends him. We’ll see which cornerback prospects actually declare for the 2027 draft, but there’s a lot of good value late in Round 2 or early in Round 3 based on my current evaluations. 2027 draft prospects in Round 2: Vicari Swain, South Carolina (Consensus: 50; Infante: 99) Audavion Collins, Penn State (Consensus: 51; Infante: 48) Jalen Mayo, Houston (Consensus: 65; Infante: 77) Andrew Marshall, Nebraska (Consensus: 50; Infante: 49) Zabien Brown, Alabama (Consensus: 82; Infante: 69) DJ McKinney, Notre Dame (Consensus: 87; Infante: 70)

title: Question of the Day: How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied?
summary: The Chicago Bears have hit the bye at 7-2 and are sitting in first place of the gauntlet NFC North. The Bears have a tough second-half schedule but certainly appear to be headed to the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Last season, the Bears won the division, won their first playoff game in 15 […]
full_text: Mike Ditka, Chicago Bears' coach, holds a press conference with the Vince Lombardi Trophy firmly in his grasp after his team wins the Super Bowl. (Photo by Bettmann Archive/Getty Images) The Chicago Bears have hit the bye at 7-2 and are sitting in first place of the gauntlet NFC North. The Bears have a tough second-half schedule but certainly appear to be headed to the playoffs for the second consecutive year. Last season, the Bears won the division, won their first playoff game in 15 years, and they were an eyelash away from reaching the NFC Championship Game. I think 99% of Bears fans, after the sting of the Rams loss wore off, were very pleased with the results of the 2025 season, even if they lost the last game they played. This year, at approximately the midway point in the season, the Bears are at or near the top of everyone’s list of a true Super Bowl contender. With more success comes more expectations. How far do Bears have to go for you to be satisfied with their season? I think as fans, when the team is building something, we want to see them improve upon the previous season. Since there were only four teams that had more postseason success than Chicago, there isn’t a ton of room to improve. That being said, I think Bears fans and NFL media around the country expect the Bears to be better than they were in 2025. Answer: I think the first obvious step is that for any level of satisfaction to be reached, the Bears have to be one of the last four remaining teams in the NFL. That’s a lofty thing to say, but I think it’s fair. I think if the Bears make the playoffs but lose in the Wild Card or Divisional round, there will be plenty of disappointment with the fan base. Yes, fans will be excited that the Bears made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 2005 and 2006, but that won’t be good enough. Even if the Bears win a playoff game in back-to-back seasons, it’ll be the first time they’ve done that since 1984 and 1985, but even then, that won’t be good enough. I think for some fans, reaching the NFC Championship Game will be enough. If the San Francisco 49ers are the 1 seed and the Bears go on the road and lose in that game, there will be a certain level of satisfaction, but I still don’t think that’s enough. I think the Bears need to reach the Super Bowl for me to walk away feeling excited without too much disappointment. Obviously, I want them to win, but if Josh Allen climbs the mountaintop and beats the Bears and wins the Super Bowl, am I going to be freaking out? No, I just think the Bears will be ready to take the next step in 2027. What say you, Bears fans? How far do the Bears have to go this year for you to be content with their season? Is it Super Bowl or bust, like it is for Bill Zimmerman? Is it the Lombardi Trophy? Or is a lower level of success good enough for you? Sound off in the comments below!
author: Bill Zimmerman

title: Bears Week 10 Flashbacks: Concannon’s Bombs, Dent’s Dominance, Vasher’s 108 yards
summary: The Bears may be enjoying their bye week, but the Gridiron Time Machine doesn’t need the week off. Instead of our usual three games, we’re digging a little deeper this week with five memorable Week 10 performances, spanning nearly 60 years of Bears history. 1. 1967, Bears vs. Cardinals: Concannon goes deep, over and over […]
full_text: Chicago Bears Nathan Vasher returns a FG for a TD during a game at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois on November 13, 2005. (Photo by Bill Smith/Getty Images) The Bears may be enjoying their bye week, but the Gridiron Time Machine doesn’t need the week off. Instead of our usual three games, we’re digging a little deeper this week with five memorable Week 10 performances, spanning nearly 60 years of Bears history. 1. 1967, Bears vs. Cardinals: Concannon goes deep, over and over again November 19, 1967 | Bears win 30-3 The 1967 Bears were sitting at 4-5 when the St. Louis Cardinals came to Wrigley Field for Week 10. What followed was one of the more explosive passing performances of the era. Jack Concannon completed only 11 passes, but those completions went for an incredible 336 yards and three touchdowns. Dick Gordon was responsible for most of the damage, catching four passes for 179 yards and two scores. The touchdowns were not exactly short ones either. Concannon connected with Gordon for a 93-yard touchdown early in the second quarter, then found Bob Jones for another 51-yard score. Before halftime arrived, Gordon struck again from 67 yards out. Three touchdown passes. All three from more than 50 yards away. Meanwhile, the Bears defense made sure St. Louis never had much of an opportunity to respond. Chicago intercepted Cardinals quarterbacks seven times, including five picks from Jim Hart alone, while forcing nine turnovers overall. The Cardinals finished with only 230 total yards and never reached the end zone. Chicago cruised to a 30-3 victory behind 461 yards of offense. For a franchise that has not exactly been known for explosive passing attacks, Concannon throwing three touchdown passes of 51 yards or longer feels almost out of place in Bears history. Almost. 2. 1979, Bears vs. Lions: Everybody gets involved November 4, 1979 | Bears win 35-7 The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1979 season sitting at 4-5 and desperately trying to remain in the playoff picture. Detroit turned out to be a pretty good opponent for getting things moving in the right direction. Walter Payton once again carried the offense, rushing for 113 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries while adding another 53 yards as a receiver. Mike Phipps threw for just 136 yards, but Chicago didn’t need much through the air. The fun really started in the third quarter. With Chicago leading 14-7, Steve Schubert returned a punt 77 yards for a touchdown. Not long afterward, Terry Schmidt intercepted Lions quarterback Jeff Komlo and returned it 20 yards for another score. Suddenly, a seven-point game had become a 28-7 Bears lead. Payton added his second touchdown in the fourth quarter to finish off a 35-7 victory. Chicago did not commit a turnover while forcing five from Detroit, and Payton finished with 166 yards from scrimmage. The win moved the Bears back to .500 at 5-5 and became part of a late-season push that eventually carried Chicago into the playoffs. The recipe probably sounds familiar. Give the ball to Walter Payton, let the defense create mistakes, and sneak in a special teams touchdown while you’re at it. Very Bears. 3. 1984, Bears vs. Raiders: Richard Dent wrecks the defending champs November 4, 1984 | Bears win 17-6 One year before the 1985 Bears defense became immortal, Chicago was already showing the rest of the NFL what was coming. The defending Super Bowl champion Los Angeles Raiders arrived at Soldier Field in Week 10 with a 7-2 record. They left having scored zero touchdowns. Walter Payton handled the offensive workload, rushing 27 times for 111 yards and scoring twice in the first half. His touchdown runs of 18 and eight yards gave Chicago a 14-0 advantage before the defense took care of everything else. And Richard Dent was everywhere. Dent recorded 4.5 sacks, which remains the Bears’ single-game franchise record. Chicago sacked Raiders quarterbacks nine times overall, forced five turnovers and held Los Angeles to just 181 total yards. The Raiders managed only two field goals in a 17-6 Bears victory. It was the first time the defending champions had been held without a touchdown in more than three years. The win moved Chicago to 7-3 and gave the Bears another indication that Buddy Ryan’s defense was developing into something special. We know what happened one year later. But before the Super Bowl Shuffle, the playoff shutouts and the legend of the 1985 defense, Richard Dent and company were already making Sundays miserable for opposing quarterbacks. The defending Super Bowl champions just happened to get an early preview. 4. 1990, Bears vs. Falcons: Vestee Jackson shuts the door November 11, 1990 | Bears win 30-24 The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1990 season as one of the hottest teams in football. Atlanta came to Soldier Field and nearly spoiled the afternoon. After falling behind 3-0, Chicago scored 24 unanswered points behind touchdowns from Neal Anderson, Wendell Davis and Brad Muster. Jim Harbaugh connected with Davis for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Bears carried a 24-3 advantage into the second half. Then things got uncomfortable. Atlanta scored two unanswered touchdowns to cut the lead to 24-17, and what had looked like a comfortable afternoon suddenly became a one-score game. Fortunately, Chris Miller threw one pass too many. Vestee Jackson jumped the route and returned the interception 45 yards for a touchdown, pushing the lead back to 30-17 with just over a minute remaining. Atlanta scored once more, but Chicago held on for a 30-24 victory. Miller threw for 239 yards and two touchdowns, but the Bears intercepted him four times. Wendell Davis led Chicago offensively with five catches for 105 yards and a score, while Harbaugh added 195 passing yards and another 47 on the ground. The victory improved Chicago to 8-1 and extended its winning streak to five games. Sometimes the defense dominates from start to finish. Other times it waits until things get interesting before reminding everyone who is in charge. 5. 2005, Bears vs. 49ers: Nathan Vasher goes 108 yards November 13, 2005 | Bears win 17-9 If you remember anything about the Bears’ 2005 Week 10 win over San Francisco, it probably isn’t the offense. That’s because there wasn’t much of one. Chicago quarterback Kyle Orton threw for only 67 yards. San Francisco quarterback Cody Pickett somehow managed just one completion for 28 yards. The real star was the wind. With gusts approaching 50 miles per hour at Soldier Field, 49ers kicker Joe Nedney attempted a 52-yard field goal on the final play of the first half. The kick fell short. Nathan Vasher was waiting. Vasher caught the ball deep in the end zone, briefly hesitated, then took off. He reversed field, found a convoy of blockers and raced all the way to the opposite end zone for a 108-yard touchdown. At the time, it was the longest play in NFL history. The return gave Chicago a 7-3 halftime lead in a game where points were extremely difficult to find. Adrian Peterson later rushed for a seven-yard touchdown and finished with 120 yards on 24 carries, while Robbie Gould added a fourth-quarter field goal. The Bears held on for a 17-9 victory, their fifth straight win, improving to 6-3 while maintaining control of the NFC North. One year later, Devin Hester would return another missed field goal exactly 108 yards against the Giants. Apparently 108-yard missed field goal returns were just something Bears defensive backs did for a while. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .
author: Gary Baugher Jr.
