title: 2026 NFL QB Rankings: Midseason Edition
summary: We are roughly halfway through the season, and it’s time to update our QB rankings once again. I thought this season was going to be a fascinating season to rank quarterbacks because I felt that the back half of the top 10 was wildly in flux. I felt that the top 5 was pretty well […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are roughly halfway through the season, and it’s time to update our QB rankings once again. I thought this season was going to be a fascinating season to rank quarterbacks because I felt that the back half of the top 10 was wildly in flux. I felt that the top 5 was pretty well established, and with Father Time catching up to Matthew Stafford, there’s even a spot in the top 5 up for grabs. But the biggest news is that we have knocked the King from the top spot. Patrick Mahomes has always been first on this list over the last two seasons, but it’s time to acknowledge a fact: Josh Allen is now the best QB in the NFL. Here’s a list of the updated rankings, and as a reminder, these rankings are my opinion based on how the QB is playing this year, but also looking at their full body of work. Justin Herbert is not one of the top 30 QBs this season in isolation, but it’s tough to rank him that low based on his previous seasons of success. 1. Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills (2, 2) The King is dead. Mahomes is still great, but he doesn’t impact the game as Allen does, and Allen has been at this level for the last couple of years. It’s time to make the switch up top. 2. Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs (1, 1) I think many of us keep wondering if we are ever going to get back to that peak Mahomes 2018 to 2022 version. He seems to be gone, but the 2023-2026 version is still very, very good. 3. Joe Burrow, Cincinnati Bengals (5, 4) Burrow is headed towards his first MVP, and it’s one he absolutely deserves. Elite play without question. 4. Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens (4, 3) In 2024, Lamar had 45 touchdowns and 4 INTs. That wasn’t that long ago, but the injuries have slowed him down significantly the last two seasons. If Lamar has another injury-riddled season next year, he may start tumbling in 2027. 5. Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (15, 9) Brock Purdy has earned this spot with his play, but I also don’t think he’s truly a top 5 QB at the NFL level. Top 10? Yes. But I don’t think Purdy is in this tier, and there are guys biting at his heels that could easily jump him before the 2026 rankings are finalized in January. 6. Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears (11, 10) Caleb’s play from week one and his three-game stretch returning from injury was better than anyone else’s in the league. But 4 INTs, even if it’s a blip, certainly has to be considered, and between that and the injury, it keeps Caleb out of the top 5 (for now). 7. Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (13, 11) I’ve been fairly critical of Love, but it’s hard to argue with what he is doing with a suspect offensive line and no running game. The Packers have the best deep-ball passing attack in the league, and it’s not particularly close. 8. Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars (14, 12) After what Lawrence has done in the back half of last season and the first half of this season with Liam Coen, he has cemented Lawrence as a top-10 QB; now it’s time to see how far he can climb. 9. Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys (7, 6) Dak has led a maddeningly inconsistent and underperforming offense. He’s still an excellent player, but he’s most accurately considered a borderline top-10 QB, and that’s where he’s sitting midway through the season. 10. Matthew Stafford, LA Rams (3, 5) Stafford’s season has been fine, but it has vibes quite similar to Tom Brady’s final season in Tampa. The numbers are down across the board. They’re still good, but not MVP-level like last year, and you have to wonder if this might be Father Time knocking at the door. 11. Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (10, 7) There may be nobody better operating from a clean pocket than Goff. Unfortunately, there are many QBs that operate far better under pressure. If Goff ever managed chaos well, he could climb as high as the top 5, but at this point in his career, that’s probably not happening. 12. Drake Maye, New England Patriots (9, 14) Patriots fans will probably see this ranking and be annoyed, but until Maye starts performing at a much better level against better teams, for me, it’s going to be hard to push him into those elite spots on the rankings. 13. CJ Stroud, Houston Texans (19, 18) He’s playing the best football since his rookie season, and he’s leading a Texans team that we thought would be carried by their defense. If the Texans make the playoffs, it’s going to be behind Stroud’s right arm. 14. Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders (17, 16) Daniels still shows flashes of who he was as a rookie, but a messy offense, injuries, and really poor decisions late in games are keeping Daniels down. He’s going to need to string together a solid couple of months of football while staying healthy if he ever wants to get out of this middle group. 15. Bo Nix, Denver Broncos (18, 19) I still don’t trust Nix, but maybe I should start. When the game is on the line, Nix makes the plays; he just doesn’t do it for the first 50 to 55 minutes of the game. If Nix starts putting together a more complete game on a consistent basis, he can surge towards the top 10. 16. Justin Herbert, LA Chargers (6, 8) Herbert entered the season with a chance to finally break into the top 5 with a big season; instead, he’s playing at a level that makes him the worst starting QB in the NFL. Tough to drop him all the way down with his history of regular season success, but he’s playing at a level that nobody can consider him one of the league’s top 10 QBs until he proves otherwise. 17. Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks (8, 13) Darnold is another guy who had a chance to start changing the narrative around his name after two great seasons and a Super Bowl championship, but he has struggled this year and arguably looked worse than his backup, Drew Lock. If Seattle is going to get back into the playoff hunt, Darnold needs to return to form. 18. Jalen Hurts, Philadelphia Eagles (12, 15) It’s tough to have Hurts much higher than this point when the Eagles are clearly stocking up to potentially replace him. Hurts being out for the year with blood clots is awful for him, but based on where Hurts was prior to the issue, the writing does seem to be on the wall here in Philly. 19. Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers (22, 17) Young had really started stringing together some good games where you had to potentially consider him being in the top half of the league’s QBs, but in the last three games, he has 5 TDs, 4 INTs, has completed less than 60% of his passes, and a Y/A of 6.1. He’s reminded us who he is as a QB. 20. Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints (23, 21) Shough had a brutal game against the Vikings but has been pretty darn good in all his other games. He needs to start leading the Saints to some wins (which he could) down the stretch to start pushing his way out of the 20s. 21. Kirk Cousins, Minnesota Vikings (31, 23) Cousins has done a nice job winding the clock back and playing some pretty darn good football. He doesn’t have a high ceiling in Minnesota, but he does have a much higher one than their other QBs, and he helps this Vikings team tremendously. 22. Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (24, 24) Rodgers isn’t playing as well as some are hyping him up to be, but he’s playing a lot better than most thought he could. He’s quite limited at this point, but he can still deliver the football when he needs to. 23. Jaxson Dart, NY Giants (20, 22) Dart awaits his chance next year to show that he’s ready to leap an NFL QB. 24. Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (16, 20) Baker is certainly showing signs of slipping. He’s 31, has been dealing with injuries, and doesn’t look like the guy Tampa has had the last three years. The Baker extension that he signed in September may age like warm milk for Tampa. 25. Michael…

title: Chicago Developers Have a New $10 Billion Plan to Keep the Bears in the City
summary: I get it. Many of you are sick and tired of this ongoing discourse about the Chicago Bears’ new stadium. It’s been years since the project got underway, nearly two years since we were promised shovels would be in the ground soon, and along the way there were several other cities, towns, and municipalities in […]
full_text: A rendering of a proposed Bears stadium that would be located in Bronzeville at the former site of Michael Reese Hospital that was made public by developers on Nov. 12, 2026. Credit: Inference via Book Club Chicago I get it. Many of you are sick and tired of this ongoing discourse about the Chicago Bears’ new stadium. It’s been years since the project got underway, nearly two years since we were promised shovels would be in the ground soon, and along the way there were several other cities, towns, and municipalities in the Chicago-land area that threw their hat in the ring to house the Bears’ brand-new, state-of-the-art, domed stadium. Yesterday, a new stadium proposal was floated, and while I won’t pretend to have a concrete grasp of the entire situation, I will say that for the first time since this ordeal began, I no longer consider the Arlington Heights location a slam dunk. Chicago developers proposed a $10 billion, 100-acre development plan for the former Michael Reese Hospital site. Yes, the Michael Reese site was previously rejected by the Bears and the NFL, but it’s back in play because this one addresses all the reasons it wasn’t deemed viable before, including the size. From the Chicago Sun-Times: But with Capri Investment Group founder Quintin Primo joining GRIT Chicago, the group of developers and investors led by Farpoint Development that purchased the Michael Reese site, the partners have nearly doubled the size of the proposed Bronzeville Lakefront development. The proposed site also includes a plan for the residents who currently live there. From Book Club Chicago: The portion of the plan that involves the existing Prairie Shores complex — at 2937 S. King Drive — could involve demolishing as many as 1,000 existing apartments, but developers pledged to build 1,500 replacement units. Developers say they would build replacement housing before removing existing units and are proposing tenant protections, including priority access to replacement housing, five years of rent protections and additional assistance for longer-term residents. The new plan also addresses what the Bears should do with the 300+ acres they bought in Arlington Heights. From Book Club Chicago: To further lure the Bears, Capri and its investment partners said they were willing to purchase the team’s Arlington Heights property. It’s “the key impediment to the team staying Downtown and fairly considering Bronzeville,” Primo said. From talking with people who understand the politics and business of this new plan, I get the sense this is actually something worth considering and not a leverage play. For more info, check out the Chicago Sun-Times or Block Club Chicago .
author: Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.

title: Caleb Williams Week 9 QB Grade: Bears vs Buccaneers Film Breakdown
summary: After three consecutive weeks of some of the best football we’ve seen from Caleb Williams, Week 9 appeared to be shaping up as more of the same. For roughly the first quarter and a half, Williams was playing about as well as you could ask of him, and Chicago looked poised for another convincing victory. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks to pass against Rueben Bain Jr. #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images After three consecutive weeks of some of the best football we’ve seen from Caleb Williams, Week 9 appeared to be shaping up as more of the same. For roughly the first quarter and a half, Williams was playing about as well as you could ask of him, and Chicago looked poised for another convincing victory. Instead, what followed was one of the strangest performances of his young career, as Williams threw four interceptions for the first time at any level of football, for periods struggled with accuracy in ways we haven’t seen the early 2025 season, and yet still managed to deliver when the Bears needed him most. Chicago escaped Soldier Field with a 27-24 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, improving to 7-2 and extending its winning streak to four games. Williams finished 22 of 37 for 279 yards, two touchdowns, and four interceptions, resulting in a 61.5 passer rating. But as is often the case with quarterback play, the box score doesn’t tell the entire story, and this week that distinction is particularly important. The Bears couldn’t have asked for a much better start, scoring touchdowns on their opening two possessions, with Williams finding Rome Odunze for a nine-yard score before connecting with Luther Burden III on a 56-yard catch and run. Through roughly the midway point of the second quarter, I had Williams charted with just one off-target aimed throw. He was consistently putting the football where it needed to be, giving his receivers opportunities to make plays and looking every bit like the quarterback who had been carving up defenses over the previous three weeks. Unfortunately, his receivers weren’t always returning the favor. Chicago had already dropped three passes during that stretch, including two by Odunze, one of which looked like it would have put the Bears up 21-3, potentially changing the complexion of the game entirely. Colston Loveland also dropped a ball that would have resulted in a nice gain of roughly 15 yards. These weren’t examples of Williams failing to execute or putting his receivers in difficult positions. He was delivering accurate footballs, but the offense was leaving opportunities on the field. The turning point appeared to come midway through the second quarter, when an unnecessary roughness penalty by Zavion Thomas pushed the Bears back 15 yards from the Tampa Bay goal line. Rather than taking what the defense was giving him, Williams attempted to get all those yards back immediately, forcing a poorly advised throw to Odunze into double coverage that was undercut and intercepted by Tykee Smith. It was a poor decision, plain and simple. Williams was trying to erase a mistake that wasn’t his to begin with, and unfortunately, that interception seemed to be the beginning of a downward spiral. Williams would throw two more interceptions before halftime and another in the third quarter, bringing his total to four on the night. For a quarterback who had never thrown four interceptions in a game before Sunday, not in the NFL, college, or even high school, this was about as uncharacteristic as it gets. But there’s an important distinction I want to make when evaluating those turnovers. Of the four interceptions, only one represented what I would consider a clear breakdown in Williams’ decision-making process. The first was an example of him trying to do too much, forcing the football to a player into coverage that gave no chance at completion. The next two came on attempted throwaways that failed to make it out of the field of play, while the fourth resulted from a deflection on a pass intended for Burden, who also ran a less-than-ideal comeback route on the play. Does that excuse the four interceptions? Absolutely not. A throwaway that ends up in the hands of a defender is an unacceptable result, regardless of the original intention. However, there’s a meaningful difference between a quarterback repeatedly failing to diagnose coverage and one who recognizes that a play isn’t with pressure baring down, but fails to execute. Three of these interceptions weren’t the result of Williams being fooled by the defense or forcing the football into coverage. They were failures of execution, with an unfortunate deflection thrown into the mix. That doesn’t mean his performance was without other serious concerns. In fact, what bothered me most about Williams’ afternoon wasn’t necessarily the interceptions themselves, but the stretch of football he played in the third quarter. This was where we began seeing accuracy issues that have been largely absent from his game in 2026. There was a sequence of six throws in which I graded four as “Below Average” or worse, including two “Poor” throws due to extreme inaccuracy. Williams was missing open receivers and failing to put the football in catchable locations on opportunities we’ve seen him convert consistently throughout the season. His footwork also became increasing erratic, as the Buccaneers began to blitz Caleb Williams repeated, eventual hitting a 68% blitz rate on the evening. Considering the noticeable strides he’s made with his ball placement and overall consistency, it was an unusually shaky stretch from the young quarterback, no doubt aided by the pressure he faced on Sunday Night. However, not all of these mistakes were pressure-induced, and there were opportunities that Williams simply failed to capitalize on. At that point, it was fair to wonder whether the rough outing was going to spiral into an outright disaster. Fortunately, when the fourth quarter arrived, Williams returned to looking like the Iceman we’ve become familiar with. He completed six of seven passes for 72 yards in the final quarter, including three of four on Chicago’s final possession after Tampa Bay tied the game at 24 with just under three minutes remaining. The biggest play came on a 38-yard connection with Loveland down the left sideline, on a perfectly designed play (more on that later) moving the Bears to the Tampa Bay 16-yard line and into comfortable field goal range. Eight plays after the drive began, Cairo Santos connected on a 38-yard field goal as time expired, sending Chicago into its bye week with another victory. After everything that had gone wrong, Williams was still the quarterback who ultimately put his team in position to win. That’s not something I’m willing to overlook. And when all was said and done, since Caleb’s return four weeks ago, the Bears have yet to trail a single second during this four game winning streak. The victory itself produced some remarkable statistical oddities. Chicago managed to score points in all four quarters for the fourth straight game, something done just twice previously in franchise history, while also accomplishing a rather unusual first , becoming the first time in NFL history to win on Thursday night, Monday night, and Sunday night in back to back to back weeks. The Bears also overcame five turnovers to secure the victory, joining some infamous statistical company , becoming just the 4th team since 2016 to overcome that hurdle. These aren’t exactly circumstances you’d want to replicate, but Chicago continues to find ways to win even when things don’t go according to plan. As for Williams, his confidence certainly doesn’t appear shaken , and neither is mine. There are absolutely things to clean up from this performance, particularly the failed throwaways and the uncharacteristic accuracy issues that plagued him in the third quarter. However, one rough outing doesn’t erase the improvements we’ve seen in his accuracy, processing, decision-making, and overall command of Ben Johnson’s offense throughout 2026. If anything, the fact that this performance feels so out of character…

title: Bengals vs. Steelers on SNF carries special meaning for Orlando Brown Jr.
summary: Cincinnati Bengals starting left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. isn’t about to pretend this is just another game. Not with the Pittsburgh Steelers coming to town with first place in the AFC North on the line. Asked whether Sunday’s showdown means more to the Bengals than any other game right now, Brown gave the answer fans […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals starting left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. isn’t about to pretend this is just another game. Not with the Pittsburgh Steelers coming to town with first place in the AFC North on the line. Asked whether Sunday’s showdown means more to the Bengals than any other game right now, Brown gave the answer fans probably wanted to hear. “Hell yeah,” Brown said in a video recently. "I usually don't say this, but I would tell you, hell yeah." Orlando Brown Jr. on if this game means more to the #Bengals right now than any other game. @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/GpZ8Nu6kEa — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) November 11, 2026 Both teams enter Sunday night’s matchup at Paycor Stadium with 6-2 records. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, giving the Bengals a national stage and a home crowd for a game with immediate consequences atop the division. For Brown, the opportunity extends beyond the players taking the field. He wants Cincinnati’s fans to experience the kind of meaningful football that makes a stadium feel different from kickoff to final gun. “I’m really excited for the City of Cincinnati,” Brown said. “Our fans deserve the opportunity to be able to pay to go to games like this and to be able to suit up in front of them with everything at stake on Sunday, and I’m looking forward to it.” That is a welcome departure from the familiar insistence that every opponent presents the same challenge, and every Sunday carries the same weight. Players can prepare with the same discipline each week while acknowledging that some games simply mean more. “I feel like we play with a chip on our shoulder for a lot of different reasons, but to tell you that this game means more to us, I normally don’t say this, but I would say, ‘hell yeah,’” Brown said. Brown’s challenge now is to help turn those words into the protection Joe Burrow needs. The Bengals will need their left tackle, along with the rest of the offensive line, to give the offense time to operate. Enthusiasm matters, but execution will decide whether Cincinnati ends the night celebrating. An unnecessary penalty, a missed assignment, or a stalled possession can quickly overwhelm whatever energy a team brings out of the tunnel. Still, there is something refreshing about hearing a veteran acknowledge the moment without trying to shrink from it. Brown understands the opponent, the opportunity, and what a win would mean to the people filling the stands.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
summary: The 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals will host the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football this week. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier this season in Pittsburgh. Can Cincinnati return the favor and take the lead in the AFC North standings? If they are going to do so, here are three keys to victory. Contain […]
full_text: The 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals will host the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football this week. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier this season in Pittsburgh. Can Cincinnati return the favor and take the lead in the AFC North standings? If they are going to do so, here are three keys to victory. Contain Jaylen Warren Jaylen Warren has been playing really well for the Steelers this season. He was a huge reason they were able to get the victory earlier this season against the Bengals. He had almost 170 all-purpose yards during that game. He does damage where the Bengals often struggle against the run, and that is to the outside. He is also an effective pass catcher who can make huge chunk plays out of the backfield. It will be a group effort to limit Jaylen Warren this week. That starts with the guys up front setting a good edge and forcing Warren to go back inside. Once that happens, they will need the linebackers and secondary players to make the tackle. Warren is elusive, shows good leg drive, and is critical for the success of the Pittsburgh offense. Slowing him down will be one of the biggest keys to earning a tough divisional victory on Sunday night. Effective running from Chase Brown Chase Brown ran for over six yards per carry on Sunday against the Falcons. While he has yet to top 100 yards rushing in a game this season, he is starting to be much more effective when his number is called. Last season, when the Bengals faced off against the Steelers at home, Chase Brown had just 11 carries. Even though he had just 11 carries, he was still able to top 100 yards rushing. You don’t have to change your identity, but running effectively will be a big key on Sunday night. Earlier this season against Pittsburgh, Brown ran for 61 yards on 13 carries. One thing that would certainly help the numbers in the running game would be to play with a lead. Getting an early lead and being able to effectively run the football will go a long way toward trying to get the victory and taking the lead in the division at 7-2. Protect the football When the Bengals played the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this season, they had two crucial turnovers that cost them the game. The first turnover was a muffed punt by Ke’Shawn Williams. Not only did Williams muff the punt, but PJ Jules tried to pick the football up instead of just jumping on it. That muffed punt came with the Bengals leading 27-24 early in the fourth quarter. The Steelers recovered the fumble and went on to add a field goal. That tied the game at the time at 27-27. After another Pittsburgh field goal put them up 30-27, the Cincinnati Bengals offense came back on the field with a chance to win the game. The Bengals got the ball with 2:08 left on the clock. After 17-yard and 13-yard completions to Ja’Marr Chase, the Bengals were driving with an opportunity to win the game, or at least send it to overtime. They had the ball at midfield with a first down. This time, Dalton Risner got beat by Derrick Harmon, and Joe Burrow fumbled the ball while looking to get the ball out instead of taking the sack. The Steelers recovered the fumble and won the game 30-27. If the Bengals can win the turnover battle, they should put themselves in a good position to win the football game. With a win, they will be sitting at the top of the division at 7-2. This is a massive matchup on Sunday Night Football in Cincinnati. There should be an electric atmosphere at Paycor Stadium this week.

full_text: Each week for our Browns Reacts results, we have been showing you the fan confidence meter with respect to the direction of the team. Then, the script flipped after the win against the Buccaneers in Week 3, and the momentum continued to build as Deshaun Watson performed better than expected. Things were at a high near when Cleveland defeated their division-rival Baltimore Ravens (after already having beaten the Steelers). However, things are on shakier ground now that Cleveland has lost back-to-back games for the first time this season (to Pittsburgh and New Orleans). As noted above and below, the Browns’ fan confidence took another hit this week, although not a substantial one. Week-to-week, fan confidence decreased by 3 percentage points down to 57%. title: Browns vs. Texans: 2 key matchups to watch on Sunday
summary: The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans on Sunday in a game with actual playoff implications for both teams. The Browns already have three conference […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans on Sunday in a game with actual playoff implications for both teams . Cleveland is currently tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff spot in the AFC, but the Patriots hold the edge with a 5-1 record in the conference. The Browns already have three conference losses, so a fourth one on Sunday would put a major dent in their playoff hopes and also give the Texans the tiebreaker. But if the Browns pick up the win? Then they will enter the bye week with a 45 percent chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator , which means meaningful football will be on the docket for the rest of the season. While much of the focus of Sunday’s game will be on how Cleveland’s offensive line can keep Houston’s pass rush, which comes into the game tied for first in the league with 29 sacks, away from quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has taken a league-high 33 sacks, there are other matchups to watch. Here are two in particular to keep an eye on, according to Pro Football Focus. Houston WR Nico Collins vs. Cleveland CB Denzel Ward Collins is second on the Texans in receptions (28), and first in receiving yards (384) and receiving touchdowns (4). But he hasn’t had an explosive game since early October when he torched the Dallas Cowboys with seven receptions for 118 yards and two touchdowns. Ward, meanwhile, is putting together his standard season of high-level play, which makes for a good matchup, according to PFF : Collins has missed time in 2026 but has been tremendously dynamic as usual when healthy. He’s notched an 82.8 PFF receiving grade along with 2.10 yards per route run, with 2026 marking his fourth straight season with numbers reaching those thresholds. Further, Collins’ 82.4% contested catch rate is the third-best among receivers with 35 or more targets. Ward has starred from the outset this season, earning a 72.0-plus PFF coverage grade in all but one game throughout the year. He’s permitted just 18 catches for 129 yards across 349 coverage snaps, numbers that warrant being a first-team All-Pro through the midway point of 2026. These two standouts haven’t gone head-to-head in a game since the 2023 postseason, although Ward has generally had Collins’ number. Collins has been held to two catches for 53 yards over their three games facing one another, with Ward winning 75% of the reps in terms of being charted as open. Cleveland WR Denzel Boston vs. Houston CB Derek Stingley Jr. Boston came close to his first 100-yard receiving day last week against the New Orleans Saints (six receptions for 98 yards), and leads all rookies in receiving yards (507). Stingley is currently going through a down year, so if Boston can play through his toe injury, this could be an area for the Browns to exploit, according to PFF : Collins vs. Ward is the meeting of two longtime great players, but Boston vs. Stingley represents the next generation of potential showstopping receiver-corner battles. Boston looks like the frontrunner for Offensive Rookie of the Year through the season’s midway point. He’s collected a 70.3 PFF receiving grade while averaging 1.55 yards per route run. Likewise, Boston’s 5.0 yards after the catch per reception sit in the 74th percentile. Like the rest of Houston’s regressing defense, Stingley has had some trouble this season — producing a career-low 65.3 PFF receiving grade with a 92.4 passer rating allowed. Although the All-Pro has let up 65-plus yards in three separate games, he’s also broken up five passes. Boston has dealt with a toe injury in practice but indicated he expects to play on Sunday. That means we should be treated to a physical showdown between the big-frame rookie and one of the game’s top defensive backs over the last few seasons. The Browns have an opportunity on Sunday to go into their bye week on a positive note and come out on the other side with a legitimate chance to stay in the playoff race. title: FAA ground stop could impact Browns vs. Texans, rest of Week 10 in a big way
summary: When it comes to things of importance, sports might be much lower on the totem pole than many of us devoted fans realize or even think about. Friday’s FAA ground stop to all outgoing flights was an example of a real-world issue impacting many people in many ways, but it could also impact the world […]
full_text: When it comes to things of importance, sports might be much lower on the totem pole than many of us devoted fans realize or even think about. Friday’s FAA ground stop to all outgoing flights was an example of a real-world issue impacting many people in many ways, but it could also impact the world of sports. Many college games on Saturday were still up in the air late Friday night into Saturday morning due to the grounding. As flights got back going after 9 PM on Friday, how airlines and systems would prioritize the restart was something important to watch. “Smaller movements will take a lower priority,” with football teams encouraged to contact the FAA to try to get their flights scheduled. The Houston Texans are still in Texas early Saturday morning. While there is unlikely to be an issue with them getting to Cleveland to face the Browns, it is possible that their schedule will be impacted, including the team’s normal Saturday walkthrough. That will likely be true for all visiting teams this week. The bigger impact on the field could come from the officials for the game. Unlike teams, referees do not travel on a specific charter that can be organized with the FAA. College officials have already raised concerns about their officials making it to their destinations: The numbers are staggering : 12,506 flights have been cancelled so far between yesterday and today, per Flight Aware. The number is expected to grow throughout the day. On Saturday morning already, 3,374 flights have been canceled and 1,008 are delayed nationwide, per FlightAware. In the NFL, like college, refs generally have full-time jobs doing other things throughout the week, and most are scheduled to work most or every weekend. While the NFL generally has backup plans, getting enough officials to their right spots might be tough given the above numbers. Visiting teams could be impacted by the FAA ground stop, but all games could see an impact in how many officials are assigned and in what position those officials are assigned on Sunday. Something for fans to remember if/when a big call does or doesn’t go the Browns’ way.

title: Shuffling the Browns offensive line is not the answer
summary: The Cleveland Browns offense has been a work in progress throughout the entire season. New faces across the board, but the one place that was reworked this offseason was the offensive line. Five new starters across the line, two being rookies. The team signed center Elgton Jenkins and guard Zion Johnson, traded for right tackle […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns offense has been a work in progress throughout the entire season. New faces across the board, but the one place that was reworked this offseason was the offensive line. Five new starters across the line, two being rookies. The team signed center Elgton Jenkins and guard Zion Johnson, traded for right tackle Tytus Howard, drafted left tackle Spencer Fano in the 1st round, and right guard Austin Barber in the 3rd round. As a whole, this group was new going into the season. As the season has progressed, it has been highs and lows, including a ton of penalties , but recently the group has been struggling. With the offensive line struggling, many fans are asking for a reshuffle or criticizing general manager Andrew Berry for not doing enough to fix the offensive line, but, overall, the line is fine. The numbers might look bad in terms of the amount of sacks that the group has allowed, but like every situation, context is needed. As a group, they are average. One of the most talked-about players on the line is the right tackle, Howard. The trade addition has struggled this season, but his play hasn’t reached the point of being benched. Dawand Jones would replace him, and his play looked far worse when he got a chance this season. Jenkins has been average, and Johnson has been better than people want to admit. In terms of the rookies, both Fano and Barber have exceeded expectations. Fano has been playing at a high level, despite some struggles. Barber took the starting job from right guard Teven Jenkins and has turned out to be a solid starter. Despite the struggles from individuals, the last thing this group needs is constant reshuffling. The five on the field are the most talented players the roster has to put out there. Much like when Jones was on the field, fans often want to see something different, until that different ends up being worse than the original. The offensive line group is ahead in terms of pass protection, especially when you take into account the number of sacks caused by the quarterbacks, but the run blocking has been inconsistent. The group will be together until the end of the season, barring injury, but overall this is a unit that has been better than last season despite their flaws.

full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are home for the first time in a month on Sunday when they host the Houston Texans. The last time the Browns were in front of the home fans, they defeated the Baltimore Ravens, part of a 5-2 start that had Cleveland sitting in first place in the AFC North. But the Browns are currently riding a two-game losing streak and have into third place in the division. First meeting: The Browns won the first meeting, 34-17, on October 20, 2002. All-time series: Houston leads the all-time series, 8-7. The Browns have won the last two meetings in Cleveland and four in a row in the regular season. Weather: 45 degrees and cloudy, with a 22 percent chance of rain. Winds from the northwest at 12 mph. title: College football draft targets for the Cowboys: Week 11
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still chasing their playoff dream this season, although it is going to be tough to get there. While that is going on, there is no reason not to take a quick peek ahead to the 2027 draft. Here are some players that might be of interest. USC vs. Indiana Indiana returns […]
full_text: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are still chasing their playoff dream this season, although it is going to be tough to get there. While that is going on, there is no reason not to take a quick peek ahead to the 2027 draft. Here are some players that might be of interest. USC vs. Indiana Indiana returns from its bye needing a win to remain in the playoff race, while USC arrives with one of the most talented passing attacks in the Big Ten. The Trojans have two receivers capable of stretching the field and a quarterback whose draft stock continues to rise. That puts Indiana cornerback Jamari Sharpe under the spotlight. On the other side, USC defensive end Kameryn Crawford must create pressure against a Hoosiers line that has protected its quarterback well for much of the season. Indiana: Jamari Sharpe, cornerback Sharpe is a clean outside cornerback who has become one of the leaders of Indiana’s defense. He enters the game with 25 tackles, seven passes defended and an interception this season. He’s consistent and has the talent to keep up on a defense that asks its secondary to understand route combinations and keep the ball in front of it. His best work comes in zone coverage. Sharpe reads the quarterback and recognizes routes developing around him. He also understands when to pass one receiver to a teammate before closing on another. His length helps him challenge the throwing window, while his closing speed allows him to break on the ball without giving every short completion room to become a larger gain. Why The Cowboys Care We live in a world where cornerback is a top draft priority. DaRon Bland has yet to regain the form that made him a valuable starter. Shavon Revel is still trying to build his career. The Cowboys cannot enter another season relying on everything to break correctly for a thin group, and that includes the addition of Joey Porter Jr. Sharpe would give Dallas size, experience and ball awareness on the outside. His comfort in zone coverage would help him contribute early while the coaching staff develops his man technique. He also plays with the physical mindset required to support the run and attack the football, which creates value beyond simply staying close to a receiver. USC: Kameryn Crawford, defensive end Crawford brings the frame teams search for at defensive end. The 6-foot-5, 255-pound junior has long arms and an explosive first step. He can rush from a two-point stance or place his hand on the ground. He has recorded 29 tackles, two sacks and seven quarterback hits this season after producing 5.5 sacks and 10.5 tackles for loss in 2025. His burst creates the initial problem. Crawford can gain ground quickly and threaten the tackle’s outside shoulder. Once the tackle opens the corner, Crawford has the length to keep himself clean and enough flexibility to flatten toward the quarterback. He can also convert speed into power when he builds momentum, driving through a blocker who sets too softly. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas still needs young pass rushers who can grow into larger roles. The defense has produced better pressure in recent weeks, but its long-term edge rotation remains uncertain. Malachi Lawrence has offered useful snaps and Donovan Ezeiruaku is still trying to break through; neither removes the need to keep adding talent at a premium position. Texas vs. LSU Texas heads to Death Valley with major questions along its offensive line. Starting left tackle Trevor Goosby is out for the season, increasing the importance of right tackle Melvin Siani. LSU counters with Princewill Umanmielen, who ranks among the most disruptive edge defenders in the country. LSU can move Umanmielen around the formation, but his opportunities against Siani should provide some of the most useful draft tape for his evaluation. Texas: Melvin Siani, right tackle Siani is a very tall and well built senior who has started all nine games for Texas, including seven at right tackle. He previously started at left tackle for Wake Forest and played on both sides at Temple, giving him more positional experience than most tackles in this class. His movement ability stands out for a player of his size. Siani gains depth quickly in his pass set and mirrors changes of direction. He has enough range to reach defenders in space. In the running game, he is at his best when Texas allows him to move. Why The Cowboys Care Terence Steele’s contract and uneven play make his future at Dallas very sketchy next year, while Tyler Guyton gives fans and coaches optimism that the left tackle position could be resolved. The Cowboys need a player capable of competing on the right side and covering both positions when injuries strike. Siani’s experience at left and right tackle gives him a clear route onto the roster. He could begin as the swing tackle and provide competition for Steele’s position to help coaches evaluate whether it’s time to move on. His ability to move in the running game would also suit the offense. LSU: Princewill Umanmielen, defensive end Umanmielen has become one of the breakout defenders of the 2026 season. He’s recorded 35 tackles, 12 tackles for loss and 8.5 sacks, adding 13 quarterback hits. He has produced at least half a sack in six games and entered November among the national leaders in both sacks and tackles for loss. His athleticism drives the pass rush. Umanmielen accelerates quickly from a wide alignment and has the change of direction to finish when the quarterback steps away from the original pressure. He also uses his hands well enough to avoid being carried beyond the pocket. Why The Cowboys Care Umanmielen fits the Cowboys’ need for a pass rusher who can contribute quickly without requiring a first-round selection. His burst would give Parker a threat from wide alignments, and his experience standing up or playing with a hand down would allow Dallas to move him through different fronts. He would not need to become a full-time run defender immediately. The Cowboys could use him in the rotation and let him attack on third down while he adds strength. That role would give the defense more speed off the edge and reduce its dependence on manufactured pressure.

title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs 49ers
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, two touchdowns and finished with a passer rating of 114.2 . He finished the game with a four-play, 65-yard game winning touchdown drive in just 29 seconds. CeeDee Lamb led the team with another massive performance through the air. He racked up an astonishing 195 receiving yards and one touchdown, also fumbling once on an odd play. Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson finished with a combined 32 carries and 178 yards on the ground. Despite these incredible numbers, the Cowboys offense failed to convert yards into points throughout the day. Held back by turnovers and penalties, it took a fantastic one-handed catch from Ryan Flournoy in the waning moments of the game to sneak out of Indianapolis with a win. DAK PRESCOTT LET IT FLY RYAN FLOURNOY ONE-HANDED CATCH (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/FnxrSX3qbx — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 8, 2026 49ers key stats from last week Brock Purdy and the 49ers finished last week with 232 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception. Purdy also rushed for 40 yards and converted a touchdown with his legs. Kaelon Black outrushed Christian McCaffrey on seven less rushing attempts, finishing with 70 yards. McCaffrey remains this biggest threat, however, finishing with 87 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The 49ers defense limited Las Vegas to just 24 rushing yards on their way to a 38-17 rout of the Silver and Black. They forced three interceptions, including one pick-six. The formula for San Francisco remains the same after all these years – play efficient offense and let the physical defense swing the game. Call an aggressively smart game The Cowboys are going to have to put up points. San Francisco just has too many weapons offensively, especially in the backfield, for this defense to shut them down for 60 minutes. It’s extremely unlikely this turns into a defensive fist fight. With that in mind, this should be the proper week to bust out the gutsy calls. 4th and inches at your own 40? Sounds like a QB sneak to me. Dallas can choose to kick a 57-yard field goal or they can go for it on 4th and 2. This is one time where it’s ok to skip leg day. Send out the offense and attack. Brian Schottenheimer needs to understand what’s at stake here. Nobody expects the Cowboys to win, but a win has the potential to turn this entire season into something meaningful. Call this game like your back is against the wall and your football life is on the line. It’s going to take a gutsy performance from every player and every coach this week if the Cowboys are to stand a chance. What do the numbers mean? The Cowboys are one of the worst rushing defenses in the NFL. The 49ers possess one of the best rushing attacks, utilizing two backs and a scheme where you never know where the ball is going to go. Dallas is also one of the league’s worst third-down defenses while the 49ers convert at a higher rate than almost every team. The 49ers are clearly the better team, especially when looking at their offense against the Cowboys defense. Yet the FanDuel line is only a 4.5 point spread . This tells me that the line setters understand that Dallas has the talent in the building to keep up and win a game against the 49ers. It just takes one week for everything to come together and see an explosion from this Cowboys team. We’ve yet to see it in 2026, however. If Dallas is to stand a chance this week, they’ll need to finally put together a complete performance for the first time this season. They’ll need to play mistake-free football while making the plays on both sides of the ball that they just haven’t done often enough in 2026. And don’t sleep on the special teams performance playing an important role in the field position battle. If the Cowboys put out their best performance on 2026 by playing mistake free football, scoring touchdowns instead of field goals, and winning the turnover differential, I give them a 40-50% chance at winning this game. But from everything we’ve seen, the Cowboys do not play mistake free football. They are unable to consistently get stops on defense, especially against good teams with good rushing attacks. This team has also played several games where the offense has struggled to put points on the board. To top it off, the head coach has made far too many questionable decisions that have directly impacted the results of these games. The Cowboys are the ultimate wild card this week. Put it all together and have a chance to steal a tough win. Play the same brand of football we’ve seen far too often this season, and this could be a multiple score loss. This is the game that determines the team they’ll be the rest of the season.

title: Cowboys aggressiveness on offense must be turned up vs. 49ers
summary: After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. They are the Bills, 49ers, Lions, and Bengals tied for first, the Cowboys in second, and the Jaguars and Rams in third just ahead of the Patriots and Chiefs. Also among these teams, the 49ers, Lions, and Bills are in the top five for fewest third downs faced per game. The Patriots, Chiefs, Jags, and Bengals are all virtually tied with the Bills to round out the top nine. Then there are the 14th ranked Cowboys, much closer to teams like the Steelers, Texans, and Browns – none of which have the QB situation Dallas does that should be keeping them out of this not-so-great company. This is a main culprit why they feel like outliers on the elite, scary, or explosive list while the other offenses are much more deserving. For even more evidence that the Cowboys offense is all about Dak right now, and that Prescott should be getting way more help than he is from all directions, there’s the fact two of the three touchdown drives last week at the Colts came in two minute situations before halftime and at the end of the game. The Cowboys need much more than just Prescott to be at their absolute best against the 49ers, but fairly or not will also need #4 to be among the players that elevates their game this week as well. The best path towards doing so is much more early down aggressiveness and the Cowboys embracing what they do best by throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb, and hopefully George Pickens, not just on third down, but all the time. Without Jake Ferguson for this game, one of the things the Cowboys are going to have an incredibly difficult time doing is persuading the 49ers defense out of loading the box. They don’t have the middle of the field threat to get behind these stacked looks, especially considering the freakish coverage ability to all parts of the field from Fred Warner. Dallas will still need to find it’s times to run the ball and doing so well on early downs would also be huge, but staying in spread looks and letting Prescott make the right decision should be their bread and butter. The 49ers use motion on 71.5% of their offensive plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL. The Cowboys have allowed +0.11 EPA per play against motion, LAST in the NFL. @DLLS_Cowboys pic.twitter.com/Gq8Gr9vUrg — John Andersen (@AndersenJA) November 11, 2026 This could also allow them to use some tempo to their advantage, getting to the line quickly to give them time to use motions, something the 49ers offense is going to do a ton of to the Cowboys defense, and Cowboys offense would be wise to try to give it back. On defense, the Cowboys need to do everything they can to limit the vast amount of plays 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan can get to at all times. If Christian McCaffrey is breaking tackles and getting considerable gains on first downs all game, the 49ers are simply too talented and well-coached to be stopped. They will toy with Christian Parker’s defense when ahead of the chains with short, intermediate, and deep layered passes. There’s also the element of Brock Purdy’s effectiveness scrambling outside of the pocket, another area Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark will have to step up in pushing the pocket and keeping contain. A complete game in both run and pass defense from the Cowboys front will give them a chance to replicate what the Atlanta Falcons did to the 49ers as the only team to beat them this season. How often QBs have had perfectly blocked plays and their EPA on those plays pic.twitter.com/Erv2iR2BIO — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 11, 2026 The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the San Francisco 49ers if… …they are horribly outcoached. Even though the disparity in records is obvious in this game between the 7-1 49ers and 4-5 Cowboys, if the game was going to solely be decided by the players on the field, I think many fans on both sides would be expecting a much closer game than they currently are. The biggest gripe from Cowboys fans when it comes to things they’re not looking forward to the most about this toughest game of the season to date is how likely it feels the 49ers coaching staff will run laps around the Cowboys staff, and separate even more on the scoreboard as a result of it. Play Caller Tendencies 🎮 The NFC North is the only division where every offensive play caller has a positive rating. The AFC North, AFC East, and NFC West are close behind, each with at least three play callers in positive territory. pic.twitter.com/kmd5AduJDw — Steven Patton (@PattonAnalytics) November 11, 2026 This chart shows that Schottenheimer is lacking creativity in his offensive formations/plays, while Shanahan is uplifting the 49ers with his usual masterclass at taking a roster hammered by injuries and still finding a way to win. The Cowboys have already lost to four of the coaches that presently rank above Schottenheimer on this chart, play the 49ers this Sunday, then still have to play the Jaguars and Seahawks in December. The only win for Schotty against a coach above him on this list is the one directly above him by the smallest of margins, Nick Caley with the Texans. The Cowboys are finding themselves outcoached all too often right now. The Cowboys have the talent to compete with this 49ers team, and they have everything left to play for in the NFC East. If they come out and continue to have communication issues on both sides of the ball, call plays like they’re playing to not lose instead of playing to win, and shoot themselves in the foot with egregious penalties, it will be all most fans need to see that this season is doomed to look like year one under Schottenheimer and fall short of the playoffs again. A Cowboys head coach that’s had the chance to work with a healthy Dak Prescott has never had as little success as Schottenheimer is now, and Prescott has not beaten the 49ers since being with the coach that drafted him Jason Garrett in 2017. The chance for this QB-HC duo to have a real signature moment is right there for the taking in week ten if the Cowboys play their best game of the season, a challenge the Dallas coaching staff needs to rise to instead of wilting under the pressure of.

title: Cowboys vs. 49ers: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 10
summary: The Week 10 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers is an opportunity for the Dallas Cowboys to prove they are a better team than the way they have played through the first half of the 2026 NFL season. With the way things have played out thus far, and due to the fact the NFC East […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images The Week 10 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers is an opportunity for the Dallas Cowboys to prove they are a better team than the way they have played through the first half of the 2026 NFL season. With the way things have played out thus far, and due to the fact the NFC East division is completely wide-open, Dallas can once again really get into the playoff chase. It seems far-fetched to believe the Cowboys can still turn things around so much, but that’s exactly what’s at stake in Week 10. If they can upset the San Francisco 49ers, arguably one of the best teams in the league this year, they could potentially rewrite their season. To do so though the need to make some impact, game-changing plays. Offense – WR Ryan Flournoy Ryan Flournoy may not have led the Cowboys in receiving yards last week against the Indianapolis Colts, but he did make arguably the most impactful play of the game. With 97 seconds left on the clock in the fourth quarter, QB Dak Prescott heaved the ball downfield hooking up with No. 19, who made a one-handed grab with All-Pro CB Sauce Gardener draped all over him. That reception was pivotal in Dallas regaining the lead. Like last week, we fully expect No. 19 to make a big impact in the Week 10 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers. With George Pickens limited all week with a hamstring injury, he’ll likely be a gametime decision. Even if he does end up playing he probably won’t be at 100%. That should give Flournoy ample opportunity to make plays, especially considering the 49ers will focus the majority of their attention on limiting CeeDee Lamb’s production. Defense – DB Caleb Downs Caleb Downs is looking to repeat the success he had last week against the Indianapolis Colts in this Week 10 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers. Last week was arguably the best game of his young career. He not only recorded his second QB sack of the season, but also end up sealing the victory for the Cowboys with a game-clinching interception. There’s good reason to believe he can be just as impactful in back-to-back weeks. The 49ers are one of the best offensive units the Cowboys defense has faced up to this point this season. Dallas hasn’t had to matchup with a group of talented playmakers thus far this season like they will Sunday afternoon against San Francisco. Due to his versatility to play all over the field, No. 13 should be in the mix of things throughout the ballgame. He’ll need to be just as impactful as last week, if not more so, to give Dallas a chance. Who is your biggest impact player for this week?

title: Young Cowboys linebacker has taken advantage of opportunities
summary: There have been very few bright spots for the Dallas Cowboys in 2026. With the defense struggling for the second-straight year and the Cowboys offense having more bumps than we’re used to seeing, Dallas fans are gearing up for yet another disappointing season. One of the few unheralded bright spots for the Cowboys defense this […]
full_text: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images There have been very few bright spots for the Dallas Cowboys in 2026. With the defense struggling for the second-straight year and the Cowboys offense having more bumps than we’re used to seeing, Dallas fans are gearing up for yet another disappointing season. One of the few unheralded bright spots for the Cowboys defense this season has been second-year linebacker Shemar James. James played quite a bit as a rookie under Matt Eberflus, but was viewed as more of a role-player and special teamer, but since being named a starter and given the green-dot two weeks ago, James has been one of the better players on defense for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys. With Dee Winters and DeMarvion Overshown battling injuries in the first part of the season, James was thrown into a heavier role in Christian Parker’s defense. After performing well during his uptick in snaps, Parker handed James the green-dot role for the Cowboys defense and through two weeks he’s handled that responsibility well for a young player. In the last two weeks, James has registered 14 tackles, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one interception. James, a smaller-built linebacker, is not quite the force against the run as a player like Jaishawn Barham, but his ability to play on all three-downs and his understanding in coverage has been a nice boost for the Cowboys defense that has struggled mightily through their first nine games. James is by no means on his way to making the Pro Bowl or receiving All Pro votes, but the Cowboys have really struggled to hit on day three picks in recent drafts. With James proving to be a solid player on defense, and his play earning him more playing time and responsibility on defense, the Cowboys may have found an impactful player on day three of the draft. It’s still early and it’s been limited action, but the early returns in year two for James is one of the rare bright spots for the Cowboys defense in recent memory. James will have his hands full this Sunday with a difficult San Francisco 49ers offense coming to town, but his impact was felt on the field against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, and we will see if he can carry the momentum into Week 10.
author: Connor Livesay

title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 3 causes for concern in Week 10
summary: After a win over the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys face a much tougher task this week, hosting the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. San Francisco has been, without a doubt, one of, if not the best team in the league nine weeks into the regular season. The Cowboys have plenty to be worried […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Strazzante/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) After a win over the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys face a much tougher task this week, hosting the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. San Francisco has been, without a doubt, one of, if not the best team in the league nine weeks into the regular season. The Cowboys have plenty to be worried about in this matchup. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Week 10. 1) 49ers Rushing Attack If you don’t stop the run, you are going to have a hard time beating the 49ers. Led by All-Pro Christian McCaffrey, the 49ers have once again been one of the best running teams in football this year. San Fran has recorded 125 or more team rushing yards in five of their eight games and ranks seventh in rushing Y/A (4.6) and third in rush EPA (-0.001), while leading the league in rush success rate (49.5). One big reason for San Francisco’s success on the ground has been the emergence of rookie running back Kaelon Black. The 49ers spent a third-round pick on Black, hoping he could share the load with McCaffrey and keep the star runner healthy throughout the entire regular season. So far, the plan has worked to perfection. McCaffrey, who has played in all eight games this season, has scored the second-most (9) rushing touchdowns in the league on just 102 rushing attempts. Both he and Black are averaging 4.5 Y/A with rush success rates of 55% or higher. The duo has worked out about as well as the 49ers could have imagined, and their run game is performing about as well as any in the league. If the Cowboys want any chance of staying in this game, their top priority needs to be winning on first and second down and keeping San Francisco’s run game from getting going. 2) San Francisco’s League-Best Run Defense Another thing the 49ers do better than any team in the league this season is limit the opposing team’s success on the ground. San Francisco leads the league in defensive rush EPA (-0.215) and Y/A allowed (3.3). The 49ers have not given up 100 rushing yards in a game since their Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, when they surrendered just 102. The 49ers have been dominant at stopping the run all season, but their last three games in particular have been as good as it gets in that department. San Francisco has allowed an average of just 53 rushing yards over those three games, along with a remarkable – 0.290 defensive rush EPA and a 34.9% rush SR . When the Cowboys’ offense has lacked balance this season, they’ve struggled. It’s going to be extremely hard for Dallas’ offense to play complementary football on Sunday against this San Francisco run defense. If the 49ers continue their trench dominance, it may be a long afternoon for the Cowboys. 3) The Kyle Shanahan Problem Few people give the Dallas Cowboys more headaches than Kyle Shanahan. The veteran head coach has been a thorn in Dallas’ side for years, with his 49ers dominating the matchup between the two teams for quite some time. Shanahan’s 49ers have won four of their last six matchups (including the playoffs) against the Cowboys, averaging 26 points per game. Dallas has not beaten a Shanahan-led 49ers team since December 2020, when they won a fairly meaningless game late in the regular season. Until we see it happen, it’s hard to have any confidence that the Cowboys can truly compete with Shanahan and the 49ers. Let’s hope the one-sided rivalry flips on its head come Sunday afternoon.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys vs. 49ers: Matchups to watch in Week 10
summary: This week’s matchup between the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys and the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers is an important one for the Cowboys playoff hopes. The Cowboys are clearly the underdog after struggling to find any kind of consistency as a team this season, making the 49ers the clear favorite to walk away the victors. For Dallas […]
full_text: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images | Getty Images This week’s matchup between the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys and the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers is an important one for the Cowboys playoff hopes. The Cowboys are clearly the underdog after struggling to find any kind of consistency as a team this season, making the 49ers the clear favorite to walk away the victors. For Dallas to pull off the upset they’ll need to be at their best and win certain matchups, which we’ve listed below. Cowboys defense vs. RB Christian McCaffrey If Christian McCaffrey has lost a step at this point in his career it’s a slight one. He’s still one of the better dual-threat running backs in the entire league and is more than capable of impacting the outcome of this Week 10 matchup with the Cowboys on his own. Dallas will need to neutralize his effectiveness as both a runner and receiver out of the backfield if they want any chance of securing a victory. That’s a lot to ask from a defense that’s allowing 372.7 yards per game (30 th ) and 147.4 rushing yards per game (31 st ) in the league. DB Caleb Downs vs. TE George Kittle Last week’s performance against the Colts was Caleb Downs’ best one thus far in his young career. He was a true difference maker and hopefully that carries over to this week’s matchup against the 49ers. While he may not be solely responsible for limiting TE George Kittle’s production, he could play a large part in neutralizing the impact he has in the game. Kittle is one of San Francisco’s best playmakers and one of their most consistent. A rookie versus a savvy veteran usually favors the latter, but Downs possesses the talent to make it an interesting matchup. DT Quinnen Williams vs. 49ers’ interior OL Quinnen Williams has been a one-man wrecking crew here lately, but may have a tougher time enforcing his will against a very good 49ers offensive line. Pro Football Focus (PFF) currently has them ranked as their top OL, which is a big reason why San Francisco’s offense is one of the better units in the entire league, despite their rash of injuries thus far this season. If Williams continues to dominate, he could disrupt their offense as both a run defender and pass rusher. That could go a long ways in keeping this game close and giving Dallas a chance of victory. What’s the biggest matchup for you in this game? And can the Cowboys win that matchup?

title: Predicting the Denver Broncos record down the stretch
summary: The Denver Broncos reached their bye week with a 7-2 record, which if you had asked most of us before the season we’d would have been overjoyed that they made it through the early season gauntlet with that record. Now comes the ‘easy’ part of their schedule — as easy as easy gets in the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrates a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the fourth quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos reached their bye week with a 7-2 record, which if you had asked most of us before the season we’d would have been overjoyed that they made it through the early season gauntlet with that record. Now comes the ‘easy’ part of their schedule — as easy as easy gets in the NFL anyway. Their remaining schedule is against mostly non-playoff teams with three very important matchups in the final eight games against actual playoff contenders: Week 11: vs. Las Vegas Raiders Week 12: at Pittsburgh Steelers (Black Friday) Week 13: vs. Miami Dolphins Week 14: at New York Jets Week 15: at Las Vegas Raiders Week 16: vs. Buffalo Bills (Christmas Day) Week 17: at New England Patriots Week 18: vs. Los Angeles Chargers Let’s predict every game and see where things land. For me, I think they have to beat the non-playoff teams. So beating the Raiders twice, Dolphins, Jets, and Chargers. That gets them 12 wins on the season. For the final three against playoff teams, I think it could go one of two ways. Either they beat the Steelers or they lose and then they split games against the Bills and Patriots. So either 2-1 or 1-2. I mean looking at it either way, that is yet another possible 14-win season. Hard to imagine given some of the struggles they’ve had early, but they also played some of the best defensive teams in the NFL to start the season. Bo Nix and the offense should have a much easier time on drives moving forward. That is all ‘what if’ subjective. Let me give my final and official prediction for each game: Week 11: vs. Las Vegas Raiders [8-2] Week 12: at Pittsburgh Steelers (Black Friday) [9-2] Week 13: vs. Miami Dolphins [10-2] Week 14: at New York Jets [11-2] Week 15: at Las Vegas Raiders [12-2] Week 16: vs. Buffalo Bills (Christmas Day) [12-3] Week 17: at New England Patriots [13-3] Week 18: vs. Los Angeles Chargers [14-3] Denver will have their 10-game win streak snapped by Josh Allen, but they’ll bounce back and finish strong. I’m not too worried about Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers. He is a statue back there and Denver’s defense is leading the NFL in pressure rate. What say you? Copy pasta the remaining schedule in the comments and let us know how you think the final eight games plays out.
