title: Jaguars vs. Titans: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 10
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re recapping the Jacksonville Jaguars’ moves at the 2026 NFL trade deadline and previewing their Week 10 divisional matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Question 1: What are your thoughts on the Jaguars’ moves at the 2026 trade deadline? Dillon Appleman: I love the moves, and while […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Josh Hines-Allen #41 of the Jacksonville Jaguars reacts during the first quarter against the Tennessee Titans at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re recapping the Jacksonville Jaguars’ moves at the 2026 NFL trade deadline and previewing their Week 10 divisional matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Question 1: What are your thoughts on the Jaguars’ moves at the 2026 trade deadline? Dillon Appleman : I love the moves, and while I understand the outside criticism regarding traditional thoughts on trade value, we know by now that James Gladstone’s roster-building philosophy doesn’t operate within conventional guardrails. Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis don’t just plug the holes left by Eric Murray and DaVon Hamilton; they provide genuine ceiling-raisers for a deep playoff run alongside Davon Godchaux, who adds needed interior depth. In a wide-open AFC, it’s now or never, and I’m fired up that this front office is treating it like “now.” Travis Holmes : The regime consistently claimed that they would be bold. They were hired to be aggressive in that regard while ushering in a new day in Jacksonville. They have certainly been bold, walking the fine line between calculated aggression and recklessness. The trade for Bates was, in my estimation, a franchise-altering move for Anthony Campanile’s defensive scheme. Godchaux providing additional interior defensive line depth for the low cost of a 2028 sixth is the cherry on top of what was already a fantastic class, headlined by the clear jewel, Davis. Personally, I loved the bold moves. Getting value back in trades is great when you’re already a perennial powerhouse. You know what’s even cooler, though? Becoming a powerhouse in the first place. Gus Logue : I had the same reaction to the draft-day trade for Travis Hunter. Was it an overpay on paper? Sure. Can I guarantee that the acquired player(s) will ball out for Jacksonville? No way. In both cases, Gladstone took a major risk — but it comes with massive upside. The Jaguars could have the NFL’s most valuable non-quarterback, and now, maybe the first pro sports championship in Duval County. This franchise has been in the gutter for most of my life, but I don’t want them to just aim for ground level. Kudos to the Jaguars for shooting for the stars. Henry Zimmer : The Jaguars went all in, and it makes sense. James Gladstone comes from the Les Sneed tree of not valuing draft capital if it means hanging a banner. And banners hang forever. The Jags took big swings but paid a solid price, so now they have to make good on those deals and win the whole thing. Question 2: Are you ready to set Super Bowl expectations for the Jaguars? Dillon : Not quite. As much as I’d love to let expectations fly with how dominant this team looks, I’m keeping both feet on the ground for now. After last year’s disappointing Wild Card exit, I need to see this group prove they can sustain this level of execution on the postseason stage before I’m ready to stamp them with Super Bowl expectations. Travis : You don’t have to get ready if you stay ready. Some of us have been waiting for the day when we could finally set those expectations for the Jacksonville Jaguars organization. The literal night of the Jaguars’ playoff comeback against the Chargers, I stated the second-half victory would set the franchise back another two to three years by holding onto Trent Baalke and Doug Pederson, despite the fact that it seemed clear neither was forward-thinking in the way necessary to succeed in today’s NFL. The goal was always Super Bowl or bust, in my mind. The 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars have finally joined the rest of the modern NFL. Hell yeah. Gus : While it’s inaccurate to say Jacksonville went “all in” at the trade deadline, their moves were certainly in the “win now” category. They recognize the opportunity that lies ahead. I understand that some scarred Jaguars fans will be wary of setting expectations too high — and it’s wiser to enjoy the present path than overthink the destination — but I also think it’d be healthy for us to start talking about the Big Game. I don’t want to reach the AFC Championship and still be thinking, “I don’t know, do they really have what it takes?” The Jags aren’t all in on this one season… but I am. Henry : Whether we like it or not, by way of the trade deadline, you have to set Super Bowl expectations for Jacksonville. I worry a bit that this has gone a step too far and the Jags are not really the Super Bowl stratosphere but we have to expect them to be of that class. One home playoff game later and here we are! Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week against the Titans ? Dillon : My X-factor this week is Parker Washington. Despite some big plays here and there, Washington has been held to under 5 receptions in five of his last six games. While much of that quiet stretch comes down to Jacksonville’s deep stable of pass catchers and a thriving ground game, Washington has also left a few plays on the field recently. Against a vulnerable Titans secondary, I’m betting he breaks out for another signature performance that has Duval tweeting “PAY THE MAN” on Sunday. Travis : A.J. Brown? Derrick Henry? Jeffery Simmons? For a scrappy Tennessee Titans team that is clearly a shell of its former self, this one ultimately comes down to quarterback Cam Ward’s ability to extend plays and find the open receiver early and on time. This Titans offense is clearly hitting its stride, scoring 24, 26, and 36 points over the past three weeks of regulation. Over that three-game stretch, Cam is averaging just 196 yards per game with 1 touchdown and 1 turnover in each matchup, and a 61% completion rate. However, his ability to extend plays while scrambling has been invaluable in keeping this Titans passing offense on schedule and on the field over the past three weeks. Gus : Bates and Davis are taking a personal bye week against the Titans. (They didn’t have a bye week this season with their former teams, and the Jaguars already had theirs, so the team is choosing to rest them this week.) The defensive tackle position should be okay with Godchaux getting added to the rotation, but at safety, Rayuan Lane III will have to hold up as a secondary starter for one more week. Can the Navy man add another takeaway to his resume before Bates replaces him? Henry : The X-Factor on Sunday will be Quinn Ewers. How many passes can Ewers end up throwing if the real Jacksonville offense plays well? Do we live in a world where Cam Ward plays the whole game, and Ewers plays garbage time in the late third or fourth quarters, yet they have comparable stats? I think we do. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Travis : Jaguars 38, Titans 17 Gus : Jaguars 30, Titans 13 Henry : Jaguars 35, Titans 6 What are your Week 10 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! title: New Jaguars Safety Jessie Bates: ‘This Group Is Really Special Already’
summary: Jessie Bates got news around 1:30 in the morning that would change his life forever. That news was that he was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Bates, Jacksonville’s first trade deadline acquisition of three this week, spoke to the Jacksonville media for the first time Thursday about what’s transpired in his life since being traded […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Montaric Brown (1) talks with Jacksonville Jaguars newly acquired safety Jessie Bates III (0), during Jacksonville Jaguars practice Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at the Miller Electric Center in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jessie Bates got news around 1:30 in the morning that would change his life forever. That news was that he was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Bates, Jacksonville’s first trade deadline acquisition of three this week , spoke to the Jacksonville media for the first time Thursday about what’s transpired in his life since being traded from the Falcons to Duval County. It’s been unsurprisingly a whirlwind but one both Bates and Jaguars fans can be extremely excited about. “Just a lot of emotions,” Bates said. “Very excited for what the future holds… I didn’t go to sleep because I was so excited.” The way Bates learned of his trade was about as unconventional as it could get. He was on Atlanta’s team plane ride back over from playing in Spain when he learned he had been traded to Jacksonville. At that point it was already around 1:30 a.m., so Bates just stayed up. And got to tweeting. WOKE UP A JAGUAR! #DUUUVAL — Jessie Bates III (@jlbiii3) November 9, 2026 Sleeping seems to be something Bates has put on the back burner since being traded, as he lamented he’s gotten around five hours of sleep (potentially total) since his Monday trade. On Thursday, defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile joked that Bates was living in the facility. The new safety said that while he’s actually staying in a hotel with his family, he’s basically living at the team buildings. “I have been staying the night here just getting caught up on installs and figuring my way about (the Jaguar facilities),” Bates said. “It’s been a blessing. A great problem to have for sure.” The three-time All-Pro spoke highly of his coaches, who in turn have spoken highly of him. Bates said of head coach Liam Coen that his energy at midweek 8 a.m. team meetings matches what he expects the energy on Sunday to look like. It’s that energy that builds championship-caliber programs in Bates’ eyes. “The urgency,” Bates said of Coen’s delivery. “How clear the message is. Who we want to be and the clear identity. Every day has to be a gameday mindset and process.” On Campanile, Bates might have found someone who sleeps less than he does. “He was ready to install (when Bates first arrived),” Bates said. “When you have leaders like that, it’s easy to play for a guy like that. You can tell why they are having a lot of success.” When the defensive coordinator talked about his new weapon, he spoke mostly about how much he respects Bates as a person. Much can be said about Bates’ ability to take the ball away but the way he carries himself goes just as far. That seems to not be lost on Bates who said his value to Jacksonville is equal parts on the field as it is off the field. “I take pride in not just being a great football player, but a great person,” Bates said. “(And) being a great light in the building.” Every good team needs a collection of savvy veterans and hungry young players. Bates slots right in the middle as a 29-year-old who’s been in the league since 2018. He’s not too old just yet, but wise enough to realize he needs to be a vocal leader to help Jacksonville reach the Super Bowl, which it sold many assets to potentially reach. “Every good team has great vets, but great young guys who are open to learn,” Bates said. “I take pride in making sure guys around me are ready. I think that goes a long way.” One way Bates can teach is by sharing his own Super Bowl experience with the Jaguars. Bates was on the Cincinnati Bengals when they made it to the big game in 2022, losing to the Los Angeles Rams by a field goal. Bates finished fourth on the Bengals with six tackles while also picking off quarterback Matthew Stafford. Former Bengals FS Jessie Bates making a timely interception in Super Bowl 56 to keep the Rams from scoring right before the half. Bates is a top __________ safety in the NFL? pic.twitter.com/tcvyzjmcLE — 𝙁𝙖𝙡𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙨 𝙈𝙪𝙨𝙚 (@ATLFalconsMuse) July 10, 2023 Bates has made plays on the biggest stage football has to offer. But he didn’t earn a ring. This time around he thinks he has the group to repeat Cincy’s success and maybe even win the damn thing. “This group is very special already,” Bates said. “I’m happy to be a part of it and to continue to build on what they’re already doing. When you talk about getting in those later playoff games, what matters is what we’re doing right now. That stuff translates. You have to prepare the same. Once you create that habit, it becomes who you are.” The first look at Bates could easily be Sunday against the Titans. Part of the reason Bates has been camping out at the team facility is that he wants to play right away. Despite this being a new team, football’s coverage concepts don’t change. The game itself stays the same. Bates thinks his years in the league have prepared him for this moment and allow him to have a leg up on playing this weekend. “Once you learn coverages conceptually you can understand what they’re doing over here,” Bates said. “It’s just different terminology. It’s a good problem to have. I feel like I’m ready. I’ve stayed in the building just to make sure I’m prepared and the guys can trust me and I can go out there and do my job at a high level.” The safety joked his learning is harder than that of fellow trade deadline pickups Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis. A safety has to know the whole defense and where everyone is going, including the guys on offense. Coach Camp spoke of Bates’ cerebral playing nature and Bates basically confirmed he’s smart enough for the challenge of learning a different defensive scheme while also being able to share his wisdom with younger players. “As a safety, it’s very important you understand the details,” Bates said. “That’s what makes defenses special. I’m happy to share my knowledge, my experiences with the young guys in the locker room.” One of those younger players Jacksonville hopes to benefit from Bates’ wisdom is Travis Hunter, who is now a locker mate with Bates. It might not be long before those two take the field together, potentially as early as Sunday in Nashville. Sleep or not, the Wake Forest product wants to play and wants to win. Good luck to Campanile and Coen on trying to stop him from reaching that. “I’m ready. I’m ready for sure,” Bates said.

title: Chiefs-Falcons: 5 Things to Watch in Week 10 matchup
summary: It’s hard to believe Week 10 is here already, but time flies in the NFL! The Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) will play the Atlanta Falcons (3-6) on the road this week in an interconference duel. The game kicks off at noon Arrowhead time from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta and will be broadcast on CBS. The […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to believe Week 10 is here already, but time flies in the NFL! The Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) will play the Atlanta Falcons (3-6) on the road this week in an interconference duel. The game kicks off at noon Arrowhead time from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta and will be broadcast on CBS . The Chiefs defeated the New York Jets last week 35-12 in a blowout at Arrowhead Stadium. During the week, the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts , who will likely make his debut on Sunday. The Atlanta Falcons were defeated 34-17 by the Cincinnati Bengals at home last week, falling to last place in the NFC South. During the week, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for draft picks. These teams are on opposite ends of the competitiveness spectrum, but they still have to tee it up on Sunday. Here are five things to watch : 1. Josh Downs’ Chiefs debut A former third-round pick out of North Carolina, Downs has accumulated 2,494 yards and 12 touchdowns through his career. At 5 feet 9 inches tall and 171 pounds, Downs relies on quick feet and good route running to win snaps against one-on-one coverage. Since Tyquan Thornton’s ankle dislocation in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders , the Chiefs haven’t found a player who can stretch the field deep and take the top off the defense. Downs has the speed and ball-tracking ability to fill this role. It will be interesting to see how the Chiefs plan to use him this week, but I would expect them to get him involved early and often. Josh Downs 91.0 grade vs Man Coverage 1.71 Seperation Score 34.0 % First Read Target Share vs Man T10 in yards vs Man this year pic.twitter.com/Iwh115QDRl — #babyglitch (@Cxmxthzine) November 10, 2026 2. Who is the punt returner ? The corresponding move to the Downs trade was releasing return man Nikko Remigio. Many thought Remigio would make it back to the practice squad, but a day later the Houston Texans signed him, effectively ending his four-year tenure in Kansas City. Beyond his ability to return punts and kicks, Remigio provided little value to the Chiefs’ offense, but special teams coordinator Dave Toub suggested the team could turn to its crop of young offensive talent to take over the return game during his press conference on Thursday. Coach Toub mentions Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen and Emmett Johnson as options at punt returner moving forward. — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) November 12, 2026 Johnson and Allen have both had shots at returning kickoffs this season, while Worthy has yet to return a kickoff and has returned only one punt. Among the players mentioned by Toub, Downs has the most experience returning punts, with 32 career returns through four seasons. “He’s got 80 reps back there as a punt returner in his career since 2023,” Toub said. “So he’s lined up back there a lot. He’s a good catcher. I went through every one of them. He’s dynamic at times when he gets out. Here's a quick look at new Chiefs' WR Josh Downs at today's practice. Participated in the WR and punt return drills during the media viewing portion of practice. #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/CD330TXhgB — Mark Poulose (@MarkPoulose) November 12, 2026 While Remigio was often reliable and secure with the ball, his lack of involvement elsewhere on the team likely led to his release, as the Chiefs also needed to give younger players chances to get involved. Hopefully, this decision wasn’t made without careful consideration, because punt-return snafus can decide football games. 3. Stopping Bijan Robinson This week, the Chiefs will face the task of stopping the league’s leading rusher, Bijan Robinson. With 880 rushing yards so far this season, five touchdowns, and an average of 5.2 yards per carry — fourth in the NFL — the Falcons’ running back is on pace for well over 1,000 yards for the third straight season. Robinson could be a leading candidate for NFL Offensive Player of the Year — in competition with Kenneth Walker — so the front seven will need to bring their A-game this week. As it stands, the Chiefs defense ranks seventh in the NFL in rushing yards allowed, with only 780 total and 3.6 yards per carry, tied for fifth in the league. Last week, the Chiefs defense gave up some pops early to the Jets’ Braelon Allen and Breece Hall, but locked in in the second half. Bijan Robinson reached a top speed of 21.78 mph on his 59-yard TD run, the second-fastest speed by a ball carrier this season and the second-fastest of Robinson's career. @ATLvsNO | #DirtyBirds pic.twitter.com/Id3snQvOyv — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 6, 2026 This week, the focus will need to be there from the jump, because one wrong move or one slow read and Robinson could be off to the races. 4. Turnover differential This week, the Chiefs will carry a +4 turnover differential, tied for 9th in the NFL. The Falcons are on the opposite end, sitting at a -8 margin, tied for 30th in the league. The Falcons have forced only 9 takeaways so far this season, but have thrown a whopping 12 interceptions — most in the league by a team — and lost five fumbles. FOUR quarterbacks have thrown interceptions this season in Atlanta, with Michael Penix throwing six, with backups Cooper Rush(4), Jack Strand (1), and Tua Tagovailoa(1) contributing as well. Michael Penix Jr. É INTERCEPTADO no final do último quarto! 😱 📺: #CINvsATL – ao vivo no SporTV2 e GE TV pic.twitter.com/wl4EEQc4Ps — NFL Brasil (@NFLBrasil) November 8, 2026 The turnover issues in Atlanta have fallen on their quarterbacks’ shoulders, and their defense hasn’t been able to make up for it. The Chiefs have forced five fumbles and intercepted six passes this year, but offensive efficiency with the ball has been the key. They lead the league in ball security and should be able to do so against the Falcons. 5. Harrison Butker (again) Any other kicker in the NFL would be released by now and planning a post-football career. However, when you have made as many big kicks as Harrison Butker has in his career, leeway is due in the eyes of the Chiefs coaching staff, even if his performance and production aren’t. Harrison Butker misses back-to-back attempts in similar fashion following a penalty. Chiefs fans boo loudly as they head to halftime pic.twitter.com/F1BfHbIiPT — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 8, 2026 The Chiefs’ long-time kicker missed back-to-back kicks last week, dropping to only 63% for the season, and was showered with jeers by the Arrowhead faithful. This week, Andy Reid and Dave Toub once again stuck with the three-time Super Bowl winner. “He’s going to come through it,” Toub said on Thursday. “I mean, we’re confident that he will. We’re just going to keep practicing him and keep working on little things, and he’s looked good in practice. There’s a reason why he’s still our kicker.” Butker is an Atlanta native and will be kicking in his hometown this week. While he will likely have support in the stands and from the coaching staff, he must perform on the field, or it should be the end of an era in Kansas City.

title: In Week 10’s ‘Reacts’ poll, Chiefs fans are split on AFC West chances
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here. And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook, the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence That’s up 22% […]
full_text: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts , a survey of fans across the NFL. Each week, we send out questions to the most plugged-in Kansas City Chiefs fans. You can see all of the recent survey results here . And be sure to check out FanDuel Sportsbook , the official sportsbook partner of SB Nation. Chiefs fans’ confidence That’s up 22% from a week ago, when we ran the same poll. I guess beating a bad team does that for you. Nothing instills confidence in a team like your team bullying a lesser opponent and stealing their lunch money, which the Chiefs gladly did to the New York Jets last week. The Chiefs have another chance to rebuild fans’ confidence in the team this Sunday when they take on the hapless Atlanta Falcons . We’ll see how quickly new addition wide receiver Josh Downs can get in the mix and start making his presence felt on the field. If so, we may continue to see the fans’ confidence rise if Kansas City can go on a winning streak. Regardless. As long as we can keep winning games, I suspect this confidence number will grow right along with it. Can the Chiefs still win the division? While it’s nowhere near the realm of possibility that Denver drops a couple of games in the coming weeks, their next five games are not exactly a murderer’s row of competition. The Denver Broncos play the Las Vegas Raiders twice, and the New York Jets , the Pittsburgh Steelers , and the Miami Dolphins each once. The Steelers are the one game where I think the other team could give Denver a run for its money. And I have to admit that it feels a little dirty to be in the awkward position of cheering on the Raiders this weekend. But here we are. I have to admit that 50% also feels about right as to whether the Chiefs can win this division. They are by no means a perfect team, but they are good enough that they could win any game they are a part of, and if a team like that gets on a roll, they can be very dangerous. It’s been something that everybody’s been very, very impressed by.” Cousins’ start will come just five days after he was acquired in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. full_text: On Sunday, the (6-2) Kansas City Chiefs are on the road again taking on the (3-6) Atlanta Falcons . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 7-1 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Falcons’ opening drive gained just seven yards before they were forced to punt on their first possession. The Chiefs’ ground-and-pound attack erupted on their first drive, highlighted by a 28-yard run from Kenneth Walker. Walker rushed for 36 yards on the drive, while backup running back Emmett Johnson added 13 yards on a third-and-10 run to move the chains. The drive would end with Harrison Butker drilling a 44-yard field goal to open the scoring. End of first quarter: Chiefs 3, Falcons 0 Second quarter The Falcons opened the quarter at the Chiefs’ 19-yard line. Drake London caught a 15-yard pass to reach the four-yard line. From the pistol formation, Michael Penix Jr. handed the ball to Bijan Robinson, who ran to the right, broke a tackle, and found the end zone for a touchdown. The Chiefs failed to reach the first-down marker on their next possession and were forced to punt the ball back to Atlanta. A 14-yard pick-and-roll pass to Jahan Dotson moved the ball to the Chiefs’ 14-yard line. Bijan Robinson finished the drive by catching a pass from Penix Jr. and scoring his second touchdown of the game. The Chiefs found themselves at midfield with a minute remaining in the quarter. On third-and-three, Rashee Rice ran a comeback route and picked up the first down to keep the drive alive. Mahomes then connected with newly acquired Josh Downs for a 12-yard gain and another first down. The Chiefs managed to put points on the board before halftime as Butker drilled his second field goal of the game, this time from 44 yards out, cutting the Falcons’ lead to eight. End of second quarter: Falcons 14, Chiefs 6 Third quarter Josh Downs hauled in an 18-yard pass on a deep out route, going up to make the catch while keeping both feet in bounds. The reception moved the Chiefs to the Falcons’ 25-yard line. Two plays later, Xavier Watts intercepted Mahomes on a high throw intended for Rashee Rice running a crossing route. The Falcons turned to their running game to drain the clock, alternating between Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson. Another 11-yard run from Bijan Robinson moved Atlanta to the Chiefs’ 11-yard line. Brina Robinson followed it up with a 10-yard run to carry the Falcons into the fourth quarter. End of third quarter: Falcons 14, Chiefs 6 Fourth quarter A toss to Bijan Robinson went untouched into the end zone for his third touchdown of the game, extending Atlanta’s lead. The Chiefs found themselves at their own 48-yard line facing a third-and-five. From the shotgun, Mahomes delivered a strike on a fly route to Jalen Royals, who hauled in the pass for a touchdown to bring the game back within one score. The Falcons reached midfield on their next possession but were stopped at the Chiefs’ 48-yard line and forced to punt. Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 16 yards to move the Chiefs to their own 48-yard line. Downs followed with a 26-yard reception on an out route. Royals then hauled in a 17-yard pass on a deep crossing route to move the Chiefs to the nine-yard line. Mahomes went back to the player who helped get the drive started. Kelce was targeted inside the red zone and came down with the touchdown to bring Kansas City closer. The Chiefs attempted a two-point conversion to tie the game, but the Falcons stopped a screen pass intended for Johnson. Kansas City’s defense came up with a three-and-out on the Falcons’ next possession, giving the Chiefs another opportunity. Atlanta was forced to punt, leaving Kansas City with one timeout and eight seconds remaining before the two-minute warning. The Chiefs crossed midfield after Mahomes connected with Kelce for a 14-yard gain. However, the next play went backward as Mahomes was sacked for an eight-yard loss. The sack put Kansas City in a fourth-and-13 situation with 15 seconds remaining. The Chiefs’ final attempt fell incomplete as Mahomes tried to make a throw while being taken down by the pass rush. Kansas City turned the ball over on downs, ending its comeback attempt. Final score: Falcons 21, Chiefs 19 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 29 for 39 passing, 293 yards, 2 touchdowns, 1 interception, 1 rushing attempt, 7 yards Kenneth Walker: 4 rushing attempts, 40 yards Travis Kelce: 7 receptions, 74 yards, 1 touchdown. Josh Downs: 6 receptions, 84 yards. Rashee Rice: 6 receptions, 41 yards. Jalen Royals: 6 receptions, 82 yards. 1 touchdown Harrison Butker: 2 for 2, long of 44 yards. Michael Penix Jr.: 16 for 22 passing, 171 yards, 1 touchdown, 4 rushing attempts, 16 yards. Bijan Robinson: 16 rushing attempts, 100 yards, 2 touchdowns Kyle Pitts Sr.: 5 receptions, 61 yards. Drake London: 3 receptions, 37 yards. Cameron Thomas: 1 sack Next week, the Chiefs are back home, welcoming the wounded Arizona Cardinals for a noon kickoff. Until then, we will see how it is played out inside the EA Universe.

title: Chiefs-Falcons Week 10 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons, our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons’ pass rush, even if their defense’s other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league’s two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs’ pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week’s game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don’t think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I’ve got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs’ 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That’s the operative phrase: slow him down. He’s coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn’t get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs’ linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City’s run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs’ chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they’ve lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They’ve got the league’s best RB and a streaky young QB– it’s an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they’re more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They’re a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can’t ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons’ offense. I’m excited to see what the Chiefs’ offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I’m keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team’s snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won’t be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn’t traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn’t need a pass to win. He has played 57% of the defensive snaps for Atlanta this season and has four tackles for loss, five quarterback hits. 1.5 sacks and a pass batted down. He has 30 tackles, one for loss, two quarterback hits and a pass defended this year. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. (back) is questionable after missing Wednesday’s practice. The former first-round pick made his season debut last week and played 15 snaps. Rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out . Branch leads Atlanta in punt returns (8) and kick returns (14) with a long of 61 yards on a kickoff return. As a role player on offense, he has 10 catches for 64 yards this season. Linebacker Josh Woods (ankle) is questionable after missing the first practice of the week and being limited on Thursday. This year, Woods has 15 tackles and one tackle for loss while playing 91 total snaps on defense.

title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Special Teams MVP
summary: There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one […]
full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. So far, we’ve awarded: Most Improved Player : DB Chris Roland-Wallace Top Defensive Rookie : CB Mansoor Delane Protector of the Year : RG Trey Smith Top Offensive Rookie : LT Kahlil Benson In this post, we’ll reveal the top special teams player: P Matt Araiza VOTING: Matt Araiza (8), James Winchester (1) On some NFL squads, special teams could feel like an afterthought. In Kansas City, a strong tradition of explosive kick and punt returns has changed the team’s fortunes. The Chiefs have also boasted some of the best kickers and punters in the league over the past 30 years– along with some of the most painful missed field goals in NFL history. Expectations are always high for the third phase in KC, as evidenced by the influence and stature of special teams coordinator Dave Toub. It’s certainly been an up-and-down season (or two, or three) for Uncle Dave’s group, making this a challenging operation to evaluate– or even understand. They’ve got a struggling kicker, a controversial kicker on the practice squad, and have a number of costly penalties seemingly every week. We could choose a special teams player of the year in 2026 via process of elimination. Returner Nikko Remigio has been released Nobody has stood out as a star on coverage ( they’ve been fine) James Winchester is a solid long snapper (but it’s hard to judge his impact on a game) And the kicker is – Harrison Butker. That really only leaves two viable options: Emmett Johnson– who has just started to come on as a kick returner OR punter Matt Araiza, who is statistically among the league leaders at his position this year. Through eight games, Araiza has punted 25 times for 1,270 yards, averaging 50.8 yards per punt. His longest punt of the season is a 69-yard boot, and he’s placed 12 punts inside the 20-yard line. His AFC Special Teams Player of the Week performance came in the Week 4 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. Araiza punted five times, and all five landed inside the 20-yard line– most impressive was the one downed at the Raiders’ 1-yard line by Xavier Nwankpa and Emmett Johnson. But Araiza’s fake punt on the first drive of the game, converting on a 4th and 4 from their own 35, is the play that we’ll all remember (even if the offense did nothing with it, turning it over on downs at the 50). The punter formerly known as “punt god” was known for highlight reel bombs in college. But, Araiza has apparently worked hard to be a complete player at his position. He’s improved his touch and directional kicking, resulting in a career-best yards-per-punt average thus far. Is Araiza the Chiefs’ most valuable special teams player through the first half of the season? Let us know in the comments.
author: Matt Stagner

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Falcons in Week 10
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs got back on track last week with a convincing 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. Now, they will try to build on that performance when they travel to face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon. Kansas City enters the matchup at 6-2, while Atlanta has fallen to 3-6 after consecutive […]
full_text: East Rutherford, NJ October 1, 2023 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Kansas City Chiefs got back on track last week with a convincing 35-12 victory over the New York Jets . Now, they will try to build on that performance when they travel to face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon. Kansas City enters the matchup at 6-2, while Atlanta has fallen to 3-6 after consecutive losses. However, the Falcons remain within striking distance in the NFC South and possess one of the league’s most dangerous offensive players in running back Bijan Robinson. Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory. Offensive key: Make Atlanta respect the wide receivers Atlanta’s defense has struggled to stop the run recently, allowing a league-high 190 rushing yards per game over its last three contests. That makes Kenneth Walker III an obvious focal point for Kansas City after he produced 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns against the Jets. It also means the Falcons should enter the game determined to make someone other than Walker beat them. The Chiefs’ wide receivers must provide that answer. During Kansas City’s 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , its wide receivers combined for only six receptions and 39 yards. The Seahawks crowded the line of scrimmage, slowed Walker and trusted their defensive backs to win their individual matchups. The production improved against the Denver Broncos with Rashee Rice’s return; the group combined for 13 receptions, 90 yards, and one touchdown. Last week against New York, Rice, Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals combined for 13 catches and 115 yards. It was another step forward, but much of the production came after the catch rather than from consistently winning downfield. That is where Kansas City’s newest addition could help. The Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts before the trade deadline. Downs arrives as a target who can create separation and find openings in zone coverage. Downs should not be expected to master the entire offense in a few days, but the Chiefs can give him a defined package of plays. More importantly, Rice, Worthy and the rest of the receiving corps must win when Atlanta commits extra defenders to the run. The goal should be at least 150 combined receiving yards from Kansas City’s wide receivers in a performance that should be able to take advantage of the attention on Walker. Defensive key: Contain Bijan Robinson and force third-and-long There is no mystery surrounding Atlanta’s offensive plan: get the football in Robinson’s hands. Robinson has rushed for a league-leading 880 yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.2 yards per carry. He has also caught 31 passes for 250 yards, giving him 1,130 yards from scrimmage through nine games. Last week against the Cincinnati Bengals , he produced 147 scrimmage yards on 25 touches. With backup Brian Robinson Jr. on the Reserve/Injured list, the Falcons could lean even more on Bijan Robinson. He is not only their primary runner but also a dangerous receiving option who can create mismatches against linebackers. Kansas City’s defense is equipped for the challenge. The Chiefs have allowed 780 rushing yards through eight games — 97.5 yards per contest — and only 3.6 yards per carry. They have also surrendered just two runs of 20 or more yards. The defensive line must control the line of scrimmage without creating cutback lanes, while the linebackers must tackle cleanly in space. Robinson is too talented to expect Kansas City to eliminate him entirely, but the Chiefs cannot allow him to consistently create manageable third downs. Atlanta has converted only 37 of its 106 third-down opportunities, a 34.9% rate. If Kansas City can limit Robinson on early downs and force Michael Penix Jr. into third-and-long, Steve Spagnuolo can turn loose the pass rush that recorded five sacks against the Jets. Keeping Robinson below 100 yards from scrimmage would put the Falcons’ offense in an uncomfortable position and force Penix to carry the game. X-factor: Harrison Butker must make his kicks This week’s X-factor is simple: Harrison Butker must deliver. Butker has converted only 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts this season, a career-low rate of 63.2%. He is just 2-for-8 from at least 50 yards and has missed a field goal in four consecutive games. Over that four-game stretch, he has made only five of his 10 attempts. The Chiefs overcame his missed 51-yard attempt against the Jets because they controlled the second half. They cannot assume they will have the same margin for error on the road against Atlanta. Head coach Andy Reid has made it clear that Butker remains Kansas City’s kicker. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub has also expressed confidence in the veteran, saying the goal is to get one perfect game and begin building a streak from there. That streak needs to begin Sunday. Kansas City does not need Butker to rescue the offense with repeated attempts from beyond 50 yards. It does need him to convert the manageable opportunities he receives. In a road game that could remain close into the fourth quarter, leaving three or four points on the field could change the outcome. The bottom line The Chiefs should be able to run the football against an Atlanta defense that has struggled in recent weeks, but the Falcons will likely load the box and force Kansas City’s wide receivers to prove they can win. Rice, Worthy and the newly acquired Downs must make Atlanta pay for committing extra defenders to Walker. Defensively, Kansas City must contain Robinson on early downs and force Penix to operate in obvious passing situations. On special teams, Butker needs a clean performance that begins rebuilding his confidence. If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they should leave Atlanta with their second consecutive victory and remain firmly in the AFC West race
author: Maurice Elston

title: Is Josh Downs enough to put the Chiefs’ offense over the top?
summary: You know the old adage, “don’t let good be the enemy of great.” It applies to the Kansas City Chiefs’ trade deadline pursuits, and it’s a lesson we could all take to heart at this time of year. A perfect option for the Chiefs did not exist. The New York Jets‘ No. 1 receiver, Garrett Wilson, […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images You know the old adage, “don’t let good be the enemy of great.” It applies to the Kansas City Chiefs ’ trade deadline pursuits, and it’s a lesson we could all take to heart at this time of year. A perfect option for the Chiefs did not exist. The New York Jets ‘ No. 1 receiver, Garrett Wilson, was never going to be traded. The Jacksonville Jaguars are trying to win the Super Bowl, and trading Brian Thomas Jr. in the midst of what should be considered an all-in season never passed the smell test. The Philadelphia Eagles might be tanking for 2026, but that doesn’t mean they’d make Devonta Smith — a player under contract long-term — available for trade. The options were limited. The pickings were slim. General manager Brett Veach made the best move that was available. Wide receiver Josh Downs isn’t a perfect player. He’s roughly the same size as Hollywood Brown. He has not proven to be much of a deep threat in his NFL career. He primarily lines up in the slot, and there’s some redundancy in that regard between him, Rashee Rice, and Xavier Worthy. He’s had a top-10 drop rate among NFL pass catchers this season. These are all reasons Downs was available for a couple of Day 3 picks. They’re also reasons he shouldn’t be viewed as a transformational agent within the Chiefs’ offense. With the limitations, though, come some real positives. Downs is excellent against man coverage, a skill the Chiefs’ wide receiver room has lacked for years . He has real ability to create separation, and he’s been a third-down machine at times. He brings some value as a punt returner. He’s known to be an extremely smart player, and there’s reason to believe he’ll pick up on the offense quicker than someone like Kadarius Toney did in the past. He’s a good wide receiver. He’s a helpful player. He makes the Chiefs better. And, ultimately, that was the goal at this year’s trade deadline. In so many ways, this move was about improving the floor at a position. It seems as though a number of Chiefs fans were instead focused on improving the ceiling. The latter is what you accomplish with an offseason move, not an in-season acquisition. At least not this year at this position. Downs has always seemed like the most logical choice for the Chiefs. He was clearly available; he’s on an expiring contract, and he has the skill to open up the offense on key downs. His ability to beat man coverage and create separation in tight spaces could also help in the red zone, an area this team has struggled more than its fair share in recent seasons. The Chiefs’ offense still lacks a deep threat. Patrick Mahomes’ average depth of target since Tyquan Thornton’s injury has been lower than at any other point in his career. That’s still something that needs to be addressed, and my belief (this is not reporting, but rather pure speculation) is that the Chiefs will look to improve that area of their offense by looking into a reunion with recently waived wide receiver Hollywood Brown. Sources: The #Eagles are waiving WR Marquise “Hollywood” Brown, as both sides agreed it would be beneficial for all involved. Brown had 49 catches for 587 yards and 5 TDs with the #Chiefs last season and is expected to land with a playoff contender. pic.twitter.com/3MGeYJnqpS — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 13, 2026 Another instance of ‘don’t let great be the enemy of good.’ Brown has his limitations, but he can still get downfield and make plays. He had as many receiving yards in this offense last year as Worthy is currently on pace to produce for the Chiefs in 2026. That’s not a bad player to add for zero draft picks and a minimum veteran contract. He would certainly produce more for the offense than either Cyrus Allen or Andrew Armstrong has provided through the first half of the season. This is a good time to mention the Chiefs offense is probably more productive than you think this season. They’re fourth in the NFL in yards per drive and eighth in points per drive. Only 5 teams average more net yards per passing attempt this season, and nobody averages more yards per carry than the Chiefs. They’re also on the fringe of the top 10 in the league in both third-down and red-zone conversions. This is a top 5-10 offense by just about every metric imaginable, and it just added another quality player to the mix. In the past, Veach has settled for scrap-heap additions at the deadline. This was not one of those instances. Downs was the best option available at the team’s biggest position of need. It’s not a home run addition, but it might qualify as a ground-rule double. It’s not perfect. But it’s pretty darn good.
author: Brandon Kiley

full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images On this Red Friday, the NFL Players Association (NFLPA) announced that Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton was named Week 10 Community MVP. Our Week 10 NFLPA #CommunityMVP @_nickbolton2 showed up big for the kids of Kansas City ❤️💛 The @Chiefs linebacker partnered with Harvesters, a regional food bank, to help pack 700 BackSnacks for Kansas City kids facing food insecurity. The BackSnacks will last throughout the… pic.twitter.com/w0CogS17mL — NFLPA (@NFLPA) November 13, 2026 According to the post, the Bolton Empowerment Foundation partnered with Harvesters and packed 700 bags of kid-friendly food to aid Kansas City students facing food insecurity this week. The “BackSnacks” are meant to last throughout the school year, “ensuring students have access to food over the weekends.” This is what Bolton had to say about this week’s action. “Packing BackSnack bags with our volunteers and partners reminded me just how much we can accomplish when we unite around a shared purpose,” Bolton said. “I’m proud of what the Bolton Empowerment Foundation is building in Kansas City. We’re just getting started!” Having experienced food insecurity himself, Bolton understands the importance of ensuring all children have access to nutritious meals outside of school. In honor of Bolton earning the recognition, the NFLPA is donating $10,000 to Bolton’s foundation. Click here to learn more about how to help Bolton’s charitable efforts . As one of this season’s weekly Community MVPs, Bolton is now eligible for the Alan Page Community Award, the highest player honor for outstanding community service awarded by the NFLPA, including an additional $100,000 donation. title: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Brenen Thompson DNP for 2nd consecutive practice
summary: If Mike McDaniel’s offense needs legitimate speed to be at its best, then we never get to see the offense in its fastest state with injuries plaguing the team’s swiftest wideouts. For the second day in a row, wideouts Ladd McConkey and Brenen Thompson did not take the field. McConkey continues to deal with back […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 1: Ladd McConkey #15 of the Los Angeles Chargers stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images If Mike McDaniel’s offense needs legitimate speed to be at its best, then we never get to see the offense in its fastest state with injuries plaguing the team’s swiftest wideouts. For the second day in a row, wideouts Ladd McConkey and Brenen Thompson did not take the field. McConkey continues to deal with back spasms that kept him out of last week’s loss to the Texans and Thompson remains unable to practice despite having already missed the previous six games. title: How will Carson Beck do against Rams on Sunday?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams under Sean McVay are 9-2 against rookie quarterbacks and that could be bad news for Carson Beck and the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. It also could be an awesome opportunity for Beck to show up the Rams and fellow rookie Ty Simpson who will be on the sidelines. If Beck wins, […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams under Sean McVay are 9-2 against rookie quarterbacks and that could be bad news for Carson Beck and the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. It also could be an awesome opportunity for Beck to show up the Rams and fellow rookie Ty Simpson who will be on the sidelines. If Beck wins, then that’d be a great start to a NFL career. If Beck loses against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, then perhaps that was to be expected. We’ll have to tune in on Sunday to see Beck is another win for the Rams against rookie signal callers, or if he earns the tough win. How have rookie QBs fared historically vs. Sean McVay and the Rams? (ramswire) “Historically, rookie quarterbacks have struggled against the Rams. The odds are against Beck to buck that trend; Arizona is a 9.5-point underdog in this game, making the Rams heavy favorites despite being on the road Rookie QB stats vs. Rams since 2017 With McVay as the head coach, the Rams are 9-2 against rookie quarterbacks, according to Stathead . The only two rookies to beat the Rams were Caleb Williams in 2024 and Tua Tagovailoa in 2020. Tagovailoa only threw for 93 yards and one touchdown in that shocking win against Jared Goff and the Rams, while Williams had just 157 yards and a score in the Bears ‘ 24-18 win over Los Angeles in 2024.“ Week 10 picks: Experts predict Rams won’t get upset by Cardinals again (sports.yahoo) “The Los Angeles Rams head into Week 10 battered and bruised , but with a winning record for the first time all season. They’ll also take on an Arizona Cardinals team that upset them in Week 6. A win would help the Rams keep pace for the Wild Card as well as deliver the team’s first divisional win in 2026. It’ll be an interesting showdown given how well the Rams defense performed in Week 9 with Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett finally on the field together, especially given they’ll take on rookie quarterback Carson Beck and a similarly-injured Cardinals offense. Arizona is also without running back Jeremiyah Love and receiver Michael Wilson. The Rams, meanwhile, won’t have Puka Nacua, Davante Adams or Jordan Whittington in this game. NFL experts are not expecting an upset this time around. Los Angeles received all 52 picks across seven major outlets, with no analyst picking the Cardinals.“ Los Angeles Rams Announce Myles Garrett Decision Amid Significant Updates (heavy.com) ““Guys that will be DNPs: Myles Garrett. He’ll be questionable for the game. He’s feeling good. It’s more of just getting him feeling as good as possible. He’s had a really good week, played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that. But we’re being smart with him,” McVay told reporters on November 13. “Steve Avila will be listed as out with his hamstring. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl will both be limited for practice today and listed as questionable. And then, Terrance Ferguson will be out for the game as well.” The most encouraging sign of Garrett’s status for Sunday is that he took the podium to speak with the media to close out the week.“ Rams’ Myles Garrett Among Multiple Questionable Players for Week 10 (sports.yahoo) “Garrett has been on the injury report with a knee ailment, which limited him on both Wednesday and Thursday. Per Rams reporter Stu Jackson , the defensive end is now questionable. In addition to Garrett, cornerback Trent McDuffie and safety Kam Curl are also questionable. McVay did state that he expects Garrett to play and “feels good” about Curl, which may likely lead to both suiting up for the Cardinals matchup. However, McDuffie is more of a worry, and his response over the weekend to working out will determine if he can play.“ Rams’ Myles Garrett expected to play at Arizona despite missing practice (mymotherlode) “Garrett was largely pleased with his performance, in which he played 61.5% of the defensive snaps, apart from needing to build up his endurance and address what he felt was a slow get-off time. “I’m sure Next Gen or PFF or somebody would tell me it wasn’t too bad,” Garrett said. “It felt terrible to me.” McDuffie is dealing with a back injury that forced him to miss the Rams’ third straight win last week, getting them over .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. McVay expressed optimism he would be able to play, provided McDuffie felt good coming out of Friday’s workout. “He was rolling, you know, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday,” McVay said. The ongoing issues with the Rams’ two marquee offseason acquisitions is indicative of their larger injury crisis that has threatened a campaign that began with them as Super Bowl betting favorites. Los Angeles is so beat up that star wide receiver Puka Nacua was placed on injured reserve Thursday to free up a roster spot, a reversal from what McVay had indicated earlier in the week when he cited the limited number of IR slots remaining to be able to bring players back later in the season. “Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces,” said McVay, while adding that nothing has changed with the timeline for Nacua’s return from knee and toe injuries.“ Rams’ $71 million injury nightmare among NFL’s worst (sports.yah00) “The Rams have watched a parade of Pro Bowlers, All-Pros and established starters limp into the training room this season, including Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Garrett, the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year , finally returned in Week 9 after undergoing knee surgery. Meanwhile, Watson is lost for the season , Adams remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, and Nacua is dealing with knee ligament sprains and turf toe. It’s enough to make the Rams’ medical staff consider asking for overtime pay. Believe it or not, the Rams aren’t even the most injured team in California, at least according to RotoWire’s formula.“ FAA flight debacle could disrupt Rams, Chargers, 49ers; NFL responds (nypost) “The Rams have spent all week preparing for the Cardinals. Now, an unprecedented travel nightmare could force them to prepare for a road trip of an entirely different kind. A nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration on Friday afternoon has thrown weekend travel plans into chaos, potentially affecting several NFL teams scheduled to fly to their respective games Saturday. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced the shutdown about 1:15 p.m. PT, citing a communications issue affecting air traffic control centers across the country.“ Rams injury report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie questionable vs. Cardinals (ramswire) “Heading into Sunday’s game, the Rams will have three players listed as questionable: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl. Garrett isn’t practicing on Friday, as Sean McVay said the Rams are just “being smart” with him. McVay expects Garrett to play, saying that he’s “feeling good” and building on a strong performance last week. McDuffie and Curl will be limited in practice, and the Rams will see how they feel before determining their statuses for Sunday’s game. McDuffie has missed three of the last four games but McVay said earlier in the week that he’s “optimistic” about a return on Sunday. Curl didn’t practice at all last week due to a foot injury and still managed to play against the Commanders.“ A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs Arizona Cardinals Preview (lastwordonsports) ““One of the calling cards for our group, and is always an expectation, is we play with passion and energy, and I think we would all agree that (the first game against the Cardinals) wasn’t quite up to our standards,” McVay said . Los Angeles will likely rely on running 13 personnel while several of their best receivers are sidelined with injuries. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford must spread the targets in order to keep Arizona’s defense off guard. “It’s not difficult to pull the trigger, I trust those guys,” Stafford said .“ Sean McVay reveals real reason why Rams suddenly changed minds on Puka…

Myles Garrett will be listed as questionable for Sunday, but is feeling good and is expected to play, Sean McVay said. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 13, 2026 Garrett says that despite missing almost two months that he still expects to lead the NFL in sacks and be named as the Defensive Player of the Year for the third time in his career . title: NFL predictions: Rams lean on defense and…special teams?!
summary: The Los Angeles Rams might have to start winning the next few regular season games the hard way. That could mean relying more on their defense and special teams than the offense. The honest truth is that this team’s offense is not in a position to score 30 points, not with the injuries currently across […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams before the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams might have to start winning the next few regular season games the hard way. That could mean relying more on their defense and special teams than the offense. The honest truth is that this team’s offense is not in a position to score 30 points, not with the injuries currently across the roster. Sometimes, winning football means finding the end zone once or twice, taking the available field goals, and letting your defense take over the game. According to FanDuel, the Rams are favorites (-9.5) on the road against the Cardinals. The Rams have the defensive personnel to make Carson Beck miserable, generate turnovers, and dictate the tempo. Special teams can also become a difference-maker by controlling field position and consistently putting points on the board. Sean McVay needs to embrace that formula rather than forcing the offense to carry the entire team. If the Rams can win with 20 points and a dominant defensive performance, there’s absolutely nothing wrong with that. Here are my five predictions for Sunday’s game against the Cardinals… BOLD PREDICTIONS 1. Tutu Atwell leads WRs & TEs in receptions We know that the offense can operate well enough with Tutu Atwell in a main role. In 2023, he was targeted 35 times in the first 4 games of the season. He hauled in 22 receptions for 270 yards. No, Tutu Atwell will not have the time of volume that Puka Nacua has but the Rams could employ a “speedy” trio of WRs with Atwell-Smith-Daniels; stretching the defense vertically and horizontally. 2. Defense sacks Carson Beck six times Mike LaFleur will likely lean on the running game early to get Carson Beck acclimated to the flow of the game. But eventually Carson Beck is going to have to sit in the pocket. But… there are not enough blockers to go around to stop Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. Byron Young, Braden Fiske, and Wesley Bailey also should get plenty of 1 on 1 opportunities. 3. Max Klare becomes primary TE target Higbee, Parkinson, and Allen have all been inconsistent in 2026. You have to wonder if the Rams can get something out of their 2026 second round pick. Klare has the same hybrid-TE ability as Terrance Ferguson. Klare also seems like a great option to use in the screen game – showing more twitch than Higbee, Parkinson, and Allen. 4. Brandon McManus kicks 4 field goals At some point, the Rams special teams will need to help with scoring because of the offense’s sluggish ability in the first half. I believe Sean McVay needs to lean into kicking more field goals; taking the points and letting his defense win these next few games while the offense heals up. 5. CJ Daniels catches redzone touchdown With Daniels having a 6’2” frame, Daniels is the next man up for being targeted in the redzone. It won’t be Tutu Atwell or Xavier Smith. summary: With Puka Nacua going on IR the Los Angeles Rams added Brennan Presley and Tyler Scott. This is a bit of a surprise (maybe) as Sean McVay reported Nacua would avoid IR, but then went back on his own statement when it was revealed that Nacua would be going on IR to miss “extended time”. […]
full_text: With Puka Nacua going on IR the Los Angeles Rams added Brennan Presley and Tyler Scott. This is a bit of a surprise (maybe) as Sean McVay reported Nacua would avoid IR , but then went back on his own statement when it was revealed that Nacua would be going on IR to miss “extended time” . The Rams will find out who steps-up in Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals. Will anyone step-up? There is an expectation that rookie CJ Daniels could get some run, and that’s exciting for the young man, but I’ll believe it when I see it. The Rams need to earn a win on Sunday to get to 6-4 before their bye, and they likely need to get healthy to hope to beat the Green Bay Packers after their bye week. One thing at a time, starting with Arizona. LA Rams Sign Two Wide Receivers Amid Major Puka Nacua News (sports.yahoo) “Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams have provided further clarity on Puka Nacua. Their latest roster moves only add further details on a noteworthy day. “LA Rams Roster Moves,” the team posted on X on November 12, listing their transactions. Reserve/Injured WR Puka Nacua Signed to Active Roster from Practice Squad WR Brennan Presley Signed to Practice Squad WR Tyler Scott “We’re not going to put him on IR, just because of some semantics with the roster and things like that,” McVay told reporters on November 11. “But he still is going to be out for an extende period of time. It wasn’t any sort of new information.” ‘Really encouraged by his development’: Rams coaches and teammates looking forward to CJ Daniels Jr. getting more opportunities in Week 10 (rams.com) “It’s been good for me,” Daniels said of these last nine weeks. “Really just staying the course, just learning the playbook, each and every (receiver) position, and battling against the defense each and every day has definitely prepared me each and every week for whenever my number is called.” That time could be this week. With wide receiver Puka Nacua expected to miss at least a month with MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe, and veteran Davante Adams still on Injured Reserve, and Jordan Whittington now on IR, Daniels’ number is expected to be called this Sunday against the Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. “He’s going to get that,” McVay said Monday, when asked what Daniels needs to show to get time on the field. “He’s done a great job. I don’t know that I could really say any areas of improvement until he gets truly his opportunity. With the way that he’s worked consistently, the way that he shows up day in and day out. I think if you asked a lot of our DBs (defensive backs) about him, they give you a bunch of positive feedback because of the looks, the challenges. He has a lot of maturity for a young guy, like I’ve talked to you guys about. He is a guy that, no question about it, will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward.” Sportsbook Insiders: How the Puka Nacua Injury Impacts the Rams’ Playoff Odds; NFC Playoff Picture (si.com) “After holding out hope that the Rams would meet preseason expectations some sportsbooks have begun to pull back with Nacua set to miss the next few weeks. “It’s a pretty significant injury coupled with Adams’ injury as well; on top of that, they had a slow start to the season,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. “This is the first week where that view is really switching to they could very much miss the playoffs. They have a difficult schedule ahead and some real significant injuries. The only thing keeping them from a big fall right now is there is still potential to get those key guys back. If they can somehow weather the storm and get in, they could be decently healthy by the playoffs.” How long is Rams WR Puka Nacua out after being put on IR? (ramswire) “After Puka Nacua went down with a knee injury and turf toe on Sunday, Sean McVay said the Los Angeles Rams would probably place him on injured reserve . Two days later, McVay pivoted and said the Rams weren’t going to put him on IR due to roster semantics. One day after that, the Rams announced that Nacua was placed on IR , changing their minds for the second time. Regardless, Nacua was always expected to miss at least a month, but there’s a slight difference between putting him on IR and leaving him on the active roster because of the bye week. Players who are put on IR must miss a minimum of four games, not four weeks. That means Nacua will be on IR for Weeks 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14, because Week 11 is a bye. So when is he eligible to return?“ Rams Restructure Kyren Williams, Kamren Curl Deals to Create About $3 Million in Cap Space (rg.org) “The Los Angeles Rams cleared about $3 million in cap space by restructuring the contracts of running back Kyren Williams and safety Kamren Curl, moves first reported by ESPN’s Field Yates and detailed by Spotrac. Spotrac reported that the Rams converted $2 million of Williams’ salary into a signing bonus and added two void years, creating $1.7 million in 2026 cap space. They did the same with $1.7 million of Curl’s salary, also adding two void years, to create $1.3 million in space.“ Cardinals – Rams Week 10 injury reports (sports.yahoo) “The Arizona Cardinals are at the halfway point of the season. They need a win very badly. Where does the team head from here? They are facing the Los Angeles Rams once again. In the first match, Arizona’s offense dominated the LA defense, but could not score touchdowns and instead came away with six Chad Ryland field goals. Remember? This time around, there are plenty of changes for the Cardinals. The offense will sport its third starting quarterback of the year in rookie Carson Beck. Center Hjalte Froholdt is in concussion protocol; WR Michael Wilson was added to IR, as was QB Gardner Minshew; and no more Jeremiyah Love, Paris Johnson, or Will Johnson, for that matter. Thursday’s injury reports after both practices for both clubs this week.“ LA Rams injury report: 2 TE added (cardswire) “Wide receiver Puka Nuca, who McVay said Wednesday would be out for an “extended” period of time but wouldn’t go on injured reserve because if issues with the number of players they have on the list, was placed on IR Thursday s isn’t listed below. The full details of their Thursday injury report are below. Starters are noted with an asterisk. Players in bold have a different status than Wednesday with that day indicated by either no status (NS), did not participate (DNP) or limited (LIM).“ Emmanuel Forbes Jr. proving capable of bigger role in Rams secondary if needed after performance against former team (rams.com) “In his return to play his former team on Sunday afternoon, cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. was thrust into a much larger role than he’s had all season. “E-man (was) extremely productive,” defensive coordinator Chris Shula said on Thursday. “A bunch of PBUs. I thought he was awesome in the run game, physical, tackling. He made that play on the screen.” Forbes has played 33% of the Rams’ defensive snaps this season, and in the two games when Watson and McDuffie played every single defensive snap, he had none. Against Washington when both Watson and McDuffie were out for the first time all season, though, Forbes played every single defensive snap and recorded the second highest grade on the defense at 90.6, according to Pro Football Focus, only behind outside linebacker Myles Garrett.“ Rams vs. Cardinals prediction: Odds, expert picks, QB matchup, injury update, betting trends, and stats (nbcsports) “Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe…
