title: Pick Six: Bills at Jets
summary: The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills’ record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can’t pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Running back Ray Davis #22 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills’ record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can’t pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It’s a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC’s top seed. We’ve seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It’s become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn’t get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole “many mouths to feed” aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can’t convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn’t abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn’t? This isn’t the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase’s Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau’s ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald’s role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald’s defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What’s the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D’Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday’s game in the comments section…

summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Will be interesting to see what, if anything, comes of this investigation into the Jalen Hurts situation. Would be nice to see some transparency about the findings. Also would be really nice to hear from Jalen himself at some point, even […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the third quarter of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Will be interesting to see what, if anything, comes of this investigation into the Jalen Hurts situation. Would be nice to see some transparency about the findings. Also would be really nice to hear from Jalen himself at some point, even if just to hear him say he’s doing well in his recovery. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator – ESPN Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts’ blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive. The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware. “As outlined by the league and NFLPA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties,” executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester’s office Friday. Eagles reportedly releasing Fred Johnson – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles continue to make moves during their bye week, the latest of which is reportedly releasing Fred Johnson. The veteran offensive tackle provided some much needed depth at tackle, and occasionally at guard, over the years, but the team decided to move forward in another direction. Can Makai Lemon Develop Into Eagles’ WR2 In The Season’s Second Half? – PHLY Eagles Podcast Will Makai Lemon develop enough to keep the Eagles from needing another first-round receiver? Will Drew Kendall or Markel Bell show enough to earn a starting spot on the offensive line for 2027? Brandon Lee Gowton and Deniz Selman go through the things still left to learn about the Eagles coming off the bye week, including a temperature check on Nick Sirianni and some leftover thoughts from Howie Roseman’s trade deadline moves and non-moves. Bye Time – Iggles Blitz The goal is to develop young talent and figure out what you have moving forward. Jonathan Greenard played well last week. You want to see more of that from him over the final eight games so you feel good about his role in 2027. Makai Lemon had 6 catches last week. He also had a pair of costly drops. You want Lemon to learn from the mistakes so that he makes the catches next year, when hopefully wins and losses are more important. The biggest goal in the bye week should be fixing the OL and pass protection. It is impossible to fairly evaluate the QBs playing in a situation where they regularly have rushers coming free at them. Give the QBs better protection and you can get a better feel for what they can truly do. That will help you to get a better feel for the TEs and WRs as well. It would also help to figure out which of the OL should be looked at as future starters. There are times now when it is tough to discern mental mistakes vs physical ability. Don’t blame the Eagles if draft position is their priority. The NFL is incentivizing a race to the bottom – Inquirer Yet, the fact remains: it would greatly behoove the Eagles to draft as high as possible. To draft No. 1 overall could rewrite their destiny in the medium-to-long-term. The difference between a short-order return to the Super Bowl and five years of mediocrity could easily be the difference between drafting No. 1 and No. 5, or even between drafting No. 2 and No. 4. This is not an exaggeration. It is not a straw man. It is reality. Howie Roseman knows it. Bet your last dollar on that. Remember the uproar in January 2021 when the Eagles pulled Jalen Hurts in the fourth quarter of their season finale against the Commanders? Remember the questions about the play-calling? The Eagles incentive on that particular day was the prospect of moving from No. 9 to No. 6. Those three spots of draft position gained them an extra first-round pick. They traded down from No. 6 to No. 12, picking up a 2022 first-rounder from the Dolphins. That 2022 first-round pick became Jordan Davis, who helped the Eagles to a pair of Super Bowls and now has landed them 2027 first- and 2029 second-round picks from the Jaguars. In hindsight, the Eagles would have been committing organizational malpractice had they not done everything within the letter of the law to maximize their chances of drafting at No. 6 in 2021. This year, the potential reward is even greater. How did the Eagles become one of the NFL’s worst running teams? – NBCSP How did the Eagles become one of the NFL’s worst running teams? When the Eagles talk about finding their identity, it usually means, “We have to start running the ball because we can’t pass protect and our quarterbacks aren’t playing well, anyway.” And lately the Eagles have been talking about finding their identity, but this year they can’t run the ball either. Nine games into the season, the Eagles aren’t just one of the worst in the NFL throwing the ball – 29th in passing yards per game, last in passing yards per play – they’re one of the worst running it, too. Bad combination. The Eagles are rushing for only 88.6 yards per game and 3.7 yards per carry. Both are 28th in the league. Both are also their worst through nine games since 2005, when they were averaging 3.6 yards per carry and 72 rushing yards through nine games and 2nd-worst since 1991 (2.8, 76.4). Eagles legend Brandon Graham live tapes podcast, talks football at Rowan – Rowan University Former Philadelphia Eagles defensive end and two-time Super Bowl Champion Brandon Graham brought his PHLY weekly podcast, “Brandon Graham Unblocked,” to Rowan University for a live taping of its most recent episode. Organized by the Center for Sports Communication & Social Impact, this marked the first time the podcast taped outside of the studio and its first time in front of a collegiate audience. Graham and co-host Bo Wulf, an Eagles insider, discussed the team’s chances of making the playoffs, their picks for this week’s NFL games and leadership moments in Graham’s career. A focal point of the episode was the recent trade announcement of Eagles’ defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars. On that and several other team topics, Wulf gauged the crowd’s opinions by asking for cheers or boos—which the hundreds in attendance enthusiastically offered. Jaguars vs Titans: Injury Report Ahead of Week 10 – Big Cat Country Trade acquisitions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis also sat out for rest and have already been declared out this week. Cam Skattebo reveals the junk food that made him barf during Giants-Commanders – SB Nation It’s flu season, and a lot of people are catching stuff going around right now — so the concern was understandable. The wild card was that Skattebo’s reaction to barfing wasn’t exactly normal. The running back was seemingly laughing about the fact he blew chunks on the bench, and appeared to wave off team doctors when they wanted to check him out. After the game he revealed that it wasn’t illness, or nerves that got the best of him — but a pretzel dog. New York Giants mailbag: Kickoff rule, Rasul Douglas interception, more – Big Blue View I wrote earlier in the week that the Giants should try to capitalize on the opportunity they have in the NFC East. You don’t know if or when that opportunity will come again. They did try to do that. They were very aggressive. They were also careful. I said earlier in the week there was a price they should not go to — meaning they should not go above…

He's been with the team since 2023. pic.twitter.com/y3Ln9Jm8kN — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 13, 2026 It’s interesting that this is one of the moves Howie Roseman would make given the struggles of the Eagles’ offensive line this season. They’ve had a slow shedding of veteran lineman this season, starting with Lane Johnson (retired) and then Cam Jurgens (traded to Baltimore), and are now making an even further commitment to a younger group up front. Fred has been a fan favorite for years, and the Eagles even traded to get him back in 2025 after losing him during free agency. title: Eagles down to 4 captains after starting the season with 7
summary: The Eagles started the 2026 NFL season having voted seven players as captains, and as we enter Week 10, the team’s bye, they are down to just four on the active roster. It’s remarkable how different this team looks halfway through the current campaign. Three of the four remaining captains have had to show their […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles started the 2026 NFL season having voted seven players as captains , and as we enter Week 10, the team’s bye, they are down to just four on the active roster. It’s remarkable how different this team looks halfway through the current campaign. Lane Johnson — Retired Jalen Hurts — Out indefinitely due to blood clots Jordan Davis — Traded to the Jaguars Three of the four remaining captains have had to show their leadership from the sidelines at many points this season, and been unable to contribute on the field. DeVonta Smith — Played in only 4 games, and hasn’t seen the field since Week 6. Saquon Barkley — Missed 2 games due to injury and returned in Week 7 on a pitch count. He suffered a new back injury early in his return, and has been on a closely monitored snap count in the weeks since. Zack Baun — Missed 1 game with a concussion. That leaves just Jordan Mailata as the only captain still on the Eagles active roster to have played in all nine of the team’s games ( and every single offensive snap! ) in 2026. The All-Pro left tackle’s voice and presence is more important than ever with the offensive line turning to younger, inexperienced players up front, and the group falling to one of the worst in the league. This season has been a huge disappointment, with the Eagles heading into their bye week riding a seven-game losing streak. Both sides of the ball have dealt with a long list of injuries, and there’s been little-to-no consistency on offense to allow for the new scheme to develop. The seven players voted as captains at the start of the season were picked by their teammates for a reason, and their leadership was expected to help shepherd a new system in Philly, but instead, the Eagles are down to just four captains and need new guys to step up.

title: Eagles News: Nick Sirianni’s job security among top storylines to monitor the rest of this season
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! How are you feeling about Nick Sirianni right now? Do you think he deserves a mulligan? I don’t think it’s accurate to frame it as one bad season when the losing dates back to the second half of last year (5-12 […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the second quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! How are you feeling about Nick Sirianni right now? Do you think he deserves a mulligan? I don’t think it’s accurate to frame it as one bad season when the losing dates back to the second half of last year (5-12 in their last 17 games). If the Eagles lose 15 straight to finish the season at 2-15 (not the most likely outcome but hardly impossible), I think it’s pretty difficult to justify bringing Sirianni back. Or if it’s not far off from that final record. If the Eagles bounce back in the second half, you have to wonder how much that should be valued. The 2011 Eagles won their final four games to get to 8-8 … only for that “momentum” to prove useless for the 2012 Eagles, who finished 4-12. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Six storylines to watch during the rest of a lost Eagles season – Inquirer The coaching staff. Nick Sirianni wouldn’t rule out coaching changes after the game Sunday, but he did say a day later that no changes have been made. “Right now, like I said earlier, we’re going through our self-scout process,” he said. “Guys are working on studies right now and we’re determined to figure things out and get on the right track, and that’s what we’re worried about right this particular time.” That wasn’t a ringing endorsement of Mannion staying in his current role. Could the Eagles make a change at play-caller as soon as this week? Could they move on from offensive line coach Chris Kuper? The self-scouting process won’t be kind to either coach. If Mannion remains in his position for the rest of the season, it’ll be worth watching if the offense can show signs of life, with Joe Milton or whoever is taking snaps at quarterback. There’s also the Sirianni of it all. Will Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman think injuries and a flawed roster outweigh the rest of the problems and decide to keep him? Is there a number of consecutive losses that warrant an in-season firing? NFL Power Rankings: Week 10 Edition – BGN 29 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 29) – After starting the season 2-0, the Eagles have lost seven straight. It couldn’t be more obvious that Nick Sirianni has no answers. The good news is that Howie Roseman is doing his part to put the team in a position to rebound beyond this season. The Jordan Davis trade was an absolute heist. 5 Questions About Jordan Davis: Jaguars Got ‘A Good Vibes Addition’ – Big Cat Country The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jordan Davis! To learn more about Duval’s newest defensive tackle, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Brandon Lee Gowton, who covered Davis’ time with the Philadelphia Eagles over the past four and a half seasons for SB Nation’s Bleeding Green Nation. International player Joshua Weru on his development behind the scenes – NBCSP Joshua Weru was the talk of training camp this summer. While draft pick Uar Bernard grabbed headlines this spring, it was the Eagles’ other International Player Pathway Program player who began to stand out in August. The edge rusher from Kenya flashed in practices and even in the preseason a bit — to the point where some worried he’d be claimed if the Eagles dared to waive him to get him to the practice squad. But that was months ago and now we’re in November. Weru has spent all season on the Eagles’ practice squad. And most days this season, Weru walks through the Eagles locker room mostly unnoticed. He’ll sit at his locker without being bothered and hadn’t really been asked for an interview all season. Until last week. So Weru seemed a bit surprised when he was approached and asked for a few minutes, which he graciously handed over. What have the last couple of months been like? “It’s been good,” Weru said. “I continue to say I’m so lucky to be here. The amount of reps we get on scout team and developmental have been good. Just seeing things better and recognizing blocks quicker. Just getting my strike stronger. Even though I’m not necessarily getting stronger in the weight room, like actual game strength is getting slightly better. Just those things because you’re more used to doing certain movements so you’re getting better at it.” 2026 Midseason All-Pro Team: Joe Burrow, Penei Sewell, Dexter Lawrence and more – PFF Linebacker: Ventrell Miller, Jacksonville Jaguars. Miller has arguably been the breakout player of the NFL season, with his 92.6 overall PFF grade leading all linebackers. He has impressed in coverage, earning a 91.3 PFF coverage grade and recording four pass breakups, and he has also been strong against the run, with an 84.7 PFF run-defense grade that ranks fourth at the position. Second Team: Zack Baun, Philadelphia Eagles. Zach Ertz surprises Julie Ertz with National Soccer Hall of Fame selection – PhiladelphiaEagles.com First year of eligibility for the National Soccer Hall of Fame? No problem for Julie Ertz, one of the best midfielders and defenders in the history of the United States Women’s National Team. Amongst many other accolades, the two-time World Cup Champion, two-time Concacaf Women’s Championship winner, and two-time U.S. Soccer Female Player of the Year was surprised with the news that she would be inducted into the Hall of Fame by her husband, Eagles tight end Zach Ertz. “(The National Soccer Hall of Fame) reached out to me about two months ago to try and figure out the best way to do it,” Zach Ertz said after the surprise. “I kind of was out of ideas, but I wanted to get the family together, not in the craziness of the house, and make it a little special.” Jameis Winston tried everything to draw the Commanders offsides – SB Nation That’s right, you heard that correctly. After using an old-school cadence right out of youth football (Hut 1, Hu2 2), Winston turned to the lyrics from “Who Let the Dogs Out,” which won a Grammy award back in 2001 for the Best New Dance Recording. Winston’s effort did not have the same level of success, and the Giants were forced to take a timeout before punting the ball away. Giants try to keep perspective, but this was a massive missed opportunity – Big Blue View You wanted them to, of course. Did you really think, though, that the New York Giants were just going to waltz to the NFC East title without things getting interesting? The Giants made things interesting, and much more convoluted, by losing to the Washington Commanders on Thursday and missing an opportunity to take firm control of the division. The 5-3-1 Giants are still in first place, and will remain there through the weekend no matter how the second-place Dallas Cowboys fare on Sunday when they host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Their path to a first division title since the 2011 Super Bowl season is now much more difficult, and uncertain. If the Cowboys can upset the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, they will be 5-5, just 1.5 games behind the Giants with eight weeks left in the season. The Commanders are now 3-5-1, and with a tiebreaker advantage over the Giants should also feel like their season is very much alive. Commanders help Cowboys’ NFC East hopes with TNF win over Giants – Blogging The Boys The NFC East just became a tiny bit easier for the Dallas Cowboys. They owe the Washington Commanders big time. On Thursday night there was an NFC East tilt that went down to the wire. When it looked like the New York Giants (5-3-1) were going to take a serious step forward, a leap to be honest, in the NFC East race, Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs to give Washington the late lead that held until the end. In case you are unaware, a Giants win on Thursday night would have just about sealed the NFC East race. Nothing is ever official obviously, but it…

title: Steelers could be forced to bus to Cincinnati after FAA grounds flights
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football for sole possession of first place in the AFC North. full_text: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football for sole possession of first place in the AFC North. However, travel plans could have to change drastically for the Steelers over the course of the next 24 hours. Just a few hours ago, the FAA grounded all flights nationwide after what they are calling a communications problem. At the time of this writing, Homeland Security does not believe that this was a nefarious attack against the U.S., but rather just an outage. This is the first nationwide ground stoppage since January 2023. Steelers senior director of communications Burt Lauten told WPXI’s Shelby Cassesse that the team is “monitoring the situation” as air travel comes to a halt. Steelers spokesperson Burt Lauten tells me the team is "monitoring the situation" as the FAA ground stop creates uncertainty surrounding air travel. The team is scheduled to fly to Cincinnati tomorrow. Fortunately, it's just a 4.5 hour drive from Pittsburgh if it comes to that. — Shelby Cassesse (@ShelbyCassesse) November 13, 2026 It’s difficult to say how long this ground stoppage could last, and it could effect sporting events all across the nation throughout the weekend. Luckily for the Steelers, the drive to Cincinnati would be something they could quickly pivot to. Since the team was not scheduled to fly out until Saturday, they are in a better situation than most right now. While a flight is quicker and more convenient for the team, a bus ride shouldn’t have a major effect on their preparation plans, as it may for other teams. title: The Steelers can’t stop talking about this practice squad WR
summary: It has been a busy few weeks of Steelers wide receiver discourse. There have been trade rumors about Josh Downs, Brian Thomas Jr., and Calvin Ridley. There’s been talk about when Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. can return off of injured reserve. And hey, did you know Brandon Aiyuk is set to be available […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images It has been a busy few weeks of Steelers wide receiver discourse. There have been trade rumors about Josh Downs, Brian Thomas Jr., and Calvin Ridley. There’s been talk about when Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. can return off of injured reserve. And hey, did you know Brandon Aiyuk is set to be available soon? But amid all the rumors, the Steelers can’t seem to stop talking about one potential addition to the room: Max Hurleman, who is currently on practice squad injured reserve. “I mean, how do you not love Max (Hurleman)?” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Thursday. “As a new coach, new coaching staﬀ, you come in here every day doing everything right. GPS (data), (he) burned it up. I mean, the guy has an incredible workload capacity, work ethic.” McCarthy said it was unfortunate that Hurleman was injured early in the season, with the receiver landing on practice squad injured reserve on Sept. 19 with what Steelers beat reporter Mark Kaboly recently described as an “undisclosed but suspected leg injury.” “I felt that (Hurleman) truly performed to a level that he deserved a 53-man roster spot,” McCarthy said. “So, it’ll be great to get him back and get him back into the fold.” It appears Hurleman could be getting close to a return. On Wednesday, quarterback Aaron Rodgers mentioned the wide receiver when asked about the Steelers getting healthier at the position. “We’ve obviously raised up a couple of our P-Squad guys who are talented. Still would love to get some opportunities for Max (Hurleman) at some point whenever he comes oﬀ,“ Rodgers told the media. ”We have Marquez (Valdes-Scantling), who hasn’t been brought up yet, so we have a lot of options. But I’m hopeful that we’ll get (Michael Pittman Jr.) and Roman (Wilson) back sooner rather than later.“ Also on Wednesday, McCarthy brought up Hurleman in the same breath as Pittman and Wilson. “We’ve got a group that I’m excited to continue to work with,” the Steelers coach said. Steelers WR1 DK Metcalf also seems excited for the return of Hurleman, coining the nickname “White Chocolate” for the second-year receiver. “White Chocolate gonna get y’all some plays, especially when he’s out there on the field, so I’m looking forward to him making his debut,” Metcalf told the media on Thursday . “(Hurleman) has been making plays since his rookie year last year, so definitely looking forward to him being out there.” Hurleman has yet to play in an NFL regular season game. “It’s very humbling whenever your name gets brought up,” Hurleman said, per Kaboly . “I’ve been working my tail off every day to come back. To get the recognition, that means a lot, but obviously, there’s a ton of work to do. Haven’t played a game yet, but it’s awesome to hear they trust me and see me as an option.” Hurleman initially joined the Steelers as an undrafted free agent out of Notre Dame in 2025. He finished his college career in South Bend after four years at Colgate, entering the NFL with experience at running back, wide receiver, cornerback and returner. He’s largely settled into a wide receiver role with the Steelers, where he’s made some highlight plays in recent preseasons. Really nice catch by former Notre Dame RB/WR Max Hurleman pic.twitter.com/kqZeMHFSKQ — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) August 10, 2025 The 5’11, 200-pound receiver still hasn’t been activated off of practice squad injured reserve, but it appears that the Steelers have some plans for Hurleman once he returns.

summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers may have to wait another week to get defensive lineman Derrick Harmon back on the field. full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers may have to wait another week to get defensive lineman Derrick Harmon back on the field. Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette said during an appearance on 93.7 The Fan that he does not anticipate Harmon making his return to action on Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals. “I don’t think so,” Fittipaldo said when asked if Harmon would play. “He’s a young guy, and (the Steelers) usually like to have their young guys get at least one full practice in before they play.” Fittipaldo added that Friday’s practice, where Harmon was eventually reported as a full participant, was a walkthrough and not the best indicator of the defensive lineman’s availability. Harmon has been limited in the Steelers’ last two practices since his 21-day return window from injured reserve was open. Derrick Harmon, speaking today to reporters, says “we’ll see by tomorrow” if he will play against the Bengals. He added he feels good after three practices. He was limited the first two days of the week. pic.twitter.com/9SNzgLu8zw — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) November 13, 2026 Harmon has been sidelined with a foot injury since Week 4, leaving Pittsburgh without one of its young defensive linemen. He was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 5 and has missed the team’s last four contests. With Cincinnati bringing one of the NFL’s most explosive offenses into Sunday’s matchup, Pittsburgh could certainly use the added depth and talent along its defensive line. However, based on Fittipaldo’s expectation, the Steelers may have to make do without Harmon for at least another week.

title: 2027 NFL Draft: Prospects to watch for the Steelers
summary: After the Steelers’ bye week and a quiet trade deadline for the black and gold — where Pittsburgh made a point to hold onto future draft capital — now is as good a time as ever to take a look at the team’s needs and a sneak peek at the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft. As […]
full_text: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images After the Steelers’ bye week and a quiet trade deadline for the black and gold — where Pittsburgh made a point to hold onto future draft capital — now is as good a time as ever to take a look at the team’s needs and a sneak peek at the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft. As college bowl season approaches, what players should Steelers fans be watching, and at what position? With the notable exception of quarterback, a position that’s never lacking media coverage elsewhere, Read & React has you covered: Wide receiver RB : Wide receiver, once again, looks like one of the biggest holes on the Steelers’ roster — not just this upcoming offseason, but during this season, as Pittsburgh was connected to a number of pass catchers ahead of the trade deadline. Pittsburgh general manager Omar Khan seemed to do a better job than in past seasons of reworking the team’s wide receiver room ahead of 2026 with the additions of Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard, but injuries, paired with with a unexpectedly poor season from presumed WR1 DK Metcalf, have things looking rough once again. What’s interesting is that, on paper, there isn’t a lot of expected turnover in the room this offseason, with Ben Skowronek being the only name set to hit free agency. He’ll probably sign on a cheap deal once again as one of the team’s primary special teamers, but spots could open up elsewhere if the team decides to move on from less inspiring names higher on the depth chart. Metcalf’s monster deal is still largely immovable — I doubt many teams would want to trade for it, and a release would yield $35.8 million and $23.9 million dead cap hits in the next two seasons, respectively. And while it’s worth noting that Michael Pittman Jr. hasn’t really played enough this season to look definitively good or bad as an addition to the Steelers, his recent extension is easier to get out of with “just” $15.1 million and $7.6 million in dead cap hits in the next two respective seasons. It’s definitely worth keeping an eye on as Pittman has had health issues and recorded just 89 yards through three games as a Steeler thus far. Elsewhere, youngsters Roman Wilson and Kaden Wetjen certainly haven’t played above the possibility of future camp competition. Wilson seems to have turned a bit of a corner this season with a respectable 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games, but consistency and health continue to be an issue in Year 3. Meanwhile, Wetjen hasn’t done much to alleviate the concerns about picking a return specialist in the fourth round; he hasn’t provided much of a spark as a returner so far his rookie season, and he hasn’t contributed a single thing as a receiver despite the rash of injuries above him on the depth chart. All of that to say, wide receiver remains firmly on the Steelers’ draft radar heading into 2027, where it could be as high as a first-round pick if the team wants to be a little forward-thinking (I’m bullish on Germie Bernard as a long-term starter, but not as a WR1). Especially considering the Steelers will likely be trying to support a young quarterback next year, building up a strong group of pass catchers should be a top priority with the offensive line rebuild largely in place already. Names to watch: Probably gone before the Steelers pick: Jeremiah Smith (Ohio State), Charlie Becker (Indiana) Nick Marsh, Indiana RP : Plenty of attention this college football season is being paid to Indiana’s other star receiver, Charlie Becker, but Marsh is the one that most intrigues me. Marsh would give the Steelers the size they were chasing when they acquired D.K. Metcalf, but Marsh’s playstyle actually fits with the vision of a physical, contested catch winner. Marsh’s catch radius is one of the largest in college football because he pairs his size and length with excellent body control and strong, reliable hands. Back Shoulder Slot Fade to Nick Marsh 🥵 pic.twitter.com/qGcCppBYqQ — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) September 5, 2026 Marsh is also a willing blocker and plays the position with the kind of controlled aggression you typically don’t get out of receivers. His willingness to mix it up as a blocker would make the eventual transition from Metcalf smoother in multiple phases of the game. People talk about “Culture” Culture is your bigtime portal WR attacking a LB in the B-Gap on 4th & 1. Curt Cignetti has mastered buy-in. pic.twitter.com/ExPGyFCI2I — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) September 5, 2026 Jackson Harris, LSU RP : Harris was not a featured prospect on any draft lists heading into this college season, but he’s certainly grabbed draftniks’ attention now with a breakout year at LSU. After spending his first two years toiling on the bench for Stanford, Harris transferred to Hawaii for the 2025 season, where he turned 49 receptions into 963 yards and 12 touchdowns. That made him an intriguing portal candidate for top programs, and he hasn’t slowed down for the Tigers in 2026. Listed at 6’2 and 205 pounds, Harris’ build and playstyle are reminiscent of recent Tiger greats: Ja’Marr Chase and Malik Nabers. While I don’t expect Harris to be drafted within the first six picks like they were, it’s hard to watch him play and not think of him as a player cut from the same cloth. Truly a Ferrari on the field. LSU WR Jackson Harris has my attention. This is what a first round wideout looks like. 20-344-2 in the last two games vs. Auburn/Bama. 📈 pic.twitter.com/yYLFGqkGhn — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) November 11, 2026 He’s totaled 47 receptions for 800 yards and seven touchdowns thus far. With LSU already suffering three losses, the Tigers are longshots to make the playoffs. But with games against No. 6 Texas, No. 8 Tennessee, and Arkansas still on the slate, he has a chance to leave a lasting impression regardless of what the postseason looks like for LSU. Reed Harris, Arizona State RP : After three seasons at Boston College, Harris transferred across the country to Arizona State, where he quickly became the Sun Devils’ top target. Listed at 6’5 and 220 pounds, Harris cuts an imposing figure and has all the looks of a classic X-receiver. He leads the Big 12 in receiving yards (907) and is second in touchdowns (9). He’s managed this despite three different quarterbacks garnering starts for Arizona State this season. A 58-yard strike from Cutter Boley to Reed Harris 😈 📺 ABC pic.twitter.com/98Wu4YI0G3 — Sun Devil Football (@ASUFootball) September 12, 2026 Harris projects primarily as a deep threat on the outside, but he offers some versatility too, as 20.8% of his snaps this season have come from the slot. With his size, he’s not going to run a blazing 40-time, but he shows good pacing and change of direction for someone of his build, and he possesses some yards-after-the-catch upside. Reed Harris moving like this at 6’4” 220 is why he’s high on my board 🔱 pic.twitter.com/PWVzRR3CAa — Jay (@DraftwithJay) November 8, 2026 Other names to watch Cam Coleman, Texas KJ Duff, Rutgers (though he will miss the rest of the season due to injury) Amare Thomas, Houston Anthony Evans III, Mississippi State Omarion Miller, Arizona State Junior Sherrill, Vanderbilt Cornerbacks RB : Besides the offensive and defensive lines, cornerback is probably the position you could argue teams should pick every draft. Good cornerbacks are hard to find and expensive to keep around. Even high-end corners can be incredibly volatile, and they get hurt quite a bit. Teams have a lot of corners on the field at all times and cycle through their depth every season. The point: The draft is a numbers game; take a gamble on corners you like often. The Steelers have a greater need at the position than previously anticipated after unexpectedly failing to reach an agreement with Joey Porter Jr. ahead of 2026. Now, the fate of the cornerback room has been left in the hands of free-agent addition Jamel Dean (30 years old, injured a lot), Asante Samuel Jr. (impending free…

title: NFL predictions: 4 game picks for intriguing Seahawks vs. Raiders matchup
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are hitting the road for the first time in a month to renew their former AFC West rivalry with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for another must-win game. Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook. While the Seahawks are […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are hitting the road for the first time in a month to renew their former AFC West rivalry with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday for another must-win game. Seattle enters the game as 6.5-point favorites on the road, their second straight week being favored by FanDuel Sportsbook . While the Seahawks are large favorites, they’ll depend on their dominant defense to get the job done yet again as their inconsistent offense is still quite injured. Seattle’s “Dark Side” defense will welcome the Raiders’ first overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, to the NFL and hope to slow Klint Kubiak’s offense, which is averaging 26.4 points per game. Here are four bets/game picks to consider ahead of Sunday’s game. 1. Jadarian Price anytime touchdown (+190) While Seattle’s rookie running back has battled injuries this season, it’s still hard to believe that he’s yet to find the end zone. Price has shown the most juice of any Seahawks running back and emerged as a receiving threat last week against the Cardinals. With Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock still hampered by injuries, Price is likely to get a lot of work in the passing and running game against a struggling Raiders defense. Las Vegas’ defense has allowed large receiving days to running backs this season, with the worst coming against the Buffalo Bills when back James Cook totaled 58 yards on three catches. While it might be hard to envision betting on the Seahawks offense after they only hung 17 on the Cardinals, a second week with Lock as the leading man should lead to a more complete game plan, allowing them to score and make a statement. 2. Maxx Crosby to record a sack (+144) With Charles Cross out and Abe Lucas struggling this season, there’s a near guarantee that the Raiders’ star pass rusher will be active in the Seahawks backfield on Sunday. Crosby leads the Raiders with four sacks, and while he hasn’t quite been in game-wrecking self this season, he shouldn’t need to be to get home against an injured Lock. 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 89.5 receiving yards (-114) Coming off his quietest outing of the year, there’s no question that Smith-Njigba should be more involved with the Seahawks offense this week. JSN has totaled over 100 yards in all, but two of his games this season and has padded his total against poor secondaries, which should include Las Vegas’ unit. While I already mentioned this in the Price prop, I’ll say it again: the Raiders’ defense is not good. Las Vegas secondary gives up an average of 234 passing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the league. Even though Lock is still dealing with an injury, JSN should be so open on Sunday he’ll only need half an arm to get it to him. 4. Seahawks -6.5 (-110) Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald is undefeated against quarterbacks making their first start, and there’s no reason this game should be different. Mendoza has limited reps as a starter and is getting thrown to the wolves against a Seahawks defense that is riding high after holding an NFC West rival to just three points last week. Lock and the Seahawks’ offense may struggle early, but there is simply too much star power for the Raiders defense to handle. Las Vegas’ defense has thrived on turnovers, so Seattle will need another turnover-free game from Lock and Price like they got last week. If the Seahawks’ offense can stay clean there’s no doubt the defense will handle Mendoza and allow the Seahawks to handle the Raiders with ease. title: Seahawks travel plans for Raiders game uncertain after FAA orders, lifts nationwide ground stop
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are scheduled to face the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium for their final game before their bye week, but there will need to be extra monitoring of their flight schedule heading into Saturday. Travel plans were disrupted throughout the United States on Friday afternoon after the Federal Aviation Administration announced a […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are scheduled to face the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium for their final game before their bye week, but there will need to be extra monitoring of their flight schedule heading into Saturday. Travel plans were disrupted throughout the United States on Friday afternoon after the Federal Aviation Administration announced a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon . The FAA said in official statement that there were “communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers.” As of about 5:15 pm PT, the ground stop has been lifted. More than 7,000 flights were canceled on Friday, and nearly 2,000 Saturday flights have already been canceled . There will be continued delays throughout the rest of Friday and likely longer. “Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data […] and they started to give us inconsistency in the data from those routers. And because of that, we shut the system down,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. “I believe that it’s going to take us some time to get back to capacity,” Duffy added. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was made aware of the outage during his media availability. “We’ll play it by ear and we’ll adjust to how we need to adjust,” Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters. “We have a plan for tomorrow and we’re leaving tomorrow, which helps obviously.” Friday’s events have already directly impacted the Saturday college sports schedule. The Washington Huskies men’s basketball team will have their road game at the Utah Utes moved to Sunday, while the Auburn vs. Mississippi State football game was pushed back from noon ET to 3:15 pm PT to accommodate Auburn’s revised travel schedule. Meanwhile, the Huskies football team intends to fly to East Lansing on Friday night for their Saturday tilt with Michigan State, but as of this article’s publish the kickoff time has not been changed. The Seahawks will take their charter flight to Las Vegas on Saturday, and hopefully any delays are either minimal or non-existent now that the order has been lifted. summary: A war of attrition remains in the trenches on both sides of the ball for the Seattle Seahawks but at least defensively, there will be slight reinforcements. After missing back-to-back games with an ankle injury, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu practiced in full on Friday and will head into Sunday without an injury designation. The ninth-year […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Uchenna Nwosu #7 of the Seattle Seahawks runs across the field during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images A war of attrition remains in the trenches on both sides of the ball for the Seattle Seahawks but at least defensively, there will be slight reinforcements. After missing back-to-back games with an ankle injury, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu practiced in full on Friday and will head into Sunday without an injury designation. The ninth-year pro appeared to be trending toward a return, after consecutive limited practices to start the week, and will now make his return after a full participation on Friday. Nwosu has struggled to stay on the field in recent years, limited to six games in both 2023 and 2024, but has produced for the Seahawks when healthy, posting 9.5 sacks in his debut season in Seattle and seven last year. Through seven games in 2026, the former Charger has just a single sack and a pair of tackles for loss. The Seahawks will need some instant impact from Nwosu, as Leonard Williams remains out with the stinger that saw him leave the game against the Chicago Bears and miss last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Williams will remain missing form the interior, Brandon Pili will be back in the rotation after recovering from his back injury. Pili practiced in full on Friday after consecutive DNPs to start the week. No such help is headed for Seattle’s offensive line, however, with Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson remaining out with their respective ankle and knee injuries. Cross’s absence is a particular blow, after he was limited in practice on Thursday before a return to DNP status on Friday. Though Sam Darnold remains out as well, backup quarterback Drew Lock will get additional help with the return of Rashid Shaheed, who got in a full week of practice as he has recovered from a knee injury. For the second straight week, Lock was limited in practice across all three days in his ramp up to start, as he continues to manage severe tendinitis , as well as the oblique injury suffered in Week 9 . title: Seahawks vs. Raiders, Week 10 preview: Seattle’s ground game has a big opportunity
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have an opportunity to exploit one of the Las Vegas Raiders’ biggest weaknesses this Sunday. Las Vegas has struggled to establish its own ground game, while its defense has been among the NFL’s worst at stopping the run. For Seattle, the path to controlling this game starts up front, on both sides […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have an opportunity to exploit one of the Las Vegas Raiders’ biggest weaknesses this Sunday. Las Vegas has struggled to establish its own ground game, while its defense has been among the NFL’s worst at stopping the run. For Seattle, the path to controlling this game starts up front, on both sides of the ball. But the matchup is more complicated than the numbers might suggest. The Seahawks have struggled to run the ball consistently themselves, and the Raiders still have enough talent to punish an offense that becomes predictable. With Drew Lock dealing with an oblique/elbow injury and Sam Darnold sidelined, Seattle may need to lean even more heavily on its ground game and quick passing concepts. The ground game could decide this matchup The Raiders are averaging just 71.3 rushing yards per game and 2.9 yards per carry through nine games. Ashton Jeanty has 362 rushing yards on 114 attempts, averaging 3.2 yards per carry. He has actually produced more yards as a receiver, with 371 yards on 42 catches. Mike Washington Jr. has been more efficient on the ground, averaging 3.9 yards per carry on 71 attempts for 275 yards. He gives Las Vegas another option, but neither back has helped establish a reliable rushing attack. That creates an opportunity for Seattle’s defense. The Seahawks have allowed just 78.8 rushing yards per game over their last five contests, including consecutive performances against Kansas City and Arizona in which they surrendered only 50 rushing yards. Chicago, however, ran for 126 yards and three touchdowns against Seattle on November 2, showing that the defense remains vulnerable when an opponent finds ways to create movement at the line of scrimmage and attacking the edges. The Raiders have struggled to create that movement themselves. Seattle should be able to challenge Jeanty and Washington early, force Las Vegas into unfavorable down-and-distance situations, and make rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza carry more of the offensive burden. Can Seattle take advantage of the Raiders’ weakness on the other side of the ball? Las Vegas is allowing 151.2 rushing yards per game and five yards per carry, both league-worst figures. That is a significant opportunity for a Seahawks offense that has averaged 110.8 rushing yards per game this season, although Seattle’s 3.9 yards per carry shows that consistency has been an issue. Zach Charbonnet’s return offers some reason for optimism. In his second game back from an ACL injury, Charbonnet led Seattle with 77 rushing yards on 16 carries against Arizona. Jadarian Price added 24 yards on nine carries, along with four catches for 54 receiving yards. Their contributions helped Seattle put together a more effective ground attack last week. Sunday will be their third game together this season, giving the Seahawks another opportunity to build on that progress. The offensive line, however, remains central to the equation. Seattle’s struggles cannot be pinned entirely on its running backs. The unit has struggled to consistently create movement, and injuries have forced changes across the line. The return of Charbonnet helps, but even the best running backs need room to work. That balance run vs pass matters even more this week. With Lock managing an additional oblique injury, Seattle has good reason to emphasize quick throws and a strong running game rather than repeatedly asking its quarterback to hold the ball and make difficult downfield reads. If the Seahawks can establish the run, they can dictate the pace, protect their quarterback, and keep Maxx Crosby from becoming the defining factor in the game. Brock Bowers is the biggest threat in the passing game Despite missing two games, Bowers has recorded 48 receptions for 658 yards and six touchdowns in seven appearances. That translates to 94 receiving yards per game, with an average of ten targets per contest. Those are outstanding numbers for a tight end, particularly one who has already demonstrated the ability to produce against different defensive looks. Bowers also brings positional versatility. He can line up as a traditional tight end, move into the slot, align outside. That flexibility forces defenses to adjust their personnel and assignments before the snap. When Bowers lines up inside, linebackers and safeties may be responsible for covering him. When he moves outside, cornerbacks can be forced into difficult matchups. His alignment can also create opportunities for Las Vegas to isolate him against a defender it believes it can exploit. The challenge does not end when the ball arrives. Bowers is dangerous after the catch, capable of turning a short completion into a significant gain. Seattle must therefore do more than simply keep him in front of the defense. Tackling and closing throwing windows will be just as important as the initial coverage. The Seahawks have shown they can limit tight ends by keeping the ball in front of them and preventing additional yards after the catch. The first matchup with Arizona’s Trey McBride provides a useful recent example to study. Seattle allowed McBride to get involved as a receiver, but limited his yard production. The Seahawks have had strong stretches defending tight ends, but spacing in the underneath zones remains an area to monitor. Bowers is precisely the kind of player who can find those spaces, settle into soft spots in coverage, and force defenders to make difficult tackles. Seattle cannot afford to lose track of him when the Raiders use motion or change his alignment. Communication before the snap will be critical, especially if Las Vegas tries to force a linebacker into coverage against Bowers. The other weapons: Tre Tucker and Michael Mayer Bowers is the centerpiece, but the Raiders have other receiving options capable of making Seattle pay if the defense concentrates too heavily on the tight end. Tre Tucker is the most obvious threat downfield. He has 33 receptions for 529 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 16 yards per catch. His 58.8 receiving yards per game and ability to stretch the field make him an important part of the Raiders’ passing attack. Michael Mayer is another player to watch. The second tight end has 39 receptions for 388 yards and a touchdown. His presence becomes particularly important when the Raiders deploy two-tight-end formations, allowing them to create different combinations of blocking and receiving threats. Jeanty also remains a receiving threat out of the backfield, adding another player Seattle must account for in underneath coverage. Protecting Drew Lock and handling Maxx Crosby Seattle’s offensive line faces a difficult test against Crosby, one of the league’s most disruptive edge defenders. He has four sacks this season, but his impact extends beyond the sack total. His ability to generate pressure, attack the quarterback’s launch point, and disrupt plays makes him dangerous even when he does not finish with a takedown. The Raiders have recorded 19 sacks as a team, with Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce contributing three apiece. Crosby is the headliner, but Seattle cannot afford to focus exclusively on him and leave the other rushers with favorable opportunities. Seattle may therefore need to favor quicker reads, shorter throws, and a greater emphasis on getting the ball out before the pass rush arrives once Lock has elbow and oblique injury. That approach also makes sense against Crosby. The longer the quarterback holds the ball, the more time the Raiders’ pass rush has to create pressure. Quick throws can neutralize some of that advantage, particularly if Seattle can pair them with an effective running game. The Seahawks have also shown that they can avoid sacks when their protection and decision-making work together. Lock has taken only two sacks in his three appearances this season, despite attempting 76 passes. Seattle should continue to use that approach rather than repeatedly asking its offensive line to hold up against Crosby…

title: Seahawks reveal their 2026 Midseason Honors
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have announced their 2026 Midseason Honors. The honors at stake include: Offensive MVP, Defensive MVP, Special Teams MVP, Top Newcomer, Best Relief Performance, Best Play on Offense, Best Play on Defense, Best Play on Special Teams, Trent to Continue, and Thing to Clean Up. Let’s see who and what items won each […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have announced their 2026 Midseason Honors . The honors at stake include: Offensive MVP, Defensive MVP, Special Teams MVP, Top Newcomer, Best Relief Performance, Best Play on Offense, Best Play on Defense, Best Play on Special Teams, Trent to Continue, and Thing to Clean Up. Let’s see who and what items won each honor. Offensive MVP: Jaxon Smith-Njigba To nobody’s surprise, the offensive MVP midway through the season is JSN. He is a front runner for his second NFL Offensive Player of the Year Award, and frankly could be a finalist for the MVP this season as well. Through nine games, JSN has 71 catches for 1,036 yards and nine touchdowns. If he were to keep up this pace for 17 games, that would put him at 134 catches for 1,957 yards and 17 touchdowns. Not only would these numbers break each Seahawk single-season receiving record, they also would put JSN as: the second most receiving yards in an NFL single season (Calvin Johnson is first with 1,964 yards); the seventh most receptions in an NFL season (Michael Thomas is first with 149 receptions); and tie for the sixth most receiving touchdowns in an NFL season (Randy Moss is first with 23 receiving touchdowns) All of these numbers make it safe to say that JSN is your offensive, and frankly team MVP midway through the 2026 season. Defense MVP: Ernest Jones IV On defense, choosing an MVP may be a little more difficult. There are multiple candidates who could take this honor. Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, Demarcus Lawrence, Devon Witherspoon, Nick Emmawori, Julian Love, the list continues. The defensive performance for Seattle is really a testament to how close knit this team is and how dialed in Mike Macdonald has them. All of that being said, the Seahawks gave this honor to the green dot himself, Ernest Jones IV. Jones IV is the leader of this defense, and a critical backbone to the number one defense for yards/game in the NFL. Jones IV leads the team in tackles (88 ), which is good for fourth most tackles in the NFL. Jones IV also has three sacks (tied for second most on the team), five passes defensed (second most on the team), and has one interception. Special Teams MVP: Michael Dickson For anyone watching Seahawks games, a huge piece of the team’s success comes from their All-Pro punter who makes pinning the opposing team’s offense inside their own ten-yard line look easy. Dickson has a 42.8 net average this season, and has 15 punts inside the 20 with only two touchbacks. Thanks to Dickson’s toolbelt of different kicks, Seattle has been able to get two turnovers off of muffed punts, and only allowed eight returns for 39 yards all season long. Top newcomer: Emanuel Wilson Entering the 2026 season the Seahawks only had a few newcomers outside of the draft. The biggest names included Emanuel Wilson, Dante Fowler Jr., Rodney Thomas II, and Trevon Diggs. Considering the last two are currently on the practice squad, and Fowler Jr. only got his first sack this last week against the Arizona Cardinals, it makes this honor a little easier to give. That shouldn’t be taken as a knock on Wilson, however. The Seahawks running game has struggled mightily throughout the 2026 season, thanks to injuries. However, the one player who helped keep the boat afloat was Wilson. Despite his noticeable lack of speed and agility, Wilson was still able to deliver big blows to defenders with his physical running style. This bruising ability really helped Seattle run the ball late in games. Take for example, Wilson was able to seal the victory over the Arizona Cardinals in week two with 92 rushing yards. Wilson was also able to show this ability in his 100-yard game against the Kansas City Chiefs in week 7. Wilson currently leads the team in rushing yards (403) and rushing touchdowns (3). Best relief performance: Drew Lock The Seahawks have enjoyed multiple great relief performances, such as Rodney Thomas II filling in for the injury-marred safety room early in the season, and recently with Josh Jones filling in for left tackle Charles Cross. However, the most important position in football still is the quarterback. Lock is currently undefeated on the season, beating the New England Patriots in Week 1, and beating the Arizona Cardinals in Weeks 2 and 8. In these three games, Lock has completed 71.1 percent of his passes, for 597 yards, five touchdowns and zero turnovers. Lock has a 116.0 passer rating. This passer rating would lead the NFL if he had enough attempts to qualify. The way Lock is performing has created a quarterback controversy in some fan’s eyes. Although it will be shocking to see the Seahawks start Lock over a healthy Sam Darnold, it will be interesting to see how each quarterback plays the rest of the season. Lock’s contract expires after 2026, could he perform well enough to make John Schneider consider keeping him over Darnold into 2027? Best Play on offense: Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba vs. Arizona 82-YARD TOUCHDOWN BY JSN 🗣️ What a way to start the game. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/BaEWTfOWWj — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 20, 2026 The Seahawks best play on offense goes to their longest scrimmage play of the season, an 82-yard touchdown from Lock to JSN. This huge touchdown happened on the second play from scrimmage in the week two victory over the Arizona Cardinals and essentially ended the game for Arizona just as it began. This early lead allowed Emanuel Wilson and the run game to take over and keep the Cardinals out of arms reach for the rest of the game. Best Play on defense: Nick Emmanwori pressures Patrick Mahomes into Ty Okada interception THAT'S TY'S BALL 🔥 @tyokada 's first INT of the season. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/VI76EKHkC4 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 The game against the Kansas City Chiefs felt a lot closer than the final score would lead you to believe. At one point in the game when the Chiefs were driving (potentially to tie or go up on the Seahawks’ 3-0 lead), Nick Emmanwori, lined up as a linebacker, used his elite closing speed to hit quarterback Patrick Mahomes and force him into an errant pass that was intercepted by safety Ty Okada. Although this play itself was very impressive, this honor felt like a way for the Seahawks to give an honor to Nick Emmanwori as well. And who can blame them? Emmanwori has been an elite chess piece for Mike Macdonald. His performance against the Chiefs may have been the most impressive performance of the star safety’s young career. Best Play on Special Teams: Michael Dickson and Nehemiah Pritchett team up to create a turnover vs. 49ers Would ya look at that 💥 @King_Mighty1 pic.twitter.com/7y1RFD4KJT — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 11, 2026 With the Seahawks having no return touchdowns this season, it makes sense to give this honor to a forced turnover made by the Special teams. As mentioned above, Michael Dickson has forced two turnovers with his various styles of kicks. In the week 5 loss to the 49ers, Dickson created one of these turnovers against 49ers returner Jacob Cowing. Cowing muffed the catch and when attempting to recover his muff was thumped by Nehemiah Pritchett, allowing Eric Saubert to recover the ball. Although this is an impressive play by Dickson, Pritchett, and Saubert, it will be disappointing if the team cannot improve on this play later this season. With Rashid Shaheed returning from injury soon, it will be interesting to see if he can house a return to the house. Or perhaps Tory Horton, or Jadarian Price can assist in housing a return as well. Trend to Continue: Overall strong play on defense This Seahawks team would arguably be nowhere without their defensive performance all season long (no disrespect to MVP candidate, JSN). Seahawks.com does a great job at lining up all of the defensive stats below: “Through nine games, the Seahawks rank first in total defense (244.2 yards per game) and passing defense (155.1), second in opponent yards per carry average (3.4),…

title: 49ers checked in on veteran Eagles tight end; Mac Jones asking price was too rich for the Vikings
summary: Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport had a trade notebook, recapping everything related to the deadline. In the article, there’s a section dedicated to San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones: The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones. When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport had a trade notebook , recapping everything related to the deadline. In the article, there’s a section dedicated to San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones: The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones . When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done. Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers. This was not the first time the teams had spoken about Jones in a possible trade and not the first time San Francisco had set a price that high. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback and would trade him only for a deal they had no choice but to accept. To add to that value, Jones won four of his first five starts in place of the injured Brock Purdy last year despite battling injuries of his own and ended up with a 5-3 record and a QB rating of 97.4 for the season. In the final year of his two-year, $8.41 million contract, Jones is a free agent after the season. The 49ers must feel pretty confident that Jones will sign a big enough contract this offseason to net the team at least a third-round compensatory pick. If you’re the 49ers, it’s wise to make a team you could face in the playoffs overpay for a quarterback. It might have been a different story if another team had inquired about Jones. Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert was on the 49ers’ radar: While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted — Dallas Goedert . Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027. Goedert has lined up as an inline tight end 48.7% of the time this year, compared to 38.1% in the slot. I think these moves tell us the 49ers were looking to get another big body to pair with George Kittle, who they can throw the ball to. He’s been a serviceable blocker, but Luke Farrell only has six targets this season. Goedert had six targets in Week 9.

title: 49ers Mailbag: Playoffs, parity, and Connor Colby
summary: Well, it’s always funnier when the 49ers beat the Cowboys. And it’s always better when we have a mailbag before a 49ers game. So I found out I have this nifty little tool that lets me link your comments to my Niners Nation Feed post directly. It’s pretty neat, so I’m using it for this. […]
full_text: Fans watch from the stands as the Arizona Cardinals play the San Francisco 49ers at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Nov. 16, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Well, it’s always funnier when the 49ers beat the Cowboys . And it’s always better when we have a mailbag before a 49ers game. So I found out I have this nifty little tool that lets me link your comments to my Niners Nation Feed post directly. It’s pretty neat, so I’m using it for this. Our mailbag requests come during the week in The Feed . I go through comments, good and/or bad, and pick a few to respond to. Those I don’t respond to are probably because I don’t have a witty-enough response or something I simply didn’t have time for (the final 53-man roster at season’s end is a great question, but I don’t even want to rack my brain on that one). Basically, it’s not you, it’s me. All you need to do is see my mailbag post on The Feed and then make a comment about what we should talk about! We had a lot of questions this week. I’ll try to answer some of them: I don’t mind parity; I do think it’s being taken a biiiiit too far, however. I’m against a top team having a first pick in the draft—that’s where you get all the NBA controversies with lotteries and such. That said NBA draft “lottery” was originally implemented to prevent all-out tanking, but somehow elite prospects get picked up by specific teams, defying the odds. Here’s what I WOULD like. I agree with your salary cap worries, but I don’t think it should be removed—instead, adjusted. Several companies that have remote workers adjust salaries based on cost of living. For example, I live in Seattle, Washington, so my salary for a position would be significantly higher than someone living in Jackpot, Nevada. I think income tax can be a key decision-maker for players, and teams that have to deal with income taxes should adjust accordingly. Washington has no income tax; California does. So adjust the salary cap accordingly based on the tax structure of that team’s state. How do you do this? I have no idea. I am the worst at numbers. My other suggestion for the salary cap is that for any player drafted by a team who accrues x years on that team and is up for an extension, a percentage of their new deal doesn’t count against the salary cap. This lets them get the deal they want without crippling the team. This also rewards teams for drafting well rather than penalizing them. It’s like a franchise tag you can use once a year on a newly signed contract. Oftentimes, players don’t want to leave their team, but the business side of things gets in the way, and the team can only offer so much. Having a rule like this in effect would create roster consistency and ensure the talent gets the salary they deserve. You can go even further, like any pick in the second round-on, while the first round has the fifth-year option. The whole idea is that teams are rewarded for investing their resources and time into a prospect rather than the player’s contract being up and priced out of whatever team wants to keep them. Probably the Minnesota Vikings now that Kirk Cousins is back. I’m still traumatized by his last game against the 49ers in the purple back in 2023. Cousins went 35-for-45 (77 percent completions), for 378 yards, two touchdowns, and a single interception. You know that game better for this stupid Steve Wilks call . This game was where the murmurs of Wilks’ incompetence pretty much spilled out into screaming rants. After this game, he left the booth and came to the sidelines to call games. You know how that season turned out. Yes, the 49ers went to the Super Bowl, but those defensive formations, man. So looking back, Kirk Cousins back on the Vikings scares me. If not for that trade this week, I’d probably lean towards the Chicago Bears, but the Vikings are my pick. I don’t get it at this point. He’s reinstated, and the 49ers have two weeks. I’ve been on the 49ers’ side for all of this until right now, when I’m wondering why they just don’t cut the cord. My guess is they don’t want to cut him and have him go to a team they may face in two weeks. I doubt he’s in football shape, but I also wonder what he could give the Seahawks and/or Vikings if he signed with them. Keeping him for two weeks makes any signing more of a crunch. But then he could go to the Rams? I just don’t know what the 49ers are doing right now. Get it over with already. Here’s a nice stat that will help you figure this out: Pressures allowed by the 49ers OL this season: Connor Colby: 23 (58.1 pass-block grade) Dominick Puni: 11 (84.7) Colton McKivitz: 9 (75.6) Trent Williams: 8 (87.6) Jake Brendel: 8 (80.3) We have a major problem at left guard pic.twitter.com/F3K1uxSVdy — Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) November 9, 2026 58.1…yet somehow the 49ers are still standing. I think Colby is surrounded by talent (hey there, Colton McKivitz), but he’s clearly the weak link of the offensive line at left guard. The rest of the line has been doing a fine job. Now that said, can he get better? I think so. This is only his second season, and it’s still an improvement over last year. If the 49ers look to add another guard in the draft (one can wish upon a star), I hope they lock up Dominick Puni so they have some consistency on that line. I don’t think Colby is horrible (remember Erik Pears? THAT was bad), but we need to see how he develops for the rest of the year. The last thing we need is Jeffery Simmons lined up against him in the playoffs. I’d say the 2023 team was maybe more balanced—once they figured their decorum out. The 2023 team had that losing streak to the Vikings and Bengals and looked awful. I don’t know what they did to turn it around, but whatever it was, it got them to the Super Bowl. The issue with the 2023 team was defensive coaching (Steve Wilks was defensive coordinator) and Brock Purdy’s inexperience (which he mitigated well). The 2026 team is balanced, but I need to see more from the defense. I don’t mind the pass rush having a hard time sacking the quarterback, so long as the secondary is making pass-catchers pay for catching the ball. Sure, the Raiders had dial-a-turnovers against the 49ers, but that’s an anomaly. A lot of those turnovers (like the end zone fumble) are simply not going to happen most of the time. The stats will tell me otherwise, as the 49ers defense is one of the better defenses in the league (especially against the run), but both the Falcons game and the Raiders game have me questioning the pass rush. Since we got Nick Bosa back and DeForest Buckner returned, I hope that changes as things gel. That sounds like something El Shorts would do. I wonder what ever happened to that guy? He was a good dude. Whichever one eliminates the team that is the worst matchup for the 49ers. The Minnesota Vikings did the 49ers fans a favor in 2019 by knocking the New Orleans Saints out, and that was the team I thought would give the 49ers the most headaches (though the Saleh defense showed itself against the Packers at the end). If I have to look at what’s there, I’d probably just enjoy Giants-Vikings and watching the Giants knock the Vikings out. Since the NFC East is not very good this year, that would provide some pretty good comedy. As far as a game, Bears-Packers would be great, since it removes one of the threats to the 49ers. Then again, Bears-Rams would be nice, but I don’t know who I’d want to win that one. So specifically wide receivers, I’m going to go with De’Zhaun Stribling, Mike Evans, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Deebo Samuel, and Keenan Allen. I think once Stribling is good to go and Evans returns to the field, Jacob Cowing could be the odd man out. I’d put Cooks on punt returns and Watkins/Samuel on Kickoff returns. I think we’ve seen what Cowing is capable of, and all I see is bad decisions, bad ball security, and quitting on plays (like Brock Purdy’s interception against the Falcons ). He’s been with the team long enough (drafted in 2024) and there…

McKivitz vs. Crosby is independent of that.” 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys “Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn’t make you totally at ease,” Shanahan said of Williams. “Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that’s enough time for him to be all right.” 49ers vs. Cowboys: The Standard’s 5 fast predictions (paywall) “ Kawakami: 49ers 31, Cowboys 24 .
