title: 49ers-Cowboys preview: Christian McCaffrey and the Niners should run wild
summary: History will lead you in the right direction more often than not. The head-to-head matchups between the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys have been one-sided. It’s why it’s a rivalry in name only. How the 49ers have fared against the NFC East and the Cowboys versus the NFC West is more evidence of what […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images History will lead you in the right direction more often than not. The head-to-head matchups between the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys have been one-sided. It’s why it’s a rivalry in name only. How the 49ers have fared against the NFC East and the Cowboys versus the NFC West is more evidence of what to expect this coming Sunday. The Niners have been terrific in that regard, while Dallas has gone 2-5 in their previous seven games — including a loss to the Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew-led Cardinals, in a game in which they allowed 30 points. Let’s preview Week 10’s matchup to see whether Dak Prescott can keep pace with Brock Purdy. What to expect when the 49ers have the ball Purdy is 3-0 in his career against the Cowboys. His fourth start against Dallas might be the biggest mismatch, at least on this side of the ball, to date. The 49ers are top-three offensively in points per game, EPA per pass, EPA per rush, passing and rushing success rate, and in third-down and red-zone efficiency. Conversely, the Cowboys are bottom-five or worst in total yards and rushing yards per game, EPA per play and rush, sacks per game, and third-down efficiency. Dallas’s saving grace on this side of the ball is that they are sixth in turnover EPA per game. Down-to-down, they’ve been lousy. The Cowboys give up a league-high 35.2 yards per opponent possession. After a mid-season quarterback change, Arizona had drives of 70, 80, 58, and 90 yards before a 44-yard game-winning field goal drive in overtime. Atrocious against the run inside Quinnen Williams is one of the NFL’s best interior linemen. He’s the ultimate disruptor. Williams leads all defensive tackles with 14 tackles for loss—five more than Jeffery Simmons. His five sacks are tied for third. The 18 run stops are tied for third. Yet, for whatever reason, the Cowboys have been abysmal against the inside run. When you watch them, the issues stem from getting moved at the point of attack. Ball carriers aren’t getting touched until they cross the line of scrimmage. The eye test matches the stats: Dallas allows the second-most yards before contact per carry this season, at 1.78 yards. They get moved, easily, despite having played only two offenses in the top-15 in rushing success rate. The 49ers are running more and more inside the tackles. They’re running inside zone at a 19.1% clip, a slight increase from a year ago. This game sets up well for the Niners to keep attacking the Cowboys’ A and B gaps. Kyle Shanahan had to be grinning as he watched the 36-play reel of the Cowboys’ defense defending —a term used loosely—inside zone. They allowed 8.08 yards per carry. Seven of those 36 plays went for double digits. They allowed a 58.3% success rate. You could build the case that the 49ers aren’t running inside enough this season. Christian McCaffrey had two 11-yard runs on inside zone last week. McCaffrey has 24 inside zone carries this year and averages 5.04 yards per carry, with a 62.5% success rate. Add in the different motions and window dressing, and it’s tough to see the defense that allowed the best rushing attack (Tampa Bay) its face this season to run for 241 yards slow down the 49ers. Trent Williams injured his shoulder in practice and is questionable. Veteran Vederian Lowe would take Williams’ place if he cannot suit up. As big a loss as that would be for the 49ers, the Cowboys are 29th in stuff rate. They do not get stops on the ground. Their linebackers get caught up in the wash, creating massive rushing lanes. Where can Brock Purdy attack the Cowboys? The Cowboys allow a good amount of chunk plays through the air. They’re 27th in EPA per pass. They’re also 25th in passing success rate. Watching Daniel Jones forgo intermediate passes last week for underneath throws was maddening. Receivers were open. They just weren’t targeted. How has Dallas held up against elite passing offenses? C.J. Stroud threw for 347 yards. Nico Collins and Jaylin Noel each had over 85 receiving yards. Jordan Love threw for 276 yards. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combined for nine catches and 168 yards. No Mike Evans again for the 49ers, but this should not be a defense where the Niners need their No. 1 target. The Cowboys don’t create negative plays. What Purdy will see this week compared to next is the polar opposite—the Cowboys blitz 20.2% of the time, the second-lowest mark in the league. In theory, Purdy should have plenty of time to scan the field and pick Dallas apart. It’s a Vic Fangio-adjacent defense, so the Cowboys will do all they can to take away the middle of the field and funnel targets to lower-percentage areas, like outside the numbers. Jordan Watkins has ten targets in the previous two games. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. looks set to return from injury and will look to slow down Watkins hot streak. The rookie will be on the radar Rookie Caleb Downs is the player the Niners could find success against. He’s primarily played nickel. Against the Texans, Packers, and Cardinals, Downs allowed all 9 of his targets to be completed for 147 yards. Heading into Week 9, Downs had allowed a 90.5% completion percentage, which was the third-highest among slot cornerbacks this season. He has one pass breakup. Dallas tried to align him closer to the line of scrimmage, almost like a pseudo-linebacker in coverage against Arizona. He played linebacker 32.1% of the time against the Cardinals. But now he’s facing an offense that thrives over the middle. Downs has nowhere to hide against the Niners. Old friend Kendrick Bourne caught a slant on Downs, broke a tackle, and gained a bunch of yards en route to a 29-yard gain. Downs was no match for Trey McBride on a 3rd-and-6 target— hello, George Kittle. Downs is not a big player. He’s 5’11”, 206 pounds, but has a 10th percentile arm length. That shows up in contested situations when he can’t make plays on the ball. Savion Williams from the Packers got Downs a couple of times on in-breaking routes. Watson and Golden each had a double-digit reception against Watkins on an out route on third down. He would’ve allowed two first-down receptions on third down last week to the Colts, but his brother dropped the ball both times. You better believe the rookie will be on the 49ers’ radar. Whether it’s the No. 1, 2, or slot receiver, the Cowboys are bottom-three in yards after the catch allowed per reception. The No. 2 third-down offense meets the 32nd third-down defense. The No. 1 red zone offense meets the No. 25 red zone defense. Dallas also has six more defensive penalties than the 31st-placed team. On paper, the only thing stopping the 49ers from scoring in this game is the 49ers. Outside of Quinnen Williams, this defense has zero redeeming qualities. Will the Cowboys fumble the game away like the Raiders? The 49ers forced five turnovers, masking the Raiders’ six potential scoring drives. Luck plays a role in every turnover. To date, the Cowboys are 22nd in turnover EPA lost per game on offense. They make mistakes. Look no further than last week when Dak Prescott fumbled on third down, or CeeDee Lamb fumbled going into score. Fred Warner and the Niners defense have a penchant for the peanut punch. They’re sixth this year at forcing fumbles, thanks in large part to the soon-to-be Defensive Player of the Year. Most potent offense the 49ers have faced to date Starting cornerbacks Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir practiced Friday for the first time. Nate Hobbs practiced in full and could make his debut, especially with Upton Stout banged up. It’ll be all hands on deck to slow down the most potent offense on the schedule yet. Raheem Morris has been a godsend for this organization. He’s developed a scheme that is third at limiting explosive plays and fifth in yards per attempt. The biggest surprise is the 49ers being first in EPA per rush this season. Warner plays a significant role in limited targets over the middle. Teams are terrified…

summary: The San Francisco 49ers’ final injury report was released. As expected, Mike Evans was ruled out with an Achilles injury. The following players are questionable: CB Renardo Green (back)CB Deommodore Lenoir (foot)CB Upton Stout (shoulder)DT CJ West (ankle)CB Nate HobbsLT Trent Williams (shoulder)LB Dre Greenlaw (knee) Kyle Shanahan said Williams hurt his shoulder and Greenlaw […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers’ final injury report was released. As expected, Mike Evans was ruled out with an Achilles injury. The following players are questionable: CB Renardo Green (back) CB Deommodore Lenoir (foot) CB Upton Stout (shoulder) DT CJ West (ankle) CB Nate Hobbs LT Trent Williams (shoulder) LB Dre Greenlaw (knee) Kyle Shanahan said Williams hurt his shoulder and Greenlaw hurt his knee during Thursday’s practice. Shanahan wouldn’t give a concrete answer about the concern level surrounding Williams. “Any time you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn’t make you totally at ease. Sunday comes fast. But hopefully, that’s enough time for him to be all right.” Shanahan said Evans’ recovery is “going well.” He added, “I’m sure if it was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals, so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction.” Shanahan said “there’s a chance” Evans can return next week, but he wasn’t sure yet. Keenan Allen “had a good week” of practice and “will have a role” Sunday against the Cowboys. How big of a role that is remains to be seen. Deebo Samuel is “healthy.” Shanahan said he’s a full go. For at least a week, the 49ers will have Samuel, Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing at receiver. The 49ers worked out a right-footed punter, but Shanahan said that was more for Cowing, the punt returner. “Just the spin of the ball. Always seeing it turn one way. And then you get into a game, and it’s turning the other way. It’s similar with deep balls. When you catch from a left-handed quarterback and go to a right-handed quarterback. It’s the same with punts. Catching punts is one of the hardest things in sports. You can’t get enough work of it.” Corliss Waitman, the Niners punter, is left-footed. The Cowboys ruled out pass rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku, tight end Jake Ferguson, running back Tyler Goodson, and safety P.J. Locke.

title: Why the Cowboys matchup could be difficult for the 49ers this weekend
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the road for a storied rivalry game against the Dallas Cowboys this weekend, as they look to improve to 8-1 after a blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders. San Francisco entered the week as 1.5-point underdogs, but the lines have shifted drastically, with the 49ers now being 3.5-point […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Deommodore Lenoir #2 of the San Francisco 49ers runs onto the field for the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the road for a storied rivalry game against the Dallas Cowboys this weekend, as they look to improve to 8-1 after a blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders. San Francisco entered the week as 1.5-point underdogs, but the lines have shifted drastically, with the 49ers now being 3.5-point favorites ahead of game day. The Cowboys do have several players injured, including cornerback Joey Porter Jr., but it looks like they’ll have star receiver George Pickens back after he started the week with two limited practices. Meanwhile, San Francisco could be without Deommodore Lenoir, Mike Evans, and Renardo Green, as the trio did not practice at all on Wednesday or Thursday. Evans was expected to miss another week, but losing both cornerbacks is a big deal, especially against a Cowboys offense looking to throw the ball. So, it’s not a surprise that the game total is sky-high at 55.5 points, with oddsmakers expecting fireworks from both offenses. San Francisco did re-sign cornerback Jack Jones to the practice squad this week after releasing him a few weeks ago. While Jones had some positive moments this season, he had really struggled before getting cut by the 49ers, and it wasn’t clear that he was going to return. But with the injuries, he could be called upon to play quickly. “I don’t think there’s ever an understanding he’s coming back,” Morris said of re-signing Jones. “This league is, we know this league, we’ve all been in it long enough, covered it long enough, done whatever, but I do think Jack Jones handled himself the right way. He was accountable to the things that he did wrong. I was accountable to the things that I could help him out to do better, so when he left, he left on great terms. When you leave a place on great terms, you always have an opportunity to come back when something presents itself. “So last week, an opportunity presented itself and I think him coming back with a different vibe about himself and a different perspective gives him the best chance. I think that’s the only way you can handle failure and the only way to get improvement is to have a little bit of failure. I look forward to what he can do and how he can help us if it’s possible and got a lot of confidence in what he was able to do before that too as well.” Well, Jones will have to handle that failure quickly, as he gets a very tough matchup this weekend going up against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The 49ers defense has graded out well by a number of metrics this season, but they are now banged up in the secondary with Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green’s statuses in question. That’s why this matchup against the Cowboys could be a tougher one than expected for the 49ers. And it gets tougher from here, as the 49ers play the Vikings, Seahawks, Giants, and Rams over their next four games. This five-game stretch will tell us a lot about San Francisco, which remains the top contender to make the Super Bowl from the NFC. Starting that stretch off with a win would be huge, but that means some players from the secondary, be it Jones or Nate Hobbs or even Ephesians Prysock, will have to step up on Sunday.

title: Which 49ers could be All-Pros in 2026?
summary: As the midseason mark approaches, we’re seeing some of the top award races in the NFL start to take shape, and the San Francisco 49ers definitely have a few worthy players in a couple of different spots. Of course, there’s Brock Purdy, who was the MVP frontrunner a few weeks ago and remains playing at […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 8: Tre Tucker #1 of the Las Vegas Raiders carries the ball against Fred Warner #54 of the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the midseason mark approaches, we’re seeing some of the top award races in the NFL start to take shape, and the San Francisco 49ers definitely have a few worthy players in a couple of different spots. Of course, there’s Brock Purdy, who was the MVP frontrunner a few weeks ago and remains playing at a high level, while leading a 7-1 49ers team. San Francisco also has a number of other stars who continue to be among the NFL’s best, which is why the team has regularly sent several players to the Pro Bowl every year. But which 49ers are excelling at the top of their position to be a potential All-Pro in 2026? At the midseason mark, let’s take a look at who could be in some of the award races and who could earn an All-Pro this year. ESPN’s Bill Barnwell compiled his midseason awards, which followed his quarter-season awards a few weeks back. Back then, Purdy was his No. 1 candidate for MVP. Now, he’s still in the mix, but at No. 2. “As a positive play machine, Purdy was my MVP pick after four games, having thrown one interception while taking zero sacks through one month,” Barnwell wrote. “That’s no longer the case, with Purdy throwing four picks and taking eight sacks over the ensuing four games, including San Francisco’s first and only loss of the season at Atlanta. A bad Purdy interception with 2:42 to go and a chance to take the lead sealed it for the Falcons. “Of course, Purdy is still running the league’s lowest sack rate at 3.3%. And in terms of creating good plays, he leads the league in QBR and EPA per dropback. He’s also No. 1 in success rate as a passer. And though Allen understandably gets plenty of attention as the league’s most significant running quarterback, Purdy isn’t far behind. He has been a valuable short-yardage option this season, with his 23 first downs as a runner ranking second behind Allen. He’s third in rushing EPA behind Allen and Drake Maye. “Purdy’s numbers often get discounted by virtue of his offensive infrastructure, which is stocked with playmakers and operated by Kyle Shanahan. Though the 49ers have still had George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey on the field all season, and Mike Evans in the lineup for most of the season, Purdy deserves more of the credit for being the guy driving the offense. More than a third of his pass attempts have gone to players such as Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and Demarcus Robinson, and Purdy has made them look good in the process. Evans looked revitalized after a down season (amid injuries) in Tampa Bay in 2025. [Trevor] Lawrence and Purdy would both be legitimate MVP picks. I just lean ever so slightly toward the guy in Cincinnati being the best in football.” Joe Burrow’s numbers have been ridiculous this year, and the Bengals are winning. So it makes sense that he’s the MVP favorite midway through the season. But a couple of years after being on the MVP ballot, Purdy has a legitimate shot at being an All-Pro this year. Christian McCaffrey will always be an All-Pro candidate, especially with the all-purpose spot, but it would be hard for him to earn the All-Pro honor at running back with the years Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker are having. Those are the two Barnwell put on his midseason ballot. However, Barnwell does have George Kittle as a first-team All-Pro at tight end, with Trey McBride coming in second. Kittle remains the best all-around tight end in football, as he does so much as a blocker. However, it feels like a part of this is because Brock Bowers was hurt for a few games earlier in the season, and with how statistics play into things, that might change by the end of the year. Still, Kittle is firmly in that top three this year and could very well earn another All-Pro honor. Trent Williams has looked like the best lineman in football this year, which is incredible at age 38. He was Barnwell’s pick for Protector of the Year at the quarter-season mark and now at the midway point of the season as well. He’s a clear contender for an All-Pro honor this year. An underrated name at guard is Dominick Puni, who is quietly enjoying a very strong third season. He’s the second-best player on one of the top offensive lines in the NFL, and has continued to ascend as one of the best right guards in the NFL. He wasn’t on Barnwell’s ballot, but with four guard spots on the All-Pro list, he could very well earn some votes this season. On the defensive side, Fred Warner is a true contender for Defensive Player of the Year. Barnwell had him second behind Will Anderson, who is having a monster season for the Houston Texans. It’s incredible considering he’s coming off a major injury. “I mentioned the five forced fumbles earlier, which is something we aren’t supposed to see from off-ball linebackers. Those are the biggest plays Warner has made, but the future Hall of Famer has just been spectacularly efficient on a down-to-down basis,” Barnwell wrote. “He has made tackles on 20% of running plays, the second-best rate among starting linebackers. “And then, of course, there’s no better linebacker in pass coverage in the league. Warner does a better job of taking away potential throws than any other linebacker, both by reading what quarterbacks are hoping to do and by running with potential receivers in coverage. His play somehow has not slipped after he dislocated his ankle a year ago. The 49ers are the league’s second-best defense by QBR against play-action throws to the middle, where teams are trying to move linebackers and throw behind them for big gains. Warner is the reason those throws aren’t working.” Warner is a clear All-Pro candidate and remains the best linebacker in football. Those are all the main candidates for the 49ers, but they could realistically have six All-Pro players this season, with some fighting for bigger awards as well. Brock Purdy is in the MVP race. Trent Williams is in the Protector of the Year race. Kyle Shanahan could win Coach of the Year. Fred Warner or George Kittle could be Comeback Player of the Year after coming back from injury. And Warner could win Defensive Player of the Year. There’s been a lot of impressive performances for the 49ers this season.

title: The 49ers are producing at historic rate in one key category
summary: The San Francisco 49ers offense has been humming this season, being in the top five in most efficiency metrics, as well as points per game, thanks to another strong play-calling year from Kyle Shanahan and an MVP-level season from Brock Purdy. Over the years, one area the 49ers have really excelled in has been the […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers looks to pass while scrambling with the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers offense has been humming this season, being in the top five in most efficiency metrics, as well as points per game, thanks to another strong play-calling year from Kyle Shanahan and an MVP-level season from Brock Purdy. Over the years, one area the 49ers have really excelled in has been the red zone. When the 49ers are clicking there, they’re usually winning games. Back during their Super Bowl campaign in 2023, San Francisco led the NFL in red zone touchdown percentage, converting over two-thirds of their opportunities. During the team’s down year in 2024, they dropped all the way to 14th. Last year, they jumped back into the top five, converting over 65 percent of their red zone drives into touchdowns. Well, this season, not only are the 49ers scoring in the red zone as they’ve been accustomed to, but they’re doing it at a historic rate. So far, the 49ers have converted a whopping 84.6 percent of their red zone drives into touchdowns this season, topping the second-highest team by over 12 percent. They’re still averaging 3.3 red zone drives a game as well. What has been the difference-maker there so far? “One, I think we’ve been pretty effective running the ball down there,” offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said about the red zone. “I think anytime you look at red zone offense, it’s got to start with running the football. When you can run the ball effectively, when you’re not in tough passing situations in the red zone, you’re usually a pretty good red zone team. You get to more goal-to-go situations. You get into second-and-short, you get into third-and-manageable and it’s things you can manage. It’s things you can execute. “When you’re in third-and-long in the red zone or second-and-long, it’s hard. There’s not a lot of space. You just run out of room. We run the ball pretty well. It helps having Mike Evans out there, a guy who’s a big target, who’s a fade target, who you can win in isolations. That’s been big for us. It helps to have a scrambling quarterback, a guy who can make plays with his legs. When you combine those things, I think it’s maybe why we’ve had success, but we’ve got to keep going. We’ve got to keep doing it. We’ve got to try to study it every week, put in the right plans, give our guys a chance to execute and keep running the ball down there.” In the air, George Kittle has been a weapon in the red zone, ranking eighth in the NFL with eight catches in the area for 51 yards and three touchdowns. He’s third in receptions inside the 10-yard line with five catches for 16 yards and three touchdowns. Of course, Mike Evans has been a big help there, not only as a big receiver commanding space, but in freeing up other things as well. And Christian McCaffrey is third in the NFL in red zone rushing touchdowns. The 49ers will likely regress a bit from their historic touchdown rate right now, but they’re executing at a really high level in the red zone, and their offense is seeing great success because of it.

Here’s a look at the dead cap hit numbers for Buckner through the next few seasons, per Spotrac : 2027 – $5.2m 2028: $3.9m 2029: $2.6m 2030: $1.3m It’ll be interesting to see what kind of extension, if any, both sides work out after this season. title: 3 stats ahead of 49ers-Cowboys: It’ll be the best offense the Niners have faced to date
summary: The San Francisco 49ers look to close out their two-step of long-term rivals with a 2-0 record, trying to follow up a win over the Las Vegas Raiders with a road win against the Dallas Cowboys. Sunday will renew the iconic NFL rivalry, with Week 10 marking the first matchup between the two teams since […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers look to close out their two-step of long-term rivals with a 2-0 record, trying to follow up a win over the Las Vegas Raiders with a road win against the Dallas Cowboys. Sunday will renew the iconic NFL rivalry, with Week 10 marking the first matchup between the two teams since the 49ers topped the Cowboys in a Week 8 Sunday Night Football game in 2024. A win on Sunday would mark the 49ers’ first five-game winning streak against Dallas (including playoffs) for the first time since San Francisco won six in a row from 1981 through 1990. If San Francisco hopes to extend the streak, these are the three numbers to know: 8/4/26 Targets/receptions/yards. Keenan Allen finished Week 9 with four receptions on eight targets for 26 yards. Keenan Allen will likely do something that doesn’t happen often in the NFL: play back-to-back weeks against the same opponent. Which means we have a rare window into just how Allen will do in his 49ers debut by looking at how he fared against Dallas. With Allen acquired on Tuesday, it’s hard to imagine he’d play more than 36 snaps, as he did against Dallas last week, but he has two things working in his favor that he didn’t have in Week 9: he’s obviously the 49ers’ No. 1 receiver, and he has Brock Purdy as his quarterback. While Allen is the Colts’ leader in targets, he shared passes with new Chief Josh Downs. And while Demarcus Robinson plays his second game from injury, it’s safe to assume Allen will be WR1 while he’s on the field in Dallas. I don’t think I really need to get into how Purdy is an upgrade over Jones. It’s certainly a unique week for Allen to face the same opponent twice in as many weeks, but I am sure he won’t complain about another chance against the poor Dallas defense. 26.2 Points per game. The Cowboys defense has allowed 26.2 points per game, seventh-worst in the league. For the fifth time this season, the 49ers face a defense in the bottom 10 in scoring through nine weeks. Last week, they faced the worst scoring defense in the league, the Las Vegas Raiders. The 49ers’ previous four matchups against bottom-10 scoring defenses are as follows: Week 2 versus Miami (23rd-ranked scoring defense) – 35 points Week 3 versus Arizona (31st) – 36 Week 6 versus Washington (24th) – 23 Week 8 versus Las Vegas (32nd) – 38 That’s an average of 33 points per game in four games against bottom-10 defense. Not too bad for the 49ers’ high-powered offense. Unfortunately, 33 points might not be enough against a high-powered Dallas offense, which has scored 33 or more points in three of its eight games, including two of its last three. 49.5 Scoring percentage. The Cowboys offense scores on 49.5 percent of drives, the third-best percentage in the league. And the 49ers haven’t really faced an offense like the one the Cowboys will offer. Just like it was against scoring defenses, last week was the most recent example of the 49ers facing a team like Dallas. The Raiders are the only other top-ten team by scoring percentage San Francisco has faced this season. Entering Week 10, the Raiders offense has scored on 45.4 percent of its drives. The 49ers held them to significantly less than that last week, allowing the Raiders to score a touchdown on two of nine drives. But outside of Las Vegas, the 49ers have exclusively faced below-average scoring offenses. Prior to the Raiders, the 49ers’ previous seven games were against offenses that entered Week 10 with a touchdown percentage less than the league average of 38.9. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb will certainly give the 49ers defense a test on Sunday, but San Francisco handled the pretest that was Las Vegas pretty well. Sunday will be the toughest regular-season test of the season for the 49ers offense.

title: Tyler’s Take – Washington Commanders need a short-yardage package
summary: I was absolutely thrilled to watch the Commanders get the win on Thursday night against the rival Giants on the road in primetime. For as pleased as I was with the effort and fight the team showed, there were some things that still need IMMEDIATE attention! I brought up one of these issues in my […]
full_text: I was absolutely thrilled to watch the Commanders get the win on Thursday night against the rival Giants on the road in primetime. For as pleased as I was with the effort and fight the team showed, there were some things that still need IMMEDIATE attention! I brought up one of these issues in my Studs and Duds article. David Blough’s gameplan looked a LOT different than previous games – IN A GOOD WAY! It actually resembled more Kliff Kingsbury than Ben Johnson with all the shotgun, tempo and chipping to help Brandon Coleman, the weak link on Washington’s offensive line. We still DESPERATELY lack a running game, but Blough did call a few designed runs to Daniels during the game which I liked. The one gripe I have is the series right before the half, when Washington was at the half-yard line. I know Jayden should have scored on the quarterback lead, but RUN THE DAMN BALL WITH YOUR RUNNING BACK! AT THE HALF YARD LINE AND WE WERE IN THE DAMN ‘GUN!!!!! Short Yardage Package: It’s VERY evident, even to the most novice observer, that Washington needs a short-yardage/goal-line “Heavy” package. With Jayden Daniels’ current elbow injury, there is not a fan on this planet (although I believe we have some fans from another galaxy), who want to see our 210-pound signal caller getting RAMMED into a defensive front and pushed forward into a pile of 320-pound immovable objects by 250-plus pound men. Some would suggest using veteran backup Marcus Mariota in this situation, but the 33-year-old has dealt with some injuries of his own this season, and I’d rather not put him in a situation where we could potentially make any of those worse. My Idea: Here me out… A lot of teams have a QB sneak package. We do not. If I’m the coach, I put in McCaffrey or Yankoff as our “Tush Push” quarterback for short yardage/goal line and have both Sinnott and Bates behind him as the pushers Ridiculous we are in gun from the 1/2 yd line! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 14, 2026 Luke McCaffrey: The 6-foot-2 200-pounder was a former 4-star quarterback recruit who committed to play at Nebraska for Scott Frost. He played two seasons in Lincoln before transferring to Rice . He started three games at quarterback in 2021 before being moved to wide receiver in 2022. Colson Yankoff: The 6-4, 225-pound tight end was a former 4-star quarterback recruit for the University of Washington. He ended up redshirting as a freshman, then transferred to UCLA . After sitting out the 2019 campaign per NCAA rules, he switched to wide receiver/running back for the Bruins. Both players have the ability to go under center and take a snap. Both guys are good with the ball in their hands and shouldn’t be viewed as a risk when it comes to ball security in heavy traffic. Each guy has the necessary size and, being former ball carriers themselves (McCaffrey was a very good rushing quarterback), each should possess the necessary ability to see a small crease in the defense and get the necessary yardage to either move the chains or push the ball into the end zone. How Washington should run this: Ideally, this would be implemented by using three tight ends (two of which line up in the backfield as up-backs), with an extra lineman reporting in as eligible and lining up as a tight end. Below you will see how this formation could look. QB: Luke McCaffrey/Colson Yankoff Left TE: Andrew Wylie Right TE: Chig Okonkwo Up-Back (Pusher): Josh Bates Up-Back (Pusher): Ben Sinnott Deep Back: Rachaad White OR Treylon Burks What to name it: The Eagles made this package famous calling it the “Tush Push” OR the “Brotherly Shove”. Washington needs their own verbiage… DC DIVE (yeah, I’m not very good at this) As long as they don’t use a stupid cadence. Then again, “Who let the Hogs out? Oink, oink, oink, oink!” Would be a great troll next time we play the Giants. — RobB407 (@RBenninghove) November 14, 2026 Cadance – Who let the Hogs Out? Oink, oink, oink, oink! Haha Here is where you come in. Design a name for this formation below in the comments section.

Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Commanders could finish ahead of Giants with the same record after Thursday’s win The good news is the Commanders now own the tie-breaker advantage with New York, something that could factor into things down the stretch. By rule, the October tie counts as half a win and half a loss for each team. Head-to-head record is the NFL’s first tiebreaker between two clubs in the same division. If Washington goes 5-3 over its final eight games and New York goes 3-5, both would finish 8-8-1. In a two-team tie, the Commanders would finish ahead of the Giants because they went 1-0-1 against them. Thursday’s win gave Washington that edge, but it still has to erase the two-game gap. That example assumes a two-team tie; a three-team tie involving Dallas would follow the NFL’s separate tiebreaking procedure. Make no mistake: Washington still has to stack wins. After the mini-bye, New York hosts Jacksonville on Sunday, November 22, and the Commanders host Cincinnati the following night. A Giants loss and a Washington win would cut the gap to one game. The teams won’t meet again this season, so the head-to-head edge only matters if the Commanders make up the ground elsewhere. Stefon Diggs with the game winning touchdown for the Washington Commanders.. "That was an amazing play" ~ @OfficialAJHawk #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/1zl8frFEHS — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 13, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Washington Post (paywall) The Commanders got burned and stayed aggressive; it may have saved their season [The Isaiah Likely touchdown] was a major breakdown, but it didn’t change how Jones operated. He maintained an attacking mindset. It proved instrumental in a 24-21 win over New York that may have saved Washington’s season. “The easy thing would be to be nervous in that spot and to back off,” Coach Dan Quinn said. “But he’s aggressive.” The previous time these teams met, Jones had a conservative approach on defense. Washington blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and ultimately settled for a tie . New York ran on its first two plays, forcing Washington to burn a couple of timeouts and setting up a pivotal third and one. The Giants were in an empty formation, but the Commanders had eight players along the line of scrimmage prepared for another blitz. It wound up being a designed run for McCarthy, but a blitzing Styles blew up the play. “Starting with coach DJ, he has confidence in us,” Styles said. “Plays are going to happen. You clean them up. Hopefully, you don’t make the same mistakes, but plays are going to happen. The other team, they make money, too. “But for him to keep that confidence as the game goes on and not pull back, I think it just shows he sees the improvement. He’s getting more and more comfortable with the guys he’s got out there, in terms of us being able to execute on a consistent basis, especially later in the game.” “Defensively, they were not only keeping us in the game,” Quinn said. “I thought they won the game.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE AHHHHHHH @SeatGeek | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/SMbY27tskN — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 13, 2026 Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Athletic (paywall) The biggest thing Jayden Daniels is doing this fall is to stay healthy and keep playing The calls for Quinn’s job won’t completely abate unless and until wins are stacked on top of each other, and this is a group that hasn’t posted back-to-back victories since the playoffs that followed the 2024 season. It’s been a minute. But what has been reestablished over Washington’s past five games — all Daniels starts — is that the quarterback gives them a chance any time they line up, and that it’s not impossible for him to stay healthy for long stretches, even entire seasons, at a time. Did you watch Thursday night and obsess over the brace that’s keeping Daniels’ left elbow in place? Me neither. When Daniels plays, he can build on his own performances. When he gets hurt — and he did miss two September games with that dislocated left elbow — he’s almost starting over, at least at this point in his still-nascent career. In the five games since his return, he has completed 67.3 percent of his throws for 248 yards per game with seven touchdowns and just the two picks. He owns the eighth-best passer rating in the league over that span. Thursday was enormous for the stability of the entire franchise. It’s important that Daniels was at the fulcrum. The winning play didn’t come completely from embattled first-year coordinator David Blough. It was third-and-4 from the Giants’ 32. “I gave a little signal to Stef,” Daniels said, “and he went on a slant — and the rest is history.” For all yall Daniels’ haters—-The Diggs Game Winner HE makes happen. @Commanders @PFTCommenter #nfllive Watch the SIGNAL at the end! pic.twitter.com/FnXRRqYRnV — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) November 13, 2026 The little signal wasn’t by accident. The little signal was developed during the course of the week. Diggs will turn 33 later this month and is in his 12th NFL season. He has seen nearly everything. His impression of Daniels, in that moment, with the season in the balance? “Baby Kobe,” Diggs said, invoking the name of Daniels’ athletic hero. “He’s gonna be the same kind of player he is in the beginning of the game and at the end of games.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE From ESPN: Daniels has played five consecutive games since sitting out two because of a dislocated left elbow. It is the most games he has played in a row since starting all 20 contests in his rookie season. On Thursday, he completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns. But playing that many games consecutively has helped him find a groove, he said. “I’m starting to get into that rhythm,” Daniels said. “It shows the more games you play consistently, the more reps you get, the more flow in the rhythm that you can [find]. And it was tough last year being in and out of the lineup and trying to catch a rhythm.” Being in a rhythm might have helped Daniels on his final throw. When New York showed a cover zero blitz, Daniels gave a signal to Diggs, who ran a slant against corner Dru Phillips and then broke his tackle attempt and sped to the end zone where he turned at the 1, paused and fell backward into the end zone. “He’ll be the same player he is in the beginning of the game as he is in the end of the game,” Diggs said. “Things will happen good and bad and he isn’t going to change.” To read more of this ESPN article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington was last in the NFL on 3rd down; what changed against the Giants? Against the Giants, the Commanders converted 7-of-14 third downs. Six came with one yard to go, including Sinnott’s third-and-goal touchdown. All three of Washington’s touchdowns came on third down. Washington ran the ball 33 times Thursday, gaining 105 yards. Daniels accounted for 11 attempts and 28 yards, and the offense still went 0-for-2 on fourth down. That’s a lot to clean up for a team that needed all three touchdowns to beat New York.…

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 10
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ much-needed 24-21 win over the New York Giants on Thursday night. Daronte Jones learned from his first meeting with the Giants In the first meeting between the Commanders and Giants, Washington’s defense played well in the first half but let New York offensive coordinator Matt Nagy dictate terms in the second. The Giants showed heavy run looks but passed out of these formations to move the ball against the blitz and loaded box looks. In response, Jones went to more basic zone coverage and away from the blitz packages. When Washington’s defense couldn’t generate pressure up front, Giants’ quarterback Jameis Winston started picking them apart. Jones went back to Cover 0 blitzes too late and the Giants capitalized on several coverage lapses in the secondary. Jones kept his foot on the gas in Thursday night’s game, continuing to bring the heat even when the Commanders regained the lead late in the game. While some defensive coordinators would have gone to a prevent defense, Jones continued to overwhelm J.J. McCarthy with blitzes and the pressure generated not one, but two chances for Rasul Douglas to secure an interception to close out the game. After dropping the first, the journeyman cornerback hauled the ball in on the second. Daronte Jones dialing up zero blitzes one after another after another on the final drive. Good for him. Lit McCarthy up with blitzes. Douglas calls game. pic.twitter.com/1SIz5KXEZH — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 13, 2026 While linebackers Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu have received a lot of justifiable praise for their play up front, the Commanders’ revamped secondary and defensive advisor Steve Wilks also deserve tons of credit for holding up behind those blitz packages. Safety Nick Cross failed to get home on a blitz that cost Washington a big play to Isaiah Likely but, for the most part, cornerback Trey Amos and company did a good job of limiting the passing game. That’s especially true of Pro Bowl wide receiver Malik Nabers, who finished the night with 44 receiving yards on five receptions, with most of those coming on a 37-yard completion early in the third quarter. Styles didn’t do all his work at the line of scrimmage, he also supported several coverage packages during the game. The Giants offense did make some plays, but Jones and the Commanders’ defense limited their effectiveness while making a few game-changing plays when needed. Malik Nabers vs WAS DBs • Amik Robertson 7/10 man routes 2 rec / 3 tgts / 34 yds • Nick Cross 1/9 man routes 1 rec / 1 tgt / 6 yds • Trey Amos 7/7 man routes 0 tgts • Rasul Douglas 1/4 man routes 1 tgt / 1 INT • Quan Martin & Jeremy Reaves 1/5 man routes 0 tgts — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) November 13, 2026 Sonny Styles makes this look extremely easy. Navigating a tight trips bunch & staying glued to the hip of the release. pic.twitter.com/2zXdnc50Gv — Last of the Fullbacks (@TheLastFullback) November 13, 2026 David Blough called his best game of the season Rookie offensive coordinator David Blough has understandably been under the microscope lately and for good reason, but he responded with his best offensive plan yet on Thursday night. Blough moved the pocket, utilized chip blocks on the edge and mixed up under center and up-tempo looks. He stuck to the run but wasn’t married to it on early downs, and although there were still some pre-snap penalties, they were reduced. The Commanders committed just four accepted penalties for 17 yards. The net result was more manageable third-down distance. Washington’s offense converted 7-of-14 third downs for an improved 50% conversion rate. When the time came, the play action was also effective, with Blough pairing elements of Kliff Kingsbury’s offense with horizontal concepts that allowed the Commanders’ offense to attack multiple levels of the field. By my count: David Blough called 14 passing plays and 10 running plays on 1st-and-10. 🏈 WSH averaged 6.5 YPP when passing 🏈 Gained 5+ yards on 11 of the 14 dropbacks 🏈 9 of the 10 runs got a total of 25 yards 🏈 They had 0 negative plays on 14 dropacks Not surprisingly:… — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 13, 2026 David Blough use some Kliff stuff but this is all Sean McVay right here. David Blough spacing the LB’s & DB’s horizontally by having them matched up against Antonio Williams in space . Burks inside release to go vertical creates the space too. I wish Kliff did this https://t.co/jbFo6Wvp22 pic.twitter.com/Yw8hXNweQO — Zonerunner (@zonerunner331) November 13, 2026 All this came on the back of the work done up front by Washington’s interior line. After being under fire early this season, Nick Allegretti responded to another starting nod with his best game of the season. According to John Keim and ESPN research , Daniels was pressured on 17.9% of his drop backs Thursday, the second-lowest pressure percentage faced in his career (minimum three dropbacks). More time in the pocket allowed Daniels to build his confidence and get comfortable within the offensive game plan. Was it all perfect? The goal-line series at the end of the first half was certainly questionable, as were the underneath throws to Chig Okonkwo. The important part though, was that Blough checked a lot of the boxes that have been missed for much of the season, and both he and the offensive line should be given full credit this week, with a nod to Ben Sinnott for stepping up when his number was finally called. "I gotta give a lot of love to the Commanders' offensive line." @willcolon66 gives credit to the @Commanders ' big men for their impact on the team's win against the @Giants 🙌 pic.twitter.com/0KWwxUWvzC — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) November 13, 2026 We finally got what we paid for….. The IDEA of what Ben Sinnott could be. Athleticism in the run game and big play ability. pic.twitter.com/nG4F6b0d7H — Deuce_Redzone (@redzoneinthelab) November 13, 2026 Larry Izzo’s special teams came up big in the third phase The Washington Commanders special teams ranked slightly below the league average headed into the game, but Larry Izzo’s squad provided a game-changing performance in Week 10. Drew Stevens’ addition has been one of the big wins of the 2026 season, with the undrafted free agent going 17-for-20 on the season and 13-for-13 from inside 50 yards. His 46-yard field goal early in the second quarter would turn out to be a deciding factor in a game where the Commanders won by three points and Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada missed from 33 yards on his first attempt. Punter Tress Way also had a good night, with four punts for 198 yards for a 49.5 yard average with none bigger than his 49-yard boot from the Commanders own goal line after the offense went three plays for minus-15 yards to start the second half. Kain Medrano got in the mix by punching the ball out on a kick return, but the teams play of the game came from Luke McCaffrey, who made a heads-up play to field a kickoff out of bounds to give the Commanders the ball on their own 40-yard line at the end of the game. There is a reason McCaffrey continues to hold a place on this team. Excellent special teams awareness by the returner! Does this on purpose. If the Commanders come back to win, remember this moment. pic.twitter.com/77mzHyU1ls — Ryan Paganetti (@RyanPaganetti) November 13, 2026 . What does Thursday night’s victory mean for the Commanders? Head coach Dan Quinn was quick to praise the team for getting a much-needed win at MetLife Stadium, and it was great to see both rookie coordinators take a big step forward. The victory kept their season alive.…

title: Commanders Vs. Giants (game two) – Studs and Duds
summary: Washington just may have saved their season on a cold, rainy Thursday night in New Jersey! In a must-win road primetime game, the Commanders came up big at the end against the NFC East-leading Giants to pull off an improbable 24-21 victory! It wasn’t the prettiest of games for three quarters, but the fourth quarter […]
full_text: Washington just may have saved their season on a cold, rainy Thursday night in New Jersey! In a must-win road primetime game, the Commanders came up big at the end against the NFC East-leading Giants to pull off an improbable 24-21 victory ! It wasn’t the prettiest of games for three quarters, but the fourth quarter more than made up for that with play that would wow even the most novice of fans. CRAZY 4th quarter – but feels great to get the WIN! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 The Commanders now sit 3-5-1 on the season and pulled within two games of the Giants for the division lead. They are also 1-0-1 for the season matchup and haven’t lost a game to John Mara’s team since Sept. 7, 2025. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: WR Stefon Diggs: Diggs came up HUGE when Washington needed him the most, splitting the defense late in the fourth quarter and taking it to the house from 32 yards in what turned out to be the game-winning score. He led all Commanders’ receivers with six receptions for 83 yards and the touchdown. Daniels finds Diggs for the 32yd TD! pic.twitter.com/sTH4Ezlq7s — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 LB Frankie Luvu: Luvu was a menace all night, showing up all over the field and making plays. He had some timely blitzes that caused some havoc in the Giants backfield and forced a fumble on Malik Nabers that Jeremy Reaves recovered. Luvu had six tackles, four pressures, a quarterback hit and the forced fumble. Luvu with the Forced Fumble on Nabors. Reaves gets the recovery. HUGE PLAY! pic.twitter.com/avSonPWYnS — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Good coverage on 3rd down by Luvu pic.twitter.com/3ujM4gjgBI — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 TE Ben Sinnott: Seldomly used in the passing game, Sinnott has really become just a glorified H-Back, however he saw an increase in targets when Chig Okonkwo went to the locker room in the first quarter and made the most of them, hauling in four receptions for 42 yards and a touchdown. He also blocked VERY well, especially when helping on the edge. Nice bounce-out by White who picks up 17 pic.twitter.com/8GLxJvmjR9 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Watch Ben Sinnott at the top of the screen clean the ⏰ of the DE😱 pic.twitter.com/Vvju2f7QI4 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 JD finds Sinnott on deep shot pic.twitter.com/Gzn7z6hkTl — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Jayden hits Sinnott for the 1/2 yard score! pic.twitter.com/tswVZoVcyt — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Watch this play by Sinnott – and TELL ME WHY HE DOESN’T GET THE BALL MORE OFTEN pic.twitter.com/nQrMQsN7L6 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 LB Sonny Styles: The rookie is REALLY growing in this defense. He was around the football all evening and made some really nice plays, none bigger than his tackle for a loss on J.J. McCarthy late in the fourth quarter where it looked like he was shot out of a cannon into the Giants’ backfield. That play may have saved the game! My only gripe is he was right there on some pass plays and was just a nano-second from making a play on the ball (however that’s me nitpicking). For the game, he led the team with 13 total tackles (five solo), one tackle for a loss and two pressures . Styles showing the speed! pic.twitter.com/i1iRI132bI — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Styles with the big POP on Scattabo pic.twitter.com/CzlKyoSkme — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Styles is a GD BEAST! pic.twitter.com/EQ3EwpQOeG — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Commanders Interior Offensive Line: Chris Paul, Sam Cosmi and Nick Allegretti were STOUT in the run game and didn’t allow a pressure in pass pro. Allegretti played a pretty clean game at center. He did a nice job adjusting protection and moving to pick up stunts and twists, while keeping his snaps nearly perfect (something Patrick struggled with a bit). Very good game for the interior! HC Dan Quinn: DQ looked in control most of the game and his use of time outs and challenges were nearly perfect. We get on him pretty hard, but he did a nice job Thursday night. Duds: THERE SHALL BE NONE NAMED! Notes: For obvious reasons, Jayden Daniels did not make my studs list, HOWEVER, how he bounced back from those two poorly thrown balls that were intercepted was a thing of beauty. I give him a hell of a lot of credit for that game-defining drive, where he eventually found Diggs for what would become the game-deciding touchdown. That’s what the great ones do. They have short memories when things go bad, and Jayden exemplifies this. KUDOS to him for staying focused and rising to the occasion in a big moment. Poorly thrown ball by Jayden to Chig. His first INT of the season. pic.twitter.com/h8yuK7adac — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 This sack is on Jayden. Gotta know better than this pic.twitter.com/iHXhzYNm3S — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Great throw across his body by Jaden Daniels to Diggs. Love the downfield block by Burks! pic.twitter.com/IOn9kED76h — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 GD 🎯 to Burks pic.twitter.com/leaJZDxZY6 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 I don’t know why WR Antonio Williams wasn’t being targeted more often. When he gets his hands on the football, good things tend to happen. He caught both of his targets for 42 receiving yards, including a 31-yard catch-and-run for a score in the third quarter. Jayden hits Antonio Williams for the TD! Great catch-and-run by the rookie! pic.twitter.com/Gmf8NQ28qD — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 OC David Blough’s gameplan looked a LOT different than previous games – IN A GOOD WAY! It actually resembled more Kliff Kingsbury than Ben Johnson with all the shotgun, tempo and chipping to help Brandon Coleman, the weak link on Washington’s offensive line. We still DESPERATELY lack a running game, but Blough did call a few designed runs to Daniels during the game which I liked. The one gripe I have is the series right before the half, when Washington was at the half-yard line. I know Jayden should have scored on the quarterback lead, but RUN THE DAMN BALL WITH YOUR RUNNING BACK! I will 1000% say I did not like that goal line series right before the half by Blough. Yes, Jayden SHOULD have scored on the QB lead but I HATED the next two plays after that. You need a damn 1/2 yard! How can you not line up and punch it in? Happy we scored, but did NOT agree… — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Blough is either chipping to Coleman’s side or rolling Jayden to his right on pass plays pic.twitter.com/RY5iXkj8AV — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 I see Blough is now chipping to Coleman’s side — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Speaking of LT Brandon Coleman – he did enough to finally get off my Duds list. Yes, he false started AGAIN early in the game and was called for a hold (that was essentially negated by a defensive holding call on the Giants), but he played a LITTLE BIT better overall, and at this point, that is all we can ask of him. CB Amik Robertson did allow some receptions during the game, but he’s SUCH a great competitor and played with effort all night. He had two big tackles for a loss and a pass defended that should have been picked. He’s turned out to be a GREAT signing. Amik nice TFL pic.twitter.com/56gNdVzvH7 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 Amik nearly gets the pick pic.twitter.com/xOC8O6clbe — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 13, 2026 TE Chig Okonkwo and Daniels were not on the same page all evening, and his blocking on some run plays was not up to par. I’m not putting him on the Duds list, but it was not his best game. It was nice to have WR Treylon Burks back.…

title: Commanders News: In 49-second drive, Daniels & Diggs rescue the season
summary: The Daily Slop – 13 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 13 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links goodnight, dmv pic.twitter.com/PETWsZsXul — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 13, 2026 Finished it @budlight | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/qZ5TeASW3u — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 13, 2026 Articles ESPN Commanders QB Jayden Daniels finds redemption with game-winning drive This season, Daniels and the Commanders failed to convert a 2-point conversion in the opener against the Philadelphia Eagles, and Daniels failed to throw the ball away in overtime, preventing a chance for a game-winning field goal. In their previous two losses, the Commanders’ final drive ended in enemy territory. Last week the Commanders failed to throw a pass into the end zone despite reaching the 32-yard line with 8 seconds remaining in a 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The losses led to Daniels being scrutinized and criticized. He told ESPN last week that he was “for sure” one of the most scrutinized quarterbacks in the NFL. Daniels, though, said Thursday night that he had only one thought as he jogged onto the field for the final drive: “One play at a time.” Then he did what he hadn’t done since his rookie season: lead a game-winning drive. He did so five times in 2024 en route to being named NFL offensive rookie of the year. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Athletic (paywall) Commanders go from frustration to elation as they rediscover late-game magic: ‘We needed that’ Here we go again. The Commanders had a habit of making close and winnable games self-inflicted disasters this season, and this one — a must-win Thursday night matchup with the NFC East-leading Giants — was on the verge of becoming the latest. Owner Josh Harris, who typically comes down to the Commanders’ sideline to watch the final few minutes of games, again took his place for what could’ve been a slow, painful ending to his team’s season. But these Commanders weren’t done. When the clock hit two minutes, Washington came alive, much like it did a couple years ago when it took the NFL world by storm with its late-game heroics. In three drives — a defensive stand, a quick go-ahead touchdown and a game-sealing interception — the Commanders saved their season, and possibly their coach’s job, to collect its biggest victory of the year, a 24-21 win over the Giants . Daronte Jones said he not going out like he did the first game. Spammed that mf Zero and called game. — Jamual (@LetMualTellit) November 13, 2026 Daniels hit Stefon Diggs on a slant and the veteran wideout sprinted upfield, stopping inches before the goal line before turning and falling backward into the end zone, a la DeSean Jackson. “Well, he probably could have waited some more,” Quinn joked afterward. It appeared that Daniels changed a signal on the play before the snap. “Maybe, maybe not. You never know,” Diggs said facetiously. . @Commanders @Giants @JayD__5 to DIGGS on 3-4 v a "Blitz Zero" look…Daniels with the game winner #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/8gUtuIpK9y — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) November 13, 2026 “Baby Kobe,” Diggs said of Daniels. “He ain’t flinch. He’s going to be the same kind of player he is at the beginning of the game as he is at the end of the game.” Cornerback Rasul Douglas intercepted McCarthy on a deep, last-gasp attempt on third-and-10 with 34 seconds remaining. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders believed and the miracle happened Maybe it was wishful thinking, the last, mournful hope of a condemned team that hasn’t been able to stay out of its own way much of this season. But they put together eight great minutes when they needed it most. The defense made three consecutive stops. Daniels is, obviously, Washington’s North Star. But Styles, the seventh pick overall, is rapidly growing into everything the Commanders hoped he’d be. The speed and force is obvious; the reads are coming, rapidly. On that third and two, Styles’ film work, with a verbal assist from defensive tackle Charles Omenihu, indicated to him that the Giants were running a crack back run, with the tight end coming down the line to clear Washington’s edge defender, and give McCarthy enough room to get the first down. Styles brushed off Giants center Bryan Hudson, shot the gap, tackled McCarthy for the loss, and gave the offense the ball back. “I think, if you’re just the player you are, the moment can never be too big,” Styles said. “I think everyone understood in that moment, ‘We’ve got to get a stop right here.’ So guys just bowed up.” Styles said he remembered the Giants ran a crack toss in the 1st game in a similar 3rd & short situation, which helped him ID this play so quickly. I believe this was the play he was referring to: https://t.co/jVOcoCQ7w2 pic.twitter.com/nSYtdskcyE — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 13, 2026 Guard Sam Cosmi looked at his teammates as Washington huddled up. “I have moments where I look, and everybody’s just locked in,” Cosmi said. “You have that, like, glare, where you know it’s game time, this is game time. We’re going to make big plays.” The Commanders won a big challenge after stopping Jameis Winston on a QB sneak on 3rd & 1. Deatrich Wise Jr. emphatically wanted Dan Quinn to challenge. Why? Simple answer pic.twitter.com/ZtWdw1lJRe — Marshall Kramsky (@marshallkramsky) November 13, 2026 Washington is still two games behind New York, with eight to play. But the Commanders, now, have the tiebreaker with the Giants, if it comes down to that. If it comes down to that, though, this already wild ride of a season will have taken an even crazier turn than what happened here Thursday, when the Commanders merely saved their season. For a couple of weeks, at least. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Washington Post (paywall) Diggs’s late touchdown secured victory after Daniels threw a pair of 4th-quarter interceptions “Back-to-back interceptions, that’s hard. It would’ve been really easy to lose the faith in that moment,” Quinn said. “So, to see us battle and stay in the fight, that’s what I was looking for. … There’s plenty to do, guys. There’s a lot to clean up, a lot to get better, but I’m definitely proud of the group. “Man, that ain’t goin’ do nothing for me — still dwelling on that,” Daniels said. “Everybody was on the sideline saying, ‘The defense is giving you an opportunity to go out and win this game.’ When I had the opportunity to go out there and win the game, take a deep breath, go out there and just capitalize on the moment.” Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and the two picks. On the other side of the ball, the defense ended the game with three consecutive stops. “We needed that,” Coach Dan Quinn said. “We needed every bit of it.” When the Commanders’ offense had success, it tended to be when it went to a more up-tempo offense. Offensive coordinator David Blough put an emphasis on huddling more often and slowing down the pace this season, but it hasn’t resulted in better results. He showed a willingness to adjust in the first half against the Giants. title: NFL Week 10 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Touchdown for Chuba Hubbard? Fantasy upside for Aaron Rodgers? Trick play from the Raiders? Let's predict 15 things for Week 10.
full_text:
Week 10 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Commanders beat the Giants on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Will the Steelers upset the Bengals? How many yards will  Trey McBride have against the Rams? Could  Jadarian Price score his first NFL touchdown? And will Raiders coach Klint Kubiak dial up a trick play in  Fernando Mendoza 's first start?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Carolina Panthers +2.5 (+110 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints 

 Quarterback  Bryce Young is getting the ball out more quickly recently without sacrificing chances downfield, which could be helpful against New Orleans' pass rush. The Saints are allowing 7.8 yards per pass attempt, giving Tetairoa McMillan opportunities to make big plays.

 New Orleans hasn't gotten much from its running game, and it will be without starting center  Erik McCoy ( biceps injury ) on Sunday . That puts more stress on quarterback  Tyler Shough , enabling Carolina to keep this close and potentially win outright.

 
 

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Cincinnati Bengals 

 Running back  Jaylen Warren gives Pittsburgh a way to control this game. He already piled up 176 total yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati , and the Bengals keep giving up long runs this season.

 Cincinnati also struggles to defend the middle of the field, where Steelers quarterback  Aaron Rodgers  has strong options in WR  Germie Bernard and TE  Darnell Washington . Bengals QB  Joe Burrow will get his points, but Pittsburgh can answer without asking Rodgers to force deep throws.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins : 11 targets, 7 receptions, 78 receiving yards, 1 touchdown 

 Every year I look for the players who are excelling in ESPN's open score -- which measures a receiver's ability to get open on all routes , regardless of target -- but struggling in catch score. That's because open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates better with future production.

 Washington fits this profile exactly with an 82 open score (tied with Garrett Wilson for second best) but just a 38 catch score (below average). So there is a decent chance Washington's production will increase, and it could happen as early as this Sunday  -- even with backup quarterback   Kyle McCord  throwing him the ball. Washington should line up against Colts nickel cornerback  Justin Walley , who missed the past two games with a knee injury and is allowing 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's well above the 1.1 average.

 
 

 Trey McBride , TE, Arizona Cardinals : 13 targets, 9 receptions, 99 receiving yards 

 If I were quarterback  Carson Beck , I would make a point of throwing to McBride when in doubt during my NFL debut . But that would be especially true now that  Michael Wilson  is out for the season with a neck injury . And even further because 23% of targets against the Rams' defense have been to tight ends, the sixth-highest rate in the league.

 As long as cornerback  Trent McDuffie isn't on McBride, he ought to be the priority target on most plays. If the Cardinals fall behind, McBride should be in line for quite a bit of garbage-time production to come close to the 100-yard mark.

 
 

 Justin Eboigbe , DT, Los Angeles Chargers : 1.0 sacks, 4 pressures, 19% pass rush win rate 

 Eboigbe recorded 6.0 sacks a year ago but has just 0.5 this season. Plus, he has a well-below-average pass rush win rate. So why am I forecasting a big game for Eboigbe on Monday ? Because of who he'll line up against. Ravens right guard John Simpson has a sixth-percentile pass block win rate at the position, while center Cam Jurgens is literally last in pass block win rate at his position since he started playing for the Ravens in Week 7.

 

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Aaron Rodgers , QB, Pittsburgh Steelers (35.4% rostered in ESPN leagues) 

 Rodgers has averaged just 8.9 fantasy points over his past two games, with Pittsburgh leaning heavily on its running game. That could change Sunday night against a Bengals offense that ranks second in points per game, which could force the Steelers to throw more to keep pace.

 Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdown passes  against Cincinnati in Week 3 , finishing with 22.6 fantasy points. The Bengals have also allowed 17.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

 
 

 Corey Kiner , RB, New England Patriots (31.9%) 

 Kiner could lead the Patriots' backfield against the Lions this week , with Rhamondre Stevenson listed as questionable ( knee tendon issue ) and TreVeyon Henderson  is  out . Kiner rushed for 55 yards and a touchdown on eight carries against the Packers last week ; he leads New England with 4.9 yards per carry this season.

 Detroit has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, so it's a tough matchup. But Kiner could see 14-plus rushing attempts, while Lan Larison handles more of the work on passing downs.

 
 

 Tutu Atwell , WR, Los Angeles Rams (8.1%) 

 With  Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both sidelined, Atwell could see a lot more targets against the Cardinals . He has drawn nine targets over his past two games and played more snaps than any other healthy Rams receiver against the Commanders.

 Arizona has allowed 32.2 fantasy points per game to wide receivers and the second-most passing touchdowns in the league. Atwell's production has been inconsistent, but his ability to make plays downfield and the opportunity for more targets make him worth considering in deeper leagues.

 

 
 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Jadarian Price , RB, Seattle Seahawks 

 Price had 78 total yards in the Week 9 win over the Cardinals , and he looked explosive in the pass game with four receptions for 54 yards. He will continue to split touches with Zach Charbonnet on Sunday versus the Raiders , but I see him scoring his first pro touchdown here -- off a screen pass.

 
 

 George Kittle , TE, San Francisco 49ers 

 Take the target volume with Kittle, plus the prime matchup versus the Dallas defense . Kittle has seen at least seven targets in three straight games, and coach Kyle Shanahan can scheme up his tight end to press the seams against the Cowboys' split-safety coverages.

 I'd expect multiple red zone targets for Kittle on Sunday. And the 49ers are the best in the league at turning those targets into touchdowns (84.6% red zone touchdown percentage this season).

 
 

 Chuba Hubbard , RB, Carolina Panthers 

 Hubbard has at least one rushing score in three of his past five games, and he is seeing consistent volume with 20 or more touches in four contests. Meanwhile, the Saints are giving up 133.9 rushing yards per game (fourth most) and have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns this season (tied for second most). With steady volume and red zone touches, Hubbard could easily find the end zone Sunday.

 

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Rams WR  CJ Daniels will score a touchdown 

 The Rams' undrafted free agent receiver is in line for his first NFL action now that Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on IR. Daniels critically has something that projected starting receivers Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell lack: size. At 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, don't be surprised if Daniels sees…

Then, analytics writer Aaron Schatz makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Schatz all give us final score picks for every game.

Coordinator Zak Kuhr said CB Christian Gonzalez had some plays he would want back, but also said there were other plays where he could have been the closest defender because of breakdowns elsewhere. Kuhr acknowledged that very little went right for the defense but thought the unit took steps Wednesday in a spirited practice that featured better communication and connectivity. Kuhr added that the team's belief in Gonzalez hasn't wavered. -- Mike Reiss 

 What we're hearing on the Lions: It's not every day that the Lions are selected to play in an international game. In fact, it hasn't happened since 2015, so this is a huge deal for the franchise. WR Amon-Ra St. Brown 's mother, Miriam, hails from Germany, and he frequently visited the country as a child. This will be a new experience for coach Dan Campbell. "As far as I've been across the pond is London, and that was for [a game]," Campbell said. "And I already mentioned, I had an extra pair of underwear and socks and that was it, all right. And a toothbrush, but that's as far as I've been over there." -- Eric Woodyard 

 Stat to know: Lions QB Jared Goff has had consecutive games with fewer than 200 passing yards for just the second time over the past five seasons. -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Patriots QB Drake Maye will not throw an interception against the Lions. His 11 interceptions this season are the second most in the league. In general, about 20% of passes defensed turn into interceptions. It's been a little lower leaguewide this season (16%). For Maye, it has been 34%. So he has been unlucky and shouldn't be as interception prone going forward. -- Schatz

However, Kiner could see enough volume to be a viable flex option. See Week 10 rankings . -- Moody

New England allows 10.6 yards per pass attempt against play-action, which Goff uses constantly.
