title: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
summary: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

 That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

 "I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

 On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

 A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

 The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

 

 "We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

 On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

 So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

 "We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr . said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

 "I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

 The Falcons have shown glimpses of that, such as last month when they toppled the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in an impressive performance. But since then, they have fallen to the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a full-on downpour and lost to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid.

 

 The schedule does not get any easier. The Kansas City Chiefs will come to town Sunday. After that, the Falcons have their bye week followed by a road game against the Minnesota Vikings , a home game against the Detroit Lions and then a trip to Cleveland. Those teams have a combined 23-10 record.

 It will be up to the team's leadership to keep the players focused on the task at hand. ESPN's FPI  is giving the Falcons only a 4.5% chance of making the playoffs, but the division remains wide open. The other three teams don't have easy schedules, either.

 Left tackle Jake Matthews , the longest-tenured Falcon and the only player left from the 2016 Super Bowl team, said Atlanta had a "really good practice" Wednesday "because everyone was kind of dialed in to 'Hey, this is our objective still and we fully expect to go out and play every weekend to win.'"

 "I think [Stefanski's] message and the point was kind of driven home that there's so much still ahead of us this season," Matthews said. "We need to double down."

title: Falcons sign DE Cameron Thomas, CB C.J. Henderson to multiyear extensions
summary: The Atlanta Falcons have signed defensive end Cameron Thomas and cornerback C.J. Henderson to multiyear contract extensions, the team announced Friday.
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are locking in defensive end Cameron Thomas to a three-year contract extension , the team announced Friday. The deal is worth up to $33 million, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
The Falcons signed Thomas this past offseason to a one-year, $3.1 million contract and he has surpassed all expectations.
Atlanta also announced Friday that it has signed cornerback C,J. Henderson to a two-year contract extension , a deal that guarantees Henderson $11 million and could top out at $20 million, sources told Rapoport.
Thomas, 26, has two sacks and leads all Atlanta edge rushers with a minimum of 150 pass-rush snaps in quarterback pressure rate (13.5%) and QB hits (12). The latter is a career high. Thomas has played 63.3% of the team's defensive snaps, more than any other Falcons defensive linemen
The Arizona Cardinals drafted Thomas in the third round back in 2022. The Falcons are his fourth team. Thomas spent two seasons with current Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski with the Cleveland Browns prior to this season.
Atlanta defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said Thomas was the first name Stefanski mentioned as the team looked to sign an edge rusher in the offseason.
"You talk about a guy that just, he demonstrates what we love about this game every single day: the toughness, the strain, the effort -- the relentless effort -- and then the high-level execution, the consistency," Ulbrich said Thursday. "If there's a guy that we can really lean on on our defense, he's one of those human beings. I've been just so overwhelmed with what he's brought to us and it's been awesome."
The extension contract was done by Equity Sports CEO Chris Cabott, Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham and Falcons senior vice president Bryce Johnston, Schefter and Rapoport reported. It was finished Thursday night.
Henderson, meanwhile, has started the past six games at boundary corner for the Falcons. Henderson, 28, was the No. 9 overall pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2020 and had bounced around before landing in Atlanta last season on the practice squad.
"It's been a fun journey with CJ because when he got here, obviously, he had a very well-known past in this league," Ulbrich explained. "To help him start to reinvent himself here, it brings me a ton of joy because he's just such an amazing young man. I'm excited for every opportunity he gets and every opportunity to show this league exactly who he is now, today."

title: Minter: Lamar Jackson 'doing everything' to return; QB had surgery, sources say
summary: Ravens coach Jesse Minter's update on Lamar Jackson's recovery process calls such timelines "challenging to predict."
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens say Lamar Jackson 's dislocated and broken right thumb has a typical recovery timeline of six to 10 weeks, with a source telling ESPN the quarterback has undergone surgery for the injury.
Ravens coach Jesse Minter addressed Jackson's status in a statement released by the team Friday in which he said recovery timelines are "challenging to predict."
"He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."
Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Jackson underwent surgery on the thumb last week.
With nine weeks remaining in the regular season, Jackson could come back as early as Week 16 against the Cleveland Browns . If Jackson needs 10 weeks to recover, a return would come in the postseason.
The Ravens (4-5) have lost four straight games but are one game out of the final playoff spot in the AFC. Baltimore's playoff chances are projected at 3.7%, according to ESPN Analytics.
To help keep the team's postseason hopes alive, the Ravens traded for quarterback Jacoby Brissett , who is set to start Monday night in Baltimore against the winless Los Angeles Chargers .
Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first play of a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. His right hand hit the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau while trying to throw a pass.
This is the second significant injury this season for Jackson, who missed three games with a high ankle sprain. He has played only 14 full quarters.
The Ravens have usually struggled without Jackson. With Jackson as its starting quarterback, Baltimore is 82-38 (.683), including playoffs, and averages 27.6 points per game. Without Jackson as their starter since 2019, the Ravens are 7-15 (.318), including the postseason, and average 17.3 points per game.

title: NFL reassigns backup refs to work games closer to home
summary: The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues from Friday's FAA ground stop, has reassigned officials to Week 10 games within driving distance of their homes.
full_text:
The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues stemming from the FAA ground stop Friday, has adjusted its officiating assignments for domestic games in Week 10, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns.
Airlines across the U.S. worked Saturday to recover from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years that canceled more than 2,000 flights, spread ripple effects around the world, stranded passengers and forced professional and college sports teams to scramble for alternate transportation.
The NFL's changes mean three backup referees -- umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard -- will work as referees on Sunday.
Heydt will be at the Carolina - New Orleans game, while Anderson will serve as referee for Jacksonville at Tennessee .
Willard will serve double duty Sunday. He will work the Miami - Indianapolis game at 1 p.m. ET and then travel approximately 110 miles for the Pittsburgh - Cincinnati game, which kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET.
The NFL said each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified who trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise.
The nationwide stop, attributed to new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system that caused "intermittent" communications and radar gaps, was the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
summary: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."
full_text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Chuba Hubbard  knows that no one is perfect. But that hasn't stopped the Carolina Panthers ' running back from chasing perfection. And after a forgettable, injury-marred 2025 campaign, during which he lost his starting job after a career season in 2024, the team captain is leading the backfield again, and he's perhaps better than ever.

 "I pride myself in hard work and staying consistent in knowing what I can do and trying to bring my best every single day, so it's more so just fighting for excellence and fighting to be perfect in every way possible," Hubbard told ESPN.

 Hubbard, 27, signed a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension during his breakout 2024 campaign, when he rushed for 1,195 yards and produced 11 total touchdowns in 15 games. Through eight games in 2026, he has rushed for 619 yards and produced seven total touchdowns, bouncing back as the Panthers have struggled to find consistency almost everywhere else during a three-game losing streak and a 3-5 start.

 

 But those numbers don't tell the complete story of Hubbard's value. He's talented, sure, but his true worth is as a tone-setter for the organization.

 Though he was selected by the franchise, while Matt Rhule was the coach, in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL draft, Hubbard has established himself as the standard-bearer for the Dave Canales era over the past three seasons. And with Carolina fighting to maintain its position atop the NFC South, his value has become apparent, if not paramount, to the team's ability to recalibrate its season.

 "What I love about Chuba is that the things that we talk about wanting to be as an organization, he represents those in spades," Canales said. "His preparation, the way that he works, the way I have to kind of reel him in and call him back a little bit because he goes so hard."

 Hubbard could be the X factor who wills Carolina to a win Sunday at the Caesars Superdome ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ), where the Panthers haven't won since the 2022 season. Hubbard, who has 70.8% of the team's carries this season, will face the New Orleans Saints , who have one of the league's worst rushing defenses (ranked 29th). A win could reignite Carolina's hopes of securing consecutive division titles for the first time since the franchise owned the NFC South crown from 2013 to 2015.

 According to those who know him best, Hubbard is ready to shoulder that burden, not only because of who he is as a player, but also because of who he is as a person and a leader in the locker room.

 

 Chuba Hubbard's style 'keeps a defense honest' and could bode well in New Orleans 

 Hubbard entered Week 10 with the 10th-most rushing yards in the NFL. He has played one fewer game than five of the backs who are in front of him on that list, and three of those playmakers ( Derrick Henry with 689, Jonathan Taylor at 656 and Javonte Williams at 629) have fewer than 70 more yards than Hubbard.

 This week, the Panthers' top back will get an opportunity to make up ground on the rushing leader list against the Saints. New Orleans allows 133.9 rushing yards per game and 4.52 yards per carry. With New Orleans also struggling against the pass (ranked 28th with 236.6 passing yards allowed per game), Hubbard could take advantage of quarterback Bryce Young 's passing threat against potentially lighter tackle boxes.

 Hubbard's ability to gain momentum throughout a game has made him a steady presence in an otherwise erratic offense. And his north-south rushing style should be a challenge for a Saints defense that has struggled to bring down ball carriers.

 Through eight games, Hubbard has averaged 26.5 rushing yards in the first half of games. He has nearly doubled that number with a 50.9 rushing-yards average in the second half. Hubbard also has 110 rushing yards over expected (RYOE), defined as the difference between actual rushing yards and expected rushing yards on a series of plays, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That total ranks sixth in the league entering Week 10.

 "That aligns with who Chuba is as a player, a person," Panthers offensive coordinator Brad Idzik said recently. "He's going to outwork you. He's going to outlast you. He's going to out-prepare you. ... Whereas some people wear down throughout the game, it feels like he gets stronger, because he's prepared for that."

 

 Hubbard's lopsided first- and second-half splits are partially due to Young airing out the ball consistently in the first half, which is wearing down opposing defenses, particularly in the second and third levels. The other part is that Hubbard is fresh down the stretch of games, and can bulldoze past (and through) defenders. He has 16 explosive runs (10 yards or more gained), which ranks eighth in the NFL.

 Hubbard "keeps a defense honest," said a pro scout of an NFC team that played the Panthers in the first half of the season. "Good size and vision to run between the tackles; enough speed and agility to be used on outside runs. ... You can't put him in one box [with] what he does well and what he doesn't do well."

 ESPN NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky said Hubbard has a "really strong lower half, is a smart pass catcher in space [and he] runs with energy." Hubbard's vision and patience help the Panthers stay ahead of the sticks. Historically, he is not the type of player to lose yardage on a carry because of his ability to read blocks, break tackles and power to -- at worst -- the line of scrimmage.

 "You're never going to have too many zero-[yard] runs with him, or negative runs; that's the thing I like about him," Panthers run game coordinator Harold Goodwin said last week. "There's really no perfect run every play, but he creates something on every play, so just as long as we get on people [with blocking], he's always going to come out with positive yards."

 Hubbard has also improved considerably as a pass blocker and receiver throughout his career. He had seven drops on 37 targets as a rookie in 2021, while mostly filling in for All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey . Hubbard also had a rough three-year stretch from a blitz-pickup perspective from 2022 to 2024.

 Those third-down woes impacted his playing time and the fan base's perception of him. So, the Edmonton, Alberta, native worked to improve himself by "chopping the tree every single day."

 

 

 Preparation is key for 27-year-old RB who 'wants to be able to do everything' 

 Hubbard has a relentless training regimen, which includes what Idzik calls "the most consistent pre- and post-practice routines I've been around."

 Hubbard spends roughly 30 minutes after practice working on the Jugs machine daily, an exercise several teammates, including tight end Tommy Tremble , have embraced over the years.

 In the five seasons since his rookie campaign, Hubbard has caught 141 passes for 965 yards and six touchdowns -- with 10 total drops (just one this season), according to ESPN Research -- as a result of the tedious steps he takes throughout the week.

 According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Hubbard gave up six sacks and 41 pressures in his first four seasons. He has allowed just nine pressures and zero sacks in the 23 games since that stretch.

 "I want to be able to do everything, from blocking to catching to running the ball," Hubbard said. "Obviously, that's something that I had to work on a lot and obviously felt the criticism. I told myself, 'I would be wrong if I didn't fix this thing.' Like, I'd be wrong if I didn't put my best foot forward to be the best I can be, especially for myself and my team."

 Hubbard has still had ups and downs on the field regardless of his preparation.

 Last season, he was effectively benched after a lingering calf injury soured the start of his 2025 season. Fellow running back Rico Dowdle -- now in Pittsburgh -- was signed to a one-year deal to team up with Hubbard, and instead of serving as Hubbard's backup, Dowdle became the primary back throughout the majority of the Panthers' NFC South…

title: NFC North: Bears win division? Cousins has Vikes in command?
summary: What will Kirk Cousins and Micah Parsons mean for the best division in football, or will the Bears hang on?
full_text:
No one in the NFL was on a bigger high coming out of last weekend than the Green Bay Packers .

 They trounced the defending AFC champion New England Patriots  45-27 and put together their best performance of the season to improve to 6-3.

 And then Packers coach Matt LaFleur killed the buzz: "The reality is this: We're in last place in our division right now."

 Such is life in the NFC North, the most victorious division in football, where the Chicago Bears are on top at 7-2, followed by the Detroit Lions (6-2), Minnesota Vikings (6-2) and Packers (6-3).

 The NFC North is the seventh division since 2002 with all four teams above .500 through Week 9, according to ESPN Research. It has the best combined record (25-9, 73.5 winning percentage) by any division in the first nine weeks of a season under the current division format, which began 24 years ago.

 

 The last time all four teams in a division had a winning record at this point in a season was 2023 with the AFC North. All four finished with winning records, and all but the Cincinnati Bengals (9-8) made the playoffs. The Baltimore Ravens made it to the AFC Championship Game.

 On the flip side of that was the 2022 AFC East, which also had every team with a winning record through Week 9 but had only two teams reach the playoffs, and neither advanced past the divisional round.

 ESPN's FPI gives the Bears the best shot at winning the division at 35.1%, ahead of the Vikings (29.7%), Lions (24.7%) and Packers (10.5%).

 So what's real and what's not in the NFC North? Reporters Courtney Cronin (Bears), Rob Demovsky (Packers), Kevin Seifert (Vikings) and Eric Woodyard (Lions) give their insight:

 

 

 Real or not: Acquiring  Kirk Cousins puts Vikings in driver's seat to win the division. 

 Cronin: Not real. Cousins' first two games leave little room for an offense adjusting to a new quarterback. Minnesota faces Green Bay at Lambeau Field in Week 10 and then NFC-leading San Francisco in Mexico City. The stretch of Atlanta, Carolina, Detroit and Washington at home is when the Vikings have the best chance to add to their six wins, but two others in the NFC North -- Chicago, with the most complete team, and Detroit, which has the No. 5 scoring offense (27.8 PPG) -- have a better shot at the division title.

 

 Woodyard: Not real. Although Cousins should be an upgrade to the quarterbacks room, this doesn't immediately fix everything that's wrong with the offense -- or team. Entering Week 10, the Vikings have the NFL's second-worst offensive efficiency (23.77) and Cousins isn't necessarily in the prime of his career at 38, but he does have familiarity in their offensive system and should stabilize the unit enough to compete for a division title.

 Seifert: Not real. It's just too early to say that Cousins can, on his own, lift an offense that ranks No. 31 in EPA enough to ensure superiority over the rest of the division. The truth is quarterback hasn't been only issue. Playcalling, run-game efficiency and, at times, pass protection, have all played roles.

 Demovsky: Not real. In any other division, perhaps a quarterback change of this magnitude on a team that has the No. 2-ranked defense in the NFL would tip the scales in its favor. That doesn't mean Cousins won't help the offense reverse course toward respectability, but it was only a matter of time before this punchless offense made water find its level with the Vikings.

 
 

 Real or not: Caleb Williams ' four picks Sunday were a blip on his way to MVP. 
 Cronin: Not real. The interceptions themselves are a blip, as Williams had the fourth-lowest interception rate (0.6) entering Week 9. Only the first of the four picks were problematic, with Williams admitting he got "greedy" trying to fit a tight-window ball at the goal line. His MVP case needed to be built off peak efficiency to make up for the three games he missed with his hamstring injury, and it's hard to envision him now catching up with the Joe Burrow and Josh Allen at the top of the leaderboard.

 

 Demovsky: Real. I'm going to give him a pass for several reasons: He played mostly interception-free before Sunday against Tampa. One of his interceptions was clearly the fault of receiver Luther Burden III because it bounced off his hands, and two others were the result of heavy pressure. The biggest thing working against his MVP case might be his three-game absence.

 Woodyard: Not real.  Williams is certainly a worthy candidate but might not even be the MVP of the NFC North with the way that Packers QB Jordan Love has also been playing -- and without missing any games. Obviously the four interceptions are an anomaly, but he will have to beat out some strong candidates with more efficient play to separate himself.

 Seifert: Not real. I think the Bears are the best team in the division, and Williams has a lot to do with that. The quarterback of a top NFL team is a natural candidate for MVP. But his four-interception game was a by-product of the way he plays -- aggressively downfield and extending plays outside the pocket. Burrow,  Brock Purdy and Allen are stronger MVP candidates.

 

 

 Real or not: Micah Parsons ' eventual return  to the Packers will be the biggest addition for any NFC North team. 
 Cronin: Not real. Jeffery Simmons would like a word given how quickly he elevated the floor of the Bears' defense upon his arrival in Week 8. Chicago went from blitzing at the fifth-highest rate (42%) prior to the All-Pro defensive tackle's arrival to being able to win with a standard pass rush more frequently. Parsons has not played since Dec. 14, 2025 and will take time to ramp up to his best form. Meanwhile, Simmons' on-field impact is only getting stronger after he logged 87% of snaps in his debut and 97% of snaps in Week 9.

 

 Woodyard: Real. Parsons is a legitimate game changer and will immediately raise the floor for Green Bay's defense. At his best, there's no question that he's one of the top defensive players in the league, but the question is how long it'll take him to get back to full speed after returning from his ACL injury.

 Seifert: Real. While it might take Parsons some time to ramp up to full strength from a conditioning standpoint, he is the NFL's best pass rusher and that alone will change how every team approaches games against the Packers. The threat alone of his presence, and the need to track wherever he is on the field, is a huge lift for the defense.

 Demovsky: Real. While the Packers didn't make any moves at the trade deadline, Parsons' return (likely on Thanksgiving eve at the Rams) trumps the Bears' trade for Simmons. Parsons has taken extra time to rehab because he wants to be as close to 100% as possible, giving him a better chance to make an immediate impact. As good a job as new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done without Parsons, he admitted recently that he thinks about what he'll be able to do with Parsons "every day."

 

 

 Real or not: The most overlooked storyline is the  Lions' defensive improvement. 
 Cronin: Real. Kelvin Sheppard's unit deserves a lot of credit for holding the Packers and Vikings (with differing levels of QB play) to 17 and 15 points in back-to-back weeks while allowing fewer than 20 points in three straight games. What stands out most is Detroit being one of 11 teams to hold opponents under 100 rushing yards in every game this season.

 

 Woodyard: Real. After the 32-26 Week 4 loss in Carolina, Sheppard was under heavy fire -- and rightfully so -- when the defense allowed at least 30 or more points in three of its first four games for the first time since the infamous 0-16 season in 2008. To his credit, coach Dan Campbell stuck with Sheppard while continuing to back him, and Detroit has gone 3-0 during their streak of holding opponents to 20 points or fewer.

 Seifert: Not real. It's always important to keep opponents in mind when evaluating statistical surges. In the past two games, the Lions have held the…

title: Untold stories of Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing
summary: For Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sunday's NFL game in Munich will mark the ultimate convergence of his dual heritage. Here are stories that shed more light.
full_text:
DETROIT -- When the Detroit Lions take the field to face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, wide receiver  Amon-Ra St. Brown  will feel right at home.

 For St. Brown, Germany is as much his home as the United States. It's where he and his family frequently took trips to visit his maternal grandparents. It's where St. Brown went to preschool (Die Rheinpiraten Kindergarten, to be exact), and where he and his older brothers, Equanimeous and Osiris, spent countless hours on bike tours and fishing trips with their grandfather, Helmut Steyer, who enjoyed entertaining his American-born grandsons.

 

 It's where Amon-Ra (and Osiris) was a standout for the country's under-19 national football team. It's where he has hosted football camps since becoming a pro in 2021. And it's where the Lions star was once asked by an uncle to stay in order to become a star in the other type of football.

 "It's not strange to him. It's all familiar ... everything," St. Brown's mother, Miriam Brown, said. "Going to restaurants, everything is different but for him it's familiar."

 The deep connection and familiarity St. Brown has with the country is because of Miriam. Born and raised in Leverkusen, in western Germany, she instilled her German values into Amon-Ra and his brothers, who are all fluent in German.

 Those values, and experiences, are a part of St. Brown's identity and have always been at the forefront of who he is. As a result, when the Lions face the Patriots in one of the country's most famous arenas (9:30 a.m. ET on Fox), St. Brown will be the headline act.

 More than 80 NFL players who were born in Germany (West Germany and East Germany included) have appeared in a game, per ESPN Research, including 10 who have debuted since 2018. Although he was born in Anaheim Hills, California, few have experienced as much popularity in Germany as St. Brown, who, according to NFL Germany general manager Alexander Steinforth, is the subject of multiple documentaries currently being produced there.

 "He's probably the poster boy for the NFL in the German-speaking world these days," Steinforth told ESPN. "He works a lot and has worked a lot with our local broadcast partners, so it's amazing to see when he's kind of talking to his German fans. He's a really big and important name for us here in Germany."

 St. Brown wears decals of both the German and American flags on his helmet. He says he's fortunate and proud to be so immersed in both cultures, each of which he has drawn from throughout his life.

 "Being half German, half American you kind of get to experience both cultures, and you admire different things in both cultures," St. Brown said. "You feel as if, you know, some things you wish the Americans would do more, some things you wish the Germans would do more.

 "But I'm both, so I can pick and choose what I like from each culture. And I think both cultures have amazing, amazing qualities. But I'm just glad that I was able to dip my feet into both cultures and be around both of them."

 What does Germany really mean to St. Brown? These are stories that shed more light.

 

 

 'Shoot the ball!' 

 Very early in St. Brown's eighth grade basketball season, coach Brian Liles began getting annoyed.

 Liles, who was coaching in the National Junior Basketball youth league in Irvine, California, had taught the boys a pass-first style of hoops that he expected his Titans team to follow. But throughout the first four or five games, John Brown -- the father of a teenage Amon-Ra St. Brown -- was in the stands instructing his youngest son to do the complete opposite.

 "Every time Amon-Ra got the ball, he would go, 'Shoot the ball! Shoot the ball!' After a while, I just walked over and I go, 'John, I'm trying to get him to pass the ball because the minute he gets the ball everybody swarms to him,'" Liles recalled. "Guys are open underneath the basket and if he makes the pass, we will be able to get an easy layup."

 

 During the chat, Liles said Brown was kind and immediately receptive.

 He said, "Oh yeah, sorry, Coach. I won't say anything else."

 Liles said Brown held his tongue for the next few possessions. Then, suddenly, he heard him calling to his son again ... but in an unfamiliar language.

 "I'm like, 'Is that German? I think he's talking in German.' And all of a sudden Amon-Ra starts shooting the basketball again," Liles said. "And I go, 'That son of a gun is telling him to shoot the ball in German!'

 

 "So, he tried to outsmart me, but I picked it up."

 Those interactions weren't uncommon for Amon-Ra and his brothers during their youth sports careers. Whether it was basketball, football or soccer, Brown was frequently on the sidelines delivering instructions in German.

 They weren't always well received by his sons.

 "This was in football specifically and my brother was in Pop Warner, and I think he was telling him to do some type of move," Osiris said. "He's like, 'Spin, spin.' And my brother, and even me, we all got annoyed that he kept yelling at us to do something.

 "So, my brother got so frustrated that he would just do the move like when he didn't need to do it, just to do it. He's like, 'You want me to spin? Forget it, I'll spin' even when he wasn't near someone."

 Brown said he learned enough German to deliver commands. He figured Liles, or anyone else, would never know what he was saying.

 "I used that to my advantage, yeah," he said, laughing.

 

 

 Summers in Leverkusen 
 As teenagers, word was starting to spread throughout Germany about the three brothers who lived in California and also held German citizenship.

 The St. Brown brothers spent nearly every summer with Miriam Brown's family in Leverkusen. In 2015, Amon-Ra played for the German U-19 national American football team alongside Osiris.

 Equanimeous, who was a freshman wide receiver at the University of Notre Dame at the time, didn't play, but the younger boys were happy to have each other for the trip.

 "So, we go to the first game and it wasn't that many people in the stands," John Brown said. "I can't recall which country we played, but when we played France, Osiris got kicked out of the game because he got into a fight with a French guy because he did something to him and he said, 'I'm not going to let some French guy talk s--- to me.'"

 Jürgen Siebmanns, team manager of the German junior national team, was responsible for recruiting and selecting both brothers and has continued to follow their pro and college careers.

 "Their talent, athleticism and attitude were not only an enrichment in the game, but also a role model for all players," Siebmanns told American-Football.com in 2020. "It was clear to everyone that both would make their way -- and of course we are all the more pleased when it even leads to such highlights and records."

 At the European Championship in Dresden, Germany, Amon-Ra, just 15 years old and undersized compared with the competition, won MVP honors -- a feat that wasn't surprising to his brothers.

 Representing Germany was meaningful to the boys and the family. And even after all these years, they still keep in contact with former teammates from that trip.

 "We were younger than these guys and a lot of these guys look like grown-ass men," Osiris said. "So, I'm like, 'F---.' But I don't even know if we ever talked about it, but then as soon as we get out there you can immediately see that these guys were at least like a good 10-15 years behind in skillwise when it came to football and we immediately started tearing it up in practice and then games."

 The experience playing sports on an international level was eye-opening for the family but not entirely shocking. When he was 5 years old, Amon-Ra's promising ability led Miriam to enroll him at the SC Hitdorf soccer club, located in the Hitdorf district of Leverkusen. He spent countless hours in the backyard of his mother's childhood home to pick up on the new sport.

 "He…

Wek 10 of the NFL season is already upon us. We've looked at the games, the odds and available props in hopes of trying to find the best value for bets.

 Bowen's favorite bets 
 We'll start with our game pick this week with the Chiefs-Falcons matchup in Atlanta. Plus, I have multiple teasers for the Week 10 slate, and I'll add a player prop on a wide receiver who is creating explosive plays at a high rate.

 Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 
1 p.m. ET on CBS; Line: KC -3, O/U: 46.5

 

 The Chiefs added wide receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline, giving Patrick Mahomes a slot target who can create numbers after the catch. The foot quickness is there to uncover. But I like the Chiefs to cover as a road favorite because of the run game and Steve Spagnuolo's defense.  Kenneth Walker III  is a difference-maker in Andy Reid's offense, averaging 23.1 touches and 130.5 scrimmage yards per game. Walker (groin) didn't practice on Friday, however, so if he can't go, rookie Emmett Johnson would elevate to the lead role. He has the vison and elusive ability to find daylight versus an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 YPC (22nd in the league), while Reid can use the heavy run action to influence linebackers on play-action concepts. Defensively, Spagnuolo's unit will mix late rotation, Cover 2 and pressure against a Falcons offense that is lacking passing rhythm right now. And quarterback Michael Penix Jr . has struggled against the blitz this season (48.4 QBR).

 

 Two-team, 6.5-point teaser (-143): Cleveland Browns +11 vs. Houston Texans , San Francisco 49ers +3 at Dallas Cowboys 

 Deshaun Watson is expected back under center, and Cleveland will have enough answers in the pass game to make plays against the Texans' core zone schemes. The Browns will need more rushing efficiency from Quinshon Judkins , but I feel comfortable with the altered spread at home because of a Cleveland pass defense that matches up well with Houston. In the other matchup in this teaser, Kyle Shanahan can scheme up a Dallas defense that is giving up 26.8 points and 372.7 yards per game. Look for play-action early with Brock Purdy targeting the seams and deep in-breakers, while the 49ers' defense creates issues for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game.

 Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-135): Minnesota Vikings +9.5 at Green Bay Packers ,  Buffalo Bills -2 at New York Jets 

 The trade for Kirk Cousins should create more volume and production for Justin Jefferson , and that will open more daylight for the Vikings' run game. But I'm taking Minnesota, with the spread being bumped to +9.5 points, because of Brian Flores' defense. I expect more zone pressure here because of the vertical ability of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but the Vikings will look to create chaos for Jordan Love . I like the Bills in the other matchup. Coach Joe Brady will have pressure answers for Josh Allen to get the ball out (catch-and-run targets for DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir ), and don't be surprised if the Bills lead with a run-heavy approach to control tempo.

 Jameson Williams longest reception OVER 24.5 yards (-112) 

 Williams has had a reception of 24 or more yards in five straight games. With his vertical ability, plus the dynamic open-field speed he displays after the catch, I like Williams to hit the over against New England.

 

 

 
 Solak's plays 

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 at Cincinnati Bengals 

 I unsuccessfully faded the Bengals last week against the Falcons in Madrid, but I'm back again with them facing the Steelers, a franchise known for its strong performance as a small underdog under Mike Tomlin that might still retain a bit of that magic under Mike McCarthy.

 I love the Steelers' potential to keep this game close because they have the sort of ball-control, run-heavy offense that can minimize the number of possessions Joe Burrow gets in this game. Since Week 3, when Pittsburgh rejiggered the right side of its offensive line, the Steelers are third in success rate and first in EPA on rushing snaps; no team has a higher explosive run rate, and it isn't close. When they faced the Bengals in Week 3, Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards. Now, Rico Dowdle is back to help.

 The Steelers are also big on targeting the backs and tight ends in the passing game, which is where you want to go after this Bengals defense, and the lingering ankle injury to  DJ Turner II  also makes Cincinnati fairly weak in the secondary. It's a divisional game, and the Bengals are too hot and cold to trust with more than a field goal against a Steelers team off the bye.

 Rico Dowdle receiving yards OVER 13.5 (-114) 

 

 Dowdle returned to the Steelers' lineup in Week 6 and had seven routes to Warren's 27 in that game against the Buccaneers. But he was targeted on four of those seven routes, and since then has 24 routes and six targets to Warren's 22 routes and six targets. The receiving volume has been fairly split since his return, and rightfully so -- Warren has been an exceptional between-the-tackles runner this season, and Dowdle has always been a capable pass catcher.

 Yet, Warren is projected for 25.5 yards and 3.5 receptions, whereas Dowdle is at 13.5 and 2.5. Given how willingly Aaron Rodgers targets the backs and how poor the Bengals' linebackers are in coverage and at tackling in the open field, backfield receiving production should be a strong part of Pittsburgh's offensive approach, and Dowdle is the far cheaper option in what should be near a 50/50 opportunity split.

 Keep an eye on this number live. If Warren starts out the first quarter taking most of the snaps on a couple of Pittsburgh three-and-outs, Dowdle's numbers will drop even more, and I'll start looking for live alts.

 Tutu Atwell receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) 

 It's worth wondering just who it is that is going to catch passes for the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua -- who had 19 targets and 14 receptions on 43 routes last week against the Commanders -- joins Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington on the injured reserve bench. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also probably out for Sunday's game at Arizona.

 The two primary route runners behind Nacua at receiver last Sunday were Konata Mumpfield and Atwell, the latter of whom was targeted five times for two receptions and 16 yards. Atwell ended the day with 37 unrealized air yards -- that is to say, he had 53 air yards to the 16 receiving yards he actually produced. In back-to-back weeks, he has had at least 50 air yards on 17 and 20 routes, respectively. Given the thinness of the Rams' receiver room, 20 routes should be a floor projection for Atwell, as long as the Cardinals' offense can keep things competitive with Carson Beck under center. Even if they can't, Atwell's downfield usage can get us home on one big reception.

 If you're looking to get really frisky in what should be a sleepy late afternoon game, Rams rookie receiver CJ Daniels to score a touchdown is +950. He's a big-framed receiver, which the Rams will need behind the smaller Mumpfield and Atwell. Worth a sprinkle!

 Tre Tucker receiving yards OVER 25.5 (-115) 

 

 Speaking of unrealized air yards, Tucker is 13th among all receivers in unconnected air yards at 227. Tucker is tied for ninth in targets…

title: Jaguars holding out new players Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates to give them bye
summary: The Jaguars are holding out newly acquired Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates to give them a bye week.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jaguars are holding newly acquired defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III out of Sunday's game at Tennessee because the duo has not yet had a bye week.
Defensive tackle Davon Godchaux , who also was acquired via trade on Monday along with Davis and Bates, will play because he has had a bye week.
"Want to be able to make sure that we're in a player safety [mode], putting them in a position to succeed, also learn the system and just give those guys a week to be able to do that," head coach Liam Coen said Friday morning. "We've been talking about it, working through it as the week goes and made the decision to ultimately do it today."
Coen also said Friday that running back Bhayshul Tuten , who didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, will practice today and will play against the Titans.
The Jaguars traded for Davis, Bates and Godchaux on Monday. They sent a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to Philadelphia for Davis, a 2027-second round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta for Bates, and a conditional 2027 sixth-round pick to New Orleans for Godchaux.
Philadelphia has its bye this week and Atlanta has a bye in Week 11. New Orleans had its bye in Week 8.

title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III (groin) misses practice, status uncertain
summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III missed practice Friday with a sore groin, leaving his status for Sunday's matchup against the Falcons in question.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- The Chiefs listed running back Kenneth Walker III as questionable for Sunday's road game against the Atlanta Falcons after he missed Friday's practice with a groin injury.
Coach Andy Reid said Walker reported tightness in his groin to the team in the morning before the Chiefs' final on-field practice of the week, resulting in the running back being held out of the session as a precautionary measure.
"We'll just see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. We're kind of feeling it out just to see where we're at with that [groin]. We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he can go. If he can't, he can't."
Walker, who joined the Chiefs in March after signing a three-year, $43.05 million contract, has been one of the NFL's best offseason acquisitions. He enters Week 10 with 872 rushing yards, second in the league behind Atlanta's Bijan Robinson (880).
If Walker is unable to play, the Chiefs are expected to rely heavily on rookie running back Emmett Johnson , the fifth-round pick who has played most often on third downs. In eight games, Johnson has been effective as a runner (111 rushing yards and one touchdown on 26 attempts) and a receiver (237 yards and one touchdown on 14 receptions).
"He'll be ready to go," right guard Trey Smith said Friday regarding Johnson, who could make his first career start. "I like Emmett, man, his juice, his energy. He oozes enthusiasm, emotion and positive energy. You can tell the guy wants to be great, and you can tell he works at it. He really cares, man. I'm really excited for him. It's not hard to root for guys like that."
Meanwhile, the Chiefs expect to have wide receiver Xavier Worthy available after he left in the second half of last week's win over the Jets with a hamstring injury. That should take a little pressure off Josh Downs , who intends to play after being acquired from the Colts just before the NFL trade deadline Tuesday in an attempt to build out Kansas City's depth at the position.
"I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days," Reid said of Downs. "He's a smart kid and knows how to play. He's been playing, which is great, and playing at a high level. He worked into the things we asked him to do and did well. I think he's ready to play in a game for us."
Downs had 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown in nine games with Indianapolis.
The Chiefs expect to have first-round pick Mansoor Delane back after the cornerback missed a couple of games with a shoulder injury. However, they likely will be without right tackle Jaylon Moore because of an ankle injury and Peter Woods due to a neck injury.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

title: Sources: Vikings made initial Kirk Cousins trade call to Raiders before MNF
summary: The Vikings initially reached out to the Raiders about a Kirk Cousins trade before their MNF game against the Bills, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
full_text:
The first time the Vikings reached out to the Raiders about a potential trade for Kirk Cousins was midday Monday, hours before Minnesota played the Bills on "Monday Night Football," league sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
During that call, the Vikings made it clear to the Raiders that they wanted to see how Monday night went first before having any further conversations about Cousins, but they would be in touch if needed.
Bright and early the next morning, hours after Minnesota's offensive meltdown, the Vikings called the Raiders before 6 a.m. PT and set the wheels in motion for a potential Cousins trade.
It was not a deal the Raiders wanted or were looking to make, especially when Minnesota's initial offer was a fifth-round draft pick, according to sources.
But once the Vikings upped their offer to a third-round pick, the Raiders had discussions about whether the trade made sense, and here's where they landed:
Not only would they be receiving a third-round pick, but they also would free up $10 million in cash for the 2027 season, as the bonus guarantee owed to Cousins would shift to Minnesota's responsibility. It was not a trade that the Raiders enjoyed making, but one they believed would be in the best interests of the organization.
The Raiders also believed 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza has looked, in the word of one source, "phenomenal" in practice. There never was going to be a right time to insert Mendoza into the starting lineup, but Minnesota made this as good a time as any.
Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, and Mendoza will make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks .
Competition committee to discuss trade snafus
The NFL's competition committee is expected to discuss a potential solution after multiple trades this week were voided or altered, according to sources.
In the last week alone, the Bengals declined to make a trade for linebacker Arnold Ebiketie after agreeing to terms with the Eagles ; the Lions and Jets altered the compensation they initially agreed to in a trade for safety Andre Cisco ; and the Broncos voided a trade with the Chargers for Daiyan Henley after concerns about the linebacker's knee and the sides were unable to agree to revised compensation.
Last offseason, the Raiders and Ravens agreed to a Maxx Crosby trade before the star pass rusher failed his physical and the deal was voided.
Now front office executives are complaining, and the competition committee is expected to address the issue during the offseason.
Various front office executives last week pointed out that trade terms should not be negotiable once they are agreed to, as the Lions attempted to do in a deal for Cisco and the Broncos attempted to do with Henley.
Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said as much to reporters Thursday, asserting that the loophole in the NFL's trade system needs to be closed so that teams cannot back out of deals.
The Eagles were not pleased that the Bengals reneged on their deal for Ebiketie after learning they would lose a third-round compensatory pick, and the Chargers were unhappy that the Broncos tried to change the terms on their deal for Henley after he took a physical that led to questions about his knee.
It is an issue that bears watching this offseason, and some around the league believe rule modifications are in order.
A possible solution would be preventing the teams from altering draft picks after a trade is agreed upon, only giving teams the option to accept or not.
The Jaguars and Bills will be in competition to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl, but both were in competition for some of the same players ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
The two teams that were most aggressive in trading for Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis were the Bills and Jaguars, who wound up trading a first- and second-round pick to the Eagles.
The two teams most aggressive for former Falcons safety Jessie Bates also were the Bills and Jaguars, who traded second- and fifth-round picks to Atlanta.
After the Jaguars traded for Davis and Bates, the Bills pivoted to two safeties: Arizona 's Budda Baker and Tennessee 's Amani Hooker . The Cardinals declined to trade their respected veteran safety, but the Titans listened and agreed to trade Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Bills for a second-round pick.
In the end, two of the AFC's best each got better. They competed for some of the same players and now are expected to be competing for the AFC championship.
Keeping up with the Joneses
The San Francisco 49ers left no doubt how much they value quarterback Mac Jones .
When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done.
Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers.
This was not the first time the teams had spoken about Jones in a possible trade and not the first time San Francisco had set a price that high. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback and would trade him only for a deal they had no choice but to accept.
To add to that value, Jones won four of his first five starts in place of the injured Brock Purdy last year despite battling injuries of his own and ended up with a 5-3 record and a QB rating of 97.4 for the season.
In the final year of his two-year, $8.41 million contract, Jones is a free agent after the season.
The Packers and Broncos checked in on Titans running back Tony Pollard , whom Tennessee would not have traded for anything less than a third-round pick.
While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted -- Dallas Goedert .
Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027.

title: Why the Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter
summary: The Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter shortly after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- There isn't a particular moment that convinced the Las Vegas Raiders players and coaches that No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was ready to be the team's starting quarterback. It's a collection of things the rookie has done since he arrived at the facility in April.

 For coach Klint Kubiak, it's Mendoza's improvement in his accuracy and knowledge of the offense each week. A month ago, backup quarterback  Aidan O'Connell  recalled watching Mendoza make a few throws in practice, causing him to turn to quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan and assistant head coach Mike McCoy and say, "Those were incredible."

 Wide receiver Tre Tucker , on the other hand, knew Mendoza was capable of being QB1 when he watched the College Football Playoff National Championship game  this past January and saw him lower his shoulder to knock off a Miami defender before diving into the end zone for a touchdown that helped Indiana secure its first-ever title.

 

 "That shows you the kind of guy we are getting," Tucker said.

 On Tuesday, Mendoza was named the starting quarterback after the Raiders traded veteran   Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings . The Raiders' decision to move on from Cousins sent shock waves through the locker room. But with Mendoza, the first quarterback taken by the Raiders in the first round since 2007, waiting in the wings, the team knew this moment would come at some point.

 As abrupt as the change of power might have felt, the Raiders believe Mendoza is ready for his starting debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks , the reigning Super Bowl champs and one of the league's most menacing defenses.

 "Obviously there's a learning curve there, but Fernando is someone who just works extremely hard," starting center Tyler Linderbaum said. "... Anytime you get that with someone who wants to be great, and then on top of that has great mentors with them, I think it's very important. He's ready. We're ready."

 The Raiders might have been more hesitant to move on from Cousins, who is second in the league in touchdown passes this season, if they felt Mendoza couldn't handle the role. To that point, Kubiak doesn't plan to make things easy for Mendoza in his debut.

 Kubiak won't hold anything back from Mendoza and believes the 23-year-old signal-caller can operate the entire playbook. That confidence comes from Mendoza preparing as if he was the starter since Week 1.

 "One of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared," Mendoza said. "All three of us prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we'd like to make."

 

 Mendoza went above and beyond to make sure he was ready in case his number was called. During games, Mendoza stood hip-to-hip with Sullivan. He wore his helmet while relaying the calls to Sullivan as delivered through the helmet communication device.

 Sullivan said Mendoza became more comfortable rattling off plays and helped make in-game adjustments on the sideline with Cousins and O'Connell. At practice, when the first-team offense was getting reps, Mendoza was off to the side with Sullivan working on his footwork, pocket management and timing.

 Playing with the scout team in practice, Mendoza impressed the coaching staff with the tight-window throws he made against the starting defense.

 Sullivan said Mendoza also did a lot of extra work on his own. At night, Sullivan said Mendoza would be on the indoor practice field at the team's training facility with the game script on his phone. Mendoza would visualize the play and call it as he would in the huddle.

 "He literally walks through the play and goes through what his reads [are], his pre-snap communication [and] footwork," Sullivan said. "His command of the offense, his ability to articulate the huddle calls [and] communicate at the line of scrimmage, has improved consistently. It's certainly credit to him."

 Sullivan saw Mendoza's training come together in his NFL debut in Week 5's loss to the New England Patriots . The game was out of reach, but New England didn't take it easy on Mendoza.

 The Patriots pressured Mendoza on 55.6% of his dropbacks, and he didn't flinch. He looked calmer and felt more in control of the offense compared with the preseason. Mendoza completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards during the Raiders' final possession.

 "It's kind of hard to come off the bench at the end to get a feel for the game, and how they're rushing and how your offense is blocking, and he handled it like a champ," tight end Ian Thomas told ESPN. "I don't think anything different this upcoming week. He'll do the same thing."

 

 Mendoza is not walking into a perfect situation. Sure, Brock Bowers has been one of the league's best tight ends. But the Raiders have lacked consistent production from their wide receivers outside of Tucker. The speedy wideout has 33 catches for 529 yards, while the rest of the receivers have 33 combined catches for 347 yards. Las Vegas has struggled to run the ball. On top of that, the defense has allowed opponents to score with ease over the past six weeks.

 Mendoza, on the other hand, has been comfortable playing in difficult situations, dating back to his time at Christopher Columbus High School in Miami. During his senior season in 2021, Mendoza had to lead a young team that featured four new starters on the offensive line.

 His former coach Dave Dunn said that was Mendoza's best season from a leadership standpoint because the team struggled in pass protection and didn't have the offensive weapons that it did in previous years. Dunn said Mendoza never complained and rallied the team to make a trip to the state semifinals.

 

 "He was taking the brunt of the pass rush, and there were times when we couldn't throw it as we did in the past, but you could never tell in his demeanor that he was upset," Dunn told ESPN. "All he did was lead the team."

 As a rookie, Mendoza doesn't have the knowledge that Cousins possesses from 15 years in the NFL. Tucker told ESPN that Mendoza, however, "has a different element to his game" that can help the Raiders. That element is Mendoza's mobility.

 Mendoza's speed is not his strong suit by any means. Nonetheless, he can use his legs when necessary to escape pressure and extend plays.

 "He's young. He will probably get out and scramble or whatever it is," Tucker said. "We always say, any guy that hasn't had a bunch of snaps, they got some fresh legs, so they're going to be out there running fast."

 Mendoza will also allow Kubiak to incorporate more designed rollouts into the game plan. When Kubiak was the offensive coordinator for the Seahawks last season, starting quarterback Sam Darnold had a designed rollout rate of 11%. On designed rollouts, Darnold completed 42 of 56 passes (75%) for 656 yards, eight touchdowns and an interception.

 In Las Vegas, Kubiak used designed rollouts on only 0.05% of Cousins' dropbacks. The expectation is for that number to increase with Mendoza under center.

 "[Mendoza] brings his own unique things, and yes, he's a young man with some juice in his legs, and he's got a lot of talent," Kubiak said. "But in this game on Sunday, it's going to be about way more than his physical talent. It's going to be about his leadership, his knowledge of the offense [and] his ability to read defense."

 The Raiders believe in Mendoza. At the same time, the rest of the team will have to do its part to ensure Mendoza's transition into the starting role is smooth. The Raiders can do that by fixing the run game, which has seemed like a tall task all season. But if they can establish a consistent rushing attack in the final eight games, that should take some pressure off Mendoza.

 

 Based on what Mendoza showed in the preseason and his short playing time against New England, he's going to target the wide receivers quite a…

title: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: 12 players who can help in deeper leagues
summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
full_text:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues. 

 Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions. 

-->

 With four teams on bye this week ( Chicago Bears , Denver Broncos , Philadelphia Eagles , Tampa Bay Buccaneers ) and some key players set to miss time with injuries, let's look at potential pickups to fill holes in your lineup.

 There are multiple ball carriers who can take advantage of opportunities in Week 10 due to injuries and elevated roles. Some will face tough matchups, but it's hard to find volume in deeper formats. The wide receiver spot has upside and some unknowns this week, and I went lighter on the quarterbacks, targeting just two superflex options. 

 

 Running backs 

   Audric Estime , New Orleans Saints (54.7% rostered; vs. Panthers) 

 Estime scored a season-high 14.7 fantasy points in the Week 9 win over the Browns, rushing 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown and adding one reception for 5 yards. Alvin Kamara will still get his touches as a change-of-pace option and receiving back, but Estime is in line to lead the backfield in carries again versus a Panthers defense giving up 27.6 fantasy PPG to running backs (second most in the league). Take the matchup and the volume in this one with Estime.

   Corey Kiner , New England Patriots (40.5% rostered; at Lions) 

 

 With Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) uncertain and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) out, Kiner's role could expand for Sunday's matchup against the Lions. Kiner scored a season-high 11.5 points in the Week 9 loss to Green Bay, rushing eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown. While the Detroit defense ranks in the top five versus running backs, managers can pick up Kiner as a backup plan if Stevenson can't go in the Munich game.

   Kaleb Johnson , Green Bay Packers (13.6% rostered; vs. Vikings) 

 Josh Jacobs ' hand injury has opened the door for Johnson to see more volume. In the Week 9 win over the Patriots, Johnson scored 12.8 points, finishing with 68 yards rushing and a touchdown on 14 carries. While I don't love this matchup versus the Vikings defense, Johnson can handle early-down volume and managers in deeper formats can play him for goal-line usage here, too.

   Dylan Sampson , Cleveland Browns (22.7% rostered; vs. Texans) 

 Sampson is the receiving back I like in Week 10. He has scored 10 or more points in two of his last three games, and he has at least three receptions in each. With the rushing volume he also sees, Sampson can give managers 8-10 touches versus Houston, and the pass-catching upside increases his value as a flex option.

 

 Wide receivers 
 

   Jordyn Tyson , New Orleans Saints (41.9% rostered; vs. Panthers) 

 

 The rookie saw his first game action last week after suffering a hamstring injury in camp, catching all four of his targets for 30 yards versus the Browns. Tyson, who ran 16 routes in that game, could see his role increase this week against the Panthers. He has the playmaking traits to produce if given more volume. Tyson is a solid flex play this week in deeper formats.

   Ryan Flournoy , Dallas Cowboys (27.0% rostered; vs. 49ers) 

 With George Pickens (hamstring) out last week versus the Colts, Flournoy caught just two of three targets for 53 yards, while CeeDee Lamb saw 16 targets. Not what I expected there. We'll monitor Pickens' status ahead of Sunday's game versus the 49ers, but let's manage expectations for Flournoy in this one. It's a tough matchup, too. I see him as a deeper-league WR3.

   Caleb Douglas , Miami Dolphins (31.0% rostered; at Colts) 

 Quarterback Kyle McCord will make his first pro start Sunday with  Malik Willis  (groin) placed on IR. McCord has the deep-ball ability and touch to make plays down the field, so let's get Douglas in the mix. Douglas has scored 13 or more points in two of his last three games, and he can win at multiple levels of the field. Target Douglas as your deeper-league flier this week versus the Colts.

   Tutu Atwell (13.7% rostered) and  Konata Mumpfield  (10.8% rostered), Los Angeles Rams (at Cardinals) 

 With both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR, someone must emerge as a perimeter target for Matthew Stafford . I think Atwell provides more upside here given his vertical ability and open-field speed, while Mumpfield can operate as a possession target for Stafford off play-action and quick throws. Neither player has more than 15 receptions on the season, so there are some unknowns here, but the matchup versus Arizona is favorable, as the Cardinals have allowed 11 touchdowns to wide receivers (second most in the league).

 

 Quarterbacks 

   Geno Smith , New York Jets (21.4% rostered; vs. Bills) 

 Smith had a season-low 7.4 fantasy points in the Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, but he scored 18 or more points (with multiple touchdown throws) in Weeks 7 and 8. I have Smith ranked as a midtier QB2 this week, so let's not get too excited. But he has enough value to fit in superflex lineups for the matchup with Buffalo.

   Aaron Rodgers , Pittsburgh Steelers (37.3% rostered; at Bengals) 

 The Steelers' passing offense has lacked explosive ability in recent games. However, in the Week 4 matchup versus the Bengals, Rodgers scored 22.68 points, throwing for 292 yards and three touchdowns. Managers will need a similar game script, but Rodgers should see opportunities to push the ball to the third level of the field in this one. Rodgers fits as a superflex starter this week.

 

 Tight end 
   Darren Waller , Carolina Panthers (26.1% rostered; at Saints) 

 In the Week 9 loss to Denver, Waller posted season highs in fantasy points (23), receptions (eight), targets (10) and yards (90). While managers shouldn't expect another breakout week for Waller, he has 12 or more points and a touchdown in two of his past three games, and the Saints rank in the bottom 10 versus tight ends. Play the matchup.

 

 D/ST 
   Miami Dolphins (5.5% rostered; at Colts) 

 The Dolphins have at least two sacks and a forced turnover in three straight games, and they now get a Colts team that just traded away wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen . Expect them to play more single-high coverage and get extra numbers in the front to limit running back Jonathan Taylor . This is a quality matchup for the Dolphins, which makes them a good pickup for deeper-league managers.

title: Despite Cousins trade, are Vikings back to square one at QB?
summary: Cousins can give some short-term relief, but his future and the search for a franchise QB remain uncertain.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings drew external praise  and generated internal celebration  this week after reacquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins , a beloved figure among team employees and a player with at least a reasonable chance of stabilizing an offense that has flopped in the past two seasons. 

 Regardless of how the next few months play out, however, the trade guarantees the Vikings will be in a familiar place next spring: looking for a starting quarterback. 

 There is a conceivable path toward keeping Cousins in 2027, but it wouldn't be simple -- and that's assuming he wants to play a 16th NFL season at age 39. Cousins' contract contains three void years from 2027 to 2029, giving the Vikings two options: Pay a $10 million roster bonus and bid him farewell, or negotiate a new contract. Anyone familiar with Cousins' business acumen knows that if he were to do anything other than demand a premium quarterback deal, it would be the first time in his career. 

 The topic surfaced briefly amid the week's chaos. General manager Nolan Teasley said there is "always potential" for exploring a future with Cousins, adding that the Vikings "understood everything that we were inheriting."

 

 Teasley was referencing Cousins' contract, but in a larger sense, it has always been clear that the GM inherited a perpetually open-ended quarterback situation when the Vikings hired him May 30.

 The decision to sign Kyler Murray to a one-year contract two months before Teasley arrived signaled the termination of the organization's faith in 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy , who was traded away in September. What has happened since is best viewed as extended triage after one of the all-time busts in Vikings draft history . Murray got six starts, a tryout hampered by a concussion and a strained hamstring, before the Vikings went looking for their next option. 

 Coach Kevin O'Connell refused to write off Murray as a failed experiment -- "It hasn't been ideal," he said, "but I wouldn't by any stretch say that's a complete thing" -- and it wasn't just coachspeak. Given the injury issues the Vikings have faced, beginning with Cousins' torn right Achilles tendon in 2023, there is a nonzero chance that Murray finds his way back onto the field in a meaningful way this season. But based on his performance so far, it's hard to consider him a realistic option to start in 2027. 

 

 The rest of the NFL's pending free agent class is, as usual, filled with veteran backups ( Jacoby Brissett , Marcus Mariota , Gardner Minshew II and Kenny Pickett among them) and flawed or limited current starters ( Deshaun Watson , Geno Smith ). It's always possible that a starter under contract becomes available via trade, whether it is the Los Angeles Chargers'  Justin Herbert or even the Los Angeles Rams ' Matthew Stafford . Former Vikings starter Sam Darnold 's future with the Seattle Seahawks  is unclear due to his contract and regression this season. ESPN's FPI projects the Vikings to have the No. 25 position in the 2027 draft.

 As a franchise, the Vikings are no stranger to the decision they're facing. Barring Murray's return, they'll field a different Week 1 starter in 2027 for the fifth consecutive season. They entered this season having had 17 different quarterbacks lead them in passing during a season in the free agent era, which began in 1993, tied for third most in the NFL. Murray was on track to the be the 18th, but Cousins would need to throw for only 1,023 yards over the Vikings' final nine games to overtake him. 

 The 2027 decision will have some heavy consequences. Most immediate among them is the impact on receiver Justin Jefferson , whose Hall of Fame arc has been threatened by the team's quarterback saga. Jefferson led the NFL in yards per game (96.5) over the first five seasons of his career (2020-24). Since Cousins' departure, Jefferson ranks No. 25 with an average of 60 yards per game. The Vikings have used eight different starting quarterbacks during that period, and Cousins' homecoming will mark the 15th time they have made an in-season change from one week to the next since the middle of 2023, when Cousins got hurt.

 Jefferson this week acknowledged what he called the "joy" of Cousins' return and said he is "pretty sure" the passing offense will elevate. But with a $49.4 million salary cap hit in 2027 that presumably will need an adjustment, he'll likely hit a natural inflection point this offseason. Jefferson has supported the team throughout the quarterback decisions that have impacted his production, but if there were ever a time for him to exert pressure on the process, it would be next spring. 

 

 Another critical ramification will be the type of offense the Vikings' 2027 quarterback will be asked to run. Lessons from the aftermath of Cousins' 2023 injury remain relevant. There is a narrow quarterback profile with a history of success in O'Connell's scheme. Murray played far below his career baseline, most notably with an 18.3% off-target rate, and McCarthy's confident performances following his trade to the New York Giants have raised some eyebrows among league sources. 

 In talking about Cousins' skills this week, O'Connell emphasized the "principles of how he plays the position -- the rhythm, the timing, the anticipation, the accuracy." Those attributes might sound central to the success of any quarterback, but there is enough of a sample size in Minnesota to suggest they need to be present at high levels for the Vikings.

 Many of the answers are in Cousins' hands. His performance over the coming weeks and months will factor heavily into whether the Vikings remain on track for the postseason and perhaps a deep playoff run. Or will his sentimental return serve as a bookend on an era approaching its natural conclusion?

 That story has yet to be written.

title: T.J. Hockenson unlikely to play Sunday vs. the Packers
