title: Vikings to start reacquired QB Kirk Cousins vs. Packers
summary: Coach Kevin O'Connell called Kirk Cousins' ability to get reacquainted with the Vikings' offense "impressive."
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Although there wasn't much question about it, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Friday that quarterback Kirk Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers , five days after the Vikings reacquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline.
"I can't give him enough credit for coming in here and how he's gone about the week," O'Connell said, "both him and the coaching staff, getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can. It's been really impressive what he's been able to do, and just the command and getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody has been very, very impressed with."
In the immediate aftermath of the trade, O'Connell had stopped short of naming Cousins his starter for Sunday, saying he wanted to make sure the veteran felt comfortable with the quick turnaround. The two spent much of Wednesday morning together, working through a playbook that Cousins first learned when the Vikings hired O'Connell in 2022. Since departing Minnesota after the 2023 season, Cousins has played for both the Raiders and the Atlanta Falcons . He had only two practices this week with the Vikings, on Thursday and Friday, but O'Connell saw no red flags.
"It's something we've always known about him," O'Connell said, "but the way he threw the football this week was just a really cool thing to see."
Cousins, however, won't have his full complement of pass catchers to work with Sunday. Tight end T.J. Hockenson won't play because of wrist and chest injuries suffered in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Wide receiver Jordan Addison , meanwhile, was added to the injury report Friday because of a thumb injury suffered in practice. The Vikings listed him as questionable.
Two other starters, linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) and defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), were also ruled out.

title: Patriots are 6-0 after a regular-season loss under Vrabel: Can they do it again?
summary: New England plays in Munich, Germany, this week. Catch up on what's happening abroad in this week's Patriots notebook.
full_text:
MUNICH -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Patriots resolve: The Patriots are 6-0 under coach Mike Vrabel in regular-season games after a loss, and they look to keep that streak alive Sunday as underdogs against the  Detroit Lions  at FC Bayern Munich Arena (Fox, 9:30 a.m. ET).

 Quarterback Drake Maye summed up Vrabel's knack for bringing out the best in his team in those situations, saying, "Coach Vrabes always says, 'Try not to ride the roller coaster. Try to ride the merry-go-round.' Keep going around and trying to keep the same mindset."

 A seven-hour international trip to Munich after the sting of last week's 45-27 home loss to the Packers has created a unique challenge. Not to mention the 6-2 Lions are among the league's upper-echelon teams, playing in arguably the league's best division, the NFC North.

 

 The 5-4 Patriots have their bye after the game, but the urgency around the team has been evident as it tries to stay afloat in the AFC playoff chase . If the playoffs started today, the Patriots would be the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC.

 Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson , who has a knee tendon issue that is threatening his availability for the game, has been pushing to play. Likewise with receiver A.J. Brown , who missed the past two games because of a knee flare-up but returned to practice this week and had Vrabel feeling "pretty good" about his status early Friday.

 As for the defense, which was carved up by the Packers in an uncharacteristic string of fundamental and communication breakdowns, the unit struck Vrabel's merry-go-round theme with its approach this week.

 "We've been there before. You get another opportunity and what you do with that is up to us," said cornerback Marcus Jones , one of the team's six captains. "We went back into the film room, accepted the situation of what we put out there on film, and our job is to not put that back out again. We have the guys that can do it."

 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez , the 2024 second-team All-Pro, is under the brightest spotlight. He was targeted relentlessly last week, allowing a career-high 10 catches for a career-high 187 yards, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Gonzalez will need to rebound against top Lions receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown (ranks ninth in receiving yards per game at 82.1) and Jameson Williams (leads NFL receivers in air yards per target at 15.43).

 Asked about the Patriots' resolve after losses under Vrabel, Gonzalez said it comes back to the team identity Vrabel preaches.

 "Leaning on the guys; after a loss, you stick together," he said. "You have a bad taste, so you want to go out there and play better."

 

 Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was pleased with how defenders responded in their biggest practice of the week on Wednesday. That was held in Foxborough before players traveled to Munich later that night, and Kuhr cited energy, execution, and improved communication and connection among defensive backs as areas that created a "let's get this thing right" vibe.

 The Patriots had a similar situation after their 35-6 loss to the Jaguars  in Week 3 and rebounded with a 29-26 upset road win over the Bills. Can they do it against the Lions in Munich?

 "It's always a good reminder after a loss. It kind of wakes you up a little bit," tight end Hunter Henry said. "And obviously, the way we lost the other day will definitely wake you up."

 2. Travel strategy : Will it make a difference that the Patriots arrived in Munich on Thursday morning and the Lions arrived on Friday morning? The Patriots went the earlier route so they could have a walkthrough Thursday and then more of a higher-tempo practice Friday.

 "Just having done this a few times, maybe how you feel coming over here Friday and what you're able to get done, I felt like we maybe wanted to do a little more than what had been done in the past on Friday," Vrabel said.

 As for the Lions, coach Dan Campbell said he was "very confident" in the approach to arrive Friday. He acknowledged Friday is the "hardest day," as he saw "a little bit of the head bob" from players in meetings, but promised things would evolve.

 "I know every eight hours here, we're going to begin to acclimate," Campbell said. "I know by the time we hit Sunday morning into that Sunday afternoon game, we're going to be ready to go."

 3. Milton's fine system: The Patriots have had seven offside or encroachment penalties over the past two games, and defensive tackle Milton Williams has had enough. He shared Friday that he has instituted a fine of $1,000 for any front-seven defender who commits those infractions this week, with the proceeds going to Patriots support staff.

 

 "I had a couple earlier in the season. I feel like we talked about it, but it's not enough consequences that come with it, other than hurting the team," he said. "So hurt your pockets -- make you think about it a little bit more."

 4. Turnover tale: The Patriots have failed to record a positive turnover differential in all nine games this season, which is their longest drought since 2005, according to ESPN Research. It has been one of the top storylines of their season, along with injuries, and the theme resonated in Munich leading up to kickoff.

 Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels pointed to timing as a key factor in Maye's three interceptions last week against the Packers, saying, "If we see things a hair earlier, it might be a big play."

 Playing a turnover-free game was a noted goal among players this week.

 "It starts with the ball for us. Obviously, we haven't treated it well and have turned it over a lot," tight end Hunter Henry said in reference to the 19 giveaways that are tied for most in the NFL. "We've got to make a change in some aspect and put our foot down."

 5. German flavor: Among the lighthearted Patriots tales from Munich:

 
 Vrabel introduced trivia in Friday's team meeting by asking players if they knew the nine countries bordering Germany. No surprise that German-born practice squad offensive lineman Lorenz Metz had some of the answers. 
 Metz hosted the weekly offensive line dinner and introduced his teammates, who included tight ends and quarterbacks, to traditional German fare. "That was a lot of pork," center Jared Wilson said. 
 Some players visited McDonald's and relayed a surprise that chicken wings were on the menu. "The McDonald's here is top tier," Wilson cracked. 
 Milton Williams and special teamer Brenden Schooler said they were wide awake at 2 a.m. Friday, trying to adjust, with Schooler hitting the weight room in the hotel at 4 a.m. to get himself moving. 
 
 6. A.J.'s faith :  DeMario 'Pop' Douglas  said having Brown return to practice this past week gave the team a boost because he's the leader among receivers, and that has also shown up behind the scenes in a different way.

 "He started a bible study with some of the guys. I'm loving his growth in faith, and I feel like that's been getting us closer," Douglas said.

 

 7. They said it : "We're just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out. At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there's pretty much nobody out there that's 100%. We have to recognize that, but we also have to find ways to do our job. And Rhamondre's one of those players looking for a way in." -- Vrabel, on Rhamondre   Stevenson pushing to play through a knee tendon issue 

 8. Maye and FIFA: The Patriots spent three days  at FC Bayern Munich's training facility leading up to Sunday's game, and that had Maye reflecting on the days he played the FIFA video game with his brothers, one of whom often beat him with Bayern.

 "First thing that comes to mind is Harry Kane. Big fan of him," Maye said, before rattling off some players on the roster in a moment the German media seemed to appreciate.

title: NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator
summary: The NFL provided some additional details about the investigation into how Jalen Hurts' blood clots were handled in response to an inquiry from a U.S. senator.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts ' blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive.
The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware.
"As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester's office Friday.
"The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely. For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA. Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance."
The joint review into Hurts' situation has not officially begun as the NFL and NFLPA work to hammer out its parameters.
Hurts, 28, is expected to sit out the rest of the 2026 season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs in October.
He was originally diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London before the Philadelphia Eagles ' Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars . He played in the game, flew home with the team and practiced in full the following Wednesday before a follow-up ultrasound that evening showed the blood clot had moved.
Hurts was placed on injured reserve Oct. 17. Two days later, his agent, Nicole Lynn, and the team released a joint statement about Hurts, saying, "After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations."
His treatment involves anticoagulation or "blood thinners," which prevents him from participating in any contact activities, including football.
The NFLPA has not invoked Article 39 of the CBA, which allows the union to launch a formal investigation into the health, safety or medical care provided by club-affiliated personnel, but as the statement shows, some of its guidelines will be used during this process.
Under the CBA, the neutral physicians must issue a written report within 60 days of their selection, and their recommendations to address and correct any issues need to be acted upon by both parties.
Blunt Rochester penned a letter to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in October seeking answers on the circumstances surrounding Hurts and clarity on the league's blood clot protocols.
In a statement Friday, Blunt Rochester expressed gratitude to the NFL for providing an update while encouraging the league to use its platform to further education around blood clots.
"We welcome the opportunity to provide additional information, and find ways to support your efforts around raising awareness and improving outcomes related to blood clot disorders," Miller wrote.

title: Eagles release wide receiver Hollywood Brown per request
summary: Receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Eagles upon his request.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Wide receiver Hollywood Brown , who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday upon his request.
The two sides came to terms on a noninjury settlement that will offer financial relief to Philadelphia as part of the agreement, a source told ESPN. The Eagles are comfortable moving on from Brown with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due to soon return from injuries, and with Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon emerging as solid options.
Brown, 29, signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. He was brought in along with Wicks, Elijah Moore and Lemon to help complement Smith following the trade of A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots .
A significant role for Brown never materialized, however, even with injuries to Smith and Wicks. He appeared in four games (one start) and had five catches for 63 yards on eight targets. All five of his catches resulted in first downs.
Brown acknowledged he anticipated playing more when he joined the team but said he wasn't taking anything personally.
"I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said in October as questions swirled about whether he'd be traded before the Nov. 10 deadline.
"It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for.
"Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play," he added, "but at the end of the day, it's not my plan."
Brown has played for the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs , Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens over his eight-year career. He had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Chiefs in 2025.

title: Seahawks are hurting with injuries, but two players will return vs. Raiders
summary: QB Drew Lock will start again for Darnold. And LB Uchenna Nwosu and WR Rashid Shaheed will return to the field in Las Vegas.
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. --  Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock had a good week of practice as he prepares to fill in again for Sam Darnold on Sunday against the 4-5  Las Vegas Raiders  (4:05 p.m. ET, CBS) -- this time despite a pair of ailments of his own.

 Lock was already dealing with an injury to his right elbow when he hurt his oblique last Sunday in Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals . He was again limited in practice all week, as has been the case since the start of Week 6.

 "Similar cadence in workload in terms of last week," Macdonald said Friday. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape."

 In addition to Darnold (quad, rib) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) -- whom Macdonald had ruled out earlier in the week -- the Seahawks will be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) again Sunday.

 They'll get outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu  (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee) back against the Raiders after each missed the past two games. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed will play Sunday after missing two days this week to tend to a personal matter.

 Lock said Thursday that he was feeling good, and that his oblique injury wasn't impacting his throwing all that much. It's on his right side, which Lock said is "way better" for a right-handed quarterback than a left oblique injury, which caused him to miss two weeks during the preseason when he was with the New York Giants in 2024.

 

 "I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week, and here we are, we've just got a little something added to it, and I think we're doing the same," Lock said. "We're doing a great job getting ready."

 Macdonald said that No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe "has done a tremendous job" while taking reps with the Seahawks' No. 1 offense as the team continues to manage Lock's workload in practice.

 Sunday's game will mark Lock's third start this season and the fourth time he has stepped in for Darnold, who hurt his glute on the fifth play of the opener, then suffered a cracked rib and a quad injury in Week 8.

 Macdonald has said Darnold might return for the Seahawks' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, following Seattle's bye.

 "I see Sam progressing with his rehab," Macdonald said. "The guys are saying he's doing a great job, and he's progressing. We'll take it a day and a week at a time."

 Williams will miss his second straight game because of a stinger. He took part in pre-practice warmups Wednesday and Thursday but was listed as a nonparticipant all week.

 "It's more of a contact thing," Macdonald said. "So, he's done a good job of staying in shape and staying fresh. He's in the meetings. He's doing all the Leo things. He's just not playing right now."

 Josh Jones will make a third consecutive start at left tackle for Cross, who also did not practice this week. Macdonald said Cross should be ready for the 49ers game on Nov. 29.

title: 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys
summary: The 49ers are listing left tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, while receiver Mike Evans has been ruled out.
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers had two important additions to their injury report this week with left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) now listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys .
According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Williams and Greenlaw suffered their injuries in Thursday's practice, with both players listed as limited for that day because of it. Greenlaw was again limited Friday, while Williams did not practice.
"Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said of Williams. "Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that's enough time for him to be all right."
If Williams is unable to play, the Niners will turn to swing tackle Vederian Lowe to step into the lineup. And if Greenlaw can't play, rookie Jaden Dugger will move into the weakside linebacker spot, according to Shanahan.
"Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday, but if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far," Shanahan said.
Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) will miss his third straight game. He's the only Niner officially ruled out against the Cowboys as he continues to work his way through the tendinitis that flared up in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders .
Shanahan offered a bit more clarity Friday afternoon on when Evans could return, saying there's "a chance" for next week against the Minnesota Vikings but adding that he's "not sure yet."
"It's been going well," Shanahan said. "I'm sure if this was the last game or something, he'd be able to go out there. But we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again, but it's going in the right direction."
In addition to Williams and Greenlaw, all three of San Francisco's top cornerbacks -- Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) -- are questionable against the Cowboys.
So, too, are defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) and defensive back Nate Hobbs (adductor), both of whom are working their way back from injured reserve and could be activated Saturday.
Meanwhile, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 5, practiced all week and is cleared to return against the Cowboys.
"He had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it, but [he] took care of himself real well while he was injured and had a good week."

title: Rookie WR Carnell Tate among multiple Titans starters ruled out vs. Jaguars
summary: The Titans will be without multiple starters against the Jaguars on Sunday, including rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- The Tennessee Titans will be without multiple starters against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), left guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), punter Tommy Townsend (left knee), along with linebackers Cody Barton (concussion) and Anthony Hill Jr . (neck), were ruled out by coach Robert Saleh before practice Friday.
Tate is the reigning AFC Offensive Rookie of the Month after posting 21 receptions for 290 yards and a touchdown across four games in October. The shoulder injury occurred during Tennessee's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 and caused him to miss the following game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Tate's 413 receiving yards led all rookie pass catchers entering Week 9. The Titans were optimistic Tate would return after the bye week, but the shoulder "stuck on him a little bit," according to Saleh.
Second-year receiver Chimere Dike will get a chance to step up in Tate's absence. Dike logged a season-high 58 snaps with Tate out. He responded with five receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown.
"It's a new opportunity," Dike said. "Obviously, it's a naturally increased role with Tate being out. But my mindset's not that much different. Make the most of your opportunities and do whatever you can to help the team win."
Skoronski injured a hamstring in the fourth quarter against the Bengals before the bye week. He was carted from the sideline into the locker room and missed practice all week. Reserve offensive lineman James Hudson III played 30 snaps in Skoronski's place. Hudson is expected to get the start against Jacksonville, but Saleh said it will be a game-time decision.
Hill leads the Titans with 82 tackles and was named the AFC Defensive Rookie of the Month for September. This will be his first time missing a game after injuring his neck in Week 8. Barton suffered a concussion in the same game, opening the door for Cedric Gray to see an increased role. Gray was a starter during training camp but suffered a concussion in a UTV accident during Labor Day weekend that made him unavailable for the season opener and relegated him to a reserve role.
"It's something I've been looking forward to all year," Gray said Friday. "It's a long season, things happen, so I kind of knew that at some point my name would be called again. I'm just looking forward to the opportunity to get out there, play a full game on defense and show what I can do."
Townsend will miss his second consecutive game after injuring the knee when the Browns blocked his punt before halftime in Week 7. The Titans signed veteran punter Thomas Morstead to the practice squad to fill in for Townsend. Morstead will get the game-day elevation from the practice squad this week.

title: Commanders QB Sam Hartman to star as 'The Bachelor' in milestone 30th season
summary: The 30th season of ABC's "The Bachelor" that will premiere in March 2027 will star the former Notre Dame standout.
full_text:
After a two-year hiatus, "The Bachelor" has found the apple of its eye for its upcoming season: Sam Hartman .

 On Friday, the hit reality dating show announced that the Washington Commanders  backup quarterback will be the lead of its milestone 30th season. The premise of the show is Hartman finding love, with the goal of a marriage proposal by the finale.

 But if the contestants want Hartman's heart, they might have to know ball a bit.

 

 Hartman, 27, went undrafted in the 2024 NFL draft before the Commanders signed the former Notre Dame and Wake Forest standout to their practice squad after selecting Jayden Daniels with the No. 2 pick in that draft.

 The Charlotte, North Carolina, native spent five seasons at Wake Forest (2018-22) and transferred to Notre Dame ahead of the 2023 season.

 He averaged 8.2 yards per pass attempt, threw for 15,656 passing yards and 134 touchdowns, and completed 59.8% of his passes during his collegiate career. 
 
 

 Athletes being featured in "The Bachelor" franchise is nothing new, though. On the 29th season of the dating show, Grant Ellis -- who played college basketball at Iona and Southern -- held the titular role. The show also counts a list of former NFL players as alumni, including Mel Owens, Jesse Palmer, Colton Underwood and Clay Harbor.

 Jordan Rodgers, Josh Murray, Dale Moss and Matt James, who played for Wake Forest like Hartman, are other former college football players who have been featured in the franchise.

 The season is slated to premiere in March on ABC -- though the filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate Hartman's day job.

title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels finds redemption with game-winning drive
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shook off two interceptions and multiple weeks of failed late-game drives to deliver when Washington needed him most.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shook off two interceptions and multiple weeks of failed late-game drives. Then he delivered when Washington needed him most -- in a game it had to win.
Daniels' 32-yard touchdown pass with 49 seconds remaining gave the Commanders a 24-21 win over the New York Giants on Thursday night.
"Baby Kobe," said Washington receiver Stefon Diggs , who caught Daniels' pass.
Washington (3-5-1) is two games behind the Giants (5-3-1) in the NFC East. Washington had struggled in late-game situations, with three of its past four games coming down to the final minute. The Commanders were 0-2-1 in those contests.
It was nearly a repeat scenario against New York, as Daniels tossed two interceptions prior to the game-winning drive -- one from the Giants' 24-yard line.
But after the defense forced a punt, Daniels and Washington needed only three plays to go 71 yards.
"When I had the opportunity to go out there and win the game, take a deep breath, go out there and just capitalize on the moment," he said. "I didn't want to let my team down."
The final drive represented some vindication for Daniels, who led his first game-winning drive since a 2024 wild-card game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
This season, Daniels and the Commanders failed to convert a 2-point conversion in the opener against the Philadelphia Eagles , and Daniels failed to throw the ball away in overtime, preventing a chance for a game-winning field goal. In their previous two losses, the Commanders' final drive ended in enemy territory.
Last week, the Commanders failed to throw a pass into the end zone despite reaching the 32-yard line with eight seconds remaining in a 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams .
The losses led to Daniels being scrutinized and criticized. He told ESPN last week that he was "for sure" one of the most scrutinized quarterbacks in the NFL.
Daniels, though, said Thursday night that he had only one thought as he jogged onto the field for the final drive: "one play at a time."
Then he did what he hadn't done since his rookie season: lead a game-winning drive. He did so five times in 2024 en route to being named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year.
"He's so cool, calm and collected all the time," Washington tight end Ben Sinnott said. "That energy goes to the whole offense, just being able to trust in him. You all were here for '24; how many drives he led us to victory, knowing what he can do and trusting in what we see every day."
Daniels has played five consecutive games since sitting out two because of a dislocated left elbow. It is the most games he has played in a row since starting all 20 contests in his rookie season. On Thursday, he completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns.
But playing that many games consecutively has helped him find a groove, he said.
"I'm starting to get into that rhythm," Daniels said. "It shows the more games you play consistently, the more reps you get, the more flow in the rhythm that you can [find]. And it was tough last year being in and out of the lineup and trying to catch a rhythm."
But he also threw his first interceptions.
"Got that out of my system, so got to move forward about that," Daniels said. "It just shows resilience and the belief that the team had in me. ... I'm going to kick myself for those mistakes in those critical moments."
Washington coach Dan Quinn said, "With the interceptions, when you come back, it said a lot about him."
Being in a rhythm might have helped Daniels on his final throw. When New York showed a cover zero blitz, Daniels gave a signal to Diggs, who ran a slant against corner Dru Phillips and then broke his tackle attempt and sped to the end zone where he turned at the 1, paused and fell backward into the end zone.
"He'll be the same player he is in the beginning of the game as he is in the end of the game," Diggs said. "Things will happen good and bad and he isn't going to change."
